not establish complete source admission, general progress or Core simulation.

## Fixed declaration ports and callable support

[ScopedSignatureGap.lean](ScopedSignatureGap.lean) proves a source-typing
obstruction in the current annotated model. `Signature` fixes one input/output
`Ty` pair for each exact effect instance and operation. Those types also contain
concrete callable-retention annotations. `Typed.resource` checks its body at
every fresh opening while keeping that same signature.

`two_openings_confine_support` proves that a fixed support list contained in
both `world ++ [first]` and `world ++ [second]`, for distinct identities, must
already be contained in `world`. `all_openings_confine_support` derives this
from universal fresh checking. Actual request typing places both operation
ports in its current world, so `generative_request_ports_confined` applies the
argument to a request whose exact instance remains unchanged across openings.
This is a theorem about the present fixed annotations. It is not a general
source-admission rule for callable payloads.

The [inside-owner fixture](fixtures/callable-payload-inside-owner.ash) allocates
a cell, installs `Send` inside that resource scope, and performs `Send.send`
with a closure containing `let held = c; 42`. Its declaration is
`send : (Unit -> Int) -> Unit`; the clause resumes with unit. The closure retains
the cell, but the selected handler is still inside its owner. The corresponding
Lean `program` is resource-name closed, has no initial runtime resource atoms,
and satisfies structural one-shot usage. Its seven-step raw execution returns
unit and completes the fresh ticket and resource. At the actual cut, the
payload's resource is visible outside the capture and is not owned by it.

Nevertheless, `safe_source_has_no_fixed_signature_typing` proves that **no**
fixed signature, result type or outgoing row can give this closed term a
`ScopedTyping.Typed` derivation. Open the resource at 0 and at 1. Deterministic
lookup gives the same `Send.send` input type in both derivations; world formation
confines its resource support to the empty intersection. Value-support typing
also requires the opened cell to occur in that input type, a contradiction.
The proof does not assume an instance-bounded signature or choose a particular
port annotation.

Current Core accepts and runs the inside-owner fixture, returning `() : Unit`.
The [outside-owner fixture](fixtures/callable-payload-outside-owner.ash) changes
only the scope ordering: its handler is outside the resource. Core rejects it
with `type.resource-escape`, even though the clause does not use the payload.
The existing test `outward_copied_payload_and_still_live_outer_dependency_remain_admitted`
in [resource scope typing](../../../../tests/resource_scope_typing.rs) also passes;
it includes a higher-order payload crossing an unrelated inner scope while its
outer owner remains live. These behaviors follow the current
[resource dependency rules](../../../../spec/static-semantics.md#scoped-cells-and-resource-dependencies),
which track stored dependencies separately and check each crossed owner.

The judgment is a **model correspondence defect** for this required case.
It does not invalidate the narrower typing theorems, establish an inconsistency,
or justify changing Core. The old administrative example with a supplied outside
resource and a fixed support-annotated signature did not establish generative
source typing. The new counterexample shows why that distinction matters.
The fixture and Lean term are a manually related comparison pair; authenticated
Core extraction and a general simulation relation are still unproved. This
does not rule out every possible encoding or semantics-preserving optimization.

The model repair must separate declared type/effect ports from value support.
Resource identities explicitly present in a declared handle type or effect
instance remain part of that type or instance. A closure's additional retained
resources instead need an independently checked support judgment, propagated
through ordinary binding, application, aggregates, handler payload binding and
resume results. Higher-order results need support-transfer information rather
than equality of one global retained list. The actual selected boundary must
still admit the operand's support; the rejected outside-owner fixture is a
required negative case. Adding the cell identity to `Send`, erasing support, or
varying declared ports arbitrarily with the allocation world would change the
problem rather than repair this correspondence. The replacement port judgment
and closed substitution are now proved below. Migration of retained-control
typing and source derivation of support checks remain outstanding; existing
type-based support lemmas cannot simply be reused with their support premises
removed.

## Declared ports and independent value support

[ScopedPortTyping.lean](ScopedPortTyping.lean) supplies a replacement type/effect
judgment for the existing scoped `Code` grammar. `Port` keeps scalar, product
and reference types, function input/output types, and latent exact effect
instances. A reference identity remains in its type, and a resource-indexed
latent request remains in its arrow. Only the additional retained-resource
list is removed from function types. `Signature` fixes these declared ports
for each exact instance and operation; it does not depend on the allocation
world or the payload value.

`typed_erasure` proves that every old `ScopedTyping.Typed` derivation yields
the corresponding new port derivation. The mutual proof includes handler
clauses and all current expression constructors. Erasure also preserves
coverage and environment extension. This transports declared types and
immediate/latent effect bounds. It does not transport access, usage, ownership,
or runtime frame annotations. World formation keeps the previous rule
boundaries: it checks reference values, formed result ports, function ports,
and the resource rule's outward row. It does not newly prove formation of
every extra allowed-row entry or every request's instance metadata.

The fixed-signature counterexample now has a port derivation for every fresh
opening. `generative_source_port_typed` uses one parameterless `Send` signature,
with input `Unit -> Int` and output `Unit`. At each opening,
`fresh_payload_same_port_with_actual_support` proves both that same callable
port and the distinct actual support list `[identity]`. Together with the
previous impossibility theorem, this proves that the new port judgment types
a term excluded by every old fixed support-annotated signature.

Port typing alone also types the outside-owner source. That is the intended
separation, not its admission: `outside_capture_rejected` proves that the
existing `AccessChecks` rejects the actual capture through the cell to the
outside handler. The payload retains the cell regardless of whether its
parameter is used. The positive cut in `ScopedSignatureGap` instead leaves the
cell outside the capture and visible to the receiving clause. Both cases keep
the same declared operation and callable ports.

`Support.Env` independently assigns resource bounds to lexical values.
`Support.evaluate` expands a code dependency list under that environment:
explicit resource atoms contribute their identities, free variables contribute
their assigned support, and ticket dependencies contribute no resource atoms.
It is a calculation on retained dependencies, not execution semantics or an
inference theorem for an arbitrary expression's eventual result. In particular,
using the empty support environment must not silently classify an unresolved
ordinary value as resource-free. Relating assigned bounds to actual lexical
values is a remaining source-analysis obligation.

`Support.substitution_support_bound` proves that substituting a closed value
transfers its independently supplied support into actual retained code. The
bound accounts for variable use and binding barriers; an unused parameter
does not add the replacement's support. `parameter_binding_preserves_support`
specializes this to the actual substituted body, and `result_excludes_resource`
derives exclusion from an independent support bound. Neither theorem infers
that bound from the declared type. The outside-owner capture must still check
the operand before any unused-parameter substitution can erase it.

[ScopedPortSubstitution.lean](ScopedPortSubstitution.lean) rebuilds closed typed
substitution for the replacement judgment. World weakening, agreement on free
lexical variables, environment transport, and value ticket/effect transport
support a mutual proof over all code and clause constructors. In a resource
body, the same declaration signature is retained; the substituted closed value
keeps its existing activation atoms while the body opens at a fresh identity.
Shadowing and nested clause parameters are handled explicitly.

The resulting binding and beta corollaries construct actual `RawStep` events
and preserve the current expression's declared port. Beta resets its lexical
ticket scope as the existing machine requires. Their syntactic readiness
premises remain explicit, and they do not establish whole-stack typing.
`selected_clause_substitution_typed` derives parameter and continuation ports
from an actual `ClauseAt` selection and the unchanged operation signature.
`selected_clause_binding_preserves_ports_and_support` then joins port and
support preservation for that same selected body and inserted operand, under
explicit operand and body support bounds.

A higher-order example returns a wrapper calling its bound callback. Typed
substitution preserves its `Unit -> Int` port, while the independent support
proof preserves the inserted callback's cell. The resulting wrapper's actual
support is exactly `[0]`, even though its declared arrow's resource list is
empty. This establishes a concrete support transfer through returned code;
general application/result support summaries remain to be derived.

These layers repair the fixed-port obstruction in expression typing and
substitution. The raw machine, sequencing syntax and structural continuation
usage are unchanged. The runtime port layer below now types retained frames
and historical ticket ports. Connected effect interfaces and the existing
`Valid`/`Ready` and progress theorems still use the old annotated typing and
need an explicit migration and preservation proof.
Source derivation of payload/result support, callable support-transfer
summaries, closing readiness, full progress and Core simulation remain open.

## Runtime port typing and capture preservation

[ScopedPortReadiness.lean](ScopedPortReadiness.lean) derives resource-name
closure and lexical dependency bounds from the replacement port judgment.
Ordinary free variables must belong to the type environment; ticket names
must belong to the current lexical ticket scope. Empty-environment typing
therefore supplies closed runtime values and binding-suffix readiness. Canonical
forms supply actual binding, application and branch transitions. These facts
do not establish live resource access.

The same layer derives each strict context's input/output ports and pending
ticket translation. `typed_focus_progress` constructs an actual machine
`PlainData` frame. Existing runtime metadata remains `Ty`; `embedPort` supplies
a canonical annotation for each inferred port, and `erase_embed_port` proves
that reading it recovers that exact port. Explicit reference identities and
latent request identities are preserved. Empty extra retention fields in that
annotation are not evidence that the actual retained code is resource-free.
Translation uses the actual dynamic owner selected by the lexical ticket scope,
not the source binder's numeral as a runtime owner.

[ScopedPortRetained.lean](ScopedPortRetained.lean) checks the existing runtime
forest directly. `FrameTyped` checks plain contexts, handler clauses, integer
cells, armed/running callback code and saved results, and completion frames.
`StackTyped` recursively checks live captures as well as the active spine.
`ConfigurationTyped` connects current code to that stack. The historical
`TicketSignatures` table stores declared input/answer port pairs. Existing raw
input/answer annotations are compared through `eraseType`, including at live
and spent clause boundaries.

Old scope, context, frame, stack and configuration typing all erase into this
judgment on the same runtime objects. This is a forward compatibility result.
Equality of erased ports does not imply equality of the old `Ty` annotations;
old `Fits` and type-based well-formedness theorems cannot therefore be silently
reused for the new judgment. Ownership, exact selection and dependency theorems
whose premises do not use those old type equalities remain separate evidence.

`handler_cut_retains_typing` decomposes an actual exact cut into typed captured
and outside forests and the selected handler's typed clauses. Resumption
recomposes the saved capture with the **full** clause prefix and spent boundary.
Historical port equality relates the value supplied by `resume` to that actual
saved input. Every raw transition whose current expression is a closed value
preserves configuration port typing, including cleanup invocation/completion,
handler/cell return, clause return and internal retirement. Plan generation
retains typed callback code and known retirement records; materialization and
actual disposal preserve this port judgment. Those plan results do not derive
closing support, outward effects or exact interpreter compatibility.

`capture_constructs_typed_configuration` constructs an actual capture step,
the substituted clause body, and a typed successor. Clause coverage and exact
selection supply the body; expression typing supplies operand closure and
parameter readiness. The new ticket records the fixed operation result port
and the actual handler's answer port. Only the new raw input annotation is
embedded; the handler's existing answer metadata is retained. Registry absence
is explicit and is not a substitute for freshness in the issued-owner history.

`capture_constructs_ports_ledger_support` connects that derived step to the
ownership ledger and live support. It takes the current support invariant,
the actual `AccessChecks`, and a fresh issued-owner list, and preserves all
three facets for the same successor. It does not assume successor typing.
`resume_preserves_ports_ledger_support` gives the corresponding full-prefix
resumption result; it derives the local access checks from the resume form.
Neither theorem claims the complete joined effect, usage, name and registry
invariant, and the supplied world is not yet related to issued history by that
complete invariant.

The safe callable fixture has port typing at its initial state, after resource
entry, at the request, after capture and resumption, and through all three
completion returns in its existing raw trace. It uses one fixed declaration
signature and a historical port record at capture. This is a concrete execution
comparison, not a universally quantified source-admission theorem. Its ledger
and positive payload boundary remain independently proved in the earlier
fixture evidence.

The old type-derived release shortcut is deliberately absent. A new negative
example gives a resource-retaining callback a resource-free declared result
port at a cell-return boundary. The new configuration port judgment holds,
but `escaping_return_access_rejected` proves that the actual release check
fails. Declared cell result ports exclude explicit local identities; actual
stored-resource exclusion must come from independent support evidence.

This migrates retained-code port composition, exact capture, full resumption
and completion/disposal typing. The following layer connects effect interfaces
and resumption. The common historical record with independent permissions,
joint validity, closing readiness and general progress still need migration.
General source support and closing analysis and authenticated Core simulation
remain outstanding.

## Ordered effect interfaces with declared ports

[ScopedPortEffects.lean](ScopedPortEffects.lean) gives the replacement port
judgment connected interfaces on the existing ordered stack. Its historical
`ContinuationContract` records declared input/answer ports and separate resume
and closing effect rows. `EffectScope` connects the lexical ticket binder to
that actual owner's complete contract. No continuation-use permission or
resource-support claim follows from these fields.

`EffectFrame` checks actual retained contexts, clauses, callback code and saved
results at each frame's incoming/outgoing interface. `EffectStack` connects
those interfaces through the active spine and checks dormant captures against
their recorded resume rows. At each live boundary both recorded resume and
closing rows must fit the outside interface. This is the existing conservative
effect condition, including when disposal is not permitted; it does not prove
that a closing plan exists or is safe.

The two stack judgments have different jobs. `EffectStack` leaves live/spent
raw `Ty` metadata unrestricted. `EffectConfigurationTyped` also requires
`StackTyped` on the **same actual forest** using the **same record's port
projection**. That second judgment compares every live/spent annotation through
`eraseType`. Their conjunction therefore connects request effects and runtime
ports without requiring equality of raw retention annotations.

Exact handler cuts preserve the captured and outside effect interfaces and the
selected handler's actual clause interface. `resume_effect_recomposition`
reconnects the saved capture through the full current clause prefix and spent
boundary. `resume_preserves_effect_configuration` joins that result with operand
typing and saved port equality from the same historical record. It only rewrites
equalities between declared ports. `resume_preserves_effects_ledger_support`
constructs the same concrete resume event and preserves connected typing,
ownership conservation and the separate live-support invariant. It still does
not establish usage, name history, closing readiness or full joint validity.

`current_request_is_interpreted_or_exported` derives a local exact interpretation
or outgoing-row membership. This disjunction is inclusive: outgoing membership
alone does not prove that lookup failed. `unhandled_current_request_is_exported`
therefore requires an actual `resolve = none` result before concluding that an
outward request is allowed. With an empty outgoing row,
`current_request_has_interpretation` establishes an actual local interpretation.
This is lookup availability, not yet request-step progress or a Core simulation.

The callable fixture now has connected typing at its source, fresh opening,
request, captured clause and resumed continuation under one fixed declaration
signature. Capture's two endpoint derivations are concrete evidence; the new
layer does not yet prove general connected capture preservation. A separate
negative example strengthens the release boundary test: the escaping callback
has connected port/effect typing with an empty outgoing row, while the actual
release access check still fails. Adding effect connectivity does not replace
stored-resource exclusion.

The following layer migrates connected capture, completion/disposal, fresh
entry and structural closing readiness. The full invariant, source-derived
support and closing conditions, and correspondence with validated Core remain
open.

## Connected capture, entry and structural completion

[ScopedPortSteps.lean](ScopedPortSteps.lean) constructs connected capture from
an actual exact handler cut, a typed value operand and an unused historical
ticket slot. The selected handler interface determines its residual row;
that row becomes both the resume and closing row of the new contract. This
is a conservative choice of effect bounds, not proof that disposal is permitted
or that a closing plan exists. The contract stores the operation's output port
and the erased actual handler answer. The successor embeds only the new input
metadata and retains the actual handler answer annotation.

`capture_constructs_effects_ledger_support` joins this constructed capture with
ownership and live support for the same event. It requires the actual capture's
`AccessChecks`, the current support invariant and issued-owner freshness in
addition to registry absence. It does not assume successor typing. The safe
callable fixture has a constructed connected capture successor and connected
typing through all completion returns.

Fixed builtin cell signatures and canonical value forms supply actual read or
write steps after exact builtin selection. A nearer source override therefore
continues to take precedence. `request_effect_progress` inspects actual lookup:
it derives either an outward request with both outgoing allowance and failed
lookup, or an actual typed step and historical registry extension. Its premise
includes an unused historical ticket slot even though only source capture uses
it; `builtin_effect_progress` needs no such premise. With an empty outgoing row,
`closed_request_effect_progress` derives a step for a value-operand request.
These are request-case progress results, not general source-admitted progress.

Every actual raw transition with a closed current value preserves connected
typing, including plugging strict contexts, handler/cell return, callback
invocation/completion, clause completion and internal retirement. Bind and beta
reduction preserve connected typing through closed substitution. These results
do not make arbitrary cell releases safe: actual stored-resource exclusion
remains separate from declaration ports and effect rows.

[ScopedPortCompletion.lean](ScopedPortCompletion.lean) derives focus frames and
handler/cleanup entry metadata, and preserves connected typing through branch
selection and world extension. Fresh resource entry uses the issued-owner
ledger to obtain an actual fresh identity, instantiates the source body, and
weakens all active and dormant retained typing into the larger resource world.
The answer metadata is `embedPort` of the declared result; its erasure equality
connects the new cell frame to the existing stack. The declared-port rule excludes
explicit local identities from the result port and residual row. It does not
infer exclusion from actual returned callable support. Fresh entry of the safe
fixed-signature callable source is inhabited by the new judgment.

`CloseReady` recursively checks a captured forest's closing effect conditions.
Plain frames and handlers disappear; cells and armed callbacks contribute to
the materialized order; nested live captures close before their internal ticket
retirement and the surviving suffix. Running callbacks, closing frames and
retirement frames have no constructor. Each callback is typed at its actual
latent requests and may use resources supplied by its remaining suffix plus
the outward closing row. `close_ready_constructs_plan` constructs the actual
`makePlan` result and a `PlanTyped` derivation; it does not take a successful
plan as a premise.

Plan typing proves that each invocation has an appropriate local effect bound.
Every resource advertised by `planProvides` resolves to the actual corresponding
builtin in the materialized suffix, even with arbitrary outside control.
`discard_preserves_effect_configuration` connects that plan to the current
historical contract and the full clause prefix using the separate port and
effect projections. `ready_disposal_effect_progress` constructs a fresh close
owner and an actual step preserving connected typing and the ledger. This
relative disposal theorem still requires the known live boundary and structural
closing derivation; it does not derive access or permission admission.

The migrated disposal example executes a callback that reads a retained cell,
then releases that cell and completes its owners. Its eleven-event raw trace,
ledger and connected typing at every listed state are checked on the same
new objects. Negative examples reject releasing the only provider before its
callback and attempting to close a running callback. A nested example places
internal ticket retirement between callback completion and outside cell
release. Another example is both connected and `CloseReady` but loses a source
override during materialization. Its original lookup returns the source handler,
whereas the plan returns the builtin; `SameRequests` is false. This demonstrates
why structural effect readiness cannot replace exact interpreter agreement.

`live_support_does_not_supply_release` strengthens the earlier escaping-result
counterexample: the same configuration has connected port/effect typing and
`AccessValid`, yet its release check fails. Its callback retains resource 0,
which is currently visible in the cell frame. Present liveness does not imply
support after that cell is released. The old `ScopedJoint.value_access_checks`
used annotated value types to establish that stronger exclusion; it cannot be
ported by replacing only the type/effect fields of `Valid`.

The conditional current-state progress theorem already takes `AccessChecks`
and can retain that premise during migration. Restoring the stronger value
progress theorem requires independent returned-value support bounds, related
to actual environments, retained contexts and historical continuation records.
Those bounds must survive substitution, calls, capture/resumption and saved
cleanup-result restoration, and exclude the local identity at every fresh
resource return boundary. Merely adding a current-release predicate to `Valid`
does not derive or preserve future source safety. This is a remaining model
proof obligation; it does not justify weakening Core's existing escape check
or restoring the globally fixed callable-retention restriction.

The current [resource dependency specification](../../../../spec/static-semantics.md#scoped-cells-and-resource-dependencies)
requires actual returned dependencies to follow selected fields and calls,
including helpers and factories; identity-free result types do not erase stored
support. The existing [Core capture analysis](../../../../src/core/capture.rs)
keeps callable result values separately from callable types, and its value
instantiation substitutes an argument into a result only when that result
refers to the parameter. This is implementation evidence for the required
separation and precision. It is not an authenticated extraction or a proof of
the analysis's soundness.

These layers migrate the local connected transition constructions and closing
effect readiness. The following layer connects the full current-state invariant
and conditional progress. Source checking still has to derive each future access
and new-capture closing condition. Source-admitted general progress and
authenticated correspondence with current Core remain unproved.

## Joined port invariants and conditional progress

[ScopedPortJoint.lean](ScopedPortJoint.lean) gives each historically issued
ticket one `TicketRecord`: a declared-port/effect contract and independently
checked one-shot permissions. `Registry.effects` and `Registry.usage` project
from that same record. `RegistryHistory` equates the record domain with issued
ticket owners; registry absence at capture follows from this history and
lifetime freshness. Other transitions retain the whole registry.

The new `Valid` has seven separate derivations for the same named state: the
ownership ledger, ticket/handler name history, current live support, connected
port/effect typing, structural usage, registry history and resource-name
closure. Connected typing uses exactly `resourceWorld` of the issued-owner
history. The independent derivations are joined; none silently supplies an
unproved result-support or future closing bound.

Capture constructs its actual selected clause, substituted body and successor.
It inserts the chosen residual contract and `policy binder` permissions into
one record at the same new runtime owner. The usage update, effect projection
and history extension therefore agree. Resumption derives its active owner
from usage and restores the full clause prefix. `active_live_contract` uses
both effect and port stack derivations to establish only equality between
recorded ports and erased raw metadata; it never substitutes raw `Ty` equality.
Disposal likewise uses generic raw input/answer annotations at the actual live
boundary. Ordinary steps, focus, handler/cleanup entry, fresh resource entry,
closed-value transitions and structurally prepared disposal preserve all seven
fields through the same concrete event. Fresh entry grows the world consistently
with the owner history.

`checked_value_event_constructs_joint_step` and `checked_value_progress` have
new, explicit names and take the current `AccessChecks`. They preserve the
strength of conditional results without copying the old type-derived release
shortcut. Resumption needs no additional caller-supplied access check: its
expression form supplies those local checks, and usage supplies its live owner.
Private proof assembly combines separately derived successor effects with the
independent invariants; public transition results derive those effects from
the actual step rather than assume a typed successor.

The safe generative callable source establishes the new seven-field invariant
and has a constructed fresh-entry successor. Conversely,
`joint_valid_value_can_lack_admitted_step` checks all seven fields for the
escaping-callback configuration, proves that it is a value, and proves that
there is no `NamedAccessStep` from it. Its actual release check fails. This
state is not claimed reachable from admitted source. The counterexample proves
that dropping the local access premise would make value progress false for
this invariant; it does not contradict conditional progress.

[ScopedPortProgress.lean](ScopedPortProgress.lean) proves conditional progress
for every current expression form. `current_progress` takes `Valid`, current
structural `ClosingInterfaces` and actual current `AccessChecks`. It returns a
terminal value, an outward request with both outgoing allowance and failed
local lookup, or a concrete named step preserving `Valid` and every old registry
record. No premise asks for an execution witness or a valid successor. Canonical
forms and syntax decomposition construct the computation cases; finite histories
supply fresh owner and handler activations. An empty outgoing row removes the
outward-observation alternative in `closed_current_progress`.

`ClosingInterfaces` checks active and dormant captures against their historical
records. It requires a closing derivation only when that record permits
disposal. At an actual discard, structural usage identifies the owner and its
disposal permission, active accessibility finds the live boundary, and registry
lookup equates that record with the closing-interface record. The plan is then
constructed at the same record's closing row. No raw metadata equality is
needed. A separate example shows that adding `ClosingInterfaces` to the escaping
value does not supply its missing release check: it has no tickets to close.

`initial_progress` derives that the source is already a value or constructs
its first step from closed source port typing, usage and empty initial resource
dependencies. The repaired fixed-signature callable
source has an actual first step even with builtin cell signatures installed;
a pure callback request also inhabits the outward observation. These are
initial-state and concrete observation checks. `Valid` at the successor does
not establish future `AccessChecks` or preserve `ClosingInterfaces`.

The current-state joined invariant and conditional progress have now migrated.
The following layer preserves closing readiness with the same records. Source
checking must still establish and preserve returned-value support and each new
capture's closing conditions. The required source-to-execution progress and
all-finite-executions safety theorem, and simulation of validated Core, remain
open. Adding current checks under another name would not close that gap.

## Preserved closing readiness with declared ports

[ScopedPortPrepared.lean](ScopedPortPrepared.lean) combines the new joined
`Valid` with `ClosingInterfaces` in `Ready`. The record, its one-shot rights,
and its closing row are shared with the actual usage and effect derivations.
Existing interfaces survive every raw transition, provided an allocation
supplies `AllocationClosing` for its new ticket. Capture checks only the actual
new record and capture: if the record permits disposal, that capture must have
`CloseReady` at its recorded closing row. A resume-only record adds no disposal
obligation. World growth, updated cells, full-prefix resumption, materialized
closing plans and retirement preserve existing interfaces.

`nonrequest_ready_progress` constructs a successor preserving `Ready` and the
exact registry for a non-request expression. It takes current `AccessChecks`.
Registry history proves equality of records when no ticket is allocated;
preservation does not merely preserve their projections. The separately named
`checked_ready_value_progress` also retains the access premise. A typed initial
source with structural usage and no initial resource dependencies establishes
`Ready`; the repaired fixed-signature source has a constructed first resource
entry preserving it.

`capture_constructs_ready_obligation` derives the actual named capture and new
joined invariant, then makes the remaining structural closing obligation
explicit at the selected residual row. It does not assume successor validity.
It also does not infer that obligation from source syntax. Finally,
`ready_value_can_lack_admitted_step` establishes `Ready` for the escaping-value
counterexample while proving there is no admitted next step. Adding preserved
closing readiness therefore does not repair unsafe normal return. Future
access and new-capture closing conditions still need source derivations.

## Independent storage and result summaries

[ResultSummaries.lean](ResultSummaries.lean) starts the missing return-support
analysis over the existing `Code` grammar. `Summary` is analysis metadata.
It adds no computation form, bind operation or monadic embedding. A callable
has separate captures and body-result metadata; products and symbolic
applications retain their structure. `unknown` and unresolved parameters or
applications have `support = none`, which never means an empty resource set.

Ordinary source variables are mapped through an analysis environment. Summary
parameters use de Bruijn indices: a callable's captures are in its outer scope,
while its result body introduces one parameter. Renaming and substitution lift
only under that result binder. Their scope-preservation theorems, and
`analyze_preserves_scope`, establish that this bookkeeping is well scoped.
`callResult` performs one known-call unfolding and keeps an unresolved call
symbolic. The structural analyzer itself leaves applications symbolic;
requests, handlers, resumption, disposal, resources and cleanup currently give
`unknown`. These are explicit analysis limits, not restrictions newly imposed
on Core or on the calculus.

`closed_value_storage_sound` connects this metadata to actual code: for every
actual closed value, its analyzed storage support is exactly the resource
projection of its syntactic dependencies. The lambda case checks captures;
it does not certify the inferred result body. A resource-retaining constant
closure illustrates the distinction: stored support is the retained identity,
but its known-call result summary is scalar. A concrete beta followed by bind
reaches the integer result through the existing `RawStep` rules. This is an
execution example, not a general result-soundness theorem. A factory example
also keeps a supplied callable's structure inside a returned callable.

Two checked counterexamples constrain the next proof. Exact syntactic equality
between analysis after concrete beta substitution and symbolic call unfolding
is false: inserting a closure expands its syntactic dependencies, while the
symbolic capture retains the whole callable summary. Both factory summaries
have storage support `[7]`. Comparing only current `support` is also too weak:
parameters 0 and 1 both initially yield `none`, yet substitution can give them
different resource identities. The eventual comparison must preserve result
and application structure and compare capture storage in a way stable under
closing substitutions. The checked mismatch is a representation issue in this
analysis component; it does not establish a Core correspondence defect.

Well-scoped metadata alone does not realize an actual value. The following
layer proves a substitution-stable comparison and analyzer correspondence to
concrete substitution. Environments backed by actual values and a fundamental
result-soundness theorem for computations and retained control remain to be
established. That theorem must derive normal-return exclusion at each fresh
resource boundary, allowing outer resources to remain. Handler operands,
continuation captures and cleanup saved results need their own bounds even
when the final result is resource free. These are obligations to prove from
structural rules, not assumed future access checks. Neither general
source-admitted progress nor authenticated Core simulation follows from this
first metadata component.

## Substitution correspondence for result summaries

[ResultTransport.lean](ResultTransport.lean) defines two comparisons over the
same metadata. `StorageEq` requires equal support observations after every
summary-parameter substitution, including substitutions that resolve previously
unknown parameters. It compares ordered dependency lists, retaining their
multiplicity. It quantifies over arbitrary substitutions, so its preservation
proofs need no hidden well-scoping premise. `ResultEq` preserves scalar,
resource, parameter, product, application, join and unknown structure. For
callables it compares captures by `StorageEq` and result bodies recursively by
`ResultEq`. It therefore forgets the internal shape of a value used only as
storage while retaining that shape when the value is returned or applied.

Renaming and substitution composition are proved with the different capture
and result-binder scopes. Both comparisons are reflexive, symmetric and
transitive. They survive renaming and substitution, including replacing their
parameters by related rather than identical summaries. `ResultEq` implies
`StorageEq`, and `call_result` preserves `ResultEq` through one known-call
unfolding. The factory summaries that failed syntactic equality now correspond.
Distinct parameters are not storage equivalent, unknown is not equivalent to
a formal parameter, and equal callable storage does not equate different
callable results.

The analyzer respects related environments. Its exact renaming and
summary-substitution laws transport metadata through the environment; these
laws alone do not concern `Code.subst`. Separate dependency-sensitive
environment congruence proves that analysis of an actual closed value is
independent of the surrounding ordinary environment. Such analysis is also
unchanged by summary-parameter renaming or substitution.

[ResultCodeSubstitution.lean](ResultCodeSubstitution.lean) connects those laws
to actual code. `code_substitution_dependencies` and the mutual clause theorem
prove exact dependency expansion: each free occurrence of the replaced
ordinary variable expands into the closed inserted value's dependencies, in
place. Surrounding ordinary-variable and ticket filters cannot remove those
resource dependencies. Shadowed ordinary parameters prevent substitution as
specified by the existing syntax. The theorem covers every expression and
clause constructor, including dependencies in handler bodies and effect
metadata. It requires an actual `ClosedValue`, not an arbitrary well-scoped
summary.

`code_capture_substitution` combines that expansion with actual closed-value
storage soundness to relate the capture metadata before and after substitution.
`analyze_code_substitution` then proves, for every code expression and closed
inserted value, that analysis of concrete substitution is `ResultEq` to analysis
in the extended environment. Lambda and bind shadowing are handled explicitly;
closed inserted values remain independent of the environment under the new
binder. The relation preserves the structure of supplied and returned callables.

`known_lambda_result` identifies one known-call unfolding with analysis of the
body in its extended environment. `beta_summary_correspondence` uses this
unfolding and the concrete substitution theorem; it does not equate a symbolic
application node directly with its reduct. `bind_summary_correspondence`
compares analysis of a value binding with the substituted body. The paired
`beta_constructs_summary_correspondence` and
`bind_constructs_summary_correspondence` construct the actual `RawStep` and
attach the corresponding metadata fact to the same reduct. Beta clears the
current ticket scope, while bind preserves it, exactly as those raw rules
specify. These theorems add no access or ownership conclusion from metadata.
The resource-retaining factory and shadowed parameter examples use the general
results.

This closes concrete closed-value substitution correspondence for the current
analyzer. It is not general result soundness: the analyzer still leaves
applications symbolic and control-sensitive forms unknown. Branch execution
also needs a result approximation relation; `ResultEq` does not identify a join
with one selected branch. A fundamental theorem must relate actual returned
values to inferred summaries through execution, interpret known applications,
and cover handler, continuation, resource and cleanup results. Those structural
rules must establish resource-boundary exclusion and preserve it in retained
control. The new theorems neither assume all future access checks nor establish
them. Source-admitted progress and authenticated Core simulation remain open.

## Canonical return bounds and the unfolding limit

[ResultBounds.lean](ResultBounds.lean) supplies an independent source of
returned-value support evidence. `Port.FirstOrder` has rules for Unit, Bool,
Int, references and products of first-order ports. It has no function rule.
`typed_first_order_value_support` proves that an actual typed value with such
a port has exactly the port's explicit resource dependencies, in their existing
order and multiplicity. It uses canonical value shapes, not the absence of
resource identities in an arbitrary declared port. A callable counterexample
still has an identity-free port and retains resource 0.

The Unit corollary proves empty actual returned support even when separate
provenance metadata is unknown. It does not rewrite unknown metadata to empty.
The cell-return theorem combines the actual value typing with the actual cell
frame's exclusion of its own identity. References to other identities remain
possible: first-order ports retain explicit reference identities rather than
requiring every result to be resource free.

`FirstOrderRelease` structurally inspects the current top frame. A cell requires
its declared answer to be first order; other current frames add no requirement.
`first_order_value_access_checks` derives the current checks for a value from
configuration typing and this certificate. `first_order_value_progress` then
constructs a successor preserving joined validity, or identifies empty control.
`first_order_ready_value_progress` likewise preserves the existing readiness
judgment and registry under builtin cell signatures. These are current-value
results. They do not prove that every later resource return has the certificate,
and first-order results are one sufficient evidence branch, not a restriction
on source programs or on function-valued returns.

The callable-payload example now has a complete seven-step `AccessTrace` over
the same `program`, handler, capture and cell definitions used in the fixed-port
counterexample. The payload retains resource 0, and its actual selected handler
boundary leaves that resource available outside the capture. That boundary
support is checked independently of the eventual Unit answer. Capture and
resumption complete, then canonical Unit support justifies normal cell release.
`callable_source_admitted_execution` adds lifetime owner freshness to enact the
trace as `AccessRunSteps`; `callable_source_final_ledger_and_support` derives
ownership conservation and live support along that execution from the initial
joined state's corresponding fields. Both resource 0 and ticket 7 are completed.
This is not a `NamedAccessSteps` execution or a proof that all seven joined
fields hold at every state. It also does not establish general source admission.
The corresponding current Core fixture returns `() : Unit`; moving the handler
outside the resource owner is still rejected with `type.resource-escape`.

The same module checks a limit on the current result-summary comparison.
Consider two closed, well-scoped pending applications of callables retaining
and returning resources 7 and 8 respectively. Their current support observations
are both unknown after every summary substitution, so `StorageEq` relates the
pending applications and `ResultEq` relates closures storing them. Explicitly
unfolding the applications distinguishes support `[7]` from `[8]`.
`current_comparison_does_not_justify_unfolding` proves that the existing relation
cannot justify even this additional observation in general.

This does not invalidate the preceding substitution theorems, which concern
the current observer. It blocks their unqualified use for stronger inference.
Before application-aware result safety, capture comparison must retain the
structure and returned results of applications used in capture positions, or
compare the intended unfolding-aware observations under substitutions. The
following layer supplies the stronger structural comparison, including nested
applications and callable results, and rebuilds concrete substitution transport.
Congruence for the eventual execution observer and its correspondence to actual
returned values must still be proved. The counterexample identifies an
analysis-model requirement, not a Core defect. Canonical port evidence remains
valid independently; higher-order result soundness, source-derived future
boundary and closing checks, and authenticated Core simulation remain open.

## Normalized capture and result views

[CaptureViews.lean](CaptureViews.lean) strengthens comparison without changing
`Summary`, `Code` or execution. It defines normalized result `View`s and capture
`Atom`s separately. A result view retains products, callables, applications,
joins, parameters and unknowns. A callable contains an ordered list of capture
atoms and its result body. Capture normalization flattens scalar, product and
join storage and keeps only a stored callable's captures. An application atom
instead contains the complete result views of its function and argument,
including any nested callable result bodies. Unknown and application atoms
remain distinct.

Renaming and substitution respect those positions. A parameter in capture
position expands to the inserted value's capture list; an application operand
receives the entire inserted result view. A callable's result body lifts the
de Bruijn operation, while its captures remain in the outer scope.
`normalize_rename` and `normalize_substitute` prove exact compatibility with
the existing summary operations. `capture_substitute` accounts for capture-list
expansion, and `normalize_call_result` commutes normalization with one explicit
known-call unfolding. The views themselves do not execute applications.

`SameCapture` compares normalized capture lists; `Related` compares complete
normalized result views. Both are equivalence relations and survive renaming
and same-parameter substitution. Replacing parameters with different values
requires those values to be `Related`, including their returned structure.
Equal replacement captures alone are insufficient: a checked counterexample
puts the replaced value in function position and obtains different returned
resources. `captured_application_operands` derives related function and
argument views from equal captured applications;
`captured_application_call_result` then proves related known-call unfoldings.
The resource-7/resource-8 applications and closures storing them are now
distinguished, while the original retaining-factory summaries still correspond.
These are general congruence results as well as concrete negative checks.

`View.encode` and `Atom.encode` provide representatives in the original summary
grammar. `normalize_encode` proves the round trip from any result view through
its representative back to the same view; the atom theorem recovers a singleton
capture list. It does not recover an original unnormalized summary from its
view. The checked injective result-view encoding supplies constructive
`DecidableEq View` using the existing finite summary equality. View substitution
identity and composition follow from the existing summary laws and the round
trip. This establishes representation and substitution properties, not actual
runtime-value realization.

[CaptureViewSubstitution.lean](CaptureViewSubstitution.lean) rebuilds the
concrete bridge with these stronger comparisons. An actual closed value's
normalized capture list is exactly the ordered resource atoms of its syntactic
dependencies. The callable case checks its stored captures, not soundness of
its inferred result body. Existing exact code/clause dependency expansion then
establishes `code_capture_substitution` without relying on the old observer
that mapped every pending application to unknown support.

`analyze_code_substitution` proves that analysis after concrete closed-value
substitution is `Related` to analysis in the extended environment. It covers
all existing expression constructors, with explicit lambda and bind shadowing.
The control-sensitive forms remain unknown on both sides; they acquire no
execution or result semantics from this theorem. General bind and beta results
attach the stronger correspondence to the same actual `RawStep` reducts.
Beta compares an explicit `callResult` unfolding with its substituted body and
clears the current ticket scope; bind preserves that scope. The retaining
factory and shadowed-parameter examples now use the general stronger theorem.

This repairs the information loss identified by the preceding counterexample
and closes concrete substitution transport for the stronger representation.
Application-aware support observation, its compatibility with execution,
precise actual-value realization and application-aware branch approximation
remain to be established. The following layer proves a conservative
returned-value bound without unfolding applications. Handler, continuation, resource and cleanup
results still need structural inference rules. The new comparison does not
stand in for those rules or for future access checks. General source progress
and authenticated Core correspondence remain open.

## Conservative normal-result soundness

[ReturnSupport.lean](ReturnSupport.lean) connects the existing conservative
support observer to every constructor of the actual scoped `RawStep` relation.
It introduces no additional expression evaluator. The resulting theorem is
partial correctness: if an actual finite execution returns a closed value and
the source analysis has a finite bound, that value's stored resources are
contained in the bound. It does not assert that the source returns normally.

`Below actual upper` orders current support observations. A finite upper bound
requires a finite actual support list contained in it; unknown upper support
imposes no bound. Containment observes membership, not multiplicity or order.
Unknown actual support cannot refine a finite upper bound. This order concerns
storage only, and deliberately does not compare callable result behavior.

`captured_monotone` and `analyze_monotone` prove monotonicity under pointwise
environment bounds. Branches combine both possible result supports. Callable
storage observes captures. Applications remain unknown even when their function
operand is a known callable. A bind analyzes its suffix with the initializer's
result summary in the bound variable's environment entry. An unused initializer
can therefore contribute no returned support, while execution still evaluates
it strictly. These properties would not justify a more precise observer that
unfolds applications.

`contextResult` follows the existing plain context constructors. Its plug law
agrees with analysis of the actual `Context.plug`, and its monotonicity follows
from the analyzer laws. It uses no synthetic variable that could be captured
by an existing binder. `stackResult` composes those transformers in stack order.
Every non-plain frame, live clause boundary and spent clause boundary replaces
its incoming result with unknown, then continues through the active outside
tail. This forgets precision about normal results at control boundaries. It
does not discard runtime frames, owned captures, or cleanup obligations.

`raw_step_result` proves that the projected successor refines the projected
predecessor for every actual transition. Focus and plug agree exactly with the
context law. Bind uses proved concrete closed-value substitution; beta refines
the unknown application observation. Branch reduction selects a result bounded
by the original join. Entry and cleanup-start rules preserve the unknown
boundary observation; normal boundary exits can reveal a more precise result.
An actual `HandlerCut` proves that the selected handler makes the old projection
unknown before the same outside tail, matching capture's new live boundary.
Full resumption and disposal preserve the outside projection through their
spent boundary. Builtin cell updates preserve the stack transformer. None of
these cases assumes access admission, a successor invariant, or normal
termination of a strict child.

`run_steps_result` and `raw_trace_result` extend that theorem to actual finite
executions. `returned_value_support` specializes it to an empty initial and
final stack and uses the proved exact storage analysis of the actual closed
returned value. Any finite source support list then contains that value's
syntactic resource dependencies. `returned_value_excludes` transfers absence
of a resource from the bound to the returned value. These statements cover
the full raw transition grammar, but their finite-bound premise excludes
sources whose result analysis is unknown. They prove no intermediate access
safety or continued liveness of a retained resource.

The checked branch example returns a closure retaining resource 7 from a source
whose two alternatives retain 7 and 8; its source bound includes both. A
separate five-step trace evaluates an ignored retaining-closure application
before returning an integer, and applies the general theorem to its empty
source-result bound. These are raw and freshness-checked execution examples;
they do not establish live owners or access admission for the referenced
resources. The bound alone establishes neither execution nor termination.
Negative examples show that unknown is not a finite bound and that this
storage order cannot be used to justify known-call unfolding.

This closes conservative normal-result support soundness, not precise
realization of normalized result views. Control-sensitive inference,
application-aware bounds, and admission at individual resource-return and
operation-payload boundaries remain necessary. In particular, the empty-stack
theorem does not supply the checks at an enclosing resource frame: this
observer intentionally forgets its incoming result at that frame. No failure
of current Core correspondence is inferred from this loss of analysis
precision, and no product or normative semantic change follows from it.

## Preserved resource-return obligations

[ReturnBoundaries.lean](ReturnBoundaries.lean) moves from an empty-stack result
bound to individual resource-return obligations throughout active and saved
control. `Excludes identity summary` requires a finite support bound omitting
that identity. `CellBound` accepts either this inferred exclusion or a
first-order declared answer that omits the identity. The latter route still
needs actual value typing before it can justify release; a function port alone
supplies no stored-support bound.

`Checked environment stack summary` follows the actual stack recursively.
A plain frame transforms the incoming summary using the proved context
analysis. A cell checks `CellBound` against that incoming result before
continuing with unknown at its outside tail. Other frame boundaries use the
same conservative result transformer. A live clause checks both its saved
capture and its active outside tail at unknown; a spent clause checks its
outside tail at unknown. Saved captures are checked recursively, including
resources in further nested captures. This is a return obligation, separate
from retained access, ownership, clause rights and cleanup requirements.

Downward monotonicity allows a more precise incoming result to satisfy an
existing check. `checked_append` decomposes an actual prefix and tail using
the prefix's transformed result as the tail's input. It does not incorrectly
give both pieces the same input. Exact cut decomposition proves that a
selected handler resets the outside result to unknown. These facts preserve
the saved resource checks on capture and on full-prefix resumption, including
the clause's intervening frames. Disposal materializes Unit-answer release
frames, so their canonical alternative supplies return checks independently
of the precision lost at earlier closing frames. This proves no cleanup
request availability or interpretation identity by itself.

`AllocationReturn` is a local certificate for newly allocated resources.
When no resource is created it is vacuous. Its cell constructor checks the
actual successor expression and cell answer. In the `enterCell` case this
expression is the freshly instantiated body, not the unopened template.
`raw_step_preserves_checked` proves preservation for every actual raw
transition under this allocation certificate. Existing active and saved
return checks therefore require no fresh hypothesis at capture, resumption,
disposal, ordinary computation or boundary completion.

`EntryChecked` pairs an actual fresh raw event with its local allocation
certificate; `EntriesChecked` composes these events into finite executions.
`entry_checked_executes` and `entries_checked_execute` erase the certificates
to existing `RunStep` and `RunSteps` derivations with the same endpoints.
`run_steps_preserve_checked` preserves the return invariant along every
execution admitted by this relation. This does not establish that every raw
execution from an admitted source has those certificates. Their general
source derivation remains an obligation. `AllocationReturn` itself still
contains only a local entry check, with no next-step witness or full
successor invariant.

There is already one source-derived entry route.
`typed_first_order_entry_certificate` uses existing declared-port typing of
the resource expression, a first-order result, fresh identity, and agreement
between the raw answer's erased type and the declared result. The result is
formed in the original world, so it omits the newly acquired identity.
`typed_first_order_entry_constructs` pairs that certificate with the actual
freshly instantiated entry transition when the source is resource-closed.
This is sufficient entry evidence for first-order answers, not a restriction
that all resource bodies must return first-order values. Freshness here is
relative to the supplied typing world. The construction produces `RawStep`;
issuance-history freshness, whole-stack typing and access admission are
separate requirements when lifting it to a fresh admitted execution.

`typed_cell_return_excludes` connects the invariant to an actual closed value
at its cell frame, using either exact analyzed storage or canonical typed
support. `value_access_checks` derives the current release check; request and
discard cases are impossible for a current value. Value transitions allocate
no resource, so they preserve `ConfigurationChecked` without an additional
entry premise. `checked_value_progress` and `checked_ready_value_progress`
produce the same actual successor with both the existing joint or readiness
invariant and the new return invariant preserved. They no longer take the
current release check as a caller-supplied premise.

Checked examples admit a closure retaining resource 8 at resource 7's return
and reject a closure retaining resource 7 there. A template counterexample
shows why entry checking must account for fresh instantiation: bound source
names have no activation atom before opening, but the returned closure then
retains the new identity. A further example captures and resumes a stack
whose resource returns a function; its return certificate uses the inferred
outer-resource bound rather than first-order shape. That example proves raw
events and return checks, not complete typing, live support or access
admission for the request and its outer resource.

This closes preservation of structural resource-return evidence with local
entry admission and strengthens value progress. General source derivation
for higher-order entry bounds, operation-payload checks, disposal and closing
certificates, precise control/application result inference, and authenticated
Core simulation remain open. The template counterexample identifies an
analysis obligation, not a defect in current Core.

The existing [Core elaboration checks](../../../../tests/resource_scope_typing.rs)
`identity_free_closure_cannot_escape_its_resource_owner`,
`copied_integer_and_constant_closure_have_no_stored_resource_dependency`, and
`outward_copied_payload_and_still_live_outer_dependency_remain_admitted` pass.
They corroborate rejection of own-resource closure escape and acceptance of
copied values and still-live outer payload dependencies. These are elaboration
checks, not a simulation proof or runtime correspondence for the raw example.

## Finite source bounds across resource opening

Here, a source expression means a term of `ScopedExpressions.Code` before
execution or a body before its resource binder is opened. It does not mean
an Ash surface-syntax file or the compiler's current Core data type. `Code`
also represents residual runtime expressions, including allocated identities;
membership in that grammar alone does not characterize an initial program.
The `SourceBound` name below denotes a local template certificate. General
calculus admission must still specify the initial term, declaration and
interpretation assumptions and derive the required execution invariants.
Its relation to current Core is a separate correspondence obligation.

[TemplateDependencies.lean](TemplateDependencies.lean) retains free resource
names in source dependency lists. A resource binder removes its bound name
from the body's dependencies, while its initializer remains outside that
binding. An already allocated identity with the same numeral is not removed.
Ordinary variables and continuation tickets have separate binders; nested
resource arguments in operation metadata also contribute dependencies.

`dependencies_instantiate` and `clauses_instantiate` prove exact ordered-list
transport under lexical opening. Two projections recover the existing runtime
dependency lists and free resource names. Runtime projection drops unresolved
bound names, so using it alone before acquisition would lose evidence. For
resource-closed code, `closed_dependencies_have_no_bound` rules out that loss.

[TemplateSupport.lean](TemplateSupport.lean) uses these lists to infer finite
stored-result bounds before opening. Literals have empty support, references
retain their resource name, pairs and branches combine support, bindings pass
the initializer's bound to the body, and lambdas retain their actual free
dependencies. Applications and control results remain unknown. This is metadata
analysis over the existing expression grammar, with no new execution syntax.

`infer_instantiate` proves that inference commutes with resource opening when
the ordinary support environment is mapped along with the expression.
`runtime_agreement` identifies the inferred result with the existing runtime
support observer on resource-closed code. The closure premise is necessary:
an unresolved source name must not become an empty runtime bound.

`SourceBound` requires a finite inferred result containing only allocated
identities from a supplied world. The Boolean `check` rejects unknown results,
unresolved resource names and identities outside that world.
`check_iff_source_bound` proves soundness and completeness for this particular
sufficient certificate, not for source admission as a whole. World membership
supplies a support bound; it does not establish live ownership.

`check_fresh_opening` proves that the same finite check gives the same Boolean
result before and after opening with an identity absent from the supplied world.
This holds for every `Code` term: unresolved names that opening replaces become
fresh identities outside the world, and therefore remain rejected; other
unresolved names remain unresolved, and allocated identities are unchanged.
It is a property of the checker, not an ownership or runtime-closure theorem.

On resource-closed code, `source_bound_runtime_iff` equates the template
certificate with a finite runtime support bound inside the world.
`fresh_opening_runtime_iff` combines both results: for a resource-closed scope
and a world-fresh opening, checking the body before opening is equivalent to
bounding the opened body's conservative result inside the earlier world.
An example shows that opening with an identity already in the world can turn
a rejected bound reference into an accepted allocated reference. Another
shows that an unresolved lambda capture can have an empty runtime projection.
These examples justify the distinct freshness and resource-closure premises.

`opened_source_bound` transports the certificate to the actual instantiated
body. With resource closure and a new identity absent from the supplied world,
`checked_source_entry` constructs both the actual `RawStep.enterCell` event and
its local `AllocationReturn` certificate. The proof uses inferred exclusion,
so the answer can be function-valued without satisfying `FirstOrder`.
Freshness relative to issuance history, whole-state typing, live access,
operation-payload checks and closing readiness remain separate obligations.

Checked examples reject own-resource captures and aliases, accept an unused
alias or an outer-resource capture within the supplied bound, and distinguish
nested shadowing from initializer capture and same-number allocated identities.
An ignored application's result need not contribute to returned storage; that
fact proves neither safe execution nor termination of the application. The
function-return example constructs a raw entry and its return certificate,
not a complete admitted run with the captured outer resource live.

The copied-read closure is a concrete precision gap: this observer reports
unknown for the read, and therefore cannot bound a closure retaining its result.
Current Ash specifies that reading copies an `Int` and permits closures retaining
only those copies to escape. The existing Core test
`copied_integer_and_constant_closure_have_no_stored_resource_dependency` passes.
This is evidence to improve the model's analysis, not a reason to weaken Core.
Type-informed result bounds still need a preservation argument that respects
the actual operation signature and execution. In particular, the current
`ReturnBoundaries` invariant checks a saved capture with an unknown incoming result.
Using a read's `Int` result inside a later closure also requires carrying that
bound through capture and proving that each actual resumption supplies a value
within it. The stored ticket input port and canonical value bounds provide
evidence for this integration. The
[continuation-bound layer](#declared-input-bounds-through-capture-and-resumption)
below now proves the runtime part; changing the analyzer's read case alone
would not establish initial-term admission. General higher-order and control
result inference, source-derived admission throughout execution and formal
Core correspondence remain open.

## Template certificates through value substitution

[TemplateSubstitution.lean](TemplateSubstitution.lean) connects finite template
bounds to replacement of ordinary variables by actual closed values.
`substitution_below` proves that replacing a variable preserves the conservative
result bound when the replacement's analyzed storage lies within that
variable's bound. It combines concrete code-substitution correspondence with
monotonicity of the existing support observer. It uses no application unfolding;
equality or containment of storage alone cannot justify that stronger step.

`BindingsChecked` checks a finite list of replacements structurally. Each entry
supplies a closed value and compares its actual analyzed support with the fixed
ordinary environment's bound. Closed-value support soundness identifies that
analysis with the value's actual stored resource dependencies. A retaining
function can therefore pass by its actual storage even though its declaration
port does not record captures. Conversely, an empty bound rejects a retaining
function. `typed_first_order_binding` derives a replacement check from canonical
typing of an actual value when its first-order port supplies the declared
support bound. It does not infer the result of a pending read or application.

`replaceAll` applies the existing code substitution in list order.
`replacements_below` preserves the support bound through the list,
`replacements_resource_closed` preserves resource-name closure, and
`replacements_instantiate` commutes those replacements with resource opening.
The list describes substitutions, not execution of nested bind expressions.
In particular, replacing variable 3 by 1 and then by 2 leaves the inserted 1;
a checked example records that distinction. Closure of replacement values
prevents resource capture and ordinary-variable capture under nested binders.

`opened_replacements_bound` carries an earlier `SourceBound` through both
ordinary replacement and fresh resource opening. `source_bound_replacements`
reflects that bound back through opening to the substituted template.
`checked_replacements_preserve_check` proves that the original finite checker
still succeeds on that template before opening. Its proof chooses a number
above the finite world only to apply the reflection theorem; this witness
does not select a runtime allocation or prove issuance-history freshness.

`checked_replaced_entry` now applies the original checked-entry construction
to the preserved check. It constructs actual entry of the replaced body and
the corresponding `AllocationReturn`, without assuming a successor return
check. An example applies the general theorem when substitution inserts a
resource-retaining function. The checker remains conservative for pending
operation and application results.

`bind_then_entry` connects this construction to an actual strict bind followed
by entry of exactly its substituted resource body. The example binds an outer
resource reference and returns a closure retaining that reference from the
new resource scope. It proves the two raw transitions and their local return
certificate. The supplied world still does not prove that the outer owner is
live, and freshness relative to that world does not establish issuance-history
freshness. Joint typing, payload and disposal checks and closing readiness
remain separate. These results connect existing local certificates; they do
not establish general calculus admission or correspondence with current Core.

## Declared input bounds through capture and resumption

[ContinuationBounds.lean](ContinuationBounds.lean) uses the existing declared
input port of a live ticket to check its saved continuation. `portBound` maps
first-order ports to their exact resource support and leaves function ports
unknown. Products containing a function consequently have unknown support too.
`port_bound_finite` proves that a finite bound implies first-order shape;
`typed_value_below_port` proves that an actual typed value fits its port's
bound. An identity-free callable declaration alone supplies no capture bound.

`resume_operand_bound` authenticates that bound against the actual live frame.
It decomposes the typed stack and uses the same historical ticket-signature
lookup to identify the operand's input port with the saved input annotation.
The comparison uses erased declared ports; it does not assume equality of
the machine's full legacy `Ty` metadata or replace stored support by type
identity occurrences.

The revised `Checked` judgment retains return obligations through active and
recursively saved control. A live frame checks its saved prefix at
`portBound` of its input port, while the outside tail remains checked at
unknown. `old_checked_suffices` transports every previous return certificate
to this judgment. Exact append, capture, full-prefix restoration, disposal
materialization and cell updates preserve the corresponding structural checks.
Resumption additionally requires that the actual supplied value fit the saved
input bound; `resume_operand_bound` derives that premise from current typing.

`capture_constructs_typed_checked` connects this to actual typed capture. It
uses the operation's signature result port to construct the live input
annotation, extends the historical type table, and returns the same raw
successor with both declared-port typing and the revised return invariant.
The captured stack is checked at that operation-result bound. Freshness here
means absence from the type table, not issuance-history freshness or live
ownership. `typed_resume_constructs_checked` constructs actual resumption and
preserves both typing and the revised return check on the fully restored
stack.

`raw_step_preserves_checked` covers every raw transition under current-state
typing, the revised return invariant and the existing local allocation
certificate. It proves preservation of the return invariant, not successor
typing for arbitrary raw annotations. The separate typed capture and resume
constructions supply that typing for their actual events. Value steps derive
release checks from the revised invariant; `checked_value_progress` and
`checked_ready_value_progress` retain it alongside the existing joint or
readiness judgment. The one-shot usage, ownership, live support and closing
requirements in those judgments remain independent.

A checked example uses a parameterless `Unit -> Int` operation inside a
resource scope whose eventual result is a closure retaining the copied
integer. The handler captures the scope and resumes with 42. The example
proves the actual raw capture and resume events, declared-port typing of the
requesting, captured and resumed configurations, and return checks for the
captured and resumed configurations. The old unknown-input invariant rejects
the saved capture; the new integer input bound passes it.

This example checks the pending request's continuation at its declared
integer result bound. It does not establish `ConfigurationChecked` for that
request using the current conservative expression analyzer, or an admitted
execution from an initial calculus term. Its operation is a generic request,
not the builtin cell read. The [operation-result analysis](#signature-aware-operation-result-analysis)
below computes those bounds for bindings and the opened copied-read closure.
Connecting that inference throughout enclosing expressions to the preserved
runtime judgment remains an integration obligation.

The analogous [Ash fixture](fixtures/copied-integer-handler-result.ash) passes
elaboration and execution in current Core, returning `42 : Int` after the
handler resumes with 42 and the returned closure is called outside the resource.
This is a concrete comparison of the observable result. It neither authenticates
a translation from that Core expression to the Lean fixture nor records the
individual capture and completion events needed for a simulation proof.

A negative raw-resumption example supplies a resource handle to the same
integer-input continuation. Its pre-state passes the revised return check,
but the restored continuation's return bound includes the closing resource
and fails that check. This proves why resumption's typing premise cannot be dropped. General
calculus admission and authenticated Core correspondence remain open.

## Signature-aware operation-result analysis

[OperationResults.lean](OperationResults.lean) adds declared operation results
to the existing expression analyzer. Its key decoder preserves nominal,
resource and nested application arguments, and returns unknown for unresolved
resource names. `decode_frozen_effect` proves that decoding the frozen form of
an actual instance returns that instance; argument and argument-list lemmas
support this direction. The reverse implication from arbitrary successful
decoding to a frozen source is not yet a theorem here.

`operation_bound_known` connects an actual signature lookup to `portBound` of
the declared output. The new `analyze` follows the existing `Code` grammar and
changes the operation case to use this bound. Bindings pass the initializer's
summary into the remaining body. A lambda still records its actual captured
dependencies separately from its body-result metadata. An operation returning
an integer does not make a closure that retains its handle resource-free.
Callable operation results and pending applications remain unknown, as do
handler, resource, cleanup, resume and discard result forms.

`closed_value_storage_sound` proves exact storage for actual resource-closed
values. Support congruence, monotonicity and `analyze_substitution_support`
prove that ordinary closed-value substitution agrees with analysis under the
extended environment. These are statements about the stored-support observer;
they do not authorize known-call unfolding or establish a general realization
theorem for computation results. `analyze_refines_old` proves containment
relative to the previous observer under corresponding environment bounds.
It is an analysis comparison, not a program or Core simulation.

The new `contextResult` agrees exactly with actual context plugging and is
monotone. Actual bind steps carry the corresponding support equality. Typed
values and actual resumed operands fit their declared input bounds under the
new analysis as well. The builtin read and write constructors pair actual raw
steps with equality of the current expression's result summary before and
after the operation. These head-expression equalities alone do not establish preservation of the
surrounding stack; the next module supplies that integration.

The opened copied-read closure now has an empty stored-resource bound, while
the old observer reports unknown. The theorem covers opening the existing
template at every supplied activation identity. A closure that reads later
still retains the owner through both its operation metadata and its handle.
