successor certificate, supplied fresh name, selected handler cut, or pre-existing
checked event.

`current_progress` decomposes the actual current expression. Values use existing
value progress with access derived from result bounds. Bind, branch and builtin
operations construct annotation-free events. Focus, handler entry and resource
entry construct their annotations from current typing. Handler and resource
identities are fresh against the complete respective histories. Requests use
ordered resolution; a source handler supplies its actual clause and declared
continuation port, then current validity constructs the checked capture record.
Resumption finds the live boundary from the usage invariant.

The result is an ordinary terminal, an explicitly allowed outward request, or a
`CheckedStep` with its exact registry update. `closed_progress` removes the
outward alternative when the outgoing row is empty. `checked_progress_preserves`
joins construction to the prior preservation theorem, giving a named event,
combined successor validity and preservation of historical records for that
same checked step.

`run_append` composes the checked relation without any validity premise.
`run_progress` uses the invariant derived along a supplied finite run and
constructs its checked extension at every nonterminal closed endpoint. It
preserves the supplied prefix and its registry choices. This closes the
`NamedAccessStep` versus `CheckedStep` coverage gap in the preceding layer.

`initial_run_safety` quantifies over every checked run beginning with an initial
`ScopedExpressions.Code` term. Its initial premises are expression typing under
empty ordinary and resource environments with no outgoing effects, independent
ticket-use checking, empty free resource support, and a structural clause-result
derivation. These premises derive the initial combined invariant; intermediate
invariants are not supplied. The conclusion gives actual named execution,
preserved combined validity and either a terminal or a checked extension of the
same run. Terminal ownership and returned support follow from the preceding
`CheckedEvents` corollaries.

This is safety and repeatable checked progress for the admitted current fragment,
not termination or an executable decision procedure. It does not admit callable
application, discard, cleanup, or all current Core declarations and types. Those
one-shot integration obligations remain open. No Core alignment, multishot,
escaping-continuation or suspension work is included.

## Callable body contracts and the actual beta step

[CallableBodies.lean](CallableBodies.lean) adds proof metadata for the existing
lambda syntax. `BodyChecked` inspects the actual lambda's unsubstituted body
under its saved analysis environment, extended with an argument storage bound.
The body has a separate result bound and starts with lexical ticket `.none`.
It may install handlers with their own checked clause tickets; it cannot inherit
a pending ticket from its caller.

`StoredFunction` pairs that body contract with a separate storage derivation for
the function value. The capture bound describes the closure itself; the argument
bound describes its supplied value; the output bound describes the body's
result. None is inferred from either of the others. These are judgments over
existing code, not computation wrappers or runtime conversion operations.

`body_world_mono` and `stored_world_mono` preserve these checks when the resource
world grows. `body_substitution` and `stored_substitution` preserve them under
closed-value substitution with the existing storage-compatibility premise.
The proof respects parameter shadowing and the environment saved with the body.
It does not widen arbitrary result bounds or replace body checking with equality
of storage observations.

`body_application_bounded` derives the substituted body's result certificate
when the actual argument has a result certificate bounded by the declared
argument storage. `argument_rebinding` derives the substitution premise from
that actual value's support. The resulting certificate uses the function's
saved environment and lexical ticket `.none`.

`beta_preserves` connects this to the machine. Its premises are current
`ScopedPortJoint.Valid`, the actual lambda's body contract, the current value
argument's result certificate, and the retained stack's result interface. Both
registry projections come from the same `ClauseJoint.Registry`. Current typing
supplies actual function and argument closure. The theorem constructs the
existing beta event, clears its current scope to `.none`, and derives
`ClauseJoint.Valid` for the exact successor with the same registry and saved
tail. No successor-validity premise is supplied. The old joint invariant already
checks the evaluated function's actual resource support; the beta theorem does
not infer its body behavior from that support.

The checked identity example starts from the typed application of an identity
lambda to `17` and reaches the integer result with the combined invariant. An
effectful application enters the existing single-handler example through beta
reduction, then completes its capture/resume execution at `17` with the recorded
ticket and final invariant. This is a concrete composition of the beta
bridge and an existing handler execution, not global application admission.
Two factories provide a negative comparison: both capture no resources, but
one returns a closure that retains its argument and the other returns a closure
that does not. Supplying resource handle `7` rules out an empty output bound for
the retaining factory. A separate theorem rejects a direct inherited resume in
a function body.

This is a local bridge into the current combined invariant. `BodyChecked` uses
`ClauseResults.Derives`, whose body fragment still excludes application,
discard and cleanup. Stored argument bounds carry no callable behavior, and a
returned function's storage certificate is not a contract for invoking it.
Global application admission must retain those contracts through values,
bindings, arguments, returns, saved frames and captures before it can extend
`CheckedProgress.initial_run_safety`. This component does not establish that
integration, an executable checker, or Core correspondence. Core remains outside
alignment work.

## Callable contracts through binding and substitution

[CallableContracts.lean](CallableContracts.lean) replaces storage-only ordinary
bindings in the new expression judgment with full contracts. `Contract` has
storage, pair and function constructors. A function contract contains its
physical captures, argument contract and result contract; the last two may
themselves be callable. `storageOf` projects only physical storage. Mentioning a
resource in a domain or result contract does not grant ownership of it.

`Derives` and `ClausesDerive` are mutually inductive structural judgments over
the existing scoped expressions and clauses. Variable lookup retains the whole
assigned contract. Application checks the function's domain against the actual
argument contract, and binding extends the environment with that whole
contract. Lambda checks its unsubstituted body with lexical ticket `.none`.
An opaque storage leaf must already be a value, and can only conclude a storage
contract; it cannot supply behavior for application. All recursive checking
premises are positive derivations, rather than a semantic assumption about the
behavior of every possible argument.

The judgment includes nested application, branch, operation, handler,
resumption and generative resource constructors. Handler clauses retain the full
answer contract. Handled-clause parameters and resume inputs use finite
port-derived storage bounds. Operation requests obtain a finite output storage
bound; operand-port compatibility remains an independent typing check. Full
callable operation contracts are not modeled here. Fresh resource bodies are
checked for every fresh opening, and the
outward result's physical storage must fit the enclosing world. Disposal and
cleanup are not constructors of this judgment. Value ports, effect interfaces,
ticket usage and runtime ownership remain independent obligations.

`value_support` derives an actual value's resource dependencies from its
contract's storage projection. Environment congruence depends only on ordinary
variables occurring in the syntax, respects parameter and ticket binders, and
survives resource opening. Closed values can therefore move between analysis
environments. Their ticket transport preserves lambda's `.none` body check.

`substitution` and `clauses_substitution` require a closed replacement value
checked at the complete contract assigned to the replaced variable. They
preserve the complete result contract, including callable domains and results.
Only the physical capture part uses the replacement's resource support.
The proofs handle shadowing, distinct binding extensions, handler clause
parameters, and the commutation of closed substitution with fresh resource
opening. No storage equality stands in for agreement about callable behavior.

`function_value` exposes the actual lambda and its body derivation from a
callable value contract. `beta_result` then derives the substituted body's full
contract with ticket `.none`; `bind_result` retains the caller's ticket.
`beta_step` and `bind_step` pair these derivations with the exact existing raw
events, using explicit closure premises required by those events. They do not
assume the successor contract. The examples check higher-order argument
passing, a bound function's invocation, and a factory returning a callable with
its own captures, domain and result. A negative theorem rejects invoking a
variable assigned only a storage contract.

These results establish expression-level contract transport. They do not yet
extend `CheckedProgress.initial_run_safety`: retained frames and historical
continuation records still use the older result judgment, which excludes
application. In particular, these beta/bind results conclude the new `Derives`,
not `ClauseJoint.Valid`, and no general erasure into that older judgment is
claimed. Integration must carry full contracts through saved control and
capture/resumption while preserving the independent checks. Disposal/cleanup,
an executable admission checker and Core correspondence remain separate open
obligations; Core alignment remains outside scope.

## Callable contracts on retained control

[CallableFrames.lean](CallableFrames.lean) carries the preceding full contracts
through the existing runtime evaluation contexts and stack forest.
`ContextReturns` checks both application positions, pairs, binding, branch,
request operands, resource initializers and resume operands. `focus_decompose`
extracts a child contract and context derivation from actual checked code.
`context_plug` reconstructs that code's result contract. Restoring a closed
value to a saved environment and lexical ticket transports its entire
derivation, including any lambda body; it does not reconstruct behavior from
the storage projection.

`StackReturns` assigns complete input and output contracts to plain frames,
cells, handlers, live clauses and spent clauses. Every interface matches
exactly. There is no implicit weakening from physical capture inclusion to
callable compatibility. `stack_append` and `stack_decompose` prove composition
and decomposition for arbitrary finite forests, including nested dormant
captures. Registry extension and world growth preserve these derivations.

Each historical `ResultRecord` contains a complete input and answer contract.
`ScopeBound` links a lexical ticket to that owner's record. A live boundary
checks its saved capture from the recorded input to the recorded answer, and
its outside tail from that answer onward. `handler_cut_certificate` derives
the actual selected handler's clause checks and answer interface from the
retained forest. `resume_recomposition` uses the same owner lookup to restore
the captured stack above the entire intervening clause prefix and spent
boundary. It neither drops nor exchanges that prefix.

`capture_step` takes an actual handler cut, selected clause, declaration lookup,
current port typing, value operand, current contract derivation and absence of
the chosen owner from the contract registry. Finite declared input support
checks the actual operand at the selected parameter's storage contract.
Full-contract substitution then checks the actual clause reduct. The operation's
finite output gives the saved continuation's exact input contract, while the
selected handler supplies its complete answer contract, possibly callable.
The theorem constructs the existing raw capture event, an extended record and
the exact successor's contract derivation. It supplies no successor-invariant
premise and does not use a storage observation in place of callable behavior.

Actual focus, plug, beta, bind, handler entry/return, clause return, resumption
and resource entry/return preserve this configuration contract component.
Closure conditions remain explicit on the raw events that require them. Beta
clears the current lexical ticket while preserving the saved tail. Cell return
uses the result's physical support to exclude the released resource identity.
It retains the abstract world so that returned callable bodies keep their
resource-opening derivations.

The checked example begins at an evaluated request inside an installed handler
and a binding that will produce an identity function. Capture records that
callable answer. The clause resumes under a pending binding of its own; after
the restored handler returns the function, that binding preserves its callable
contract. The outside application invokes it and returns `17`. The eleven-step
raw trace records one created and one discharged ticket, and the contract
derivation is propagated through each step. A negative theorem rejects filling
that saved application position with a storage-only result contract.

This closes local full-contract transport through the represented saved
control. It does not yet extend `CheckedProgress.initial_run_safety` or replace
the old combined invariant. `ConfigurationReturns` takes an abstract world;
identifying it with issued resource history remains a joining obligation.
Registry absence establishes record extension, not lifetime-fresh owner
allocation. Raw type annotations, ordered effect interfaces, ownership,
one-shot authority and name history still require their independent checks.
The capture theorem uses current port typing, but does not claim its
preservation. The example starts after frames are installed and proves no
initial-term admission theorem. Contract subsumption, full callable operation
contracts, disposal/cleanup, general progress and executable admission remain
open. No Core alignment work is included.

## Joining callable contracts to the machine invariant

[CallableJoint.lean](CallableJoint.lean) combines the full retained-contract

state against ownership accounting, name history, live resource support,

and full result contracts. The contract world is explicitly

One `TicketRecord` contains the independent joint type/effect/usage record and

the handler answer's callable behavior from a port or storage bound.
`recorded_history` identifies both projection domains with issued tickets.
Fresh lifetime allocation implies absence from both registries, and insertion
preserves every previous record. `active_input_contract` connects an actual
live boundary's input annotation to that same contract witness.

`initial_configuration_valid` establishes the joined invariant from scoped
empty-environment typing, structural one-shot usage, empty free resource
support, and a full contract derivation. These are judgments over initial
calculus code; they are neither Ash surface admission nor a Core translation.

`capture_preserves` uses one actual cut, selected clause, operation lookup,
fresh owner and successor for all projections. The clause's substituted body
receives its full answer contract. The recorded declared input agrees with
the actual captured stack, and the operation/type/effect record drives that
same owner's usage update. The named step preserves ownership, names and live
support. No successor-validity premise is assumed. The stronger
`capture_without_payload_premise` derives payload access from the current
invariant: finite argument support follows the declared effect-instance
resources, and the selected handler's retained support makes those resources
available outside the capture. It still requires an actual cut and a fresh
owner; general request progress must construct them.

Resumption preserves the joined invariant while restoring the full captured
prefix and consuming the same ticket. Beta and binding derive actual closure
and suffix readiness from current typing before using full-contract
substitution. Plugging and handler/clause/cell returns retain all projections.
Cell return derives release exclusion from actual returned storage; it does
not erase the returned callable's body contract. `entry_preserves` checks

judgment, which inspects current code and retained interfaces rather than
assuming a valid successor. Owner and handler freshness remain explicit.
`focus_preserves` constructs its annotation from current typing and an actual
focus, then derives the joined successor.

Two examples establish concrete executions. A closed higher-order application
passes the four initial checks and reaches `17` through two beta events with
the joined invariant. A second closed program installs a handler beneath an
outside application, requests an operation and captures a continuation whose
answer is a function. Its clause resumes beneath a pending binding. The full
callable answer survives the restored handler, that binding and the outside
invocation, reaching `17`. The fourteen-event named execution starts from
initial code with empty owner and activation histories, issues ticket `5`
once, and finishes with that ticket recorded as completed. The proof derives
joined validity initially and propagates it at every intermediate state; it
does not import the preceding raw trace as a validity assumption.

This closes the local join for these transition families, including a concrete
initial-to-final callable-answer capture execution. The following layers extend
next-step coverage and finite checked-run preservation to this callable
judgment. Full callable operation contracts, disposal/cleanup and executable

proves termination of arbitrary programs or Core correspondence. Core alignment
and the deferred continuation targets remain outside this work.

## Progress and checked runs with callable contracts

The proof derives the actual expression form from independent value typing.

[CallableRuns.lean](CallableRuns.lean) supplies the finite-execution theorem.

callable. The checker does not recover callable behavior from a storage bound.
The preservation theorem derives the actual successor for that exact supplied

`CheckedEvent` distinguishes stable computation/return/resumption, checked

Checked progress also constructs an event in this same relation from current

For a terminal checked run, issued owners are a permutation of completed

## Induction and closing-effect checking

Arbitrary nesting does not require an unbounded collection of proofs. The
structural induction case for a live continuation uses one hypothesis for its
saved capture and another for the outside suffix. Execution safety uses
induction on finite execution length. The remaining source-admission problem
is establishing and preserving the premises in those finite rule cases.

[ClosingRequirements.lean](ClosingRequirements.lean) discharges the effect-row
component for concrete typed captures. `requiredEffects` computes each callback's
requests that are not supplied by its remaining disposal suffix, then combines
them with that suffix's outward requirements. `least_plan_row` proves that this
row is sufficient and contained in every admitted closing row, relative to the
callbacks' declared request rows. It does not infer minimal callback effects.
`mem_required_append` proves ordered composition by list induction. This is
sequencing of close actions, with no monadic embedding or commutation law.

`generated_plan_supplies_readiness` proves the converse of the earlier plan
construction theorem by stack induction. Plain and handler frames are skipped;
resources add releases; armed cleanup checks its callback against the remaining
suffix; a live capture composes its two induction hypotheses around retirement;
spent frames pass through. Running, closing and retiring frames reject planning,
including when nested in saved captures. Combined with retained callback typing,
`check_closing_effects_iff` proves that a Boolean plan-and-subset check is exactly
`CloseReady` for the concrete stack. Positive and negative examples check callback
order and nested capture/protection behavior.

This replaces the effect-readiness proof premise with a finite exact check for
an already typed stack. It does not derive resource access or exact interpretation
agreement, grant disposal permission, or prove that every capture reached from
an initially checked term passes these conditions. Those source and preservation
obligations remain; induction over execution cannot assume them at each step.

## Executable structural closing admission

[ClosingAdmission.lean](ClosingAdmission.lean) supplies the other concrete
closing checks. `checkRequests` requires every retained request to resolve to
the same actual `Target` in the original and surviving contexts. Equal effect
instances alone do not suffice; two different handler activations reject.
`checkAction` independently checks that callback ticket dependencies are empty,
retained resources remain visible and request interpretations agree.

`checkedPlan` follows the constructors of `Closes`. It checks the outside suffix
first, then uses that actual plan as the surviving context for an armed callback
or recursively owned capture. Soundness uses control induction; completeness
uses derivation induction. Both branches of a live capture are covered at
arbitrary finite depth. `checked_plan_iff` relates the computed result to the
existing judgment without assuming a supplied plan or its safety.

`checkedDisposal` adds finite inclusion of pending ticket work in the capture's
owned live tickets. `checked_disposal_iff` exactly characterizes `Discardable`.
The existing ownership theorem then accounts for every captured owner in the
accepted plan and excludes protected frames. The independent ownership invariant
must still establish uniqueness, and the caller's usage contract must grant
disposal permission. Activation-history uniqueness remains necessary for a
resolved handler identifier to identify one interpretation occurrence.

`checkCaptured` combines this structural check with closing-effect checking.
Given retained `StackTyped`, `check_captured_iff` proves equivalence to an actual
scoped `makePlan` result with `PlanTyped` and `Discardable` for that same erased
plan. Agreement follows from actual plan erasure and uniqueness of the computed
raw plan. This connects callback typing and effects with resource access,
interpretation identity, protection and pending-ticket checks; it does not
silently admit an unrelated plan.

Eight examples check preserved and changed handler activations, retained and
already released resources, outside and internally owned pending tickets,
nested protection and combined scoped checking. These establish exact concrete
closing admission. Establishing these conditions from initial source checks at
every future capture, preserving them during execution and integrating them
into complete progress remain open. A failed dynamic check is not a substitute
for the required source-derived safety theorem.

## Ordered contexts and protection modes

[ProtectionContexts.lean](ProtectionContexts.lean) establishes the context
component of a source protection judgment. `protectedMode` has two values:
false for no protected work in a captured forest, and true for at least one
running cleanup, unfinished close, finishing resource or retiring ticket.
`protected_mode_iff` proves exact agreement with the existing recursive
`Control.protected` definition.

The ordered `Context` contains interpretation entries and protection barriers.
`contextOf` preserves active handler and builtin entries. A live ticket adds
the protection mode of its saved forest, without activating that forest's
dormant handlers. `select` accumulates protection only until the nearest exact
interpretation. `select_target` proves that its target agrees with actual
resolution. `source_cut_mode` proves that a source capture receives precisely
its captured prefix's protection mode; `scoped_cut_mode` also identifies the
actual selected scoped handler activation. These are induction theorems for
arbitrary finite nesting.

Capture transfers the captured mode into the clause's live boundary.
Resumption preserves the total protection mode while restoring the capture
and retaining the clause prefix. It does not discharge running work merely by
moving it. An explicitly spent boundary contributes no protection of its own;
other retained protected work still contributes. `SupportsMode` is the
necessary condition that a protected capture cannot receive disposal permission.
It does not establish the other closing conditions or a safe clause body.

The nested example captures running cleanup in ticket E, then places a pending
resume of E before its live boundary while E's clause requests outer effect F.
The checked `SourceCut` for F owns that entire boundary. `InternalUses` accepts
the internally owned pending E demand, while structural disposal rejects E's
saved running cleanup. Thus one-shot usage and a resume-only E action profile
do not establish transitive protection safety. Conversely, a handler installed
inside cleanup before the running frame intercepts an unprotected prefix.
Blanket rejection of disposal anywhere in callback syntax would be too strong.

The remaining source rule must check clauses in the incoming protection modes
they support and propagate the selected mode into their bodies. A disposal
clause may support only the unprotected mode. A resume-only clause still needs
its further outward requests checked while it owns protected work. Resumption
and completion must update that ownership state. Callable contracts need latent
protection requirements checked at invocation; checking a lambda only against
its creation-site handlers would be incorrect. These source rules and their
substitution/execution preservation are not proved by context realization alone.

## Finite protection contracts at invocation

[ProtectionContracts.lean](ProtectionContracts.lean) defines the finite contract
interface for the remaining source rule. A `Demand` records an exact effect
instance, operation and protection introduced inside the summarized computation
before any interpretation in its receiving context. A `Footprint` is a finite
list of these demands. It records outward requirements; locally interpreted
requests must be accounted for before exporting a footprint. Ambient protection
at function creation does not become a latent demand.

Each operation's `ClauseContract` has a disposal bit and optional outward rows
for the two incoming capture modes. A missing row rejects that mode. On a
request, the ordered context accumulates barriers until the nearest exact
handler. The selected row must exist, and a protected mode requires disposal
to be disabled. The row's outward demands are then checked against the tail
outside that handler. Builtin selection does not capture a source continuation;
this protection checker leaves builtin operation typing to the independent
port/signature layer.

`Admitted` states these rules structurally. Induction proves soundness and
completeness of `checkRequest`; `checkFootprint` checks every listed requirement.
Footprint concatenation is conjunction at one invocation context. Qualification
by a protection bit is equivalent to inserting its barrier before that context,
and consecutive qualifications compose by Boolean disjunction. Removing demands
preserves acceptance. Distinct mode demands cannot be silently collapsed:
arbitrary supplied mode tables need not be monotone.

`Selected` records the exact operation lookup at the nearest source-handler
occurrence. `selected_target` agrees with ordered mode selection.
`checked_capture_contract` combines this with an actual scoped `HandlerCut` and
context realization: if its captured forest is protected, the selected summary
has disposal disabled. Context erasure preserves target identities and barriers;
it does not authenticate operation summaries against executable clauses or the
fixed source policy. That authentication remains necessary before the theorem
can establish the runtime ticket's actual permission.

The phase-specific row is essential. A protected E capture may require protected
F before E resumes; a genuinely exported F request after E's captured work
completes may lack that contribution. Selecting a protected row therefore does
not force every demand in it. The remaining outside context still contributes
its own barriers. Requests executed inside a resumed capture must first be
checked with its reinstated interpretations; treating them all as direct
requests to the selected handler's outside tail would be incorrect.

Eight Boolean examples distinguish ordinary/protected forwarding, an inner
disposable handler, a supplied after-completion row, remaining outside
protection, invocation versus creation context, missing operations and distinct
mode requirements. They check the contract interface, not source execution.
The callable source component below derives latent demands and preserves them
through substitution. Complete source coverage, clause-phase preservation and
authentication at actual capture remain open. These contracts are independent
admission evidence for the same direct effect syntax.

## Source callable protection and substitution

[CallableProtection.lean](CallableProtection.lean) defines structural
`Summarizes` rules on the existing scoped `Code`. Literals, references and
variables have no immediate demands. Pairs and binds compose their constituent
footprints; branches require both alternatives. A lambda stores its body's
footprint in a function contract. Application combines evaluation demands with
the function's latent demands. A request contributes its exact instance and
operation, using qualified input and result contracts supplied by declarations.
These contracts retain the same information inside higher-order arguments and
results. The `scalar` contract distinguishes non-callable protection shape;
ordinary port typing must separately distinguish Unit, Boolean and other ports.

`substitution` uses induction on expression size, with environment agreement and
shadowing lemmas. Replacing a variable with a closed value of the declared
contract preserves both the result contract and the exact footprint. This covers
arbitrarily nested functions without enumerating nesting depths. `beta_step`
and `bind_step` connect that result to actual `RawStep` rules: beta clears the
lexical ticket scope, while bind retains it. Both preserve `CheckedAt` under
the same supplied protection context. No premise yet relates that context to
the runtime tail, so this is not a machine-invariant preservation theorem.

`actual_request_admitted` extracts the invocation check from a source request's
summary. For cleanup, callback evaluation and the armed body contribute their
ordinary demands; only the callback's latent footprint gains a running barrier.
`cleanup_invocation_checked` proves that a checked cleanup with a value callback
admits its application to Unit beneath that barrier. It does not yet construct
the actual cleanup transition or its retained callback certificate. Independent
port typing must establish that the callback has Unit input and output.

Ten examples derive a function's latent request from its body, admit its creation
and ordinary invocation, reject invocation beneath a protected barrier with a
disposable handler, preserve demands through higher-order substitution, and
distinguish accepted and rejected cleanup callbacks. The rejection proofs range
over every possible summary in this component, under the supplied context tables.

There are no `Summarizes` rules yet for handlers, resume, discard or generative
resources. Operation-supplied higher-order result contracts still require
authentication against implementations and handler bodies. Integrating those
source forms, ticket phases, retained control, resource support and ordinary
typing remains necessary for complete one-shot source admission and execution
safety. The bridge below supplies runtime context realization and local frame
transitions. This component is design evidence and does not establish
correspondence with current Core.

## Protection at runtime frames and policy selection

[CallableProtectionFrames.lean](CallableProtectionFrames.lean) derives
`contextOf` from the actual scoped runtime stack. Active handler occurrences
retain their exact effect instance, activation and annotated clause table;
cells contribute builtin interpretations. A live ticket contributes the
protection of its saved capture without activating its dormant handlers.
`context_realizes` proves by stack induction that erasing this context gives
the existing interpretation/protection projection. `Checked` therefore checks
source requirements against the actual stack, rather than an unrelated context.
Handler rows remain supplied annotations at this stage.

`ContextSummarizes` structurally records each represented evaluation position's
hole contract, result contract and residual footprint. `focus_decompose` splits
a source summary into the focused child's footprint followed by those residual
demands. Already evaluated operands contribute an empty immediate row, including
an evaluated function whose contract still carries latent demands.
`context_plug` reconstructs the summary. `Pending` checks the retained frame's
residual demands at its actual tail; `focus_step` and `plug_step` construct the
actual runtime transitions and preserve these certificates. Plugging a closed
value transports its full contract into the saved analysis environment.
Beta and bind use the same stack-derived context and the preceding substitution
theorem. These are local frame certificates, not a complete stack invariant.

Cleanup entry produces a body check beneath the armed frame and an `Armed`
certificate for future callback execution under the running barrier. Starting
cleanup constructs the actual callback application and retains a `Saved`
certificate for the returned value's complete contract. Finishing restores that
value and the action's saved scope, discharging the cleanup owner in the raw
transition. The outside continuation keeps its separate pending certificate at
the tail context throughout these local transitions. No theorem weakens a
protected check by removing a barrier: mode tables can support protected mode
without supporting unprotected mode, so that inference would be invalid.

`clauseTable` reads every clause's disposal bit directly from the fixed
`TicketPolicy` at that clause's actual ticket binder. Its two outward rows are
still supplied. `clause_lookup` follows the actual first matching `ClauseAt`;
`cut_contract` follows the actual `HandlerCut`, carrying protection across both
active frames and dormant owned captures. This does not require handler
activation identifiers to be unique. Together,
`protected_request_denies_policy_disposal` proves that a checked source request
with a protected actual capture selects a binder whose fixed policy denies
disposal. Existing allocation rules use that policy for the ticket record.
This authenticates the disposal bit, not the supplied rows or the handler body's
transitive behavior. It does not prove that every reachable request passes
`Checked`.

Six examples realize a concrete running-cleanup stack, construct its actual
handler cut, reject a disposable policy, and retain a callable result through
the local cleanup entry/start/finish certificates. They do not claim a complete
callback execution trace or full source admission. Structural clause-body
requirements, operation-result contract authentication, capture/resume phase
preservation, generative-resource source rules, and integration with the joint
ownership/type invariant remain open. Current Core correspondence is unchanged.

## Residual requirements across capture and resumption

[ProtectionResiduals.lean](ProtectionResiduals.lean) computes the finite
requirements that remain after an ordered interpretation prefix processes a
supplied footprint. A barrier qualifies each demand. A matching builtin
consumes it. A matching handler checks its operation and incoming mode, then
replaces the demand with the corresponding outward row. That row proceeds only
through the remaining context; it is not handled again by the interpretation
that supplied it. Its individual protection bits remain unchanged. Unmatched
demands survive to the outside edge. Failure means a missing operation,
unsupported mode or forbidden disposal inside the prefix, rather than an
unhandled request at its edge.

`residual_check` proves exact factorization for every outside context: checking
the original footprint through a prefix and tail equals checking the prefix's
residual through the tail. `residual_append` proves that processing two prefixes
in order equals processing their concatenation. `residual_rows_append` proves
composition over concatenated demand lists. These are laws of the finite
analysis; they introduce no source computation forms or alternate sequencing
operation. They do not allow handler scopes to commute.

`context_append` connects the computation to actual stack append, including
live boundaries whose saved interpretations remain dormant. `resume_requirements`
uses the precise stack installed by `RawStep.resume`: captured frames, waiting
caller frames, the spent ticket boundary, then the surviving tail. The spent
boundary contributes no protection. The captured prefix's residual is checked
against the waiting frames followed by the surviving tail. The corresponding
iff theorem makes successful residual construction and that outside check
necessary and sufficient for this footprint's admission at the restored stack.

`capture_resume_recomposition` starts from an actual `HandlerCut` and a checked
footprint at its original stack. It derives a residual admitted by the original
tail, then proves the exact rechecking equation for every waiting caller stack.
It does not assume that inserting caller frames preserves admission. A concrete
example checks an E demand beneath a running barrier and an E handler exporting
a protected F request. An outer resume-only F handler admits it; inserting a
disposable F handler into the waiting caller stack rejects it after restoration.
The original successful check therefore cannot replace the resumption check.

Eleven examples cover empty-prefix export, phase-specific unprotected exports,
surviving barriers, protected forwarding, handler/barrier order, missing
operations, nonmonotone mode tables, the two contexts in the resumption example,
its exact residual, and inactive dormant handlers. The examples compare supplied
footprints at concrete stacks. They do not establish that those stacks occur in
a reachable source execution or that the supplied handler rows describe their
bodies completely.

The remaining source proof must derive the requirements of the entire retained
continuation, including pending evaluation frames and cleanup callbacks, and
check them at the appropriate ticket phases. This factorization theorem does
not establish that derivation, authenticate outward handler rows, or prove
whole-machine preservation of resumption. Ownership preservation and ordinary
typing remain separate components to be joined. Current Core correspondence is
unchanged.

## Source clause phases and protection requirements

[ClauseProtection.lean](ClauseProtection.lean) defines a structural `Derives`
judgment on the existing scoped `Code`, indexed by the existing `UseState`.
Its ticket contract supplies the lexical binder, full input and answer
contracts, owned protection, and footprints exported by captured execution and
its disposal plan. Deriving those two footprints from retained control remains
an independent obligation. An inside context represents the waiting frames
above this ticket; the eventual outside context represents the surviving tail.

Pairs and binds thread the phase through their children. Branch arms must agree
on the final phase. Function application and operation requests use the phase
after argument or operand evaluation. The stable callable source judgment
supplies forms with no ticket actions, including lambda bodies with latent
requirements. While the ticket is available, its owned protection follows the
inside interpretations and precedes the surviving tail. After consumption, only
that ticket's contribution disappears. Barriers belonging to other owners remain
in the inside or outside context.

Resume requires its declared right and an operand whose endpoint is available.
It exports the captured residual through the waiting inside context, without
the consumed ticket's barrier, and leaves the phase consumed. Disposal requires
its declared right and an unprotected capture. It exports the supplied disposal
residual through a closing barrier followed by the waiting inside context.
The residual is understood to lie outside the planned frames but before that
generated closing barrier. These rules do not themselves construct a valid
capture or close plan.

Cleanup threads callback construction and body evaluation in order, then checks
the callback's latent demands at the body's final phase beneath a running
barrier. This rule describes normal callback invocation. If another continuation
abandons the armed cleanup, callback requirements must instead be derived from
the actual close plan and its invocation context. The hypothetical final phase
of the abandoned body cannot justify that route.

`derives_usage` projects every derivation to the existing one-shot `Uses`
judgment. `phase_monotone` rules out making a consumed ticket available again.
`protected_discard_rejected` and `consumed_resume_rejected` reject those source
actions directly. Environment agreement and closed substitution preserve both
endpoint phases, the full result contract, and the exact exported footprint.
`value_summary` recovers the stable callable contract of a returned value;
the beta and bind summary theorems use it to preserve the phase judgment under
their actual substitutions.

`available_stack_check` and `consumed_stack_check` equate phase-context checks
with the actual live/spent stack shapes. The available case identifies owned
protection with the saved capture's protection. They do not authenticate the
lexical binder against a runtime ticket owner or establish its port contracts.
`resume_stack_check` and `closing_stack_check` place a supplied, realized residual
at the exact restored or closing stack order. Their residual-realization
premises still require retained-code proofs; these are check equalities, not
whole-transition preservation theorems.

Ten examples derive source requirements around resume, project the result to
structural usage, reject double resume and lambda capture of the ticket, retain
another owner's protection after consumption, qualify a normal cleanup callback
after resume, and qualify disposal work under closing protection. In the
`F; resume; F` example, the first protected F and final unprotected F come from
source phase threading. The middle protected G comes from the supplied captured
resume footprint. No example claims an authenticated full captured execution.

Source checking for handlers and generative resources, authentication of offered
clause rows against these derivations, captured execution/closing footprint
construction, and integration with retained-frame and joint ownership/type
invariants remain open. This is still the one-shot design experiment; neither
current Core nor its correspondence status changes.

## Source certificates for offered clause rows

[CertifiedClauseRows.lean](CertifiedClauseRows.lean) connects the finite handler
table to actual source clauses. `Certified` follows `Clauses` in source order.
Each entry obtains the operation argument and result contracts from one lookup:
the parameter receives the argument contract, and the captured continuation's
input receives the operation result contract. The ticket answer is the handler's
full answer contract. Disposal permission comes from the actual ticket binder's
fixed policy.

An `Offers` certificate either marks a mode unavailable or supplies both its
mode-permission check and a `ClauseProtection.Derives` proof for that actual
body, from available to consumed. The body is checked under its parameter's
input binding and an empty inside context, matching immediate clause entry
above the new live boundary. An arbitrary inside context would be unsound here:
it could hide requests behind handlers absent at runtime. Captured execution and
disposal rows remain inputs to the clause's ticket contract. Thus the certificate
justifies the offered row relative to those inputs, not their provenance.

`selected_contract` and `selected_body` follow the actual first matching
`ClauseAt` and retain that body's certificate. `cut_offered` follows the actual
`HandlerCut`, deriving its selected row and successful checking at the actual
surviving tail, with protection from both active frames and dormant captures.
The proof does not rely on activation-label uniqueness. Unavailable modes cannot
supply this selected row.

`request_operand` extracts the closed payload's full protection contract from
the checked request and its operation lookup. `capture_clause_certificate`
transports that contract to the clause's analysis environment and applies the
closed-substitution theorem. Its conclusion contains the substituted body's
phase derivation and the exported row's actual-tail acceptance; neither is
assumed as a successor-state certificate. `capture_step` additionally constructs
the actual raw capture transition and projects the body derivation to source
usage. It still requires the independent `ClosedExcept parameter body` premise.
The theorem does not connect the raw operation-result `Ty` or handler answer
metadata to ordinary port typing, nor establish registry freshness, support or
the joint machine invariant.

Twelve examples certify a protected-only mode, reject an empty offered row that
omits a supplied resumed G request, reject protected mode under a disposal
policy, and connect a concrete checked request, cut, substituted body and raw
capture. The main body's first protected F and final unprotected F are derived
from source sequencing around resume. Its intervening G still comes from the
captured execution input. The outside F/G handler rows in the concrete context
are supplied; this example does not certify every active handler or prove a
complete reachable execution. A separate parameter-binding example substitutes
Unit for the variable actually used as a resume operand; the main capture
fixture's parameter is unused.

The next integration must retain these table certificates throughout execution
and realize each selected ticket's captured execution and closing inputs.
Source rules for nested handlers and generative resources, operation-contract
authentication, and the joint preservation/progress theorem remain open.
An unavailable mode does not certify its body; independent ordinary typing and
whole-source policy checks remain necessary. Current Core correspondence is
unchanged.

## Disposal requirements from executable plans

[DisposalProtection.lean](DisposalProtection.lean) derives a disposal footprint
from the actual close plan and source contracts of its retained callbacks.
`plan_context_realizes` identifies the interpretation context of `closeControl`:
releases provide exact cell instances, armed callbacks add an unprotected
barrier, and retirement adds a protected barrier. The plan contains no source
handlers. Any generated closing boundary and waiting caller frames belong to
its outside context.

At invocation, a running barrier precedes the remaining plan. Consequently,
`callbackResidual rest latent` removes exactly those demands whose effect
instance occurs in `planProvides rest`, then sets protection on all survivors.
Order and duplicates are retained. A cell does not provide a user effect merely
because that effect has the cell as a resource argument. The residual theorem
proves that checking this footprint outside the plan equals checking the
callback's latent footprint at its actual invocation context. It does not
authenticate builtin operation numbers or ordinary argument/result types.

`Contents` retains actual callback source contracts while `makePlan` traverses
the captured stack. Its live-continuation induction case transports contracts
from both the saved capture and the outside suffix. `Rows` computes requirements
only after that complete plan is assembled. Concatenating previously computed
inner rows would be incorrect: cells appended by an outside suffix can satisfy
demands previously exported by an inner callback. `captured_disposal_row`
constructs a row from retained contracts and successful plan construction.

`Ready` checks each callback's source contract and latent requirements under
its running barrier and exact remaining suffix. `ready_iff_rows` characterizes
this judgment by existence of a derived row accepted outside the plan. The
existential statement does not claim unique or principal callback contracts.
`ready_invocation` follows the actual `InvocationAt` position.
`invocation_armed` realizes that callback's check against the materialized
suffix, including the scope and Unit answer installed by `closeControl`.
`invocation_step` constructs `RawStep.startCleanup` and derives a checked source
application in its resulting running frame. This is local invocation evidence;
it does not prove execution from the plan's beginning reaches that position.

`Retained` checks callbacks already stored in armed or running frames,
recursively through dormant captures. Stack induction and ordered append prove
that capture, resume and disposal preserve these contracts. The judgment does
not inspect future cleanup expressions inside plain contexts, handler clauses
or arbitrary stored callable bodies.

`discard_ready` connects the source phase rule to a plan whose `Rows` certificate
matches the ticket's disposal footprint. `discard_step` additionally requires
that `makePlan` built this same plan from the live capture and that the current
scope resolves the source binder to its runtime owner. It constructs the actual
raw discard transition and derives readiness at the generated closing stack,
together with callback retention in the entire successor. It does not assume
these successor certificates as premises. Twelve example lemmas include
before/after release, a user effect indexed by a cell, suffix extension through
nested capture, a source-derived discard of that capture, invocation after
retirement, and acceptance/rejection of outward protected requests.

The remaining integration must preserve readiness during callback execution,
derive contracts when future cleanup expressions install callbacks, and connect
all ticket allocations to authenticated captured execution and disposal rows.
The protection contract's scalar shape is not ordinary Unit typing. Ordinary
ports, resource support, exact interpretation agreement, fixed permissions,
fresh owner identities, the ownership ledger and `Discardable` remain separate
checks. These results do not establish the joint machine invariant, full source
admission, or Core correspondence. Multishot, escape and suspension are excluded.

## Cleanup installation and normal return phases

[CleanupProtection.lean](CleanupProtection.lean) connects source cleanup checking
to stored callback contracts. `summarized_callback` and `clause_callback` derive
the contract of the actual closed callback in the current cleanup expression.
`raw_step_retains` preserves existing callback contracts through every raw
transition; its only installation premise concerns this exact expression at
cleanup entry. Source-summary and clause-phase wrappers discharge that premise.
The cell-update case preserves contracts recursively through dormant captures
while changing only the selected cell payload. This proves retention, not
invocation safety or preservation of the current source judgment.

The `Normal` certificate separately records the callback's source contract and
its accepted latent requirements under a running barrier, the inside context,
the body's final ticket phase, and the outside context. It is a certificate for
future normal return. It need not provide an `Armed` check against an earlier
live boundary if the cleanup body will consume that continuation.

`cleanup_decompose` derives the body's phase judgment, acceptance of its exported
row, and `Normal` from the checked source cleanup. It covers both an explicit
phase cleanup derivation and a stable source summary. The closed callback has
no immediate demands, so its evaluation changes neither phase nor exported row.
The stable case splits residual requirements to derive the body and callback
checks; it does not assume either result.

`inside_congr` transports source derivations across contexts with exactly equal
residual transformations. `under_armed` applies this to the inert false barrier
of a newly armed frame. It does not assume that strengthening protection or
adding arbitrary frames preserves checks. `cleanup_entry` constructs the raw
entry transition and derives the body judgment under that barrier, the future
normal-return certificate and callback retention in the new stack. The context
parameters still require realization as part of the whole-machine invariant.

`normal_available_armed` realizes the final phase at an actual live boundary,
requiring the ticket's protection flag to match the actual saved capture.
`normal_consumed_armed` realizes it at an actual spent boundary. Both use the
actual waiting prefix and outside tail in order. `available_start` and
`consumed_start` obtain the returned value's full contract from its source phase
derivation, then construct the actual raw callback invocation and checked
application while retaining that full saved result contract. These local
theorems require the return configuration; they do not prove execution reaches
it from cleanup entry or identify its historical owner record.

Seven example lemmas check source installation, stable cleanup decomposition,
cell updates with a dormant callback, and the distinction between current and
future invocation contexts. In the phase example, E's supplied handler row
emits an unprotected F request. The pending live boundary protects that request
and rejects F's disposal policy; after consumption, the spent boundary permits
it. The source cleanup derives the latter normal-return certificate. Runtime
cleanup identities are distinct and the source resume binder has a runtime
scope binding, but the fixture still does not establish a jointly valid
execution prefix. Its handler rows and captured execution row are supplied.

The remaining invariant must connect current source derivations, actual pending
frames, future cleanup phases and certificates for active handlers and live
owners. In particular, it must derive the requirements of each actual captured
prefix and prove they are covered by its recorded resume row; a clause and
protection mode alone do not identify that prefix. It must then preserve these
facts during cleanup-body and callback execution. Scalar protection contracts
do not establish ordinary operand types or progress. Current Core comparison
and the exclusions of multishot, escape and suspension are unchanged.

## Pending contexts and source continuation phases

[ClauseProtectionFrames.lean](ClauseProtectionFrames.lean) connects the source
phase judgment to actual `ScopedExecution.Context` positions. `ContextDerives`
records the hole's return phase and full contract, the enclosing expression's
final phase and full result contract, and the remaining exported footprint.
Its constructors cover pair, application, bind, branch, operation, resume and
cleanup contexts admitted by the current phase judgment. There is no resource
context rule yet, matching the missing generative source rule.

An application context retains the argument's derivation and the function's
latent requirements, using the phase after argument evaluation. An already
evaluated left operand or function retains its full contract with an empty
immediate row. A bind checks its suffix in the saved environment extended by
the initializer's full contract. A resume operand must return available; its
context then exports the captured requirements through the inside prefix and
ends consumed. A cleanup context checks its body from the callback's return
phase and its invocation requirements at the body's final phase.

`context_plug` recomposes a source derivation from a child derivation and its
context. `context_usage` projects the suffix to structural one-shot usage,
using Unit only as a placeholder for the hole's usage. It does not assign Unit
the hole's type. `context_phase_monotone` consequently forbids a consumed
context from returning to the available phase.

`split_export` splits residualized requirements, preserving their exact
concatenation. `stable_context` uses this law to turn ordinary callable context
summaries into phase contexts, including selected handler rows and cleanup's
running qualification. `focus_decompose` then covers both stable and explicit
phase source derivations. It yields a child from the original entry phase to
an intermediate phase, and a context from that intermediate phase to the final
phase. The original exported footprint is exactly child row followed by
context remainder.

`Pending` stores the saved analysis environment, expected hole-return phase
and contract, final phase/result, and the exact accepted remainder.
`focus_step` constructs the actual raw focus transition and derives the child
certificate under the new plain frame's inert false barrier. `plain_context`
identifies that barrier in the actual stack projection. `plug_step` extracts
the closed returned value's full contract, proves that its current and return
phases agree, and transports the value into the saved environment. It restores
the raw frame scope and reconstructs the suffix from the hole-return phase,
with exactly the stored remainder. It does not replay the child's earlier
requirements or restart at the original expression's entry phase.

The local bind and beta bridges use the existing closed-substitution results
and construct their actual raw steps, including beta's scope reset. They
preserve exact endpoint phases, full results and footprints. Branch selection
derives a checked row for the selected arm from the original accepted branch
row; it does not claim that the remaining row equals the former union.

Sixteen example lemmas include focus and plug around a resume followed by F.
The initial row contains the supplied resumed G demand and an unprotected F;
the plugged suffix contains only F and starts consumed. Checking F at the old
protected phase would reject its disposal policy. Other examples reject a
consumed resume context, split a row transformed by a selected handler, retain
a callable initializer under the saved environment, derive its bind result and
actual beta reduction, and check cleanup's final phase and branch selection.

These are local source certificates and raw transitions. The inside/outside
analysis contexts remain supplied independently of the raw tail in the step
theorems. Raw frame port annotations are not authenticated, and equality of
phase indices is not a runtime owner-state correspondence theorem. The examples
do not compose an admitted resume trace. The remaining invariant must realize
these contexts, scopes, ports and phases on the same historical owner records,
derive actual captured-prefix requirements, and preserve the combined facts
through handler and resource transitions. The boundary and joint-step results
below discharge part of this integration. Full source admission and progress
remain open; Core comparison and the continuation exclusions are unchanged.

## Runtime phase boundaries and joint capture

[PhaseBoundaries.lean](PhaseBoundaries.lean) makes a source phase refer to an
actual owner boundary. `Boundary.live` identifies the live owner, captured
stack, raw answer type and outside tail, and equates the ticket's protection
bit with the captured stack's protected mode. `Boundary.spent` identifies the
spent owner, raw answer type and outside tail. The waiting prefix stays
explicit. Both interpretation contexts are computed from these actual stacks.

`boundary_check` equates phase-context checking with checking the whole runtime
stack. `exported_check` connects the source's exported row to that same check.
`request_checked` uses a value operand's empty immediate row and unchanged
phase to produce the source request certificate needed at actual dispatch.

Boundary occurrence and phase uniqueness reuse the existing ticket-name
accounting. An available boundary owns its ticket and excludes that owner from
completion history. A consumed boundary places its owner in completion history
using both the ledger and name history. `consumed_never_available` combines
these results with the existing induction over executions: an owner consumed
earlier cannot become available later, regardless of nesting depth or whether
its original spent marker remains. No additional registry is introduced.
`recorded_answer` derives the actual boundary's answer port from ordinary
effect/port typing and the existing owner registry. It does not equate the
source protection contract language with ordinary ports.

`focus_preserves` obtains the new plain frame's context, scope and port
annotations from `CompletionJoint.Valid`, then derives the child and pending
source certificates using the actual prefix and outside tail. The same named
step preserves that joint invariant. `plug_preserves` derives value closure
from ordinary typing, checks its current boundary phase, and restores the
pending suffix at the value's return phase. Its source derivation contains
only the remaining row. These are joined local preservation theorems;
preservation of all pending certificates across intervening steps is not yet
established.

`capture_preserves` uses one selected clause, fresh owner, ordinary operation
lookup, registry extension and successor for the source certificate and
`CompletionJoint.Valid`. The latter derives payload closure and access checks.
The source table certificate checks the selected clause body and its substituted
payload. The resulting source ticket's protection bit is computed from the
same actual captured prefix, and its boundary is the live boundary installed
by that named step. Source and ordinary operation lookups are both retained;
general agreement between their contract languages remains unproved.

Eight example lemmas reuse the callable-handler execution from
`CallableJoint.CaptureExample`. They certify its source clause and selected
handler table, join capture to the machine invariant, and compose an actual
execution from an ordinarily admitted initial term through capture, focus,
one resumption, the original handler's return, and the clause's pending bind.
That bind receives the returned function at the consumed boundary with the
same ownership history. Negative examples reject an incorrect protection bit
and any available boundary for that completed owner. This is a concrete
admitted execution prefix, not general source admission for handler syntax.

The capture rows remain supplied by `CaptureRows`; their provenance from every
actual saved prefix is still required. Source binder resolution to runtime
owners, protection-contract agreement with ordinary ports, source handler and
resource rules, combined preservation for all transitions, and whole-program
progress remain open. Core correspondence remains an assessment; no alignment,
multishot, escaping or suspending continuation work is included.

## Requirements at saved frame positions

[SavedFrameRequirements.lean](SavedFrameRequirements.lean) derives outward
requirements from source evidence for the actual saved frames. Each ordinary
plain frame carries a `ContextSummarizes` derivation for its pending code.
An armed cleanup carries its callback's callable source contract and contributes
the latent row qualified by its future running protection. Running cleanup
retains a source summary of its saved value; returning that value does not
invoke its latent effects. Handler, cell, closing and retiring frames add no
pending source computation of their own.

`Sources` retains this evidence recursively, including inside dormant live
captures. `Rows.push` exports a frame's source row through the interpretation
context of that frame's remaining suffix, then appends the suffix's own outward
row. It does not collect all frame requirements and check them at the original
stack top. A provider above a pending frame has already exited when that frame
is reached. Counting that provider would admit requests that no longer have an
interpretation. Live boundaries retain their dormant capture's source evidence
separately; dormant handlers are not active providers, and the dormant code's
effects are not automatically executed on return past that boundary.
Neither judgment supplies a return rule for an available live boundary.

`Checked` expresses source checking at each actual frame position against an
arbitrary receiving context. Induction proves that it holds exactly when some
derived `Rows` footprint is accepted by that receiving context. This is an
existential equivalence; it does not assert uniqueness or minimality over all
possible callable source contracts. Stack append and decomposition preserve
these positional checks. `capture_rows` applies decomposition to an actual
`HandlerCut` and derives a row for its saved prefix from the retained source
checking. `resume_recomposition` checks that row at the new waiting caller and
checks the caller's own pending code separately. No arbitrary caller weakening
is used.

`plain_pending` and `armed_pending` recover the earlier local plug and cleanup
invocation certificates at the surviving tail. `source_resume_checks_caller`
extracts the receiving-context check from the source phase rule once its
operand is a value. `resume_joint` requires `Rows` for the actual capture and
the source ticket's resumed row, then proves the positional checks on the
installed stack together with the same named resumption step and
`CompletionJoint.Valid`. This replaces a supplied whole-prefix footprint
residual with frame-source provenance for this component.

Thirteen example lemmas include a pending cell read before and after its
provider's release position. The latter is rejected even though checking its
request at the original stack top would succeed. Other cases distinguish
dormant providers, derive protected cleanup callback rows, and check cleanup
with a remaining cell provider. The callable-handler example now derives its
saved frame rows and composes an admitted execution prefix through actual
resumption with positional checks and the ownership/type invariant on the same
successor. The provider-order examples establish checking properties; they are
not additional jointly admitted execution traces.

This source evidence uses ordinary callable context summaries. A pending frame
whose code itself resumes or disposes a continuation requires integration with
`ContextDerives`; it is not silently assigned an empty row. General alignment
of frame hole/result contracts with actual values and neighboring source
contracts, authenticated handler rows, preservation of positional certificates
across all transitions, and complete initial source admission remain open.
The existing `CaptureRows` table scheme has not been replaced throughout the
calculus. These results do not prove whole-program progress or change Core
correspondence, and the excluded continuation targets remain excluded.

## Source phases and scheduled runtime owners

[PhaseFrameUsage.lean](PhaseFrameUsage.lean) connects source continuation phases
to the existing runtime usage invariant. It introduces no registry or admission
predicate. A shared syntactic path fixes the lexical binder of a consuming
one-shot protocol. Combining the source usage projection with `CodeDemand`
then derives the actual saved scope, runtime owner, permission-record lookup
and singleton consumption demand. A source derivation whose entry and exit
phases agree instead forces the runtime consumption demand to be empty.

These results apply to `ContextDerives` through its existing usage projection.
The Unit hole remains a usage placeholder, not a proposed type for the value
that fills the frame. `stack_frame_owner` extracts the exact frame demand from
`StackUsage` and places its owner in the active tail or the saved capture's
explicit external-access interface. `scheduled_frame_owner` specializes this
result to an active frame in a complete configuration, where the external
interface is empty. Structural induction on the active spine locates the
corresponding actual live boundary; dormant ownership alone cannot supply it.
The existing ledger excludes that active owner from completion history, and
`scheduled_frame_not_completed` obtains this fact from `CompletionJoint.Valid`.

Ownership balance also constrains composition. Two sequential pending frames
cannot both demand the same runtime owner, even under different source binder
names. Nor can the current expression consume an owner already demanded by a
pending frame. The proofs use the unique owned-ticket list and its permutation
with current and retained demands. Alternative branches remain valid: their
source usage records one consumption on each path, rather than adding both
branches' syntax occurrences to a sequential demand.

Fourteen example lemmas connect the nested usage example's source binder 10 to
owner 5 and its dormant binder 11 to external owner 7. Resuming owner 3 preserves
the waiting access to owner 5. Other cases reject consumption through a spent
boundary, duplicate pending demands and a current/pending duplicate. Branch
alternatives retain one owner demand. A consumed suffix has no demand, and an
idle saved scope may still name a consumed owner: a historical scope name does
not itself require active access. The nested examples reuse checked usage and
resumption evidence; they are not new full source/type-admitted executions.

This closes source-binder/runtime-owner agreement for consuming pending frames
and source-phase/runtime-demand agreement for unchanged phases. It does not
infer an idle frame's eventual available/consumed phase from its saved scope.
Phase-sensitive saved effect rows, agreement of source hole/result contracts
with actual values, authenticated handler rows, and preservation of the full
source invariant remain required before general admission or progress can be
claimed. Core correspondence and continuation-target exclusions are unchanged.

## Phase and contract composition of pending contexts

[PhaseContextChains.lean](PhaseContextChains.lean) supplies a structural `Chain`
judgment for contiguous pending plain frames. Each constructor connects the
previous context's exit phase and full callable contract to the next context's
entry phase and input contract. All contexts share one source ticket and an
analysis environment. Plain frames introduce inert interpretation barriers;
`plain_prefix_residual` proves that their prefix does not change residual
requirements. This result does not remove handlers, resources or protected
boundaries.

Induction on the chain proves composition and decomposition at arbitrary
positions, reconstruction of source syntax, and monotonicity of the consumed
phase. There is no bound on chain length. The induction hypothesis retains
intermediate phases, full contracts and effect rows; matching only an ordinary
result type would lose latent callable requirements. Source reconstruction uses
one shared source environment and is not an operational removal of saved scopes.

`Source` pairs the current expression's promised return phase and contract with
the pending chain that accepts both. It checks their combined remaining row.
Focus decomposes this evidence without changing that row. Returning a value
removes its empty immediate row; plugging it into the next context leaves the
current phase unchanged, even when the newly exposed code will later consume
the ticket. Bind and beta reduction preserve the row, while branch selection
retains the selected branch's requirements. A resumed computation's waiting
chain starts at the consumed phase and the ticket's full answer contract.

`current_at_actual_prefix` and `current_request_checked` connect this source
account to actual stack positions and a live or spent runtime boundary.
`focus_joint` and `plug_joint` preserve both source evidence and
`CompletionJoint.Valid` on the same named successor, deriving frame annotations
and closed returned values from the existing typing evidence.

Nine example lemmas check resume followed by application, rejection of two
sequential resumes, and rejection of a callable answer in a scalar request
hole. A returned function retains its latent operation requirement; the earlier
resumption requirement is not replayed. The callable handler example preserves
its actual pending chain from focus through the return to its clause, together
with the existing joint invariant. Its intervening captured frames use the
existing transition proofs; the example does not establish preservation of
`Source` at every intermediate state.

This closes phase and full-contract connections between neighboring plain
contexts. The judgment does not yet relate every saved scope to its supplied
source ticket, or align its contracts with all ordinary runtime ports. Handler,
resource and cleanup boundaries, multiple source ticket environments,
authenticated capture rows, complete initial admission and all-transition
source preservation still require integration. The induction structure is
finite even though programs and stacks have arbitrary size; missing cases
require adequate constructor premises and preservation lemmas, not enumeration
of possible stacks. General progress and Core correspondence remain unproved.

## Ownership balance determines the source owner

[ChainOwnerAgreement.lean](ChainOwnerAgreement.lean) removes the separate
binder-to-owner equality premise from resumption at a plain source segment.
Its `Demand` relation is a projection proved from the existing source and
runtime usage derivations: equal source phases yield an empty demand, and an
available-to-consumed transition yields a singleton runtime owner. Induction
composes those projections over arbitrary finite plain-frame chains. It adds
no admission assumption or owner registry.

The ownership argument uses the actual live boundary below that prefix.
`live_boundary_demand_excludes_owner` proves that its saved capture and outside
tail cannot demand the boundary's own owner. The capture receives only outside
active owners, and ownership uniqueness excludes aliases within the capture
or tail. Configuration ownership balance nevertheless requires that live owner
to be consumed. Therefore it must occur in the current expression or the
pending plain prefix. Their combined source demand contains at most one owner,
which fixes that owner's identity.

`live_source_requires_available` derives the source segment's available entry
and consumed exit phases from those premises. `live_source_pending_owner` and
`live_source_current_owner` derive the saved or current scope's exact resolution
for every consuming source use. The current resume and discard forms specialize
that argument without adding a resolution premise. A consumed source segment
has empty current and pending demands; idle saved scopes need not be cleared
or required to name live owners.

`resume_joint` applies the derived owner equality to the actual named resume
transition. It preserves `CompletionJoint.Valid` and retains the waiting source
chain at the consumed phase and the ticket's full answer contract. The existing
focus and plug proofs preserve the source and runtime premises from which owner
agreement is derived, so no separate scope predicate must be maintained for
those steps. The new resumption result does not claim a full `Source` invariant
through the newly installed capture.

Eleven example lemmas include a live owner 5 whose dormant capture must consume
outside owner 7. The pending source frame is proved to resolve owner 5; assigning
that use to owner 7 or abandoning owner 5 is rejected. A historical spent scope
retains no consumption demand. The callable example derives its actual pending
frame by focus, resumes without supplying an owner equality, and connects the
result to the existing admitted initial-to-capture execution prefix.

The proof applies when the entire active prefix above the selected boundary
consists of the plain frames described by `Source`. Its capture and outside tail
may contain other frame kinds and nested owners, checked by the existing runtime
invariant. A handler or resource interleaved within the source prefix still
requires source-invariant integration. The ownership projection does not itself
authenticate protection contexts, capture effect rows or ordinary value ports.
Complete source admission, all-transition source preservation and general
progress remain open. This evidence changes neither current Core nor the
correspondence status, and it does not enter the excluded continuation targets.

## Phase-neutral source and derived saved rows

[NeutralFrameRows.lean](NeutralFrameRows.lean) connects the phase judgment to
ordinary callable summaries and positional saved-frame requirements.
`neutral_code_iff` and `neutral_context_iff` prove equivalence when entry and
exit phases agree: the ordinary summary retains the full value contract and
raw footprint, and interpreting that footprint through the phase context yields
the exact phase judgment's exported row. Structural induction uses one-shot
phase monotonicity to show that every sequential intermediate phase also agrees.
Resume and discard cannot occur along such a phase-neutral derivation.

The equivalence retains protection. An available protected ticket still marks
outward requests as protected. After consumption, its own barrier becomes inert;
other interpretation layers remain in their positions. Cleanup's invocation
footprint retains its explicit protection even at a consumed boundary. Latent
function requirements remain part of the full callable contract and contribute
when the function is applied.

`consumed_chain_rows` derives `SavedFrameRequirements.Rows` from the actual
pending contexts of an arbitrary consumed plain-frame chain. No separate row
annotation is chosen. `consumed_chain_rows_append` composes the chain with a
remaining interpretation suffix: each plain frame's raw source footprint is
interpreted through that suffix, then the suffix's own pending rows are appended.
