coverage premise from resume-site construction. A local source checking view
replaces only the selected owner's resume row with the requirements evaluated
at the actual receiving stack. The caller must accept this row together with the
waiting segment's row. The original captured row remains evidence for its
original receiver.

`source_view`, `context_view`, `frame_view` and `segment_view` use structural
induction to show that changing this field preserves a derivation after the
selected owner is consumed. A valid trace cannot consume it again, so later
resume and discard lookups refer to other owners. `configuration_restore` uses
this fact to return from the temporary view to the original source registry.
`shared_source_view` retains shared value annotations, and `shared_view_ports`
proves that specialization preserves the full ordinary runtime port registry.

`resume_at_receiver` constructs retained requirements from the supplied saved
source. Successful evaluation at the actual caller and acceptance at its outside
interface derive both the before-source in the specialized view and the
restored after-source in the original registry. `resume_at_receiver_joint` joins
this construction to the same named runtime step, preserves the established
runtime invariant and indexes the after-source by the actual owned tickets.
Its premises still include that runtime invariant, the saved-source certificate,
the waiting segment's source and agreement with the initial ownership map.

The changed-handler example resumes an actual saved segment whose old row was
empty and whose new receiver exposes a second effect. The explicit outside
interface accepts that effect; an empty outside interface rejects it. Both
source states agree with the actual stack ownership maps. This is an open
fragment with supplied handler contracts, not closed-program admission.

The source view is checking evidence, not a runtime registry update or a new
computation form. This result closes the cached-bound obstruction for one resume
construction. Referenced continuation rows still require authentication, shared
annotations must cover saved segments, and the source invariant must be
maintained across all transitions before whole-program preservation or progress
can follow. No Core alignment is implied.

## Recursive capture-source authentication

[CaptureAuthentication.lean](CaptureAuthentication.lean) makes the resume-source
component of retained record authentication recursive. `Certified.saved` connects
an owner's actual registry entry to a `SavedSource` for its actual captured stack.
The certificate retains its historical receiver and source phase endpoints.
`Retained.live` requires that certificate, a recursive derivation for the dormant
capture, and another for the active tail. Push and spent boundaries recurse into
the tail; the empty stack has no capture obligations. These rules are structural
in the existing runtime stack and introduce no expression or computation form.

`append`, `decompose` and `cut` prove that splitting and recomposing an actual
stack retains all nested certificates. `resume` restores the checked dormant
capture ahead of the checked waiting frames. `discard` removes it and retains
the waiting captures; closing plans contain frames rather than live captures.
`cell_update` proves that mutating an active cell does not alter the saved capture
certificates. `non_capture_step` covers every raw transition that allocates no
ticket, including resource and cleanup allocation. It derives after-evidence
from before-evidence, without assuming after-authentication.

`capture_from_source` handles the remaining transition family. The actual handler
cut and current source judgment construct the new saved-source certificate.
Fresh insertion extends every older certificate, and the cut supplies recursive
evidence for the saved contents and waiting tail. `capture_step_from_source`
connects this construction to the actual raw capture step. It still requires the
current source judgment and source-registry freshness; this theorem does not
construct a complete source admission judgment or runtime port agreement.

`certified_source` retrieves checked saved code from the selected registry entry.
`certified_rechecks` derives finite requirements and reconstructs its source at
any receiver where evaluation succeeds. `resume_with_requirements` combines this
retrieval with the actual resume step and recursive after-authentication. The
historical phase endpoints stay explicit: agreement with the current ownership
map and acceptance of the new row remain necessary for the resume-site source
construction proved above.

The negative example has a valid outer certificate whose saved segment contains
a live boundary hiding an unregistered owner. The earlier active-segment rule
accepts that segment because it skips dormant contents; `Retained` rejects the
nested missing certificate. Positive examples check actual nested resume and
disposal steps. Their disposal result establishes retained-capture evidence only,
not approval of the recorded close contract.

This proves preservation of historical resume-source provenance through stack
movement and constructs that provenance at fresh capture. It does not yet
maintain one combined invariant for closing contracts, shared ordinary ports,
referenced continuation rows and current phases. Handler/resource source
admission and whole-program preservation/progress remain open. Historical
certificates do not make a cached residual row valid at every future caller.

## Shared saved-segment annotations

[SharedSourceSegments.lean](SharedSourceSegments.lean) extends shared value
annotations through the retained machine. `Context` covers the ten pending
positions admitted by the owner-aware expression judgment, including resume.
Its source and ordinary-port projections use the same hole and result
annotations. `stable_context`, `focus_decompose` and `context_plug` construct and
recompose those choices from source expressions. The resource context checks
its initializer and retains the stable fresh-body evidence described
[below](#resource-source-entry-with-combined-records).

`Frame` checks the metadata and retained code of each frame using these choices.
Plain frames derive both analyses from the shared pending context. Armed and
running cleanup frames check shared unit-to-unit callbacks, and a running frame
retains the saved result's annotation. Handler frames still require ordinary
clause typing and an answer annotation; source checking of their declared
protection tables and implementations is not derived here.

`Segment.live` checks both the dormant capture and active tail recursively.
The historical saved segment has exactly the record's shared input and answer
values, consumption demand and a row covered by its recorded resume row. Runtime
input and answer metadata agree with the same values' ordinary ports. Its held
flag agrees with the actual saved stack. `segment_source`, `segment_ports` and
`segment_authenticated` derive the owner-phase source judgment, ordinary stack
typing and recursive historical capture authentication from one witness.

`segment_append` and `segment_decompose` preserve these connections through
actual stack composition. `capture_answer` additionally derives the saved
answer's port from the handler selected by the actual cut. `capture_interface`
connects the same captured input to the shared operation entry and returns all
three projections for the saved computation. Independent protection and ordinary
derivations are no longer chosen for its input or result.

Fresh registry extension preserves the context, frame and recursive segment
judgments. `capture_record` constructs the shared input/answer annotation,
protection flag, saved demand and resume row from the actual segment cut. It
extends older records and derives the new live boundary, including its recursively
checked capture. `capture_step_record` joins this construction to the actual raw
capture step and operation entry. The initial consumed phase of the fresh owner
is an explicit premise; the result is the pending live boundary, not admission
of the executing handler clause. Close fields and ordinary resume/close effect
lists remain supplied annotations.

The configuration `Source` combines a shared current expression, its effect
scope, a shared pending segment and outside row acceptance. Its projections give
ordinary configuration typing, owner-phase source checking and recursive capture
authentication. Bind and beta reduction preserve this combined source evidence.
General preservation for fresh entry, handler clauses, resume and disposal still
needs the remaining source rules and phase/row transport.

The examples construct an integer-input, Boolean-result saved computation,
a concrete fresh capture that retains an older registry entry, and one actual
resume with both shared source states. A pending resume frame has the same
integer and Boolean annotations. Negative examples reject an incorrect plain
frame input and incorrect live-capture metadata even though scalar protection
shapes cannot distinguish integer from Boolean. Handler clauses in these
examples are ordinarily typed and their protection tables are explicit; this is
not yet general source admission of provider implementations.

This closes shared saved-type agreement and construction of the resume part of
capture records. Closing obligations, ordinary effect-list authentication,
referenced continuation-row specialization and current phase agreement must
still be combined into a preserved invariant. Handler/resource source admission
and whole-program preservation/progress remain open. The Core comparison remains
an assessment; no Core changes are made.

## Shared closing-plan source

[SharedClosingSource.lean](SharedClosingSource.lean) connects executable disposal
plans to the shared saved-stack judgment. `plan_contents` follows the actual
`makePlan` computation and the recursive segment derivation. It extracts each
callback's shared unit-to-unit annotation and every retired owner's registry
entry. `Rows` derives the protected footprint after interpreting each invocation
through its actual remaining plan suffix. Its protection projection is the
existing disposal-row judgment.

`effects` computes ordinary outward instances from that same suffix order.
A callback can use a cell that is still present later in the plan; an earlier
release cannot discharge its requests. `rows_ports` constructs ordinary plan
typing from the shared callbacks and this computed bound. `plan_source` constructs
the materialized plan's shared source segment, including unit input/result types,
retirement transitions and callback footprints checked at the actual receiver.

The consumed-owner transport lemmas preserve shared expressions, contexts and
frames when their ordered projections agree. `segment_fixed_spent` retains each
nested capture's historical certificate while transporting the active segment.
`pending_live_to_spent` derives the shared waiting stack after changing the
selected boundary from live to spent. It does not assume that arbitrary changed
handler stacks are equivalent.

`disposal_plan` derives plan existence from the actual capture's unprotected
state, as checked by the shared source judgment. It supplies shared rows,
ordinary plan typing and agreement between plan retirements and captured owners.
`discard_source` then reconstructs the after-source by composing the actual plan
with the preserved waiting segment. It checks retirement order against the
recorded close demand, ordinary outward effects against the recorded close
effects, and the receiver's computed footprint against the recorded close row.
These finite bounds are explicit premises, not automatically authenticated
fields of every source record.

`discard_joint` connects that source construction to the same named runtime
transition and full runtime invariant. The source operation signature must agree
with the declaration signature, and its complete ordinary continuation registry
must agree with the runtime registry. The shared callbacks derive the required
ordinary plan typing. Runtime name history derives separation between scheduled
retirements and the surviving suffix; the resulting source judgment uses the
actual after-state ownership map. Fresh close allocation and access checks remain
premises. This is a conditional combined preservation theorem, not complete
admission or whole-program progress.

Cleanup start and completion, close completion, nested-owner retirement and cell
release now preserve the shared source judgment. Starting cleanup derives the
protected callback application and retains the same saved-result annotation.
Completion restores the saved value and the effect scope determined by the
registry. Retirement requires the owner to be available and advances its phase.
These results do not yet cover every intervening callback or source-entry step.

The examples execute a disposal plan whose callback reads a cell before its
release. Both ordinary outward effects and the source footprint are empty after
the plan supplies that cell. Reversing the order leaves an outward cell request;
the empty recorded ordinary bound and empty outside source interface reject it.
The actual disposal and cleanup-start steps have shared source states, and beta
reduction derives the callback body's source. A Boolean-returning callback
illustrates a separate gap in scalar-only protection checking: the shared
unit-to-unit requirement rejects it.

General call-site specialization and phase/row preservation, authentication of
closing bounds at every admitted capture, handler/resource source admission and
whole-program preservation/progress remain open. No claim of Core alignment or
support for the deferred continuation targets follows from these proofs.

## Source rechecking at current owner phases

[PhaseRechecking.lean](PhaseRechecking.lean) removes the frozen owner-phase
indices from the earlier requirement evaluation. `Requirements` is finite
checking data extracted from an existing shared source derivation. Its index is
that derivation's one-shot consumption demand. It adds no computation forms or
sequencing operators to `ScopedExpressions.Code`.

`evaluate` takes both a receiving interpretation context and an initial owner
state. A consumption check requires distinct available owners and advances that
state before checking the next requirement. Requests are interpreted through
their retained nearer frames followed by the receiving context, at the state
where the request occurs. A boundary guard requires its owner to have been
consumed. These checks preserve the distinction between the active segment's
future consumption and a retained capture's historical ownership certificate.

Branches check both arms from the same state. Their demand lists must be
permutations, which gives the same final owner state even when consumption order
differs. Their effect footprints are combined as alternatives that both require
admission; the arms are not executed in sequence. `evaluate_trace` proves that
successful evaluation produces the indexed ownership transition, and
`evaluate_once` derives distinct consumption from that transition.

`source_rechecks`, `context_rechecks` and `frame_rechecks` extract requirements
and reconstruct the same shared value annotations after successful evaluation
at any new receiver and initial owner state. `segment_rechecks` composes these
requirements in stack order. Its live-boundary case preserves the original
historical certificate for the dormant capture and rechecks the active tail.
It does not replace a historical certificate with a claim that the dormant code
has already been checked at every future caller.

`configuration_rechecks` combines the current expression and pending segment.
Successful evaluation and acceptance of the resulting outside footprint derive
the new configuration's shared source judgment. The final owner state is
computed by spending exactly its demand from the new initial state. Ordinary
ports and recursive capture authentication therefore remain projections of the
same reconstructed judgment; an independent after-source premise is unnecessary.

The examples admit two branch arms that each resume owner 19 once, reject two
sequential uses, and preserve unrelated owner 23. Different consumption orders
in alternatives reach the same owner state; different consumption sets cannot
satisfy the branch requirement. An available protected boundary rejects a
disposing interpretation. Consuming its owner before the request removes that
boundary and admits the request; reversing the sequence rejects it. Concrete
resume expressions, pending resume frames and nested saved boundaries reconstruct
shared source at changed owner states while retaining their ordinary types.

Referenced continuation rows remain literal annotations in these requirements.
Their recursive call-site specialization and authentication must still be joined
to current phase agreement and closing bounds. The theorem reconstructs source
after a successful finite check; it does not prove that initial source admission
guarantees success of all later checks. Handler/resource admission and general
preservation/progress remain open. Core correspondence is still assessment only,
and the deferred continuation capabilities remain outside this kernel.

## Shared resumption at current callers

[SharedResumption.lean](SharedResumption.lean) connects current-phase rechecking
to actual one-shot restoration. `selected_capture` decomposes the waiting stack
at the resolved live boundary and retrieves that capture's historical shared
derivation. The same record supplies its input and answer ports, ownership
demand, protected state and historical footprint bound. The saved derivation is
not supplied independently of the actual selected capture.

`resume_from_rechecked` composes the capture, checked at the actual restored
suffix and current owner state, with the waiting caller. It derives the raw
resume step, the current invocation's specialized expression typing, and the
shared source of the restored configuration. The caller's footprint must accept
the computed invocation row together with its own pending row. Coverage by the
historical cached row is unnecessary.

The invocation's row is a local checking view. The waiting segment and all
historical captures continue to use their original shared registry.
`invocation_ports` proves that this local expression view and the unchanged
pending segment describe one ordinarily typed configuration. The restored
configuration has a complete shared source judgment under the original registry.
This does not claim a shared before-configuration under a globally rewritten
registry: changing every historical certificate is a different obligation.

`resume_requirements` extracts finite requirements from the selected historical
derivation. Their successful evaluation at the current caller constructs the
received segment and its endpoint. Neither equality with the historical phase
map nor an after-source premise is assumed. `resume_source` obtains the operand,
permissions, ownership transition and pending segment from an existing shared
source judgment. Its extra finite recheck is still necessary; the existing
source judgment alone does not establish its success.

`resume_joint` joins this reconstruction to the same named runtime transition
and full runtime invariant. Its source starts at the actual stack's available
owners, and its conclusion uses the actual restored stack's owner map. It still
assumes the runtime invariant and source annotation independently; it does not
derive their complete registry/signature coherence or initial admission.

The first example saves a pending request under an interpretation that hides
it. At a caller without that interpretation, the request becomes outward. The
new outside interface accepts it, although the original empty row cannot cover
it. Both configurations have ordinary port typing, and restoration preserves
the original source record. The example is an open configuration with an
explicit outside interface, not a closed-program progress result.

The nested example gives a sharper boundary. Owner 19's capture resumes owner
29, whose historical capture contains the pending request. Both records advertise
empty source rows. The outer invocation's finite check succeeds because its
reference to owner 29 still uses that advertised row. An actual resume followed
by plugging the value into the pending context reaches the inner invocation.
The shared source judgments persist through those two concrete steps, and their
phase maps agree with actual stack ownership. Rechecking the inner capture then
exposes the request, which the empty outside interface rejects.

This example disproves sufficiency of the represented historical source and
per-invocation checks for future admission. It does not prove that this state is
reachable from a fully admitted initial program; that admission judgment is
unfinished. The next invariant must authenticate referenced continuation rows
recursively, or establish equivalent maintained call-site evidence, before
initial checking can imply every later check. Ordinary effect bounds, closing
contracts, handler/resource admission and whole-program preservation/progress
still need integration. Core alignment and the deferred continuation targets
remain outside this work.

## Recursive continuation requirements

[RecursiveRequirements.lean](RecursiveRequirements.lean) gives a finite recursive
checker for the continuation-reference gap above. Its requirements are checking
data for the existing execution syntax. Request, retirement, consumed-boundary,
sequence, callback-footprint and branch nodes preserve their phase-sensitive
roles. An invocation stores an owner/mode key, a continuation demand and the
nearer interpretation prefix. It stores no cached invocation row.

The finite store associates keys with demand-indexed requirement templates.
Invocation requires an entry with exactly the expected demand, distinct
available owners for the invocation's owner plus that demand, and successful
active selection by `OwnerPhases.consume`. The structural `Checked.invoke` rule
carries the corresponding `Consumes` derivation. A matching spent boundary
rejects selection; a dormant capture is not searched. The checker consumes the
invocation owner in its phase map, then recursively checks the referenced body
at the nearer prefix followed by the receiving context. The resulting row becomes the
invocation row. Resume and disposal keys are distinct; deriving their permissions
and source/closing templates remains an authentication obligation.

`Calls` structurally identifies references inside requirements. `call_decreases`
proves that the referenced body's demand is shorter than the containing demand:
the invocation includes its own owner in addition to that body's demand.
Sequence preserves this strict inequality, and branch permutation supplies equal
demand lengths for either alternative. `Edge` connects a reference to its actual
matching store entry. Strictly decreasing ranks prove that linked reference
paths cannot cycle and that recursive invocation is well founded.

The executable evaluator uses fuel across invocation edges and structural
recursion within each template. The public checker chooses the requirement's
demand length. `fuel_stable` proves that any two fuel amounts at least this large
give the same result, including rejection. This bound is derived from the indexed
structure, not a guessed depth limit. Missing entries, demand mismatches and
unavailable owners reject before their bodies can justify admission.

`Checked` is the corresponding structural judgment. Its invocation rule contains
the actual store lookup, active selection, and a recursive derivation for the
referenced body at the consumed-owner state. `evaluate_sound` and `checked_complete` prove exact
equivalence between this judgment and successful evaluation. `checked_trace`
derives its complete ownership transition; `checked_once` derives distinct
consumption. Prefix composition commutes with evaluation and with `Checked`,
including the contexts passed through recursive invocation nodes.

The nested example uses the same owners, stacks and inner saved request as the
shared-resumption example. Its stored outer template invokes the inner template
instead of reading owner 29's cached row. Historical interpretation still hides
the request. At the current caller, recursive checking exposes it before the
outer invocation is admitted. The empty outside interface rejects immediately;
the explicitly supplied interface accepts. The inner template's successful
evaluation reconstructs the actual shared saved segment at arbitrary receivers
and phases. The example's demands agree with the existing shared records.

Further examples reject missing or mismatched templates, an inconsistent cyclic
store, unavailable nested owners and two sequential invocations of one owner.
Branch alternatives may each invoke that owner once. Another example owns a
nested continuation and has its template but rejects direct invocation while
its boundary is dormant. The outer invocation remains accepted because its
restored template exposes the inner boundary before the inner call. Additional
fuel leaves the result unchanged.

This closes the demonstrated cached-reference failure for the constructed
templates and proves the recursive checker's structural properties. It does not
yet extract and authenticate every template from admitted source or preserve
that association through every runtime step. In particular, the general relation
between recursive rows, local invocation views and shared historical source
judgments remains to be proved. Ordinary effect bounds, closing templates,
handler/resource admission and whole-program preservation/progress remain open.
No Core alignment or deferred continuation capability is included.

## Source-derived continuation templates

[SourceTemplates.lean](SourceTemplates.lean) connects recursive checking data to
the shared source grammar. `Expression` derives requirements for the same
`ScopedExpressions.Code` forms and shared value annotations. Its resume and
discard rules retain the resolved owner, continuation permission, demand and
ordinary effect bound. Their source rows come from recursive invocation nodes,
not historical cached rows. Branch rules retain the permutation of consumption
demands; callbacks retain their shared unit-to-unit type and protected footprint.

`expression_from_source` constructs this derivation for every expression admitted
by the existing owner-phase shared judgment. The corresponding context and frame
theorems cover all represented pending positions and frame forms. Ordinary typing
is a projection of these structural derivations, with the same scope and shared
value choices. Handler frames still carry supplied ordinary typing; this is not
yet source admission of their complete interpretations.

`Segment` follows both the active stack and dormant saved captures. Its active
requirements preserve frame order and prepend each remaining saved suffix to
the current frame's requirements. At a live boundary it checks the saved
segment against that owner's shared input, answer and demand, and collects a
resume entry containing the resulting template. The collected store also
contains entries from nested captures and the active tail. Consumed-boundary
guards remain in the active requirements. Retirement is a direct owner check.

`segment_from_source` derives the segment and its collected store from the
existing shared saved-stack judgment. `CapturedIn` locates captures throughout
that retained forest. Each `Certified` lookup result includes such a location,
the owner's shared record, and a structural derivation for that actual captured
body. The certification theorems follow the collection through saved and active
branches. They do not certify an unrelated body merely because its ports happen
to match. `ActiveCapture` separately follows the active spine through frames
and unrelated boundaries, stopping at the selected live owner. It does not
search dormant bodies and cannot pass a matching spent owner. Its derivations
correspond to successful context selection and construct the actual runtime
stack decomposition, by induction at arbitrary depth. Distinct owned tickets
make all retained locations for one owner agree on the same capture.
`certified_selected` therefore identifies the source-derived lookup template
with that exact selected body.

`Configuration` combines the current expression, pending segment and collected
store. `configuration_from_source` constructs it from an existing shared source
configuration. `CheckedConfiguration` additionally requires distinct owned
tickets, a successful recursive check starting at the actual stack's available
owners, and acceptance of the resulting outside footprint. It derives ordinary configuration typing,
the complete indexed consumption transition and absence of repeated consumption.
It is a checked current state, not a claim of complete initial admission with
preservation and progress at every later state.

`checked_resume_step` joins source derivation, owner uniqueness and a checked
resume invocation at the actual stack context. Given lexical resolution and a
closed operand, it constructs the raw resume step without a supplied stack cut.
The restored capture carries the exact source template used by the recursive
check, and the same step consumes its owner while retaining every other owned
ticket. The conclusion includes the trace between the actual runtime owner
maps. `checked_configuration_resume_progress` derives the invocation premises
from a checked current configuration with a closed value operand. It constructs
the selected step and ownership trace with no additional access or template
premise. This is the current-state resume progress case; it does not yet
construct a recursively checked successor configuration or prove preservation
for all transitions.

Contract extension preserves expressions, contexts, frames, saved segments,
lookup certificates and checked configurations. The existing template data and
its source locations stay the same under an extension that retains all older
records. This handles one part of fresh allocation; it does not yet prove the
stack change or the new template's installation for every capture step.

The nested example now derives the complete current expression, both captures
and the two-entry store using these source rules. The inner lookup certificate
locates owner 29 inside owner 19's actual capture. Recursive checking starts at
the actual `[19, 29]` ownership map, exposes the inner request, rejects the empty
outside interface and accepts the explicit interface. Ordinary ports and
one-shot consumption are derived from that same checked configuration. The
example also derives an actual outer resume step and its runtime ownership
trace from the checked configuration. The inner template is authenticated but
cannot be invoked directly while dormant.

The collected store currently supplies resume templates. Closing templates must
come from actual disposal plans, retaining their ordering and callback checks.
Preservation of call-site selection and template associations through stack
changes, ordinary effect-bound authentication, source admission of
handler/resource entry, and whole-check preservation remain open. Those results are required before this construction yields
whole-program preservation/progress. Core correspondence remains assessment
only, and the deferred continuation targets remain excluded.

## Recursive checks across consumed callers

[RecursiveTransport.lean](RecursiveTransport.lean) transports the recursive
checker through the physical caller update and the spent owner's removal from
the template store. Its `normalize` function removes live or spent markers only
when their owner is consumed in the shared phase map. Ordinary interpretation
layers retain their order. A spent marker whose owner is still marked available
remains, so inconsistent duplicate names cannot bypass selection. The normalized
context has the same protection projection and the same selection result for
every available owner. Further consumption preserves these equalities.

`checked_transport` proves by induction over the complete recursive derivation
that the check survives two simultaneous changes: normalized receiving contexts
agree, and template lookups agree for every available owner. The invocation case
transports both its structural selection and its recursively checked body.
Sequencing and callback emission transport their later phases as well.
`checked_transport_iff` and `evaluate_transport` give equivalence, including
rejection, rather than only preservation of successful examples.

`removeOwner` deletes both resume and disposal entries for an owner. A consumed
owner can no longer justify a lookup, so this deletion preserves all remaining
checks. `resume_caller_transport` combines deletion with the physical
live-to-spent boundary update. `selected_caller` constructs that actual waiting
stack from structural selection, without a supplied cut or extra name-history
premise. `checked_resume_body` joins these results to the authenticated saved
source: the body used by the invocation remains checked at its actual waiting
caller and the successor's actual runtime owner map. Historical shared contracts
remain available for ordinary typing and scope resolution.

The template store can change order as captured stacks are restored. Lookup and
checking are invariant under a store permutation with distinct owner/mode keys.
This permits a resume and a disposal entry for the same owner. The current
source-derived resume store obtains key uniqueness from the runtime ownership
invariant: its owner list is a sublist of the stack's owned tickets. Store
permutation does not change the interpretation context or establish permission
to exchange handlers.

The nested example now constructs the complete checked successor of the outer
resume. It restores the actual capture, removes owner 19's template, retains
owner 29's source template, and carries the exposed request through the physical
waiting caller. The successor uses the actual `[29]` ownership map and retains
ordinary configuration typing. `nested_resume_preserved` joins the original
checked configuration, the raw resume step and the checked successor. It uses
the general caller/store transport result; acceptance of the restored state is
constructed rather than supplied as a premise. Additional examples retain a
spent selection barrier when its owner is marked available and allow distinct
resume/disposal keys for one owner.

The saved-body transport theorem alone does not recompose every captured
segment with an arbitrary pending caller. The following general recomposition
proof constructs the new segment requirements and collected store and joins
their checks. Fresh capture, closing-template construction, ordinary effect-bound
associations, handler/resource entry and whole-program preservation/progress
remain open. Core correspondence stays assessment only; the deferred
continuation targets remain excluded.

## General resumption recomposition

[RecursiveRecomposition.lean](RecursiveRecomposition.lean) extends the previous
saved-body result to complete resumption preservation for the current
source-derived configuration judgment. It constructs the successor's segment,
requirements and collected store from the original checked state. No supplied
successor check, stack cut, future access check or new capture certificate is a
premise of `resume_preserves`.

`segment_append` composes any two source segments with matching shared value
annotations. The combined demand and collected store are their concatenations.
Its evaluation theorem checks the first segment at the second segment's ordered
context, then checks the second after the first demand is consumed. It proves
exact equality of the resulting checks for arbitrary stores, receiving contexts
and phases. The induction covers every active frame and live/spent boundary;
dormant saved-source certificates retain their own bodies. The corresponding
`segment_append_checked` constructs the combined successful check.

`replace_live` constructs the pending caller with the selected live boundary
replaced by its spent boundary. It extracts the actual saved source and proves
how the collected records move: the selected entry and captured records can be
placed before the surviving caller's records. The pending requirements have the
same evaluation once the selected owner is consumed. This holds through an
arbitrary prefix, including other live boundaries and their dormant captures.
Runtime owner uniqueness identifies the extracted template with the invocation's
lookup and justifies deleting the selected entry before the remaining store is
reordered. These record permutations do not reorder handlers or pending code.

`resume_segments` joins replacement, store transport, segment append and the
actual runtime ownership transition. Both the restored capture and the surviving
caller contribute checks from the original configuration. It constructs their
combined check at the successor's actual owner map, with the actual collected
store and distinct remaining owners. Closed value operands have empty immediate
demands and footprints, so their source summary supplies the successor's current
expression without an additional request or consumption.

`resume_cut_preserves` supplies preservation for every cut satisfying the raw
resume rule's premises. `resume_step_preserves` then quantifies over every raw
step from a checked resume with a closed value operand. Focus cannot apply to a
value operand, and value-completion rules cannot apply to a resume expression.
The theorem derives a successor `CheckedConfiguration`, the same output
annotation and checking footprint, unchanged operand and scope, and the exact
creation/discharge events. The original demand is the consumed owner followed
by the successor demand; the ownership trace relates the two actual runtime maps.

`resume_preserves` combines this universal preservation theorem with the earlier
current-state progress theorem to construct a preserved next step. Ordinary
typing, one-shot checking, source-template provenance and outside acceptance
therefore remain connected for every such transition, not only for one selected
successor. These results cover arbitrary captured segments and pending caller
prefixes.

The existing nested case now follows from this general theorem. A second case
adds a nonempty caller prefix containing an effectful bind. Its footprint
contains the inner captured request followed by the bind's later request. The
general theorem constructs its checked successor and retains both requests,
while consuming owner 19 and leaving owner 29 for the nested continuation.
The universal theorem is also applied to the explicit raw transitions for both
examples, deriving checks for those exact successors.

This closes value-operand resumption preservation for the current judgment,
not preservation/progress for every expression or complete initial admission.
Fresh capture, closing-template generation and its integration with this store,
ordinary context steps, handler/resource entry, effect-bound associations,
and the whole-program theorem remain open. Core correspondence remains an
assessment task; alignment and the deferred continuation targets are excluded.

## Ordinary recursive source reductions

[RecursiveExpressions.lean](RecursiveExpressions.lean) connects closed
substitution and ready ordinary reductions to the recursive source judgment.
The substitution theorem retains the exact shared result annotation, demand and
requirements data. Its structural recursion covers all current expression
constructors, including continuation invocation and disposal. A closed value
cannot introduce a new continuation demand. Binder shadowing and distinct nested
binders use the same environment annotations as the source derivation.

`bind_expression` and `beta_expression` construct the reduced source and prove
equality of checking results for every template store, receiving context and
owner state. The former substitutes the value into the pending body. The latter
uses the function's shared latent summary and resets the current ticket scope
to `none`, matching execution. Both retain the original demand and footprint.
Their configuration preservation theorems retain the actual pending segment,
collected templates, outside acceptance and runtime ownership.

`branch_expression` constructs the selected source and proves that its demand
is a permutation of the original demand. A successful original check supplies
a check of the selected branch whose footprint is a sublist of the original
footprint. Both alternatives were checked, but execution selects only one;
request requirements for the unused alternative can disappear. A permutation of
the consumed owners gives the same resulting owner map. `branch_preserves`
therefore retains the pending caller's check and derives outside acceptance of
the smaller complete footprint. This argument does not exchange interpretations
or execute the unselected branch.

`Ready` identifies binds with a value initializer, applications of a lambda to a
value, and branches with a Boolean condition. `ready_step_preserves` covers
every raw step from such a checked expression, rules out focus and value
completion, and proves that the runtime stack and creation/discharge events
remain unchanged. The result annotation is retained; demand permutation and
footprint inclusion account for branch selection. `ready_progress` derives the
raw lexical premises from ordinary typing. `ready_preserves` combines these
results with an empty runtime ownership trace. It requires no supplied check of
the successor or additional closed-substitution premise.

One example substitutes a bound unit operand into a resume expression with a
source-derived nested capture. The resulting checked configuration feeds
directly into general resumption preservation, consuming owner 19 and retaining
owner 29. Another checks both branch alternatives invoking the same outer
continuation. Their footprints are combined for admission, while their demands
are alternatives; selecting the false branch preserves a checked resume with a
sublist of that combined footprint.

These results close the ready bind/application/branch cases for the current
judgment. The following context result supplies focus and plugging integration.
Fresh capture, disposal/cleanup, handler/resource entry, effect-bound associations
and whole-program preservation/progress remain open.
This is informative evidence about the experimental source calculus; it neither
changes current Core nor establishes a formal Core correspondence.

## Recursive evaluation contexts

[RecursiveContexts.lean](RecursiveContexts.lean) connects the recursive checker
to evaluation-context movement. A plain pending frame adds an ordinary
unprotected barrier to the ordered context. `plain_export_middle` and
`plain_consume_middle` prove that this layer changes neither effect interpretation
nor continuation selection, at any position and owner state. Checking transports
across that insertion, including every recursively referenced continuation body.
`evaluate_plain` proves equality of complete evaluations, including rejection.
No handler or resource interpreter is exchanged or removed by this result.

`stable_context` reconstructs recursive requirements for the stable shared
context summaries. `context_plug` and `focus_decompose` then cover the nine
current pending positions: both pair positions, both application positions,
bind, branch, perform operand, resume operand and cleanup callback. They retain
the exact shared annotation at the hole. Demand splits by concatenation, and
checking evaluates the child first, then the pending context after that child's
owners are consumed. The resulting footprint is their ordered concatenation.
The equations hold for every template store, receiving context and initial owner
map. No successful successor check is an assumption.

`prepare_plain` derives lexical ticket translation from source typing and scope
resolution. The frame's input and output annotations embed the shared ports.
`focus_preserves` uses the actual decomposition to construct a raw focus step and
a complete checked successor. Its current code sees the new neutral frame; the
frame's pending code is checked at the original receiving context. Sequencing
associativity joins those checks with the existing caller. The collected
continuation store, total demand, footprint and actual owner map are retained.
This theorem constructs the frame from typing; it does not claim that arbitrary
annotations supplied to the raw focus relation are well typed.

`plug_preserves` handles return to any source-checked plain frame. A closed value
has an empty immediate demand and footprint, and its shared summary can be used
under the saved frame's scope and allowed effects. Recomposition therefore
restores that scope while retaining the pending caller, its collected store and
the complete check. `value_closed` derives lexical closure from empty-environment
typing. `plug_progress` uses it to construct the actual return step and an empty
runtime ownership trace without a supplied closure premise.

The example begins with a bind inside the operand of a resume whose saved body
contains another continuation. It constructs and checks focus, bind reduction
and plugging, then feeds the reconstructed resume configuration into general
resumption preservation. The three context/ordinary steps retain owners 19 and
29; resumption consumes 19 and leaves 29. Its source-derived templates are
retained throughout, and the later inner request remains in the checked
footprint.

These results integrate ordinary context movement with the recursive source
checker. Fresh capture, disposal/cleanup, handler/resource entry, effect-bound
associations and the whole-program preservation/progress theorem remain open.
They are informative proof evidence for the experimental source calculus. Core
correspondence remains an assessment task; alignment and the deferred
continuation targets are excluded.

## Recursive fresh capture

[RecursiveCapture.lean](RecursiveCapture.lean) derives the captured source and
new resume record from the actual selected handler cut. `capture_segments`
splits a source-derived stack into the saved segment, including the selected
handler, and its surviving caller. The shared answer annotation agrees with the
handler's declared answer port. Demands and collected stores split by exact
concatenation. Its checking equation interprets the saved requirements at the
surviving caller, then checks that caller after the saved demand is consumed.
Induction covers every prefix frame and live/spent boundary, retaining the actual
bodies of nested captures. `capture_segments_checked` extracts both successful
checks from the original segment check.

`owned_registered` proves that every currently owned ticket has a source
contract, including tickets retained for retirement. Thus a fresh registry key
cannot already be owned by this stack. `capture_owned`, `capture_unique` and
`capture_phase_consumed` establish the runtime change: capture prepends exactly
the new owner, preserves uniqueness, and spending that owner restores the old
owner map. Registry freshness here implies current ownership freshness; complete
initial admission must also connect registry allocation to issued-name history.

`capture_record` constructs the new shared contract, its captured requirements
and its live-boundary source derivation. Its input, answer, resume demand and
historical resume row come from the cut and the original successful check.
Its collected store is the new resume entry followed by the entire old store.
Registry extension preserves both saved and surviving source derivations. Adding
the entry preserves their old checks because the fresh owner was consumed in
the old map. No stored continuation body is replaced by an independently
supplied summary. Closing demand/row and ordinary effect-list annotations remain
explicit inputs; this theorem does not authenticate those annotations.

`fresh_resume_configuration` joins the new boundary with an immediate resume
clause. After the new owner is consumed, the captured check transports to the
actual live caller context; its boundary is inactive in that owner state. The
remaining caller check follows at the resulting map. The constructed expression
and pending segment therefore check together using the actual collected store.

`capture_immediate_resume` connects that construction to an actual selected
clause of the form `resume binder reply`. The reply has a structural shared
summary with an empty immediate row under the request parameter's environment.
The actual operand's shared summary supplies closed substitution. Ordinary
selected-clause typing derives lexical readiness and answer-port formation.
The theorem constructs the capture step and a complete checked successor whose
demand is the new owner followed by the original demand. Its footprint is a
sublist of the original footprint, so outside acceptance follows. It covers
arbitrary saved nesting and surviving callers within this clause class; no
successor checking premise is supplied.

The example starts from a checked request under a handler and a pending bind.
Capture constructs owner 23 with integer input and Boolean answer. Its checked
resume with integer 17 then feeds directly into general resumption preservation,
which restores the pending computation and consumes owner 23. The example
therefore joins actual capture and resumption, rather than checking unrelated
before/after annotations.

The complete capture theorem for arbitrary clauses remains open. Source
admission must establish the clause requirements and ordinary effect bounds;
disposal/cleanup must derive the closing templates and contracts. Handler/resource
entry, allocation-history integration and whole-program preservation/progress
remain unfinished. The immediate-resume clause class is proof coverage within
the proposed calculus, not a restriction of the target calculus. Core
correspondence remains an assessment task, with alignment and deferred
continuation targets excluded.

## Structural clauses and authenticated invocation

[RecursiveClauses.lean](RecursiveClauses.lean) connects the existing shared
owner-indexed source derivation to recursive requirements. It introduces no
new computation syntax or bind. The proof covers all ten constructors of that
derivation: stable expressions, pairs, application, binds, branches, requests,
resume, discard, cleanup and resource expressions. The resource body has a stable
summary; its initializer may consume the local continuation. Handler installation
and resource bodies with enclosing-continuation actions still require admission.

A clause's ticket scope resolves every direct continuation action to the same
owner. `available_unchanged` proves that if the owner remains available, the
clause has performed no continuation transition: its demand is empty and the
entire owner map is unchanged. `entry_after` propagates this fact through
sequencing. Consequently an invocation in the clause occurs at the initial
owner map, even when ordinary effects precede it. Effects following invocation
are checked at the map produced by the actual saved computation's demands.

`compile` reconstructs source templates and a recursive check by induction on
the structural clause derivation. It requires authenticated resume and offered
disposal invocation checks at the initial map; it does not assume a check for
the whole clause or its successor configuration. Branches check both alternatives
and derive agreement of their owner demands from the shared endpoint. Their
footprints include both alternatives, retaining conservative effect accounting.

For a contract offering resume only, `demand_shape` proves that the clause's
demand is either empty or exactly the local owner followed by the saved
computation's demand. Sequential duplicate invocation is impossible because
the first consumes the owner and the second requires it available.
`consuming_demand` excludes the empty case when the clause starts with its owner
available and ends with it consumed. The demand is thus derived from structural
checking, rather than supplied as an independent compatibility condition.

`fresh_resume_check` authenticates invocation from the actual saved requirements
at the new live boundary. It transports the saved check into the physical
caller after consuming the new owner. `fresh_clause_configuration` joins that
invocation, a completed structural clause derivation, and the surviving caller
into a complete checked configuration. It derives the caller's incoming owner
map from the clause's demand. The source-collected store still offers resume
only, so this join requires the contract's closing row to be absent. The more
general compiler's disposal premise is not yet discharged by that store.

The example checks a clause with an outward request, a branch whose alternatives
each resume, another outward request and a Boolean result. Its actual saved
continuation takes an integer and returns a Boolean. The two requests remain in
the outside footprint, and a separate example rejects sequential double resume.
This demonstrates the structural clause join at a supplied actual live boundary;
it does not establish that installing an arbitrary handler generates the clause
proof or that the offered handler table bounds its footprint.

The remaining capture admission work must connect each actual selected clause,
its parameter substitution and ordinary effect bounds to this judgment, and
relate its derived footprint to the handler's offered table. Ordinary port typing
of retained clauses alone is insufficient. Closing authentication, handler and
resource entry, allocation history, and whole-program progress/preservation
remain open. These are obligations for the full one-shot target; the resume-only
join does not narrow that target. Core remains unchanged.

## Structural clauses at actual dispatch

[RecursiveDispatch.lean](RecursiveDispatch.lean) connects structural clauses to
actual selected handlers and request-argument substitution. `request_evaluation`
identifies the exact recursive-check result of a value-operand request with
its residual through the current owner-indexed context. At the actual ownership
map, that context projects to the active interpretation stack.

`cut_residual` follows the actual handler cut. Nonmatching ordinary frames and
live captured boundaries accumulate protection without changing the selected
handler. The theorem derives its exact table lookup, permitted protection mode,
offered row, and the equation interpreting that row through the actual surviving
tail. This requires no uniqueness assumption on unrelated activation labels and
preserves nearest exact selection, including builtin blockers represented in
the cut. It does not infer a clause proof from a supplied table entry.

`capture_from_structural_clause` constructs the shared captured contract and
retains the source/check evidence for saved and surviving segments. It derives
an exact decomposition of the original footprint into three parts: the selected
request's residual, the saved computation's residual, and the surviving caller's
row. The captured demand is a sublist of the original demand. The selected offer
and its residual equation remain connected to that same decomposition.

The theorem then accepts a structural derivation of the actual selected clause
under the request parameter's shared input annotation. The clause must consume
its local owner and every demand in its derived row must occur in the request
residual or the saved computation's row. Closed substitution binds the actual
request operand while preserving that derivation. The preceding clause join
constructs the complete successor check; appending the surviving caller's row
proves that every successor demand is covered by the original footprint.
Outside acceptance therefore follows from the original check. Capture constructs
the raw step with the derived input annotation and adds exactly one owned ticket.

Coverage uses membership, not list order or multiplicity. These footprint lists
record checking obligations, while the source and runtime judgments retain
sequencing and interpretation order. A clause can place its saved computation
between two ordinary requests; alternative branches can each contribute the
same saved obligations. Requiring a sublist would reject those cases even
though every request is covered. Two finite witnesses check that distinction.
Coverage retains the exact demand, including its protection flag, and implies
outside acceptance because footprint checking checks each demand independently
against the same outside context. This changes no operational ordering law.

This is a conditional dispatch theorem with explicit structural clause and row
premises. It neither assumes a recursive check for the whole successor nor
claims that handler installation already derives those premises. The current
construction authenticates resume and sets the closing row to absent; closing
templates and their source integration remain required for the full one-shot
target. Ordinary resume-effect annotations remain explicit inputs, and allocation
must still join current freshness to issued-name history.

The example's actual handler clause makes a request, chooses between two
resumptions, makes another request and returns a Boolean. A pending bind gives
the saved continuation integer input and Boolean answer. The handler offers both
outward requests; dispatch derives that offer and a fully checked captured
successor using the general theorem. The example discharges its structural
clause and row premises rather than supplying the successor check. An empty
offer fails the exhibited clause's bound. The surrounding interpretation accepts
the outward requests; a complete run through that surrounding handler is not
claimed by this example.

Handler admission must now provide the selected clause derivation and its bound
for every capture it offers. Ordinary retained-clause port typing is weaker and
cannot substitute for that proof. Handler/resource entry, disposal/cleanup,
allocation history and the combined preservation/progress theorem remain open.
Core correspondence remains a status assessment, with no alignment changes.

## Recursive closing templates

[RecursiveClosing.lean](RecursiveClosing.lean) derives closing templates from
the same retained source forest used by recursive resumption. `plan_contents`
follows successful `makePlan` construction, extracting actual shared callback
summaries and retired-owner contracts, including those in dormant nested
captures. Running cleanup, closing and retiring frames have no successful plan.
The existing structural row construction then determines each callback's
protected residual through its actual remaining plan suffix.

`plan_template` constructs a source segment for the materialized plan and proves
an exact equation for its recursive checker. For any continuation store, checking
the template returns the exported ordered callback row if all retirement owners
are available and distinct; otherwise it fails. Retirement owners must be absent
from the receiving suffix's owner names, so their phase changes cannot alter its
interpretations. This separation remains an explicit premise. It needs the
name-history and closing-admission join, not just uniqueness of currently owned
tickets.

The proof is structural over releases, retirements and callback invocations.
Releases retain builtin interpretation only at the corresponding plan position.
Callback requirements are protected and interpreted through the remaining plan
before the receiving suffix. Retirements consume their named owner and pass the
resulting map to the rest. No template-store lookup participates in this plan
check. Consequently unrelated, missing or changed continuation records cannot
alter its result. `plan_checked` connects the equation to the structural
recursive checking judgment.

`captured_template` joins actual plan construction, retained source contents,
callback rows and the materialized source template. Its retirement list is a
permutation of the captured ticket owners. A successful plan also derives that
the capture contains no protected running completion. These facts do not replace
the abandoned pending-use check: disposal must still prove that dropping ordinary
frames loses no outside scheduled continuation consumption.

`materialized_transition` derives the owner transition for a complete materialized
plan followed by its caller. Its initial map comes from that actual stack, and
retiring the plan's owners leaves exactly the caller's owner map.
`materialized_configuration` combines the plan's check with the caller's source
and check to construct a complete checked configuration starting with unit.
The collected store is the surviving caller's store; the plan's retired captures
need no retained resume records. This is a construction of the materialized
state, not yet preservation of every cleanup transition from it.

`disposal_check` authenticates an invocation entry from the actual plan and its
rows. Consuming the selected live owner removes its boundary from interpretation;
the same template then checks in the physical caller context. Its demand is the
selected owner followed by the actual retirement list. This is component evidence
for a disposal entry, not a complete source-checked live boundary containing both
resume and disposal entries.

The examples use a callback that reads cell 4, then release that cell and retire
a nested owner. The materialized configuration checks with an empty continuation
store. A disposal invocation consumes outer owner 23 and schedules the check of
nested retirement 19. Reversing cell release and callback invocation exports a
protected read of the missing cell, which an empty outside context rejects.
A structurally typed duplicate-retirement plan fails the recursive checker for
every store. These examples distinguish checking obligations from executable
plan order; footprint membership coverage does not permit exchanging callbacks
and releases.

The collected closing records below authenticate these entries against live
captures and their actual retirement demands, and derive the abandoned-use check.
The remaining disposal join must connect the other contract fields to handler
admission. Recursive consumption below preserves the richer checking judgment
through raw disposal. Cleanup and value-state
completion are covered by the following construction.
Handler admission, source entry, allocation history, full resource/access
invariants and whole-program progress/preservation remain unfinished. Core
correspondence remains a status assessment, and later continuation capabilities
remain excluded.

## Recursive cleanup and value completion

[RecursiveCompletion.lean](RecursiveCompletion.lean) proves progress and
preservation of the recursive source check for every value-state transition.
`value_pending` derives that the current value contributes no owner demand or
immediate effect, leaving the exact check of its pending segment. The proof then
follows the actual stack constructors; it requires no separate progress or
successor-check premise.

Starting an armed callback moves its protected effect obligations into the
current application, under the running-cleanup barrier. Finishing the callback
restores the saved value and scope. Finishing a closing guard, leaving a handler
or cell, leaving a spent clause, and plugging into a plain frame preserve the
same remaining demand and footprint. Retirement removes exactly the leading
ticket from the demand and consumes it in the actual owner map.

`value_step_preserves` covers every raw step from a checked value, preserving the
output type and footprint and accounting for the ticket-completion events.
`value_progress` derives either an empty terminal stack or an actual raw step.
In particular, the recursive check rules out returning directly through a live,
unconsumed continuation. For running-cleanup, closing and retirement frames,
source typing forces the current value to be unit. `value_preserves` combines
these results into a checked successor with the corresponding owner transition.

The example starts from a materialized closing plan with a callback and nested
ticket retirement, above a closing guard and a spent outer continuation. Six
actual steps start the callback, reduce its application, complete cleanup,
retire the nested ticket, finish the closing guard and return to the empty
caller. Each successor has a complete recursive source check. The initial state
comes from the plan-materialization theorem; the example does not establish its
entry from a source disposal expression.

This proves preservation of the recursive check, not the full resource/access
or allocation-history invariants. In particular, leaving a cell retains the
historical source world; resource lifetime safety still needs the corresponding
support invariant. The collected closing records below extend the checking store;
preserving that richer check, the combined usage invariant, handler/resource admission and whole-program
progress/preservation remain open. Core correspondence remains a status
assessment; multishot, escape and suspension remain excluded.

## Collected closing records

[RecursiveRecords.lean](RecursiveRecords.lean) collects disposal records from
actual live captures, including dormant nested captures. It uses the existing
expression and stack calculus. The added judgments describe checking evidence,
not additional computation syntax or a conversion between computation models.

`RecursiveClosing.PlanTemplate` has structural rules for empty plans, resource
release, ticket retirement and callback invocation. A callback contributes its
source-derived protected footprint at its actual remaining plan suffix. The
existing plan-source and exact-evaluation theorems now follow from these rules.
Changing the materialization scope preserves the template because that scope
does not change the plan's interpretation context.

`Records` follows the retained stack. A live capture contributes a disposal entry
when `makePlan` succeeds and its pending continuation uses belong to that
capture's live tickets. The latter condition is the existing structural
`InternalUses` judgment; its proved Boolean check supplies the collection rule.
The record derives from the plan and recursively collects saved and caller
records. Failed plan construction or an outside pending continuation use omits
the capture's own disposal entry, while still collecting nested records.
`collect` constructs this judgment from every existing source segment.
Each entry is certified against its actual capture location and executable plan.
Its demand is the plan's actual retirement list; it is not copied from the
contract's declared closing demand.

The combined store appends these records to the existing resume records.
`combined_unique` proves unique keys from unique owned tickets: resume and
disposal share an owner but use different modes. `capture_records` retains the
old closing records and adds only the new owner's disposal entry when both checks pass,
including under contract-registry extension. `resume_records` recomposes the
saved and waiting records and proves that the result is a permutation of the
original closing store with the consumed owner's entries removed. These are
structural record-transport results; they do not yet preserve the complete
recursive check for the richer store.

`checked_discard_step` connects a checked disposal invocation to the active
runtime capture. Unique ownership identifies that capture with the record's
certified location. The actual lookup derives equality between the declared
demand and the plan's retirement list, supplies the plan-body check after owner
consumption, and constructs the raw disposal step. It derives the structural
abandoned-use condition as well. It does not take successful `makePlan`,
`InternalUses` or an authenticated whole successor as extra premises.

`CheckedState` combines the existing structural expression/segment derivation,
the collected closing records, actual owner uniqueness, the recursive check of
the combined store and outside acceptance. `existing_state` embeds every state
that passed the previous resume-store-only judgment; adding records preserves
all successful old lookups. `discard_progress` derives a raw disposal step from
every discard expression checked by this richer judgment. This is admission of
a current experimental state, not complete initial-source admission.
`discard_internal` separately derives `InternalUses` for every actual raw
disposal cut, including cuts other than the one constructed by progress. The
full retained-usage invariant still needs to be joined to execution.

Examples check resume and disposal for the same inner owner using one store,
disposal of an outer owner whose plan retires the inner owner, and a complete
`CheckedState` for that disposal expression. An incorrect empty closing demand
is rejected against the actual nested-retirement record. Structural resumption
preserves the nested closing record while removing the outer owner's record;
that example does not assert that the outer resume expression itself is admitted.
A negative example has a successful raw closing plan but a pending use of outside
owner 29. Its structural internal-use check fails and collection omits its
disposal record, demonstrating why plan construction alone does not admit disposal.

Recursive consumption below preserves `CheckedState` through resumption and
disposal. The other transition families remain to be joined to this richer
judgment. The combined usage invariant, allocation history, full
resource/access invariants, handler/resource source admission and whole-program
progress/preservation also remain open. Core correspondence remains a status
assessment. Multishot, escape and suspension are excluded.

## Recursive state preservation through consumption

[RecursiveConsumption.lean](RecursiveConsumption.lean) proves progress and
preservation of the richer `CheckedState` for ready resumption and disposal.
The state contains both authenticated record modes. The proofs cover every
actual raw step of those expressions; they do not assume a checked successor.

For resumption, `resume_segments` splits the actual saved and waiting source
segments and recomposes their records. The consumed owner's resume and disposal
entries are removed together; the resulting combined store is a permutation of
the original store with those entries deleted. The saved body checks at the
physical waiting caller after consumption, and the caller checks after the saved
demand. Recomposition preserves the exact footprint and output type, using the
actual successor's owner map. The expression, cut, raw-step and progress
theorems lift this result to `CheckedState` at arbitrary stack depth.

For disposal, `discard_segments` authenticates the selected closing template
against the actual raw cut and derives the declared retirement demand from that
template. The template contains explicit retirements and no continuation
invocations, so its evaluation is independent of the template store. Adding
the closing guard also preserves checking: callback demands are already
protected, and the intervening plan contains only builtin providers and
barriers. These two transfer results require no extra caller-name-separation
premise.

The surviving caller's check follows after the selected owner and the planned
nested retirements are consumed. At that phase, lookup cannot observe any
discarded capture record. The proof therefore removes those records and keeps
only the caller's resume and disposal records. The plan and caller then form a
complete source segment and recursive check for the actual materialized
successor. The successor still owns the tickets scheduled for later retirement;
the disposal step itself consumes exactly the selected owner. The corresponding
cut, raw-step and progress theorems preserve the exact remaining demand and
footprint, rather than merely an upper bound.

The mixed example has an outer saved continuation containing a pending bind
whose body disposes its nested continuation. Both record modes for both owners
are collected. The saved requirement invokes the nested disposal template, and
the actual outer resume produces a checked successor with that disposal still
pending. This example proves the resume step; the recursive execution construction
below completes the intervening bind, nested disposal and return. A separate
disposal example uses the preceding module's admitted outer disposal and proves its actual
successor with the nested retirement plan installed.

These are preservation/progress results for the two consuming forms. The
recursive execution construction below transfers ordinary expression and value
transitions to `CheckedState`. Builtin-provider and fresh-capture
transitions still require transfer. Handler/resource source admission,
the combined usage/resource/access and allocation-history invariants, and the
whole-program theorem remain unfinished. Fresh closing identities still need
the name-history check. Core correspondence remains a status assessment, with
no alignment changes; multishot, escape and suspension remain excluded.

a raw successor unless the stack is empty. An available live owner cannot be

rejects that state. Cell return here retains the historical source world;

The mixed example now executes seven actual steps: resume the outer owner,

The ownership bridge reuses `checked_sequence_parts`, `checked_trace`, phase

When entry phases come from the actual owned tickets, `checked_demand_owned`

It uses the demand permutation to transfer the already checked waiting tail to
