actual resume and disposal records, closing-plan construction, operand
substitution and recomposition from the existing capture theorem. The older
phase-indexed clause theorem now reuses this preparation through its established
compiler. Its statement and existing examples remain checked.

`capture_from_recursive_clause` uses the same preparation with the recursive
source judgment. Its conclusion supplies an actual capture step, a combined
successor `CheckedState`, ownership permutation, footprint inclusion and exact
new-owner registry equation. It derives ownership balance from the clause's
source provenance and actual check. A disposal invocation check follows when
the actual closing row exports through the surviving caller as declared.

The `ResourceClauseExamples.capture_preserved` witness begins with a checked
request under an existing handler frame. The selected clause is
`resource 8 (integer 17) (discard 1)`. The recursive resource rule checks its
opened body, and the generated actual disposal invocation supplies its check.
Capture derives the resource-clause successor with exactly the fresh owner's
remaining demand. The handler remains in the saved continuation, matching the
existing deep-handler execution rule. This example exercises a resource body
that uses its enclosing continuation; the older stable-body clause rule cannot
supply that body.

This connection does not derive complete handler admission. The requesting
state still supplies the existing handler frame and table. The general capture
theorem requires the selected clause's recursive source and actual check,
consumption of the fresh owner, and its footprint bound. Handler admission must
derive those premises and the actual closing-effect obligation. Source handler
installation and the combined initial-source theorem remain open.

## Fresh handler registration and entry

[RecursiveHandlerTables.lean](RecursiveHandlerTables.lean) connects handler
registration to the existing recursive source forest and activation history.
`context_congr` and `segment_congr` preserve source requirements and collected
resume records when table assignments agree at every retained activation name.
They use the existing `Control.activations` traversal, which includes dormant
captures as well as the active caller. The current expression and its requirement
template remain unchanged.

Executable closing plans contain resource releases, callback invocations and
owner retirements. Their frame prefixes contain no handler interpretation.
`closing_context_congr`, `template_congr` and `records_congr` therefore retain
the same actual disposal templates under a handler-table registry change.
`checked_state_congr` combines these facts: the original recursive evaluation,
ownership uniqueness and accepted footprint are reused exactly.

`register` assigns a table at one activation name. `register_preserves` proves
that registration at a name absent from the retained activation traversal keeps
the existing combined `CheckedState`. `history_support` obtains that absence
from the established lifetime invariant's count bounds, and
`registration_from_history` reuses the fresh-name theorem to select a name outside
the complete history. This covers retired activations as well as retained ones.

The `registration_retains_dormant_capture` example reuses the preceding
resource-clause capture. Registering activation 74 preserves the state containing
the dormant handler at activation 73. The `dormant_interpretation_changes`
counterexample explains the stronger agreement boundary: replacing activation
73's table leaves the active owner-phase context equal, but changes an operation's
residual under the saved handler from an empty successful row to rejection.
Active-context equality alone cannot authenticate retained source.

Activation names distinguish runtime handler occurrences. A fixed handler table
has the same residual action at every activation name. `checked_activation`
transfers a recursive check from one handler label to another at a selected
context position. It reuses ordinary-frame owner selection and induction on the
existing `Checked` derivation, including each authenticated invocation body.
This permits a source checking label to be replaced by a fresh runtime activation.

`handler_entry` constructs an actual entry step and its combined successor from
explicit local premises: the recursive body source, scope and clause port typing,
operation coverage, unique clause keys, actual pending and closing source,
ownership uniqueness, the ordered body check under the supplied table, the
waiting-tail check and its accepted footprint. It chooses an activation outside
history, derives the frame's answer annotation and ticket barrier using existing
port lemmas, registers its table and retains both old continuation stores. The
body check is transferred to that actual activation and the waiting source is
recomposed around the new handler frame. Entry preserves the exact owned-ticket
list.

`install_resource_clause_handler` now starts from the complete initial handler
expression in the shared source judgment, using the connection below. It reuses
the resource/disposal clause's port derivation and constructs the actual installed
requesting state. Declaration admission must still justify the supplied table
and derive selected-clause checks, completion, footprint bounds and actual
closing effects. The combined initial-source theorem remains open.

## Shared handler expressions and ordered resource discharge

`SourceTemplates.Expression.handler` checks a handler's body with the handled
instance added to its residual effects. Its clause port derivation, operation
coverage, unique clause keys and residual-effect inclusion use the existing
port rules. The supplied operation table is placed before the receiving context
by the existing `Requirements.prepend` operation. A canonical checking label is
replaced by a fresh runtime activation at entry. The source and runtime continue
to use the existing `Code.handle` expression and one sequencing form.

The new source case reuses port projection, world weakening and contract
extension. Closed substitution uses the existing clause-substitution theorem
and preserves operation keys. Handler expressions enter directly, so they add
no focus-context constructor. The existing `calls_prepend` and
`retirements_prepend` lemmas preserve source ownership provenance. The analogous
invocation projection retains each declared owner, mode and demand. The complete
checked-state ownership-balance and recursive clause-capture proofs therefore
continue to apply.

`RecursiveHandlerTables.handler_preserves` starts from a combined `CheckedState`
whose current expression is a handler. Inverting that source rule and the
existing recursive check supplies the body check under the local interpretation,
the waiting-tail check and the clause ports. The established `handler_entry`
construction then supplies a fresh registered handler, the actual raw step and
the combined checked successor with the same demand and footprint. No successor
check is assumed.

Resource discharge now accounts for source interpretations that precede the
builtin. `ResourceRequirements.Hides.requestThrough` and `emitThrough` first
residualize the nearer ordinary interpretation layers, then remove the local
cell's demands from the resulting row. `export_hidden_after_interpretation`
reuses ordered residual composition and builtin discharge to prove the exact
checking equality. Invocation discharge retains its entire nearer context;
sequencing, branches and owner demands retain their established structure.

The `nearer_handler_exports_local` regression has a source handler translate a
cell-7 request into a user-effect request. Correct discharge retains the user
request; prematurely erasing the cell request produces an empty row. The
`nearer_handler_introduces_local` regression checks the other direction: a source
handler emits a cell-7 request, which the following builtin discharges. These
examples distinguish the interpretation orders directly.

`initial_handler_checked` admits a complete handler expression at an empty
stack. Its installation example now uses `handler_preserves` rather than
constructing local entry premises separately. In
[RecursiveEntries.lean](RecursiveEntries.lean), `ResourceHandlerExamples` wraps
that handler in a resource expression. Its source derivation uses ordered
discharge, and a two-step raw trace enters the fresh resource and installs the
handler inside it. Both successor checks are derived by the existing entry
proofs.

These results cover the shared computational handler rule. Handler table rows
are still supplied annotations, and the stable callable-summary judgment still has
no handler constructor. Complete source admission must cover handler-bearing
callable bodies and justify the table and clause premises. Resource-dependent
invocation contexts must also satisfy the structural discharge relation; no
unrestricted prefix-commutation rule is assumed. Full initial-source safety
remains unproved.

## Declaration capabilities and table modes

The computational handler rule in [SourceTemplates.lean](SourceTemplates.lean)
now requires `ClausesUse policy arms`, the existing structural judgment for
exact continuation consumption on every clause path. Port typing, effect rows
and continuation usage remain separate checks. A clause that simply returns
unit can have the right result port but fails this usage requirement.

[RecursiveClauseUsage.lean](RecursiveClauseUsage.lean) connects that existing
usage evidence to the recursive ownership check. It reuses
`selected_clause_usage` and `consuming_use_retains_ticket`: a clause that consumes
its lexical continuation must retain that ticket in its dependency analysis.
Induction on the shared source derivation locates the corresponding direct
invocation, including inside resource bodies. Induction on the existing
requirements locates its owner in the demand list. The existing checked trace
then establishes the consumed phase. Neither induction enumerates capture
shapes or introduces a new execution relation.

`declared_clause_completed` supplies the completion premise of the existing
recursive capture theorem. `capture_from_handler_usage` reuses that theorem's
allocation, actual resume and disposal stores, recomposition, and exact
ownership permutation. The selected clause's source derivation, actual effect
check and footprint bound remain inputs; usage alone cannot establish them.

`ClauseModes` structurally pairs each clause with its operation-table entry.
If the clause's existing `requiredActions` analysis includes disposal, the entry
must advertise disposal. This is a conservative bound: advertising disposal for
a resume-only clause remains permitted, though it can reject protected captures
that a more precise table would admit. Ordinary port types and outward effect
rows do not grant continuation actions.

The existing action-substitution and instantiation lemmas prove transport of
`ClauseModes`. Selection yields the actual entry's bound, so
`selected_clause_permissions` can recheck the selected continuation with resume
permission and exactly the table's disposal permission. This reuses the existing
usage repermission lemma; nested clauses retain their own policy. If a protected
capture passes `modeCheck`, `protected_clause_resume_only` derives usage with
resume-only rights. Excess permission in the original binder policy cannot
conceal a disposing clause behind a resume-only table entry.

Handler installation now returns both clause usage and mode evidence for the
actual registered handler. The capture theorem connects them to the table entry
selected by the recursive request check. `ignored_clause_rejected` and
`concealed_disposal_rejected` cover missing completion and an understated disposal
flag; `conservative_resume_mode_allowed` checks that safe overapproximation is
retained.

`specialized_schema_modes` derives this same structural check for tables
produced by the existing parametric clause compiler. Its table entries already
carry the policy's disposal flag; the existing usage-to-required-actions lemma
supplies the bound. The result holds for every specialization of resume and
disposal rows. It requires independent clause usage even when both schema
offers are unavailable, since an unavailable offer alone supplies no usage
derivation. No new table compiler is introduced.

These results close the declaration-to-completion and declaration-to-mode
connections. The table's effect rows, actual clause checks and closing effects,
handler-bearing callable bodies, and preservation of one combined invariant
from the initial source remain unfinished.

## Outward summaries before caller interpretation

[RecursiveOutward.lean](RecursiveOutward.lean) derives an outward row from the
shared source judgment when its enclosing continuation scope is `none`. This
includes computational handlers and scoped resource bodies. It does not yet add
handler-bearing bodies to the stable callable-summary judgment.

`Outward` follows the existing recursive requirements: requests beneath ordinary
interpretation layers, sequencing, emitted requests and branch alternatives.
It has no continuation invocation, retirement or owner-phase test constructor.
`Ordinary` gives structural inversion of the same cases; its equivalence to
existence of an `Outward` derivation avoids assuming a new admission condition.
Source induction derives these cases, and the existing resource discharge
relation transports them through fresh resource bodies.

The `evaluation` theorem factors the existing recursive checker into two
ordered stages. First, the expression's own interpretation layers compute its
outward row. Second, the actual caller's current phase projection interprets
that row. The proof reuses residual composition, distribution over row append,
ordinary-layer projection and the existing recursive evaluator equations. It
permits neither exchanging handlers nor reusing a row already interpreted by
another caller.

The derived demand list is empty, so this checking stage preserves every
pre-existing continuation owner's phase and does not inspect the continuation
store. These are properties of the source requirements, not a claim that
execution allocates no local captures or resources. Local handlers still use
their supplied clause effect rows, whose declaration justification remains
unfinished.

`checked_source_summary` extracts a present outward row from a successful source
check. Under any other store, receiving context and phase map, checking the same
requirements is equivalent to interpreting that row in the new caller. The
isolated interpretation proves uniqueness of the row. A missing outward row
records failure inside a local interpretation; it is distinct from a present
empty row and cannot be repaired by a different caller.

`checked_from_bound` reuses `UniformClauseBounds.residual_coverage`. If the actual
outward row is covered by an advertised bound and the caller successfully
interprets that bound, the actual requirements check with a covered residual
row. This provides the row-transport prerequisite for callable effect contracts
without inventing another clause compiler.

The examples check both distinctions. A local handler translates a user-91
request into a user-92 request; one caller handles the resulting request and
another retains it. A nearer exact handler missing the requested operation
fails even when an outer handler could otherwise accept it. These are checks of
the recursive interpretation account. The callable connection below uses this
account for source bodies and substitution. Table-row justification and the
combined initial-source safety theorem remain open.

## Shared callable source bodies

`SourceTemplates.Expression.lambda` retains its body in the same recursive
source judgment as a computational handler or resource expression. The body is
checked without an enclosing continuation binding. Its function annotation
contains an outward row justified by `RecursiveOutward.Outward`; the existing
factorization determines how the caller interprets that row.

[CallableSources.lean](CallableSources.lean) generalizes the ordinary summary
component by retaining this full body evidence at a lambda. The other summary
rules retain the existing row equations. `Expression.callable` embeds that
checking derivation with its canonical request certificate. This introduces no
runtime syntax, computation model, conversion operation or sequencing operator.
The operational terms and steps remain `ScopedExpressions.Code` and the existing
scoped execution relation.

The full expression and its callable component form a nested inductive
judgment. Resource-body summaries use that component as well. The shared value
evidence retains function bodies through pairs and pending argument positions.
Port typing, resource-world weakening and owner-contract extension now transport
the full body derivation. No capability to retain an enclosing continuation in
a function value is introduced.

[SourceCallableTransport.lean](SourceCallableTransport.lean) proves environment
agreement and closed-value transport using existing dependency and fresh-resource
bounds. It derives the existing usage judgment for a source without an enclosing
continuation; local handler clauses retain their declared usage checks. It also
transports allowed effect sets and extracts a lambda's typed body and outward
certificate.

[SourceCallableSubstitution.lean](SourceCallableSubstitution.lean) proves closed
substitution for both source judgments. The resulting expression retains exactly
the original owner demand and requirement certificate. The proof reuses binder
shadowing and commutation, port and clause substitution, resource instantiation,
mode preservation and value transport. Mutual recursion decreases term size;
moving from the full source derivation to its ordinary summary at the same term
size decreases a second finite index. This is a proof measure, not an execution
or termination claim.

[SourceCallableExamples.lean](SourceCallableExamples.lean) checks a function
containing a handler, rejection by the old stable summary, and substitution of
that function into an application previously typed by the stable variable rule.
Function-application, bind and branch preservation reuse the shared substitution
proof. Context decomposition, capture and collected consumption retain the same
callable evidence. The existing clause compiler and allocation construction are
reused before applying shared closed substitution.

Cleanup callbacks and saved values now retain the full callable evidence in
`SourceTemplates.Frame`. [SourceClosingRows.lean](SourceClosingRows.lean) carries
that evidence into closing-plan contents and rows, with the existing plan order,
retirement rules and callback-residual equation. Its transport from the earlier
stable row judgment preserves earlier examples. Closing templates and collected
records now carry the same continuation policy as their source expressions;
world and contract transport retain each callback body.

Cleanup installation, invocation, completion, resource entry and request progress
have passed the grouped checks with these interfaces. The request mode proof
uses the existing admitted request row and handler-cut contract lookup; it no
longer requires an old stable summary of a handler-bearing payload.
[SourceCleanupExamples.lean](SourceCleanupExamples.lean) derives an initial
checked cleanup whose callback contains a handler. The existing installation,
invocation and beta-preservation theorems construct three actual steps and a
checked handler body under the running cleanup frame. The same callback has a
closing-plan row. This example does not claim selected-clause admission or a
complete cleanup run.

The full integration check passes: 177 modules and 4,396 theorem-dependency
reports, including these callable and cleanup interfaces. Dependencies remain
limited to the standard Lean axioms listed in the verification account. This
checkpoint does not establish the remaining initial-source safety theorem.

## Recursive effect bounds

[RecursiveBounds.lean](RecursiveBounds.lean) extends the existing ordinary
row-coverage theorem through the recursive requirement checker. Its `Bounds`
judgment follows the requirement constructors. Literal request rows may grow;
owner demands, invocation keys, resume/disposal modes, interpretation positions,
retirement entries and spent-owner tests remain exact. `StoreBounds` follows the
finite record list, preserving lookup order and each template's demand.

`fuel_below` reuses ordinary residual coverage and append coverage. Induction on
the existing evaluator's fuel handles saved-body lookup; structural induction
handles sequencing, alternatives and emitted requests. Fuel decreases only at
an invocation. `checked_below` uses the existing evaluator soundness and
completeness theorems to derive the actual `Checked` judgment and an exported-row
bound. `admitted_below` then reuses footprint coverage to derive acceptance.
The nested-record example retains consumption of owners 19 and 29 while its
actual inner body requires fewer effects than the bound.

`RecursiveClauseUsage.capture_from_handler_usage` now uses this connection. It
takes the clause's source derivation, structural bounds for its requirements and
records, and a checked upper certificate. The theorem derives the actual clause
check, its effect bound and the existing capture successor. Independent
clause-usage checking still supplies completion. `bounds_invocations` proves that
effect bounds preserve directly named continuations, modes and demands;
`bounds_cannot_change_mode` rejects changing resume to disposal.

`RecursivePlanAdmission.captured_bounded` derives an actual closing export and
its bound by reusing ordinary residual coverage and the established retirement
check. `captured_bound_admitted` derives outside acceptance from an admitted
upper row. These results cover the actual ordered plan and its surviving caller.

The bounds do not yet derive handler declarations' upper certificates. The
chosen-template allocation connection below now removes the separate actual
closing-export premise from the bounded handler capture path.

## Chosen closing templates

`RecursiveDisposalCapture.source_closing_template` derives a plan template from
the retained source and the actual handler cut. This happens before selecting a
new continuation's closing-row annotation.
`RecursiveRecords.capture_records_with_template` inserts that exact template;
`RecursiveAllocation.capture_record_with_closing` transports the chosen records
through the fresh contract extension. The existing allocation theorem reuses
this factored proof, and `capture_record_with_template` retains the selected
closing requirement in its result.

`closing_invocation_from_record` reuses the existing retirement, phase transport
and template evaluation proofs with an explicit lookup of the chosen record.
`prepare_capture_with_template` uses that lookup instead of collecting another
template witness. `prepare_capture_bounded_closing` first computes the actual
closing export from an admitted upper bound, then allocates the contract with
that row and constructs both invocation checks. Disposal no longer requires a
caller-supplied actual export on this path.

`RecursiveClauseUsage.capture_from_bounded_handler` joins this construction to
independent clause usage and recursive effect bounds. It derives the actual
closing row and actual clause check, then reuses the capture successor and
ownership-balance proofs. The clause's source and upper certificate are still
inputs; they must come from declaration admission in the complete theorem.

The existing nested-disposal example now takes this path. Its closing template
contains retirement of owner 19. The computed row becomes the new owner 23's
closing annotation, and the existing capture, disposal and completed execution
proofs remain checked. This is a runtime-state example, not a complete initial
source-admission theorem.

The full integration check passes: 177 modules and 4,396 theorem-dependency
reports, including recursive bounds and chosen-template allocation. Dependencies
remain limited to the standard Lean axioms listed in the verification account.
The declaration and combined initial-source obligations below remain open.

## Clause declaration source families

[SourceClauseDeclarations.lean](SourceClauseDeclarations.lean) uses the existing
`SourceTemplates.Expression` judgment for clause bodies. A declaration supplies
a family of those derivations for fresh continuation contracts with its declared
full input, answer and effect types. Capture-specific demands and rows remain
abstract; the existing capture ownership theorem supplies the demand balance.
This family does not assume a checked successor or a whole-capture safety
predicate.

`selected_family` follows the runtime clause selection and the matching offered
mode. `instantiate` specializes the family to a fresh contract, and
`instantiate_payload` reuses shared closed substitution to bind the operation
payload. Existing source transport proves that body families, mode offers and
clause lists survive resource-world growth and contract extension. Closed
substitution now preserves the families, respecting clause-parameter shadowing;
dependency agreement transports them between environments. Both connections
reuse the established shared source proofs. They preserve the declared full
answer type. Equal erased ports do not suffice:
the example proves that two function types can have equal ports and different
latent operation footprints.

The positive example returns a function containing a handler after resumption.
Its declaration supports both ordinary and protected capture modes. This checks
the source-typing component only: `SourceOffer` does not certify its annotated
footprint. Declaration-derived upper certificates and retention throughout
executable saved code remain open. The hereditary transport below strengthens
this source evidence to retain declarations inside clause and function bodies.

## Retained declarations and selected allocation

[SourceClauseCapture.lean](SourceClauseCapture.lean) connects the source families
to actual retained handler frames and fresh allocation. `DeclaredSegment`
attaches full clause source declarations to the full value types at handler
frames, including handlers in dormant captured segments. Its structural basis,
`RecursiveCapture.AnnotatedSegment`, erases to the existing segment judgment.
It introduces no execution rules or additional expression syntax.

`declared_handler_entry` now installs a handler with its full declaration on
the new frame. The factored `RecursiveHandlerTables.handler_entry_with_frame`
returns the constructed frame and its exact effect identity; the previous
entry theorem erases that additional evidence. Table agreement transports
declarations in active and dormant segments, and fresh registration preserves
them. The example installs a handler whose answer is a function with a handler
in its body. Entry still takes the declaration as a premise; executable source
typing must supply and preserve it.

The capture splitter now preserves these frame annotations in both the captured
segment and the surviving tail. It also retains the selected handler's full
answer annotation and the previous exact demand, record and effect
decomposition. The previous unannotated splitting theorem uses the strengthened
theorem with trivial annotations.

`RecursiveAllocation.allocate_split_with_frames` allocates from that chosen
split. This permits clause selection to determine the full answer and effect
annotations before allocation. The previous allocation interfaces call the
factored proof and erase the additional evidence.

`SourceClauseCapture.allocate_selected_clause` selects the available clause
source family, allocates with its declared effect annotations, derives
resume/disposal demand balance through
`RecursiveDisposalCapture.captured_segment_balance`, and specializes the family
to the actual fresh contract. It retains the chosen closing record, saved and
tail requirement checks, exact decomposition and unique ownership. Declaration
evidence survives contract extension throughout the new boundary.

The regression reuses the integer-to-Boolean capture example. Its policy permits
disposal while its handler advertises a resume-only bound. This exposed an
unnecessary equality between policy permission and advertised disposal in the
initial source-only declaration rule. That equality is removed: source typing
does not establish the capability bound. The existing independent usage and
mode judgments must still check it.

This connection derives the full clause source from retained declarations;
it does not yet derive the clause's upper effect certificate or prove preservation
of declarations in executable code. Closing-row admission remains a separate
input to this source-typing allocation theorem. The existing bounded closing
and clause checking results supply the next connection.

`SourceClauseCapture.capture_with_upper_certificate` now joins the retained
declaration path to bounded closing and clause checking. It computes the offered
request row and closing row through the surviving interpretations, obtains the
full clause derivation from the declaration, and authenticates both invocation
checks from the retained resume and closing templates. Given a structural upper
store/requirement certificate, it derives the actual clause check, performs
payload substitution, constructs the runtime capture step and checked successor,
and proves ownership permutation and effect containment. Existing clause-use
checking supplies completion; it is not an assumed final phase.

The concrete `declared_capture_steps` example constructs its certificate from
the authenticated resume check. `resume_value_certificate` reuses the existing
value-evaluation and empty-demand theorems for the operand. The example reaches
the actual capture step and successor typing without a supplied whole-clause
check.

The general theorem still requires an upper certificate. It covers the path
with a constructed closing plan and internal captured uses. It does not prove
general declaration-derived bounds or preserve declarations in executable code.
These remain part of full admission. In particular, the existing counterexample in
[SourceReinterpretation.lean](SourceReinterpretation.lean) rules out replacing
the retained requirements with their cached exported row when interpretations
change.

`allocate_selected_without_disposal` covers either structural reason a captured
segment cannot be disposed: `makePlan` returns `none`, or its abandoned code
fails `InternalUses`. It reuses the same annotated splitter and allocation proof
and retains the existing nested and caller records. The new contract has no
closing row, and allocation creates no disposal record. Its unused closing
demand is set equal to the actual resume demand; this permits the existing
parametric source family to instantiate without asserting a closing plan.

`unavailable_disposal_rejected` reuses exact record certification and selected
capture uniqueness. A hypothetical checked disposal would supply both a plan
and an internal-use proof for that capture, contradicting its unavailability.
The result holds for any proposed disposal demand and nearer interpretation
context. `capture_without_disposal_with_upper_certificate` combines this
rejection and the authenticated resume check with declaration-derived typing
and the existing bounded successor proof.

The `guarded_capture_steps` example places a running cleanup callback between
the operation and its handler. Its source is typed, its pending requirements
check, and the segment is protected with no closing plan. Capture derives a
checked resume clause and rejects disposal. `guarded_capture_then_resume` then
applies the existing `RecursiveConsumption.resume_preserves` theorem to take a
checked resumption step. This covers the running-cleanup case without imposing
disposal availability on one-shot resumption.

The full integration check passes 177 modules and 4,396 exact theorem-dependency
reports, with only the standard Lean axioms. It includes declaration-derived
capture with or without disposal, declaration transport, the hereditary source
judgment and source-derived handler entry below. A targeted group of nine
modules and 143 exact reports passed before this integration checkpoint.

## Hereditary source declarations

[DeclaredSources.lean](DeclaredSources.lean) strengthens the existing expression
judgment so that handler declarations remain present recursively in clause,
callable and resource bodies. It uses the same `ScopedExpressions.Code`, full
value types, owner demands and recursive requirements. `expression_erase`
preserves all those indices and recovers `SourceTemplates.Expression`; no
execution rule or sequencing syntax changes.

An available clause offer carries a body derivation for each fresh captured
contract with its declared input, answer, effects and protection mode. Its body
uses the stronger judgment too, and retains a local row certificate at the
same requirement index. Its header records the captured owner and contract,
the declaration's disposal mode and advertised row. Selecting a clause therefore
retains both nested declarations and its row certificate. `selected_body` follows the actual clause selection and offered
mode. `handler_parts` extracts the full declaration from a typed executable
handler. `lambda_body` retains it when exposing a function body.

The current experimental offer rule also connects used continuation effects to
the declaring handler's residual row. If the body requires resumption,
`resumeEffects = allowed`; if it requires disposal, `closeEffects = allowed`.
Here `allowed` is the residual row shared with the caller by the structural
handler judgment. The guards use the body's independently inferred
`requiredActions`, so an unused bound remains unconstrained. These equations
are source-admission rules, not claims that closing preserves every requested
interpretation. The [capture interface proof](#source-derived-capture-interfaces)
uses them at the actual cut.

Contracts are indices in this mutual judgment because a clause family extends
them with a fresh owner. Lean does not permit that varying contract index in
the nested parameter of the existing generic callable summary. The indexed
`Callable` representation has proved conversions to and from that same generic
summary with hereditary bodies. `Callable.erase` then reuses
`CallableSources.map_body`. This representation detail adds no callable rule.

[DeclaredSourceEntry.lean](DeclaredSourceEntry.lean) uses `handler_parts` to
supply the declaration at actual handler entry. `HandlerSegment` retains these
hereditary declarations on handler frames, including dormant captures. Table
transport uses the factored
`RecursiveHandlerTables.annotated_segment_congr`; the older declaration layer
now uses that proof too. Entry reuses `handler_entry_with_frame` and returns the
actual step, checked successor, exact ownership equality, stronger current body
and installed handler declaration. The executable example derives these from
the typed handler expression and its current requirement check.

The examples also type a clause that resumes and returns a function containing
another handler. These results establish recursive declaration retention in
the source rules and handler installation. `HandlerSegment` still uses `SourceTemplates.Frame` for
non-handler frame expressions. The later indexed frame layer below retains
hereditary source for those expressions too. Clause-row certificates are now
required by the stronger source offer; closing-cut compatibility remains a
separate obligation.

## Hereditary transport and substitution

[DeclaredSourceTransport.lean](DeclaredSourceTransport.lean) preserves the

family case uses the factored `extension_fresh` and `insert_extension` arguments
from the preceding declaration proof. Callable transport reuses the existing
generic summary lemmas through the proved conversions.

[DeclaredSourceValues.lean](DeclaredSourceValues.lean) reuses hereditary

`request_callable` recovers a callable summary from an expression with a bare

[DeclaredSourceSubstitution.lean](DeclaredSourceSubstitution.lean) proves

reuses the expression theorem and `request_callable`, so it does not need a
second recursive substitution proof. Body, offer and declaration projections
reuse that result. Legacy summaries pass through the existing callable forms,
allowing a replacement function to contain a handler.

`selected_payload` follows exact clause selection and binds the operation
payload under the fresh contract. It retains the hereditary body at the
contract's full answer type. The examples substitute a handler-bearing function
into an application and into a clause that resumes before returning that
function; another checks clause-parameter shadowing.

`beta_body` reuses lambda-body extraction, closed substitution and allowed-effect
widening. `beta_source` joins it to the existing `RawStep.beta` rule, which enters
the function body with continuation scope `none` and leaves the stack unchanged.
The resulting source derivation retains its declarations and outward
certificate. This is not yet a whole-state preservation theorem. Retained
handler segments also survive resource-world growth and contract extension by
the existing annotated-segment transport proofs.

The subsequent frame and execution connection is described below. Exact
closing-template evidence and capture allocation are supplied there.
Source-derived closing-cut compatibility and the combined initial-source theorem
remain open.

The targeted group passes twelve affected modules and 192 exact
theorem-dependency reports, including 49 new reports since the last full
checkpoint. Only the standard Lean axioms occur. The 180-module script includes
these additions; a new full run is deferred to the next integration checkpoint.

## Hereditary frames and execution

[DeclaredSourceFrames.lean](DeclaredSourceFrames.lean) retains hereditary source
in all eleven waiting-context forms and seven execution-frame kinds. Handler
frames retain full declarations, continuation-use evidence and advertised modes; armed and running cleanup frames retain
callback evidence, and running frames retain their saved value. The same full
input/output values, owner demand and recursive requirement index each frame.

`RecursiveCapture.AnnotatedSegment` now indexes its frame predicate by the
exact demand and requirement too. Its existing erasure, capture splitter and
allocation proofs retain the annotation in active and dormant segments.
World, contract and table transport reuse those generic proofs.

[DeclaredSourceContexts.lean](DeclaredSourceContexts.lean) proves focus
decomposition and context recomposition with hereditary evidence. Callable
decomposition reuses `CallableContexts.focus_decompose` with hereditary bodies;
requirement evaluation reuses the established sequence, choice and export
laws. [DeclaredSourceExpressions.lean](DeclaredSourceExpressions.lean) connects
closed substitution to bind, beta and branch reduction. Beta follows the
existing scope reset to `none`.

[DeclaredSourceStates.lean](DeclaredSourceStates.lean) pairs hereditary current
source and pending segments with collected closing records, ownership
uniqueness and the actual finite requirement check. The subsequent batch below
strengthens the records to retain hereditary callback evidence too. Exact erasure
recovers `RecursiveRecords.CheckedState`. Local progress reuses that erasure;
preservation retains the stronger source through ordinary reductions, context
steps, cleanup start/return, handler/cell/clause return, closing completion and
owner retirement. It preserves the existing demand, row and ownership
relations for those transitions.

[DeclaredSourceEntries.lean](DeclaredSourceEntries.lean) derives handler,
cleanup and resource installation from the stronger current source. Handler
registration preserves all existing frame declarations. Resource freshness
uses the existing finite-check opening proof.
[DeclaredSourceCells.lean](DeclaredSourceCells.lean) retains the stronger
segments through builtin read/write transitions and reuses record and ownership
transport.

[AnnotatedRecomposition.lean](AnnotatedRecomposition.lean) lifts segment append
and live-boundary replacement to the indexed frame predicate. The evaluation,
normalization and record permutation lemmas remain the established ones.
[DeclaredSourceResumption.lean](DeclaredSourceResumption.lean) uses these results
to restore the saved capture with its hereditary evidence. Both record modes
for the consumed owner are removed, the actual waiting caller determines the
receiving interpretation stack, and the existing one-shot phase trace supplies
ownership preservation.

These local results do not yet establish a preserved initial-source invariant.
The following connection strengthens closing records and capture. The selected
declaration now supplies its clause-row certificate; closing-cut compatibility
remains a separate obligation.

## Hereditary closing records and capture

[DeclaredSourceClosing.lean](DeclaredSourceClosing.lean) constructs closing
plans from hereditary saved-frame evidence. `PlanTemplate` follows the existing
release, retirement and callback constructors. Its callback retains the full
callable type, including the latent row used in that exact recursive
requirement. `template_erase` recovers the existing template at the same raw row
and requirement index. `template_source` retains that evidence in the actual
closing-control stack.

The collected `Records` judgment follows the existing live, spent, unavailable
and closable cases. Erasure preserves the exact store. Collection derives the
template from the saved source; it does not choose an unrelated callback type
and assume it matches an existing check. Scope, world, contract and table
transport preserve the retained evidence. Splitting and resumption retain the
same record permutations, reusing existing ownership and lookup lemmas.

`DeclaredSourceStates.CheckedState` now uses these stronger records. Its prior
ordinary, value, installation, cell and resumption results pass with the exact
erasure to `RecursiveRecords.CheckedState`.
[DeclaredSourceDisposal.lean](DeclaredSourceDisposal.lean) authenticates the
selected stored template, composes its closing-control segment with the waiting
caller, and proves the actual disposal successor. Record removal, protected
callback interpretation and the one-shot ownership trace reuse the established
proofs. Hereditary callback bodies survive disposal and their subsequent
execution.

`checked_disposal_plan` factors out the authenticated template selection already
used by recomposition. `current_disposal_plan` obtains that evidence from the
checked current discard: the actual plan, its exact hereditary template, and
its checked residual in the surviving caller. The residual is contained in the
current state's row and accepted by its outside context. Neither theorem adds
an induction or assumes a successor configuration.

`checked_disposal_template` now reuses the existing structural disposal checker
to construct an executable plan and a hereditary callback template from the
captured source. The result retains `Discardable`, internal pending uses,
retirement accounting and the absence of protected completion. It reuses the
checked-plan equivalence and erasure theorem; it does not reprove the closing
algorithm. This connection has targeted verification after the full checkpoint
below. It does not yet prove that every source request passes the checker, or
derive the closing row's bound from the captured requirement tree.

[DeclaredSourceAllocation.lean](DeclaredSourceAllocation.lean) chooses the
hereditary clause family before allocating the fresh contract. The existing
`allocate_split_with_frames` supplies the exact contract, saved and tail checks,
and ownership uniqueness. The retained closing records are extended under
that same contract; the indexed frame evidence is reindexed under the proved
extension. Available disposal uses a chosen hereditary template. Unavailable
disposal retains the structural unclosable or external-use witness and leaves
its closing row absent.

[DeclaredSourceCapture.lean](DeclaredSourceCapture.lean) joins both allocations
to payload substitution and actual capture. The successor retains hereditary
current source, saved frames and closing records. Existing clause completion
and balance proofs derive the owner-demand permutation. Allocation also retains
the selected body's exact row certificate. `capture_from_declaration` and
`capture_without_disposal_from_declaration` instantiate it using authenticated
continuation invocations; neither assumes an independently supplied whole-clause
upper certificate.

The closing path still requires a constructed plan with internal pending uses,
an admitted closing-template bound and containment of the actual closing row
in the captured resume row. The path without disposal requires the offered
disposal mode to be false. These are concrete remaining cut obligations, not
consequences claimed from expression typing alone. In particular, closing
removes source handlers, so its effect budget and interpretation must be checked
at the actual closing positions.

[DeclaredSourceAdmissionGap.lean](DeclaredSourceAdmissionGap.lean) distinguishes
the source-only offer from the stronger declaration rule. Its clause performs
an operation and then resumes exactly once. Hereditary body typing and linear
use hold, and the earlier `SourceClauseDeclarations.SourceOffer` permits an
empty advertisement. The actual requirement check produces a nonempty row.
`empty_upper_impossible` rules out an empty upper certificate for the original
requirement tree, including structurally bounding stores.

`every_body_check_contains_effect` reuses request evaluation to show that every
checked source derivation of this same clause includes the operation. It does
not require uniqueness of source annotations. `empty_admitted_offer_rejected`
then proves that the strengthened `DeclaredSources.Offer` rejects the false
advertisement for every possible requirement witness. The conditional capture
proofs remain valid; this closes their former clause-row evidence gap, while
leaving the closing-cut conditions stated above.

## Contextual clause-row certificates

[ContextualClauseChecks.lean](ContextualClauseChecks.lean) opens the existing
recursive requirement checker into a finite derivation with explicit
continuation-invocation assumptions. Each assumption retains its owner, mode,
demand, complete ordered receiving context, phase map and result row. Literal
requests still require successful interpretation. Sequencing checks its second
operand after consuming the first operand's demand; it introduces no second
computation syntax or bind operation.

`close` substitutes authenticated invocation checks into that derivation.
`open_checked` supplies the converse, so this representation has exactly the
existing checker's meaning. `relocate` moves a context prefix into requirements
without changing any invocation's complete context. It proves reassociation,
not exchange of interpretations or reinterpretation of a cached row.

The owner-membership proof uses induction on the requirement derivation and
the existing branch-demand permutation. It shows that an owner-free derivation
has no invocation assumptions. Existing outward factorization then supplies
such derivations for work before and after a resumption, including local
handlers and resources. The suffix retains the phase map after the invocation.
The row-containment lemma does not reorder runtime actions.

[ClauseRowContracts.lean](ClauseRowContracts.lean) defines the local invocation
interface and row schema used by `DeclaredSources.Body`. The interface supplies
an authenticated resume check. When the clause permits disposal, it also
supplies an authenticated closing check, disposal availability and containment
of closing effects in the exported operation advertisement plus the resumption
row. This combined budget is the same bound used by the clause-row conclusion;
disposal need not fit within resumption alone. `Interface.of_resume` constructs
the complete interface from a resume check when disposal is forbidden, regardless
of unused closing metadata. `ClosingBudgetGap.resume_only_unused_closing` checks
this separation with an actual stored closing row that exceeds the empty budget.
Syntax-level permission and use checking remain separate. Each schema instance
is a finite contextual derivation for the exact source requirement tree, bounded
by the exported advertisement and resume row.

[ClauseRowAdmission.lean](ClauseRowAdmission.lean) exposes that same hereditary
body judgment; it no longer wraps a weaker independently chosen source. Its
instantiation theorem returns source and checking at the same requirement
index. Existing exact-requirement transport and substitution retain the schema
through executable bodies, nested declarations, callable bodies, resource
bodies, saved frames and closing callbacks. Immediate resumption, resumption
followed by a value, and disposal have constructed schema proofs. The disposal
proof uses the interface's explicit availability and closing-effect bound.

This is not complete initial-source admission. At a new capture, the retained
schema must be instantiated with an interface justified by the actual cut.
The current capture theorems derive its invocation checks but still expose the
closing-cut conditions described above. They do not assume that those
conditions hold for every source-typed request.

## Protected closing interpretations and nested budgets

[ProtectedClosingRows.lean](ProtectedClosingRows.lean) connects the existing
structural request-preservation check to the callback's protected effect row.
If the original and closing controls select the same target for every request,
and the captured and outside activation names are distinct, both interpretations
produce the same row. The proof retains the actual common outside handler
tables. It does not equate two different handlers merely because their activation
numbers match. Builtin discharge and owner phases reuse the existing residual
and projection laws; a live boundary may already have been consumed.

`checked_callback_residual` checks the exact callback footprint.
`checked_action_residual` uses the existing action metadata check when its
declared requests cover that footprint. That coverage is an explicit premise,
not a theorem of the current full source judgment. `checked_action_export`
recovers the exact closing export from the callback's normal requirement check;
`checked_armed_budget` places it within the surrounding sequence's budget.

[NestedClosingBudgets.lean](NestedClosingBudgets.lean) reuses the existing open
invocation derivations and stored-record authentication. Each listed call's
effect row and complete owner demand are contained in the enclosing derivation's
row and demand. Expanding a call uses its selected stored body at the exact
receiving context and phase after consuming its owner. Its nested calls inherit
both bounds. This is structural proof decomposition, not execution or handler
reordering.

The existing `RecursiveDisposalCapture` lemmas show that source expressions
have no generated retirement requirements and account for retirements in saved
frames. A successful closing plan excludes those frames.
`captured_invocation_partition` reuses these facts to
partition its checked demand into invocation demands without duplicate owners.
The proof selects one branch alternative for owner accounting; both branches'
effects remain in the checked budget, and runtime branch selection is unchanged.
`invocation_body_smaller` reuses one-shot uniqueness and the standard list-length
bound to prove a strict decrease at each nested invocation edge. These results
provide a finite induction measure and prevent assuming that a saved live
boundary executes merely because it occurs in the stack.
`captured_owned_partition` then reuses `captured_segment_balance` to identify
the partition with every owner of the captured region, including dormant
captures. Its structural internal-use and entry-availability premises remain
explicit; it does not derive disposal permission from ownership alone.

For resumption, `selected_resumption` recovers the hereditary captured segment
at the selected record's exact requirement index. For disposal,
`selected_disposal` recovers the hereditary closing template actually checked
by that invocation, together with its captured location, executable plan and
internal-use evidence. Both results bound the selected check by the enclosing
budget. They avoid assuming that independently typed templates for the same
callback syntax use identical annotations.

These two modules pass a grouped targeted check with 30 exact dependency
reports, using only standard Lean axioms. They are registered in `check.sh`;
that batch brought the inventory to 198 modules and 4,612 reports. Its full checkpoint remained
196 modules and 4,581 reports. The remaining construction must connect all
callbacks of the new closing plan to these authenticated checks and establish
their interpretation and budget obligations. The local results do not prove
that every source-typed request admits disposal.

## Closing and resumption budgets can differ

[ClosingBudgetGap.lean](ClosingBudgetGap.lean) checks a nested one-shot
continuation whose saved callback requests an effect. Normal resumption runs
that callback beneath an inner handler with an empty advertisement. Closing
abandons that handler and runs the callback under a surviving outside handler
with a nonempty advertisement. Both handlers have hereditary source declarations;
the outside declaration conservatively advertises more effects than its pure
resume clause requires.

The example retains source typing for the captured and surviving segments,
distinct activation names, a successful structural disposal check and a source
closing template. Its normal requirement check exports an empty row while its
closing check exports a nonempty row. `complete_records` uses the existing
hereditary record collector to supply all disposal records as well. Thus these
premises do not imply that closing effects are contained in normal resumption
effects. This is a counterexample to that proposed bound, not a complete initial
source program with an unsafe execution or a Core correspondence failure.

The structural disposal check preserves the callback's original physical
selection during closing. Normal execution can instead resume a nested owner
at another receiving context. `ProtectedClosingRows` compares matching physical
contexts and remains valid; it does not identify those two execution contexts.
No new ownership induction repairs an invalid effect-containment implication.

The local `ClauseRowAdmission.Interface` therefore uses the already advertised
operation row plus the saved resumption row as the closing budget. Its disposal
schema and capture theorem reuse the existing invocation, row-composition and
ownership proofs. Capture still explicitly requires the actual closing row to
fit that combined budget. The correction removes an unnecessary restriction;
it does not prove the remaining source-wide capture admission obligation.
`combined_interface` checks both actual invocations with an empty resume row
and a nonempty closing row. `discard_with_advertised_budget` applies the
existing disposal schema to that interface and its covering advertisement.
That row check supplies no syntax-level permission to dispose.

The budget correction and regression pass the affected group of 22 modules
and 240 exact reports. Together with the successful integration-run prefix,
verification covers all 199 registered modules and 4,629 reports, using only
standard Lean axioms. At this batched checkpoint, the preceding clean single
full run covered 196 modules and 4,581 reports.

## Request capture from one checked source state

[DeclaredSourceRequests.lean](DeclaredSourceRequests.lean) joins actual request
selection to the hereditary capture proofs. `request_operand` uses constructor
inversion and the existing value-row and empty-demand lemmas to retain the
payload's full callable evidence. `request_parts` then derives the operand type,
closed value, exact selected clause, capability judgment, table offer, mode check
and exported request row from one `DeclaredSourceStates.CheckedState` and its
actual `HandlerCut`. It reuses request evaluation, cut residualization, source
segment decomposition and operation coverage. These inputs are no longer
independently supplied to the capture join.

`capture_from_checked_request` applies the established declaration-derived
capture theorem. Its successor retains hereditary source and closing records,
the full output type and an accepted effect row contained in the original row.
The successor's demand is a permutation of the fresh owner followed by the
original demand; its physical owned-ticket list has exactly that fresh owner
prepended. No new capture or ownership induction is introduced.

`capture_from_checked_disposal` additionally uses the existing structural
closing checker and source-template construction. A successful disposal check
supplies the actual executable plan, callback source typing, interpretation and
access compatibility, internal-use evidence and retirement ownership accounting.
The remaining local premises check that plan's outward effects and their
containment in the exported advertisement plus the actual resumption row.
The result does not derive these two effect checks from ordinary source typing.

The unavailable-disposal path uses the same request decomposition.
`capture_without_disposal_from_checked_request` requires a selected offer that
denies disposal and either failed raw plan construction or a pending use of an
outside owner. It constructs the preserved successor with no closing row.
For protected captures, `capture_protected_request` derives both the failed plan
and the selected offer's denial from the existing exact protection classification
and the checked request's mode evidence. `capture_unclosable_request` uses the
same classification in the reverse direction. Thus every checked value request
at a protected handler cut has this preserved capture step at a fresh owner;
no separate closing or mode certificate is needed for that case.

This does not assert that every unprotected source cut is admitted. Cuts with
outside-owner obligations still need the appropriate handler restriction;
other unprotected cuts still need callback compatibility and their closing
effect budget. These are the unresolved cases of source-wide capture admission,
followed by the combined initial-source finite-execution theorem.

The seven new theorems pass a targeted module check with only standard Lean
axioms. The registered inventory is 200 modules and 4,636 reports; the preceding
batched integration covered 199 modules and 4,629 reports. No existing proof
module changed in this addition.

## Capture-sensitive outside-owner checking

[CaptureOwnerChecks.lean](CaptureOwnerChecks.lean) connects the existing finite
internal-use checker to the selected operation's disposal capability.
`checkSelected` looks up that operation in the actual handler table. Resumption
passes this owner check; an offer permitting disposal requires every pending
ticket use to belong to the recursively owned captured region. Protection,
callback compatibility and the closing-effect budget remain separate checks.
A missing operation entry fails the check.

`selected_external_iff` reuses `OpenOwnerUses.external_empty_iff_internal`:
under the existing structural usage and owner-separation premises, the new
check is exactly the requirement that a disposing offer have no external owner
demand. `selected_denies_external` reuses the established outside-use obstruction
to show that a passing offer must deny disposal when such a demand exists.
`capture_outside_request` then applies the already proved hereditary capture
path, preserving the full result type, checked source and closing records,
effect bound and exact fresh-owner accounting.

The composition law checks each segment's pending uses against the live owners
of their combined capture. It reuses the existing inclusion/`InternalUses`
bridge; only the two structural append projections need a new induction.
This does not exchange runtime frames or handler interpretations. It explains
why marking every frame with an outside use as permanently nondisposable would
be too restrictive: a larger cut can include the owner itself.

The examples reuse `OpenOwnerUses`' pending resume of owner `9`. Two actual
handler cuts in the same expanded stack leave that owner outside the smaller
capture and include it in the larger one. Both captures have the same pending
use list. The smaller cut rejects the disposal capability; the larger cut passes
this ownership check. Resumption passes at the smaller cut as well. These
examples establish the ownership check only, not the other disposal premises.

`effect_check_does_not_check_owners` also verifies that the ordinary effect and
protection check accepts the request at the smaller cut while its ownership
check rejects disposal. The new check therefore cannot be inferred from that
row check. It has not been silently added as a theorem of
`DeclaredSourceStates.CheckedState`.

Current [Core capture inference](../../../../spec/static-semantics.md#effects)
already distinguishes stored values from latent requests and follows requests
through caller continuations, retaining control summaries for functions and
aliases. The new theorem covers a concrete selected cut. Deriving and preserving
its finite owner check from initial source summaries remains unproved, as do
the remaining callback and closing-budget obligations. This is informative
calculus evidence; no Core implementation or specification changed.

The module passes 14 exact theorem-dependency reports with only standard Lean
axioms. The registered inventory is 201 modules and 4,650 reports. This addition
uses targeted verification and changes no existing proof module.

## Ordered owner-use summaries

[OwnerUseContexts.lean](OwnerUseContexts.lean) adds owner and pending-use
information to the existing ordered interpretation context. These are analysis
data for the same direct calculus. A live boundary records its owner and dormant
capture's pending work without activating the dormant handlers.

`select_projection` and `select_target` establish that the richer context
preserves the existing nearest-exact target and protection mode. `scoped_cut`
reuses the established handler-cut erasure and protection result to identify
the selected capture's exact owner and pending-use lists. `scoped_selected_check`
then equates the summary query with the existing finite check on that capture.
`capture_outside_from_summary` applies the previous hereditary capture theorem
to this evidence; it does not repeat its ownership-preservation proof.

`source_focus_summary` reuses `DeclaredSourceStates.focus_preserves`. The source
evaluation context and scope translation determine the newly pushed frame's
pending-use entry, alongside the same raw step and preserved checked source.
This avoids an independently supplied frame annotation. It covers the existing
focus forms, but does not establish the summary obligations of future function
calls or new captures.

The new inductions concern the added summary representation and its projections.
The existing proofs supply target selection, actual cuts, hereditary capture
and source focusing. All 11 dependency reports pass with standard Lean axioms
only. This additive targeted check brings the registered inventory to
202 modules and 4,661 reports. Complete initial-source admission and its combined
progress and preservation theorem remain unproved.

## Source grouping is lost by flattening

[ScopedRequirementShapes.lean](ScopedRequirementShapes.lean) retains scope
grouping in analysis data indexed by the existing `RecursiveRequirements` tree.
Its effect evaluator is the existing evaluator at that index.
`scope_evaluation` reuses `evaluate_prepend`; `checked_phase_trace` reuses
`evaluate_sound` and `checked_trace`. These results introduce no second
computation syntax or effect semantics.

`Shape` retains sequencing, choices, requests, continuation references, explicit
source interpretation scopes and the existing structural resource-discharge
evidence. `Describes` relates those shapes to source constructors and retains
the typing evidence of existing summary leaves. `source_shape` derives a shape
and that structural relation from `SourceTemplates.Expression`. The hereditary
source judgment can use its existing erasure to supply this premise. The new
induction constructs analysis data; it does not repeat the established
ownership or execution-preservation proofs.

Request sites record the receiving owner-use context. A sequence places the
second computation's pending demand outside the initializer's own scopes.
A scope enclosing the sequence instead places that pending demand inside its
interpretation. Pending demand is an analysis summary, not a general equality
with a runtime frame's direct pending-use list; their connection still uses
the structural usage interface.

The two examples represent these different source nestings:

```text
bind (handle request H) (handle (resume k) H)
handle (bind request (resume k)) H
```

Their full flattened requirements are definitionally equal: distributed
`prepend` records the same handler context on the request and on the subsequent
resume. The existing requirement checker accepts both. Nevertheless, their
first request sites differ. In the first, the selected handler lies before the
pending resume, so capture leaves that work outside. In the second, capture
includes the pending resume while leaving its owner outside. The first passes
the selected disposal offer's owner check; the second fails it.

`separate_describes` and `shared_describes` connect the shapes to concrete
`Code` terms. `swapped_grouping_rejected` prevents pairing either term with the
other grouping. `runtime_contexts`, `separate_cut` and `shared_cut` connect the
site contexts to actual stacks and handler cuts. `actual_capture_checks` then
reuses the previous summary/cut equality. These are source-structure and
capture-check examples, not fully admitted initial-program executions.

`no_flat_owner_classifier` proves that no function of the old requirement tree
alone can return both required ownership decisions. Thus this missing connection
requires retained source information; another proof about the unchanged
flattened index cannot recover it.

The current extraction retains existing callable summary leaves. It does not
expand their latent bodies or prove their future captures safe. Recorded
invocation sites refer to continuation templates and still require expansion
with their source evidence. Preservation of these qualified summaries, callback
compatibility and the combined closing budget remain source-admission work.

All 17 dependency reports pass with standard Lean axioms only. This additive
targeted check brings the registered inventory to 203 modules and 4,678 reports.
No existing proof module changed, and this was not a new full-suite run.

## Callable grouping and selected clause tables

[CallableSourceShapes.lean](CallableSourceShapes.lean) uses the existing
parameterized callable judgment. Its body judgment retains hereditary source
typing, a grouped requirement shape, and the structural `Describes` evidence
for that body. `enrich` and `erase` reuse `CallableSources.map_body` and the
existing generic-callable conversions. No new callable rules or callable
induction are introduced.

`body_substitution` and `callable_substitution` reuse hereditary closed
substitution and derive the resulting code's grouping at the same requirement
or row index. They do not claim that the shape is unchanged by substitution.
`lambda_shape` exposes the retained body and its existing outward certificate.
`application_shape` uses the actual closed argument, existing beta-body
substitution and outward factorization to expose the instantiated body. Its
effect evaluation agrees with the latent row under every ordered caller
context and owner phase. `checked_application_shape` consumes that established
effect result using the old checker.

The example reuses `DeclaredSources.Examples`' function with a local handler
and an empty latent row. After argument instantiation, its source grouping
still begins with that handler, while its outward effect evaluation remains
empty. Thus empty exported effects do not erase the local structure needed
for subsequent capture analysis. This does not yet establish the owner and
closing checks for every capture inside the function or its clauses.

[OwnerOfferContexts.lean](OwnerOfferContexts.lean) retains each actual clause
table and its owner-use information in one ordered context. Its projections
recover the existing effect context and owner-use context of a runtime stack.
`selectedOffer` selects the nearest exact interpretation's operation entry;
`checkOwner` uses that selected capability. Missing operations cannot fall back
to a more distant handler. Builtin selection remains distinct from a missing
source offer.

`check_cut` reuses the established owner-use projection and exact-cut check.
The new induction only identifies the table at the actual cut. Source grouping
sites now carry this combined context, so their owner check takes no separately
chosen table. The updated grouping examples still agree with actual runtime
cuts. Another example shows that identical target and owner projections can
have different ownership permissions because their selected clause offers
differ; retaining the table is necessary.

The affected three-module group passes all 36 dependency reports: eight for
ordered offer/owner contexts, 17 for the updated source grouping, and 11 for
callable bodies. Registered inventory is 205 modules and 4,697 reports. This
was a targeted group check, not a new full-suite run.

Callable bodies are now exposed with their grouping and effect evidence, and
source sites select their actual offers. Source admission must still establish
and preserve the per-capture owner checks, callback compatibility and combined
closing budget, including captures reached through callable bodies and
continuation-template expansion. The final initial-source progress and
preservation theorem remains open.

## Locally closed prefixes and caller owner checks

[CallerOwnerChecks.lean](CallerOwnerChecks.lean) proves an ownership composition
result for outward requests. Suppose a callee prefix has a structural
`StackUsage` derivation with no outside owners, the caller has its existing
closed usage derivation, and their combined stack has unique ownership. If the
prefix does not interpret the requested effect, adding it leaves the caller's
selected owner check unchanged.

`closed_prefix_internal` reuses `OpenOwnerUses.pending_access` to derive internal
pending uses from the empty outside interface. `caller_pending_separate` uses
the caller capture's usage bound and unique ownership: a pending caller use
belongs to its own captured region or surviving tail, so it cannot refer to a
fresh owner in the callee prefix. `internal_prefix_neutral` then applies the
existing ordered composition law and inclusion lemmas. No captured-ownership
induction is repeated.

`prepend_cut` extends an actual caller cut through a prefix that does not
interpret the request. This structural cut extension is the only new induction.
`outward_owner_check` combines it with the previous exact-cut table/owner check
and the existing capture-usage decomposition. The result is an equality of the
executable selected-owner checks, for both disposal-capable and resumption-only
offers.

The example reuses an existing region with nested owned continuations and the
earlier caller obstruction involving owner `9`. Adding the locally closed

[DeclaredReturnAdmission.lean](DeclaredReturnAdmission.lean) connects the

`resource_entry` takes a checked source resource expression, the finite check

`value_access` derives the local access checks for a current value from the

evidence. The current release check is a conclusion, not a supplied premise.

support invariant.

The examples reuse the existing retaining-outer closure and retaining-own

`checked_source_return_gap` connects the rejected case to execution: the

plus initial return checking cannot replace it.

`checkBinding` compares an actual closed value's captured resources with the
support bound assigned to its variable. `check_binding_iff` identifies this

imposes no constraint; the resource body's independent template check must

`resource_substitution` preserves the hereditary source derivation at its

The alias example now completes three actual transitions: substitute resource 8

The entry regression identifies a separate annotation-selection obligation.

These are not equal units of effort. The classification below accounts for all
