## Closing requires interpretation agreement

[DeclaredClosingRouteGap.lean](DeclaredClosingRouteGap.lean) strengthens the
existing non-disposing source regression. `normal_connected` constructs the
normal effect interface for the armed callback and its two enclosing handlers.
`shared_source` uses that interface at the same allowed row as the current
source derivation. Thus merely sharing the current source annotation does not
exclude this example. `closing_effects_ready` also types its generated plan
with the callback's entire declared row.

Nevertheless, `no_open_closing` rejects every outward row. Before closing,
the callback's declared request resolves to a local handler inside the captured
segment. The plan removes that handler. The structural `OpenRequests` rules
can neither preserve its target nor treat the request as an outside request,
because the original local target exists. Constructor inversion proves this;
no new induction is needed. Plan uniqueness then gives `no_certificate` for
every owner record on this fixed capture.

This separates normal source/interface checking and closing effect typing
from closing interpretation agreement. Widening the outward row cannot repair
the fixed capture. The callback is pure with a conservative request annotation,
so the result does not rule out a compatible annotation chosen at source entry.
It also does not establish reachability from an admitted initial program or
failure of a disposing source clause: the selected clause only resumes.
Complete source admission must establish the structural closing obligation
when a selected clause can dispose. Neither this result nor the existing
resume-only capture proof imposes that obligation on clauses which cannot.

## Initial cleanup interpretation counterexample

[InitialCleanupRouteGap.lean](InitialCleanupRouteGap.lean) tests the closing
obligation with a concrete initial program. Its outer handler discards; its
inner handler resumes. The inner body registers a cleanup callback that
actually performs the inner effect, then performs the outer operation.

`source`, `checked`, and `initial_run` construct the hereditary source
derivation, its empty accepted footprint, and the full
`DeclaredConnectedSources.Run` at entry. `signature` includes the required
builtin cell signatures, and `result` checks the separate completion contract.
The callback's effect is an executed operation in its body, unlike the pure
callback with a conservative annotation in the preceding local example.

`entry_trace` gives the three raw handler/cleanup entry steps.
`selected_cut` identifies the actual outer capture. `disposal_selected`
checks its unprotected mode, disposing clause, and concrete closing plan.
That plan removes both handlers and retains the callback invocation.
Reusing the preceding closing argument, `no_open_closing` rules out every
outward effect row, and `no_certificate` rules out every owner record's closing
certificate for this capture. No new induction is used.

This is a counterexample to deriving the required closing certificate from
the current initial judgment along these raw entry steps. It does not yet
construct an entire named access-checked trace or refute raw progress. The
current source judgment needs a restriction or an interpretation-dependency
annotation before the intended closing guarantee can hold. Merely widening the
closing effect row cannot restore a removed handler. The following bounded
source-rule experiment distinguishes a disposing cut that removes a required
interpretation from a resuming cut or a cut that preserves it. Core and the
operational removal of source handlers are unchanged.

## Source cleanup dependency experiment

[SourceCleanupRoutes.lean](SourceCleanupRoutes.lean) adds a finite structural
route judgment for a diagnostic fragment of the existing `Code` syntax.
Handlers have literal resuming or discarding clauses. Cleanup callbacks contain
unit, literal requests, and sequential bindings. Their dependency lists are
extracted structurally from their bodies; no callback dependency list is
accepted on trust. The ordinary hereditary type judgment remains separate.

`select` stops at the nearest matching source handler and returns the captured
annotation prefix. `Closing` checks each cleanup against the handler suffix
that follows its own registration point in that prefix. A cleanup's effects
must not be interpreted by a source handler that closing removes. `Request`
requires this derivation only when the selected clause disposes. Neither rule
uses a future machine state or a successful runtime plan as a premise.
The finite checkers have soundness and completeness proofs for these structural
judgments.

Effect requirements use membership, not usage counts. `closing_membership_congr`
allows any replacement with the same members, and `closing_duplicate` removes
a repeated requirement. `repeated_effect_program` accepts two sequential uses
of the same effect in a cleanup. A set or multiset representation is therefore
adequate for these callback requirements. Interpretation scopes remain
ordered: `same_handler_multiset` shows that the rejected and accepted contexts
contain the same handler multiset, while `outside_copy_rejected` checks that an
outside handler for the same effect cannot replace the nearer removed one.
Explicit per-use names and counters are unnecessary for this fragment.

The three bounded tests are checked: `initial_program_rejected` rejects the
preceding complete initial-program counterexample; `surviving_program` accepts
the same cleanup with its required handler outside the disposing boundary;
`resuming_program` accepts the original arrangement when the outer clause only
resumes. These are route-analysis results, not a replacement type-safety theorem.

`Realizes` connects arbitrary finite sequences of handlers and resource-free
cleanup actions to the same actual stack and constructed closing plan.
`Realizes.open_closing` derives the existing `Admission.OpenCloses` judgment
for any outward effect row containing the callback requirements. It keeps the
caller abstract. `Realizes.certificate` reuses retained callback typing and
`ClosingRequirements.requirements_supply_plan` to construct the existing full
closing certificate, including pending-owner inclusion. `surviving_certificate`
constructs that certificate for the concrete accepted arrangement. Thus the
positive route check supplies the interface that the rejected example lacks.

Builtin providers and resource-bearing callbacks are handled by the following
extension. Dormant captures and hereditary callable/clause bodies remain
outside these fragments. The full source judgment
must retain these annotations through substitution and execution and tie
selection to the independently checked clause capabilities. The membership
test against all source handlers must not be copied unchanged into a resource
fragment: a nearer retained builtin provider can make a later source handler
irrelevant. Full capture/disposal preservation and initial-source progress
remain open.

## Resource cleanup dependency extension

[SourceResourceRoutes.lean](SourceResourceRoutes.lean) extends the structural
annotation to arbitrary finite sequences of source handlers, builtin cells,
and cleanup actions. `Route` follows the nearest interpretation: a matching
cell supplies a local builtin, a mismatching handler or cell is skipped, and
an unresolved request must belong to the outward effect row. There is no rule
that passes a matching source handler, since closing removes it. `Closing`
checks each callback's effect collection against its own remaining suffix.
The annotation still depends on membership, not counts of effect use.

`Realizes` aligns that annotation with an actual stack and constructs its plan.
Its `route` theorem supplies exact before/after lookup and the callback effect
bound together. Its `visible` theorem shows that materialization preserves the
accessible cell suffix. Consequently, `interfaces` reuses the existing
`Supported` judgment for callback resource access and existing
`PlanContentsTyped` evidence for callback types. It derives both `PlanTyped`
and `Admission.OpenCloses`; it does not assume successful closing. The existing
`plan_provided_resolves` theorem supplies the connection between retained
provider membership and physical lookup. `certificate` connects these results
to the established closing-certificate interface. No new ownership or callback
typing induction is introduced.

The tests reuse the existing cell-reading callback and its retained type from
`ScopedPorts.CompletionExamples`. `cell_closing_interfaces` closes that callback
using a cell in its plan suffix, without an outward effect or resource
requirement. `release_before_callback_rejected` excludes the reverse order.
`builtin_shadows_handler` accepts a nearer retained cell even when a source
handler for that instance appears later; `handler_shadows_builtin` rejects
the reverse selection. These distinguish the new route judgment from the
earlier handler-membership test.

This extension connects finite scope annotations to closing evidence. It does
not yet infer those annotations from arbitrary hereditary source bodies or
preserve them through capture and resumption. The following recursive
connection separates normal lookup from materialized closing lookup. Full
source integration, capture/disposal preservation, and initial-source progress
remain open.

## Recursive cleanup dependency connection

[SourceRecursiveRoutes.lean](SourceRecursiveRoutes.lean) handles arbitrary
finite nesting of saved continuations. Its `Shape` annotation includes plain
sequencing frames, handlers, cells, cleanup actions, live captures, and spent
boundaries. `normal` skips dormant providers; `closing` includes their retained
cells in disposal order. `Scope` relates each projection to the corresponding
actual control. It preserves actual handler activations while reusing the
preceding structural `Route` judgment for dependencies.

`Closing` carries both source scope projections. For each callback, its two
route derivations must identify the same builtin or both delegate to the
outward row. In the live rule, the saved branch receives the normal outside
suffix and its separately projected closing suffix; the active branch is
checked recursively as well. The rule does not flatten dormant cells into
normal lookup and has no future-execution premise.

`Realizes.interfaces` proves `PlanTyped` and `Admission.OpenCloses` together,
using the actual stack, its retained ordinary typing, and existing resource
support. It generalizes over both outside scopes. Closing may expose more
cells, so support transports by inclusion rather than by the flat fragment's
equality. The live case reuses `plan_typed_append` and `OpenCloses.live`.
`certificate` reaches the existing closing-certificate type with the separate
structural `InternalUses` premise. `owner_accounting` reuses
`raw_plan_accounting` through erasure: every owner in the same realized capture
is represented in its generated closing plan. There is no new ownership
induction.

The positive test reuses the existing nested cell-reading callback. It
constructs a certificate for invocation followed by continuation retirement
and cell release. The negative tests reject a removed source override and
reject silently changing an outward request to a builtin newly exposed by
closing. Both rejections hold for every outward effect row.

This discharges the recursive connection from structural scope annotations to
closing evidence. It does not establish that the full hereditary source
judgment produces those annotations or preserves them through substitution
and execution. The existing initial-program counterexample still applies to
that unchanged judgment. The next integration must retain the annotations at
the same source, clause, and captured-continuation indices; supplying an
unrelated closing witness at runtime would not close that gap. Complete
capture/disposal preservation and initial-source progress remain open.

## Hereditary source dependency annotations

[SourceDependencyAnnotations.lean](SourceDependencyAnnotations.lean) retains
cleanup dependencies in a structural source judgment over the existing `Code`.
A cleanup node keeps three distinct annotations: its callback's required
instances, the callback body, and the body that runs while cleanup is armed.
Function types retain their body's dependency annotation, and application uses
that same annotation. Bindings and operation signatures share the enriched
value types. Handlers retain both mode-specific clause families; resources
retain the existing family over fresh identities. These families are proof
annotations, not a completed executable inference algorithm.

The judgment has rules for all current calculus expression forms. It has no
flat-summary entry rule that can bypass annotation of nested cleanup or callable
bodies. `cleanup_dependencies`, `application_dependencies`, and
`lambda_dependencies` recover the exact corresponding source premises.
`cleanup_not_pure` and `lambda_cleanup_not_flat` reject dropping the cleanup
node, including beneath a function boundary. A higher-order example binds a
function containing cleanup and then calls it; its resulting annotation retains
both cleanup dependencies and the enclosed body's request.

`expression_erase` reuses the existing `DeclaredSources` judgment. It preserves
its complete ordinary value annotations, owner demand and recursive requirement
tree. The mutual proof also preserves clause-row certificates and whole offered
clause families, including every old continuation contract at the fixed input
and answer types. It does not rebuild the ownership or operational proofs.
Physical running protection and the existing continuation capabilities retain
their previous meanings.

This establishes source retention of the additional information, not source
admission. The annotations still need a structural capture check and preservation
through continuation allocation, resumption and disposal. Substitution and
ordinary bind/beta reduction are covered by the following connection. The
new source judgment alone still admits unsafe arrangements; the old initial
counterexample is not repaired merely by recording its dependencies. Connecting
this annotation layer to the preceding recursive closing judgment and the
combined execution invariant remains required before claiming initial-source
progress.

## Substitution with dependency annotations

[SourceDependencyTransport.lean](SourceDependencyTransport.lean) follows the
existing hereditary source transport proofs for the enriched value types.
Environment agreement, world growth, effect-bound weakening and continuation
registry extension preserve the dependency index exactly. The proof reuses
ordinary clause typing and resource-dependency bounds. Additional equality
lemmas concern the enriched values; erasing them would lose the distinction
that the source annotation is intended to retain.

[SourceDependencySubstitution.lean](SourceDependencySubstitution.lean) proves
closed substitution for every annotated expression rule and, in the same
mutual induction, both offered clause families and their bodies. It preserves
the result annotation, owner demand, requirement tree and dependency annotation.
The proof follows the existing substitution construction and reuses ordinary
clause substitution, usage, coverage and resource-instantiation lemmas. A
value's immediate checking nodes can be normalized without changing its latent
function annotation.

[SourceDependencyReduction.lean](SourceDependencyReduction.lean) connects this
to bind and beta reduction. The reduced expression retains the corresponding
body dependency annotation; only silent value prefixes disappear. Existing
value-demand and recursive evaluation lemmas prove that the old requirement
check remains equal for every store, receiving context and owner phase. The
higher-order example instantiates the actual `RawStep.bind` and `RawStep.beta`
rules: binding and then calling a function containing cleanup exposes the same
cleanup annotation, with source derivations for both intermediate expressions.

These results close the annotated substitution and ordinary bind/beta
connection. They do not establish preservation of a dependency checker, which
has not yet been defined for the full source layer. The local capture guard
below supplies its recursive scope test; deriving that guard at each source
capture, annotated continuation-store allocation and the disposal/resumption connection
remain necessary, followed by the combined initial-source progress proof.

## Local capture guards for dependency scopes

[SourceDependencyCapture.lean](SourceDependencyCapture.lean) defines a local
capture guard on ordered dependency scopes. These scopes retain pending code,
handler tables and both clause dependency families, armed callback annotations,
cells, running completion, and recursively saved continuations. The guard does
not traverse all pending code or establish its safety. It selects the nearest
matching interpretation, checks the selected mode's availability and physical
protection, and requires compatible recursive closing when disposal is allowed.
A missing operation on the nearest handler cannot fall through to an outside
copy. A matching builtin blocks source-handler selection.

`route_iff` and `check_closing_iff` prove soundness and completeness of executable
checks for the existing resource route and recursive `Closing` judgments.
Unresolved exported requests remain distinct from failed routes. Callback
requirements use membership; no effect-use counter is introduced. The checks
retain both normal and closing lookup, including cells exposed only by closing
a dormant continuation.

`check_capture_iff` equates the executable guard with the structural
`CaptureGuard` judgment. `disposing_capture` obtains the existing closing
judgment for the exact selected scope and outward bound. `capture_certificate`
then reuses the recursive certificate constructor at the same scope projection,
with explicit stack realization, ordinary typing, resource support and owner
inclusion premises. It introduces no new ownership induction and does not
assume a successful future execution.

`declaration_lookup_presence` ties annotation availability to the hereditary
source table's mode row. `selected_body` extends the established clause-selection
proof: it recovers the actual source body family, at the same dependency family
chosen by the guard, for every fresh continuation contract. The selected body
still needs its own capture guards checked. This is not an assumption that the
body executes safely.

The examples reject a removed callback handler for every outward row and accept
its surviving arrangement and repeated callback effects. Recursive cases accept
a dormant callback using a retained cell and reject a source override of that
cell. Running completion, missing-nearest-operation and builtin-blocking cases
check the independent selection and protection conditions.

The missing source connection is now explicit: derive and check these scopes
from the annotated computation and retained source frames, establish the guard
at every capture, and preserve the annotated continuation store through
resumption and disposal. The local guard is not a whole-program checker and
has not yet been joined to the complete initial-source progress proof.

## Dependency scopes and actual captures

[SourceDependencyScopes.lean](SourceDependencyScopes.lean) relates dependency
scopes to the same actual recursive execution stack. Each frame preserves its
runtime interpretation, callback requirements and physical protection. Handler
tables and clause dependency families are attached to that actual handler.
The relation does not authenticate the pending code or callback body annotation;
those remain obligations of the hereditary source layer. It does prevent
checking a different callback requirement list or interpretation arrangement.

`Realizes.cut` follows an actual `HandlerCut`. It derives both annotated segments,
their exact reconstruction, and the matching selection result for every operation.
`Realizes.held` equates the source scope's flag with physical running protection.
`capture_scope` retains the same recursively saved scope at a new live boundary;
`resume_recomposition` restores it before the waiting caller and spent boundary
in the order used by the existing resumption rule. These are scope-realization
results, not preservation of guard success under an arbitrary caller.

`Realizes.closing` constructs the existing recursive plan realization from an
unprotected scope and its actual stack. `checked_cut` combines it with the local
guard at that same cut. It derives a plan, physical absence of protected frames,
the closing-route judgment and exact recursive owner accounting. The accounting
reuses the existing raw-plan theorem. `checked_certificate` then constructs the
existing closing certificate from ordinary callback typing, resource support
and owner inclusion. A successful plan or separate captured-shape realization
is no longer a premise of this joined theorem.

The nested test uses the existing cell-reading callback and actual outer handler.
The derived plan invokes the callback, retires continuation `6`, and releases
cell `4`. A negative test rules out realizing that callback with an empty
requirement list. The tests exercise the generic cut and plan connection.

The retained-source connection below now constructs these scopes from actual
pending code and recursively saved source. Source computations must still
establish guard success at every capture and preserve it through clause entry,
resumption and disposal. Scope realization alone does not establish that a
source program satisfies those checks. The combined initial-source progress
theorem remains open.

## Retained source dependencies through capture and recomposition

[SourceDependencyFrames.lean](SourceDependencyFrames.lean) connects the richer
source annotations to actual pending frames and recursively saved continuations.
`Context` derives dependencies from the code waiting in each evaluation context.
`Frame` retains the actual callback source, handler declarations and clause
families. Adjacent `Segment` frames agree on enriched values, including the
latent dependency annotation of a function; equality of erased types alone
cannot connect them.

A live continuation retains its saved source derivation even when its clause
cannot resume. That derivation has an explicit historical effect boundary.
Only an offered resumption requires that boundary to fit the contract's resume
interface. `Segment.erase` recovers the existing shared source/effect segment
with identical owner demands and records. `Segment.realizes` derives the actual
dependency scope, including recursively saved branches. Neither erasure nor
realization asserts that arbitrary annotated source passes the capture guard.

`capture_segments` follows the actual handler cut. It preserves rich input and
answer types, source derivations on both sides, the exact scope reconstruction,
selected table and family, and the owner-demand and record split. Its evaluation
proof reuses the earlier capture equations. `segment_append` proves the converse
composition with the same intermediate rich value and ordered scope, using the
existing append and phase laws.

`capture_certificate` now takes the retained source segment and a successful
local guard at the actual cut. It derives the ordinary callback typing and scope
realization needed by the existing closing-certificate constructor. It returns
the source segments and a certificate whose plan accounts for exactly the
captured owners. Resource support and internal owner inclusion remain explicit
premises; a separately typed capture, chosen plan or scope witness is unnecessary.

`extract_live` recovers the same rich saved source independently of whether
resumption is offered. `replace_live` specializes it using the independently
permitted resume action and the saved effect-boundary inclusion. Extraction
also retains the exact front/tail scope split and realization of the actual
caller prefix. It replaces the selected live boundary with a spent
boundary through an arbitrary caller prefix, preserving the other captures.
The old record-permutation and consumed-phase transport lemmas prove its
accounting. Together with append, this supplies retained-source recomposition;
it does not establish preservation of capture-guard success under the caller.

The examples construct an actual pending application frame whose lambda contains
cleanup, reject assigning it a pure latent annotation, and check its source and
requirement evaluation through the generic append theorem. The module contributes
twenty-eight theorem-dependency reports, including source transport and action-independent
extraction. Targeted builds reuse unchanged dependencies.

Three integration obligations remain: make structural source checking establish
the local guard for all its requests, including selected clauses and continuation
invocations; preserve that check and the enriched source/store invariant through
allocation, resumption and disposal; then join the initial-source progress and
preservation theorem. The existing counterexample remains admitted by unchecked
annotations. These new retention proofs do not close that source-admission gap.

## Structural invocation checks and receiving callers

[SourceDependencyInvocations.lean](SourceDependencyInvocations.lean) supplies
structural lookup and scope transformations for continuation invocation.
`OwnerCut` walks the active spine to the selected live owner. Its miss rule
preserves a dormant captured branch without searching it. `find_owner_iff`
proves that executable lookup and this structural judgment agree.
`OwnerCut.reconstruct` recovers the exact caller prefix, saved scope and tail.

`ResumeChecked` requires this access path, the independently declared resume
permission and the owner's available phase. `check_resume_iff` establishes its
executable check. The result restores the captured scope before the caller
prefix and the spent owner boundary. `Realizes.find_owner` derives the matching
actual stack decomposition; `checked_resume_step` constructs the existing raw
resume transition and realizes the scope of its actual target.

`DisposeChecked` uses the same access and phase disciplines, the dispose
permission, absence of protected work and the existing structural closing-route
judgment. `check_dispose_iff` establishes its executable check. `Scope.forClosing`
drops abandoned expressions and source handlers, retains callback dependency
trees and cells, and schedules protected retirement markers for dormant owners.
`Realizes.forClosing` derives the existing plan and the annotations of its
actual scheduled callbacks. `checked_dispose_step` constructs the existing raw
disposal transition and reuses the established exact plan-owner accounting.
No separately supplied plan is needed.

After the existing `spend` operation marks an owner consumed, both checks reject
another invocation of that owner. This is continuation ownership checking;
ordinary effect requirements remain reusable membership permissions. The
checks do not replace lexical resolution, ordinary source typing or the full
runtime access invariant.

The examples distinguish dormant ownership from active access, expose the saved
owner after resuming its enclosing continuation, reject a spent owner and an
unpermitted action, preserve nested callback dependencies during closing, and
reject protected disposal and a removed callback handler.

A further scope-level example makes caller rechecking necessary. A saved cleanup
requiring `F` can initially perform `G` through a disposing `G` handler while its
`F` handler remains outside that capture. Resuming beneath an additional caller
`F` handler places that interpretation inside the later `G` capture. The resume
check succeeds, but the later capture guard rejects removing the callback's
selected interpretation. The example is an annotated-scope calculation, not an
initial-source program derivation.

These twenty-three theorem-dependency reports establish local invocation access,
scope correspondence and closing accounting. They do not establish that requests
in the restored source pass their guards at the new caller. The structural
source judgment below now expresses that contextual obligation and accounts for
consumption at invocation. Uniform clause-family checking and preservation
through all control transitions remain necessary for initial-source safety.

## Structural source checks and retained work

[SourceDependencyChecks.lean](SourceDependencyChecks.lean) defines two mutually
inductive judgments over dependency annotations and ordered scopes. `Local`
checks a computation's immediate dependency tree. `Pending` checks code and
callbacks retained by the current finite control forest, including dormant
captures with their original receiving tails. These judgments inspect present
source annotations; neither refers to future executions or a successful runtime
successor invariant. A request additionally checks the callback forest scheduled
by its selected disposing capture, under the surviving tail and running
protection. This premise uses the present owner phase, before fresh allocation.

Sequencing checks the initializer with its suffix retained in a plain frame,
and checks the suffix at its receiving scope. Branches check both alternatives.
Handler and resource entry install their interpretation before checking the
body; resource entry quantifies over fresh identities. Cleanup checks its body
under an armed frame and its callback under running protection. Handler clause
families remain attached to the frame; this rule does not yet validate each
family's body against every capture it may receive.

An invocation requires the independent access/capability check and `Pending`
for the projected restored or scheduled scope, with that owner marked consumed.
The projection below removes spent markers from source checking only.
This is stronger than the earlier invocation-access checks. It checks the saved
source at the receiving caller and checks scheduled callbacks under their actual
running context. It does not infer uniform clause correctness from permission
or from an ordinary effect row.

`Pending.append_iff` splits and joins the same retained source at an ordered
boundary. `Pending.capture` transfers it into a live capture without changing
its receiving scopes. Phase-map extension now follows from the transport proof
below; action-map extension and the complete current-source/ownership invariant
remain separate preservation obligations.

`substitution_preserves_local`, `bind_preserves_local` and `beta_preserves_local`
reuse the existing annotated substitution and reduction proofs. Silent prefixes
introduce no immediate checks, so their removal preserves the body's exact
check and requirement evaluation. `branch_preserves_local` retains the selected
branch's check and owner-demand permutation; the existing choice decomposition
supplies row inclusion.

`perform_guard` derives the capture guard from a checked source request at its
receiving scope. `capture_from_local` combines that derivation with the same
retained source segment and actual handler cut, producing the existing closing
certificate. A separate successful capture-guard premise is unnecessary.
Resource support and internal owner inclusion remain explicit inputs.

The higher-order example checks the actual function containing cleanup through
bind and beta reduction and rejects its unsafe caller order. The invocation
examples retain an explicit pending `G` request in the saved scope: the stronger
rule accepts its original caller and rejects the additional interleaved `F`
handler. Disposal accepts a callback whose handler supports running protection
and rejects one whose selected handler would cancel it. The invocation examples
are dependency-scope fixtures, not complete initial-source program derivations.

The module contains twenty-seven theorem-dependency reports. It establishes current
structural checking and several preservation connections, not the full source
proof system. The clause schemes below supply uniform checks for admitted
captures. Those schemes, the rich retained source, contextual source checks
and existing ownership checks must form one invariant preserved through
capture, invocation, entry and completion. Initial-source progress and
preservation then require the complete transition coverage. The older unchecked
source annotation judgment still admits the disposal counterexample.

## Projected source contexts and uniform clause schemes

[SourceDependencyProjection.lean](SourceDependencyProjection.lean) removes spent
markers from the dependency-checking scope. It retains pending code, ordered
handler tables and clause families, cells, cleanup bodies, running protection
and both branches of every live capture. This is a source-checking projection;
runtime stacks, owner history and consumed phases retain their existing meaning.

Structural inductions prove that projection preserves handler selection,
protection, closing routes and active owner lookup. Projection commutes with
append and closing-plan scope construction. Resume and disposal produce the
same projected result before or after projection, with the same permission and
phase map. These laws justify ignoring spent markers when comparing receiving
contexts. They do not permit invoking a consumed owner.

[SourceDependencySchemes.lean](SourceDependencySchemes.lean) defines `Checked`

`CaptureSource` specifies finite source obligations for a supplied capture and

`ClauseFamily` checks a dependency family uniformly over owner names, phase maps,
