when a new disposer takes over a builtin request. Its pending resume, live
owner, retained resource and effectful callback receive explicit structural
checks; the earlier target request theorem is not used as an input.

This closes the request-case assembly relative to those source checks and the
recursive callback transformer. The following structural judgment discharges
recursion by mutual induction when its constructor-level evidence is supplied.
Uniform derivation from general clause admission remains open.

#### Structural source adaptation and mutual compilation

[SourceScheduledHandlerAdaptation.lean](SourceScheduledHandlerAdaptation.lean)
replaces the recursive proof-transformer parameter with two mutually inductive
source judgments. `Adapt` relates checks of the same actual plan at two
receiving forests. `Retained` describes adaptation of actual stored code and
callbacks, with both receiving suffixes explicit. Context changes are still
established separately by `Insertion`, `Split` and authenticated cuts; an
adaptation derivation is source-checking evidence, not a runtime transition.

The local rules follow the plan constructors:

- Identical contexts reuse their existing check. Pure code and directly
  supplied operation capabilities use the existing primitive rules.
- Fresh request checking supplies the structural capture guard, pending-owner
  bound and actual callback checks. Retained requests instead carry an
  inductive adaptation of the old closing forest and waiting suffix, conditional
  on disposal permission. Their exact cuts and split reuse the old owner proof.
- Resume and disposal retain the selected owner, saved forest and independent
  permission checks. Their recursive `Retained` premise describes the actual
  recomposition at the spent-owner phase, including the running boundary for
  disposal.
- Sequence retains the second plan as the first plan's pending frame. Choice
  checks each arm. Handler entry preserves the actual declaration plans and
  checks their finite requirements at the new suffix. Cleanup checks body and
  callback separately. Resource entry quantifies over the existing fresh
  activation rule and extends the resource world.

The retained rules walk every frame. Plain frames adapt their actual stored
plan at the changed suffix; cleanup adapts its callback under running
protection. Live frames recursively check their saved forest against its
complete receiving suffix and check the tail. Handler insertion checks only
its finite requirements and reuses the original retained source. Existing
handlers retain their declarations and recheck their requirements at the new
suffix. Cells, running markers and spent history preserve their structure.

`sound_all` proves both compilation results together by induction on these
judgments. `Adapt.sound` takes the original local check and constructs the new
one. `Retained.sound` does the same for pending source. There is no assumed
function from an old callback check to a new check, and no whole target
`Local`/`Pending` or successful runtime successor is an annotation field.
Fresh requests still check actual callback source through the previously
established structural `Callbacks` judgment.

The invocation rules do not require a separate finite compatibility certificate.
Their recursively compiled pending check supplies compatibility; the existing
`interface_of_check` theorem extracts the handler interface along the actual
recomposition insertion. Existing `resume_admitted` and `dispose_admitted`
then transport access. Thus permission and phase remain independent checks,
while the source traversal establishes the interpretation requirements.
`Retained.owners_preserved` proves equality of the retained owner lists,
including order and multiplicity. It does not count the separately indexed
outside scope as captured ownership.

The examples in [SourceScheduledScopeExamples.lean](SourceScheduledScopeExamples.lean)
include the earlier resume/dispose cases, a waiting request, and a nested
resume-19/dispose-23 derivation with an effectful callback using resource 7.
The nested derivation traverses a stored invocation and its closing callback,
with both owner phases updated. `shadowing_adaptation_rejected` reuses the
existing missing-operation counterexample: the new judgment cannot justify
resumption through that shadowing handler.

This establishes mutual compilation for explicit structural adaptations.
General consuming declaration recipes still need rules that produce these
derivations for their actual captures and context changes. The adaptation theorem alone does not extend declaration admission. The
bounded internally handled prefix rule below extends the recipe grammar;
complete initial admission remains open. In particular, this
module depends on the scheduled checker, whose handler constructor already
uses recipe declarations; it cannot simply be imported back into the earlier
recipe definition. Integration must expose the required structural annotations
at the declaration boundary without replacing them with an opaque whole-body
success premise. General handler and effectful-cleanup recipes, complete
initial admission and universal finite-run preservation remain open.

#### Source contexts before declaration checking

[SourceRetainedPlanData.lean](SourceRetainedPlanData.lean) exposes the existing
retained forest, append, closing construction and append injectivity before
recipe checking. [SourcePlanRequirementSites.lean](SourcePlanRequirementSites.lean)
exposes the existing primitive requirements, actual source sites and selected
clause plans at that same earlier boundary. Their namespaces and definitions
are preserved. This data layer imports neither contextual recipes nor the
planned or scheduled checker; interpreting its requirements remains in
[SourceScheduledRequirements.lean](SourceScheduledRequirements.lean).

`Site.context` derives a structural caller context from source traversal.
Sequence adds the actual pending plan; handler, resource and cleanup entry add
their corresponding frames; callback traversal adds running protection.
`Context.trans` composes these traversals. `Context.owners` preserves the exact
owner list, including order and multiplicity: lexical entry does not allocate a
continuation owner. `Context.owner_cut` then transports an authenticated owner
cut through that context, retaining the identical saved forest and waiting
suffix. The existing `Site.owner_cut` theorem now reuses this result.

These contexts include bodies whose operations become available only after
handler entry. In [SourceScheduledScopeExamples.lean](SourceScheduledScopeExamples.lean),
`LocallyHandledClause.request_site` locates such an operation beneath its actual
new interpreter. `prefix_checked` proves a local composition for any effect,
resource world, permission map, owner phase map, receiving forest and checked
remainder: install the single-operation disposer, perform its operation, then
continue with that remainder. Only the new handler boundary is captured; the
pending remainder remains outside. The proof reuses `request_from_callbacks`
and the existing declaration recipe for disposal.

`followed_by_outer_resume` instantiates that rule with an outer continuation.
`body_before_installation_rejected` proves that the same operation body fails
checking without its new interpreter. Thus adaptation of an already checked
body cannot be the only rule for admitting general handlers. These are local
source checks, not a complete execution or admission theorem. The earlier data
layer permits declaration rules to refer to actual sites without an import
cycle; deriving their capture obligations and compiling general consuming
recipes remain outstanding.

#### Source-local requirement templates

A source-local requirement template is an existing `Site` derivation whose
initial receiving forest is empty. Its resulting forest contains the caller
frames contributed by that source position. It does not contain the actual
saved continuation or waiting tail. The existing `Site.context` and
`Context.owners` results establish that this caller forest has no live owners.
Resource templates retain the fresh-identity premise and extended world; they
are parameterized source derivations, not an enumeration of runtime identities.

`Site.append` in [SourcePlanRequirementSites.lean](SourcePlanRequirementSites.lean)
instantiates such a template by appending any actual receiving forest. Conversely,
`Site.factor` in [SourceScheduledRequirements.lean](SourceScheduledRequirements.lean)
extracts a template from every actual source site. It proves equality of the
receiving scopes and heterogeneous equality of both hints and retained plans.
The induction reuses the existing append-associativity proofs. It accounts for
pending sequence bodies, branches, installed handlers, armed cleanup, callback
running protection and fresh resource scopes.

`satisfied_iff_templates` proves that checking all instantiated source templates
is equivalent to the existing site judgment. `compile_from_templates` reuses the
existing whole-plan compiler; it adds no checking or runtime rule.
`resume_clause_scopes` in
[SourceScheduledScopeExamples.lean](SourceScheduledScopeExamples.lean) now uses
this interface to compile a handler/resource/cleanup body with resumption inside
those scopes. It supplies only installation and invocation obligations and
reuses the previous exact resumption proof.

This separates the source caller context from the eventual capture without
assuming the body checked before handler entry. The template checker still has
to establish primitive capture, callback, invocation and declaration obligations
at the actual receiving forest. Neither this equivalence nor its universal
premise is added as an opaque consuming-recipe constructor. General declaration
rules must derive those obligations; their integration and initial admission
remain open.

### Shared scheduled state and capture preservation

[SourceScheduledState.lean](SourceScheduledState.lean) defines a single state
indexed by the retained source-plan forest. Its constructor contains the current
expression at the signature of its actual plan, the typed pending segment, exact
saved-plan map agreement, structural closing layout, exact stored closing
certificates, local capability checking, owner uniqueness, and the combined
requirement check for current and pending code. Pending scheduling follows from
the typed segment; it is not a second independently supplied witness. Erasure
recovers `DeclaredConnectedSources.State`. Initial construction has an empty
stack and stores, with explicit current source and local admission checks.

`bind_preserves` and `beta_preserves` retain the body plan from the original
local check and reuse the existing source substitution and requirement-evaluation
proofs. They leave the forest and stored certificates unchanged; beta reduction
uses the source theorem's empty lexical ticket scope.

`capture_preserves` constructs a successor of this same state for every physical
capture at an empty outward guard, subject to explicit resource support and
selected-clause contextual requirements. It also takes the actual cut, value
operand, selected clause and table lookup, and fresh names in the three maps.
Source typing derives payload closure and the selected advertised row. The
actual captured stack determines the allocation branch:

- With a closing plan and internal owner uses, `capture_with_closing` retains
  the exact new closing certificate. If disposal is permitted, the existing
  `closed_capture_budget` and template proofs derive its budget from source and
  support. Resume-only offers do not require that budget.
- Without a closing plan or with external pending owner uses,
  `capture_without_closing` derives disposal denial, inserts only the resume
  record and preserves the prior disposal store. Protected captures are included.

Both branches reuse `consuming_usage_completed`, `consuming_clause_balance`,
`capture_phase_consumed` and the saved/tail row checks. These establish the
clause's consumption of the fresh owner, permit checking the waiting segment at
the resulting owner phases, and bound the combined successor row by the original
row. The successor demand is a permutation of `owner :: demand`; its owned-ticket
list is exactly `owner :: ownedTickets whole` and remains duplicate-free.
Contract refinement retains the same source signature, saved forest and exact
closing template. No successful future execution or successor-state premise is
part of the theorem.

This closes the capture connection for the shared scheduled state at an empty
outward guard. General source admission must still derive the contextual site
requirements, including nested handler installations. Resource support and map
freshness still need to come from the full runtime invariant; the remaining
transition families and finite-run induction have not been integrated into this
state. General outward closing budgets and initial-source progress remain open.

`focus_checked_step` reuses frame preparation to construct the actual raw step,

`SourcePlannedRecipeDeclarations.Declarations` judgment for its actual plans.
Its erasure supplies the older premise, preserving reuse of earlier proofs.
The syntactic installation requirement uses that same stronger judgment.
[SourcePlannedRecipeCongruence.lean](SourcePlannedRecipeCongruence.lean)
transports declaration recipes between source-authenticated clause witnesses
through equal stable signatures. `Recipe.signature_congr` follows the recipe
structure, and `Modes.congr` now requires equality of mode signatures. The
declaration proof uses both mode equalities retained by its clause signature.
The former whole-plan uniqueness theorem is removed from this interface; only
the existing uniqueness of genuinely silent prefixes is needed.

This distinction matters for scoped plans. The regression
`scoped_signatures_equal` exhibits handler plans before and after source clause
substitution with equal signatures, while `scoped_plans_distinct` proves the
plans themselves differ. `altered_requirement_rejected` checks that equal
dependency indices cannot conceal changed provider requirements.
`substituted_recipe_retained` uses the new transport to retain the actual
declaration recipe. This transport now supports the resource and pure-cleanup
consuming rules. General handler and effectful-cleanup recipes remain open.

[SourceScheduledHandlers.lean](SourceScheduledHandlers.lean) proves
`handler_preserves`. Source decomposition supplies the actual body,
declarations, coverage and continuation modes. The strengthened local rule
supplies the structural recipe for those declarations. A fresh activation
registers the table, dependency family and declaration requirements together.
Registry agreement preserves the pending source, and the established activation
relocation theorem preserves requirement evaluation. The result is the full
scheduled successor with the same ownership demand and effect row, retained
body plan, saved-plan agreement and closing certificates. No new declaration
admission or successor scheduling check is a premise of this transition.

This theorem targets the default structural recipe evidence, not arbitrary
user-supplied declaration predicates. Its consuming recipe grammar still lacks
general scope-bearing clause rules. Resource entry and builtin cell operations
are connected below; complete runtime integration, initial-source checking and
full progress remain open. These proofs do not change current Core or
establish general Core correspondence.

### Scheduled resource installation and cell operations

The existing `SourceScheduledTransport.local_transport` induction now has a
more general `local_transport_world` form. It retains the actual plan and forest
while extending phases, permissions and the resource world. Resource bodies
use freshness in the larger world to recover freshness in the old world, then
extend both worlds by the same identity. Structural declaration recipes supply
certification in the larger world. The older local and pending transport entry
points are specializations, so their clients keep using the same proof.

[SourceScheduledWorld.lean](SourceScheduledWorld.lean) reuses expression world
transport for typed bodies, offered clauses and contexts, then lifts it to
scheduled frames and segments. The induction includes dormant captures and
their waiting suffixes. Closing templates and certificates retain exactly the
same plans, requirements and saved-forest equality under world extension.

[SourceScheduledResources.lean](SourceScheduledResources.lean) proves
`resource_preserves`. The initializer's source typing exposes its integer value
and empty ticket demand. Existing finite requirement checking chooses a resource
identity fresh both for the current world and the checked requirements. The
source rule supplies its instantiated body, hidden resource requirements and
actual body plan at that identity. The local resource rule supplies the body
check. Installing the cell and transporting the caller and certificates yields
the complete successor with unchanged demand and effect row. No additional
body-check premise is required.

[SourceScheduledCells.lean](SourceScheduledCells.lean) proves
`update_segment` for the unchanged forest, preserving the source requirements,
records and owner phases. The existing payload-update equation preserves the
ordered interpretation context. `request_reply` uses the typed builtin result,
existing ownership equation and raw-step capture-origin theorem to retain the
actual disposal templates. The operation's checked row is removed, leaving a
sublist of the original row. `read_preserves`, `write_preserves` and
`builtin_step_preserves` connect these results to the actual cell transitions.
These are source-state results; the runtime join remains a separate obligation.

### Scheduled runtime disposal progress

[SourceScheduledExecution.lean](SourceScheduledExecution.lean) defines `Run`
with an explicit retained forest. The source and runtime share a coherent
continuation registry, while the existing runtime supplies access, ledger,
name history, result contracts and usage invariants. Saved-plan annotations
retain their issued-owner history. `Run.erase` recovers the earlier connected
runtime. `initial_run` joins explicit source, scheduling and completion judgments
with declaration-signature agreement and the executable `checkInitial` result;
it is not a complete source-admission checker.

`checkInitial` evaluates the supplied requirements in the empty initial store
and context, checks their residual row against that empty context, and checks
literal resource dependencies of the actual code. Evaluation failure, an
unhandled residual request, or an unissued resource dependency returns `false`.
`checkInitial_iff` reuses evaluator soundness and completeness to derive a
structural requirement check with an empty row and empty resource support.
`checkInitial_iff_previous` proves equivalence to the three earlier finite
premises, so combining them does not restrict the previously admitted cases.
`initial_run` and `initial_finite_prefix` use this interface directly; callers
no longer choose the initial row or supply a separate evaluation derivation.

The checked `InitialAdmissionExamples` in
[SourceScheduledFiniteRuns.lean](SourceScheduledFiniteRuns.lean) construct a
complete initial `Run` for unit and reject an unresolved continuation reference
and an unhandled request. A separate resource example uses an unused handler
for `.user 91 [.resource 7]`. Rich source typing, local scheduling, empty-row
evaluation and completion typing all hold, and the operation signature agrees
with the declared builtin signature. Its code still depends on resource 7,
which is absent from the empty world, so `checkInitial` rejects it. This proves
that the support check cannot simply be inferred from those other premises.
It does not establish a reachable failure of the checked runtime invariant.
Source typing, scheduling, completion and signature authentication still need
their complete combined admission judgment.

`assemble_entry` reuses the established runtime assembly for steps allocating
no continuation. Its scheduled successor uses the actual advanced action map,
resource world and retained forest. Existing usage and retained-certificate
preservation supply those runtime components without new semantic rules.

`Run.discard_preserves` handles every actual access-checked disposal from this
invariant. Usage identifies the selected owner and dispose permission. The
retained certificate identifies the actual extracted plan. Registry coherence
connects its advertised closing effects to the strong source contract, deriving
`PlanTyped` instead of assuming it. Scheduled disposal preservation supplies the
full successor; the existing completion proof supplies its result contract.
`Run.discard_progress` reuses the established existence of an access-checked
disposal step and preserves the stronger source for that same step. Demand loses
exactly the selected owner and the effect row is unchanged.

All scheduled runtime transitions, including capture, are connected below.
The consuming recipe grammar still needs general scope-bearing declarations.
Complete initial-source admission and preservation for a final checked-execution
interface remain open. This disposal theorem closes its previous typed-plan
interface gap; it does not settle those admission questions or establish general
Core correspondence.

### Scheduled runtime control and ordinary transitions

[SourceScheduledRuntimeControl.lean](SourceScheduledRuntimeControl.lean)
connects the proved source-state transitions to `SourceScheduledExecution.Run`.
`focus_progress` retains the actual context plan. `value_step_preserves` and

All these joins reuse the established runtime and completion proofs for the

[SourceScheduledRuntimeComputation.lean](SourceScheduledRuntimeComputation.lean)
connects bind, beta and branching through `ready_step_preserves` and

the source proof supplies its checked successor and row.

[SourceScheduledRuntimeEntries.lean](SourceScheduledRuntimeEntries.lean)
connects resource, handler and cleanup installation. Source construction chooses
the actual resource or handler annotation. Existing ledger and activation
freshness proofs supply the named transition, and existing completion proofs

[SourceScheduledRuntimeCells.lean](SourceScheduledRuntimeCells.lean) connects
builtin replies to the same runtime invariant. `request_selection` reuses exact

### Capture obligations from current handler requirements

[SourceScheduledChecks.lean](SourceScheduledChecks.lean) retains each handler's

judgment by structural induction, including saved continuations whose receiving

Handler installation obtains this evidence from the existing `Local.handler`

[SourceScheduledRecipeCapture.lean](SourceScheduledRecipeCapture.lean) proves

The result retains the exact captured and waiting forests, updated owner

`saved_requirements_supplied` accepts a dormant handler whose waiting suffix

whose nearer handler masks that provider without implementing the operation.
These are local judgment checks, not complete admitted executions.

The handler-requirement retention gap is closed. The source theorem also

The empty outward interface permits the existing outward-weakening lemma for

### Scheduled capture and exhaustive progress

[SourceScheduledRuntimeCapture.lean](SourceScheduledRuntimeCapture.lean) reuses

The ledger supplies contract, action and saved-annotation freshness and captured

[SourceScheduledFiniteRuns.lean](SourceScheduledFiniteRuns.lean) reuses

`initial_finite_prefix` composes this with the existing initial-state theorem.

The finite check derives the empty initial row and resource support. `Run.terminal_accounting`

Finite-prefix existence is not preservation for every arbitrary machine trace:

`SourceDependencyState.capture_preserves` now constructs the complete enriched

substituted clause and live boundary and supplies a disposal certificate for a

`check_capture_outward_weaken` preserves the actual selection when the outward

This lets the empty-outward guard supply a certificate at the new contract's

[SourceDependencyState.lean](SourceDependencyState.lean) defines a candidate

`Run` connects this enriched state to the existing runtime invariant through an

`Run.capture_preserves` now joins the actual source successor to the existing

The new runtime record has exactly the rich contract's erasure. Capture

for all three registries follows from freshness in the name ledger.

`Run.capture_progress` chooses that fresh owner using the existing finite-ledger

[SourceDependencyOwners.lean](SourceDependencyOwners.lean) defines `Within` by

The source-to-usage proof shows that a context whose annotation excludes an

The `Local.request` rule now requires `PendingWithin` for the exact selected

`capture_internal_uses` connects the rule to the actual typed cut, so neither

`initial_run` derives an empty initial owner demand and constructs this joined

## Finite coverage of an intercepted operation interface

[SourceHandlerCoverage.lean](SourceHandlerCoverage.lean) adds an executable
sufficient check for a new resumptive handler to cover the operation interface
of the nearest existing interpreter for the same effect. `operationDomain`
stops at that interpreter. A matching handler contributes its declared table
keys, including any conservative extra keys without dependency annotations;
a matching cell contributes its typed read and write operations. An incomplete
nearer handler blocks lookup instead of exposing an outer handler's keys.
Dormant captures do not participate in the active lookup path.

`check_iff` connects the finite Boolean test to the existing independent
`RequestCapability` judgment for every key in that domain. Both ordinary and
protected modes must be available, with resumptive control use. Requirements
use membership rather than use counts. `selected_in_domain` proves that every
previously selected typed operation belongs to this interface;
`selected_capability` then supplies its capability under the replacement.
This is a sufficient coverage condition, not a claim that every individually
safe interception must cover the whole old interface.

The builtin typing premise is explicit. The abstract dependency selector can
return a builtin for any operation number, while
`ScopedPorts.withCellSignatures` permits only operations 0 and 1.
`builtin_typed_of_signature` derives that finite bound from the existing typing
signature. The proof therefore does not assume that all untyped selector
results denote executable operations, and it does not alter builtin selection.

The typing premise is now derived at actual source requests.
`selected_builtin_effect` authenticates the requested instance from exact
lookup, including lookup beneath arbitrary intervening scopes.
`builtin_typed_of_source` in
[SourceScheduledFreshRequests.lean](SourceScheduledFreshRequests.lean) projects
the operation signature from the existing structural `Expression` derivation.
`request_from_source_coverage` uses that fact without a separately supplied
`BuiltinTyped` premise. Its operand may still require evaluation. The negative
example `invalid_cell_operation_rejected` rules out operation 2 under the
declared cell signature for every operand and resource world.

[SourceScheduledRuntimeCells.lean](SourceScheduledRuntimeCells.lean) supplies
the corresponding `Run.request_builtin_typed` projection from retained source
typing and the declaration registry. `Run.request_covered` then admits the
primitive request beneath a covering caller handler. These proofs reuse the
existing port projection and request inversion. They do not authenticate every
latent dependency signature in an abstract callable type: that still requires
the callable-contract admission work, and no global latent-signature validity
claim follows from typing one actual request.

[SourceScheduledFreshRequests.lean](SourceScheduledFreshRequests.lean) uses the
coverage result in `request_from_coverage`. The request may lie beneath any
caller prefix through which the effect passes. The proof reuses capability
prefix transport and the existing request constructor, without a previous
whole-body check or a future schedule premise. Checked examples cover a
same-effect replacement under running protection, both cell operations under
an arbitrary passing prefix, and rejection of missing operations or a missing
protected mode. A read-only replacement does not cover a cell's full interface.

This follows the research principle that control-use obligations belong in
operation contracts and must constrain their handlers; see Tang et al.,
[Soundly Handling Linearity, section 2.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2307.09383#S2.SS2).
The paper does not establish this experiment's disposal or cleanup rules.
The coverage proof is local evidence for one request obligation, not reuse of
the paper's complete soundness theorem.

General handler-bearing consuming declarations still need to derive and retain
these and the other primitive obligations at their actual source templates.
Requests supplied only by the new handler use the existing direct capability
or selected-capture rules at that new scope; they need not have checked before
installation. Rechecking an outer continuation additionally requires its actual
saved code and callback schedules. This coverage result alone neither proves
that transport nor extends the consuming-recipe grammar. It also makes no
observational-equivalence claim about old and new providers.

## Constructing handler-bearing clauses at capture

[SourceScheduledClauseHandlers.lean](SourceScheduledClauseHandlers.lean)
separates two obligations that cannot share a before-installation check. The
original consumer has a structural recipe whose check follows from the
pre-capture request and retained forest. Its saved computation must be adapted
to the new handler. Newly introduced requests are then checked in the installed
scope, where their provider exists.

`capture_handler` performs that construction using the existing recipe capture
and structural `Adapt.sound` theorems. The new handler's declarations retain
their existing recipe checks, and both its external requirements and the added
requests use finite capability checks. `requestPrefix` is an abbreviation for
ordinary sequencing plans. Duplicate requests reuse the same operation
capability; continuation use remains checked separately. The theorem takes no
old check of the complete new body and no replacement `Local` or `Pending`
certificate.

`selected_capture_handler` authenticates the full wrapper against actual clause
selection. `source_capture_handler` joins its scheduling result to the existing
source declaration theorem. Selection uniqueness makes the two proofs refer to
the same plan, including its handler declarations. The resulting source body
retains the established type, effect, ownership-row and fresh-contract premises.

Checked examples exercise three cases: a clause installs a previously absent
provider, requests its operation twice and resumes beneath it; a saved request
is reinterpreted by a new handler for the same effect as its former waiting
provider; and disposal runs a saved effectful callback under the new handler
and running protection. These are source-checking examples, not complete
machine executions or observational-equivalence proofs. They reuse the existing
capture, owner-cut, recomposition and callback proofs. The request and callback
cases now generate their retained adaptation with the compiler below.

This does not complete general declaration admission. The existing declaration
recipe grammar still rejects the full wrapper, as
`old_declaration_recipe_rejects_wrapper` proves. General admission must generate
the adaptation certificate from retained source interfaces at every capture
and retain the resulting declaration evidence through execution. Arbitrary
handler nesting, new effectful cleanup scopes in clause bodies, initial-term
admission and full execution preservation remain open. The rule is a capture
component for the intended calculus, not a smaller replacement milestone.

## Compiling adaptation from source interfaces

[SourceScheduledAdaptationCompilation.lean](SourceScheduledAdaptationCompilation.lean)
removes two parts of handwritten adaptation. `outside`, `inside` and `split`
construct the retained derivation by induction over the actual forest or
insertion. They retain the source plan at each affected position, move callback
checks under running protection, and traverse dormant continuations at their
new waiting suffix. Unaffected suffixes reuse their existing derivations.
The inputs are finite handler-requirement checks and adaptations at affected
code positions, not a replacement whole `Pending` judgment. Each position is
authenticated in both the original and resulting forest.

`resume` and `dispose` use this traversal at the existing owner cuts. They
generate the recomposed or closing derivation under the spent owner phase.
The existing `Adapt.sound` theorem still supplies independent access and
ownership reasoning. No execution or declaration rule accepts a universal
successful-body transformer as a field.

`RequestFootprint` supplies the code-position adaptation for a useful class of
stored code. It applies the structural signature interface described below to
the existing plan, with a finite list of operation requirements. Sequencing and choice concatenate lists.
Cleanup combines the callback and body requirements. A handler checks the
operations it intercepts and exports its own declaration requirements together
with the body's unhandled requests. A resource binder checks its body under
its local read/write interface and the outer requirements. Weakening permits
a larger finite annotation. These lists do not count operation uses.

`RequestFootprint.adapt` generates an entire code adaptation from this annotation
and one `checkRequirements` result at the new receiving scope. Nested handler
declarations retain the original source evidence through `Adapt.sound`; the
footprint does not establish their admission. External request capabilities here require
resumptive handlers in both protection modes. The internal-disposer source rule
below adds a separate case. Other code needing the general disposing-request
or continuation-invocation rules still uses those rules.
`RequestFootprint.no_invocation` proves that an operation footprint cannot
silently discharge an explicit continuation use.

The capture examples now compile retained adaptation for a reinterpreted saved
request and an effectful disposal callback. Further checks cover repeated
requests in cleanup surrounding a nested handler and choice, a resource's
read/write footprint, and reinterpretation inside a dormant saved branch.
These results generate adaptation for the stated source annotations; they do
not derive those annotations for every typed source program. General consuming
declarations must still generate the appropriate interfaces, including explicit
continuation uses, and retain them through source and runtime frames. Complete
initial admission and full execution preservation remain open.

## Request interfaces through source substitution

[SourceRequestFootprints.lean](SourceRequestFootprints.lean) places the request
interface on `SourcePlanSignatures.Signature`. Callable source types already
retain that signature, whereas literal clause witnesses may change after
substitution. The plan-facing `RequestFootprint` is now an abbreviation for
this same judgment applied to `signature plan`; it is not a second interface
definition. The annotation imports neither runtime forests nor source-success
judgments.

The adaptation compiler's `signature_adapt` consumes a signature interface,
an actual plan with that signature, and the finite operation check at its new
receiving scope. Structural induction produces the same `Adapt` derivation as
before. `RequestFootprint.adapt` specializes this theorem to a known plan, and
all previous callback, disposal and resource examples retain their statements.
Actual declaration typing remains independent of this interface proof.

[SourceRequestInterfaceRetention.lean](SourceRequestInterfaceRetention.lean)
reuses the existing rich-source substitution and beta-reduction theorems.
Substituting a closed value preserves the checking signature. Beta reduction
returns the function's declared body signature together with the established
ownership-requirement evaluation equality, so its interface is retained without
another substitution induction. The existing higher-order source example now
carries a finite interface through both bind and beta substitution, including
its effectful cleanup body.

Handler decomposition authenticates the actual clause plans from the rich
source derivation. Equality of their clause signatures transfers the interface
from a reference plan to this actual witness. A separate checked example
changes a literal clause by value substitution and retains its interface using
the existing declaration-signature theorem. The negative signature example
shows that changing a handler's external requirements changes its signature
even when the dependency index stays equal.

This resolves interface retention for these source transformations. It does
not produce an interface for every source signature, validate phantom latent
operation signatures, prove general declaration admission, or extend runtime
preservation. In particular, explicit continuation uses still require their
own structural interfaces. The new source representation keeps those remaining
obligations separate from literal plan-witness bookkeeping.

## Compiling disposal from callback interfaces

[SourceScheduledAdaptationCompilation.lean](SourceScheduledAdaptationCompilation.lean)
now compiles the retained-request case as well as continuation invocation.
`request` takes the original and resulting selected cuts, their structural
insertion relation, and the finite target capture-guard check. It generates
closing adaptation from the original callback positions. When the inserted
handler lies inside the capture, `request_inside` needs no callback adaptation
premise: the established equality of closing forests reuses the old schedule.
Insertion in the waiting suffix rechecks affected callback code using the
shared retained traversal. The selected disposer and captured owners retain
their original evidence through `Adapt.sound`.

A newly selected disposer cannot assume that its predecessor had a disposal
schedule. [SourceScheduledCallbackInterfaces.lean](SourceScheduledCallbackInterfaces.lean)
instead annotates the actual retained forest with `Interfaces`. Each cleanup
position stores a finite operation list and a `RequestFootprint` of its actual
callback plan. Ordinary pending computations contribute no callback obligation;
live continuations retain annotations for both their saved branch and tail.

`Interfaces.compile` consumes the original normal `Pending` derivation and
rechecks each callback at its closing position. Its inputs contain no target
callback `Local` proof or complete closing `Pending` proof. Existing source
evidence supplies each callback's original check, and footprint adaptation
changes its receiving context. Saved branches acquire the running boundary
required by the existing closing construction.

`Interfaces.exposed` computes one finite list for the whole captured forest.
`Interfaces.check_iff` proves that checking this list at the receiving scope is
equivalent to checking all annotated callbacks at their closing positions.
The proof reuses ordered capability lookup and requirement filtering. Closing
prefixes contain builtin providers but no source handlers, so they either
provide an operation or pass it to the outside; no previously successful
disposal check is assumed. A builtin in a live continuation's closing tail can
therefore discharge a requirement of its saved callback. Repetition in the
list does not count operation uses.

`installed_request` combines that finite list with the separate capture guard
and captured-owner bound. Checked examples replace a resumer with a disposer
for the same effect, reinterpret an existing disposer's callback through a
new waiting handler, and reuse callbacks when an unrelated inserted handler is
captured and removed. Negative checks distinguish missing callback providers
from a changed closing route: callback capability checks can pass while capture
must still be rejected. The source-connected disposal example in
[SourceScheduledClauseHandlers.lean](SourceScheduledClauseHandlers.lean) now
derives its callback evidence from the pre-capture retained source through this
compiler.

These are local request and callback-admission results. Callback bodies covered
by `Interfaces` use `RequestFootprint`; explicit continuation invocations and
more general internally disposing callback code still need their appropriate
structural interfaces. The new requested operation itself may dispose, and the
retained-request compiler accepts general structural callback adaptation.
General consuming declarations must generate and retain these interfaces.
Complete initial-source admission remains open. Universal execution
preservation is connected later in the [common event relation](#checked-annotated-events);
no Core alignment or later continuation mode is included.

## Direct callback and initial scheduling admission

[SourceScheduledSourceInterfaces.lean](SourceScheduledSourceInterfaces.lean)
adds `Declared`, a structural annotation over the checking signature. Its rules
follow pure terms, requests, invocations, sequencing, choice, handlers, cleanup
and fresh resource bodies. A handler retains its actual declaration recipes;
no rule stores a `Local`, `Pending`, or successful future-body transformer.
Declaration annotations are independent of the receiving forest and operation
availability. Signature equality preserves them, including when substitution
changes literal clause syntax.

`compile_signature` combines this annotation with `Footprint` and one finite
operation check at the receiving scope. Induction constructs the existing
scheduled `Local` judgment directly. It reuses declaration-signature transport,
exact request selection, and requirement propagation through handler, cleanup
and resource scopes. `declared_of_local` extracts the annotation for existing
clients without changing their accepted programs. Direct continuation
invocations remain outside `Footprint`; they still require independent access
and recomposition evidence.

The interface now has a separate `handledRequest` rule for the established
internal-disposer pattern. This handler supplies its own operation and disposes
its empty capture. The adaptation compiler reuses the same exact cut, guard,
captured-owner bound and callback rules as the existing source proof. It needs
no outer resumptive provider. Existing sequence, choice, cleanup and resource
interface rules compose this case. This extension does not claim to cover
every internally disposing handler.

[SourceScheduledCallbackInterfaces.lean](SourceScheduledCallbackInterfaces.lean)
retains these declaration annotations structurally at callback positions.
`Interfaces.compile_declared` constructs closing callback checks from those
annotations and the finite operation check, without a previous normal pending
schedule or a checked target callback. `installed_request_declared` uses the
result for a newly selected disposer; capture routing and captured-owner bounds
remain independent checks. The old interfaces derive annotations from normal
source evidence and reuse the new compiler.

[SourceScheduledInternalCallbacks.lean](SourceScheduledInternalCallbacks.lean)
checks nested effectful cleanup and choice whose callbacks handle operations
internally and dispose their own captures, including when the enclosing callback
runs under closing protection. Its declarations are supplied structurally;
its callback and closing checks are compiled. A negative check confirms that
the internal disposer is not an external resumptive capability, and a second
rejects using an operation interface to justify an arbitrary outside disposal.
These are source-plan examples, not fully admitted Core programs.

[SourceAnnotatedInitialInterfaces.lean](SourceAnnotatedInitialInterfaces.lean)
uses a closed operation interface and structural declaration annotations to
derive the initial scheduling premise. It then reuses existing annotated
runtime assembly and common-event proofs: every supplied finite trace can
finish or extend, and every terminal endpoint has exact-once owner discharge.
The theorem still takes annotated expression typing, the finite initial check,
structural completion, and signature agreement separately. General consuming
declarations and complete initial-program admission remain open. This is a
partial admission connection within the original one-shot target.

## Retained operation interfaces at invocation

[SourceScheduledRetainedInterfaces.lean](SourceScheduledRetainedInterfaces.lean)
annotates every ordinary pending plan and cleanup callback with its finite
operation requirements, structural footprint and source declarations. The
annotation follows all retained frame constructors, including both branches of
a dormant capture. It stores no checked `Local` or `Pending` premise.

`Interfaces.check` checks each plan against its actual receiving suffix. A
callback runs under the additional running boundary; a dormant saved segment
receives its own waiting tail. `Interfaces.compile` derives the normal pending
schedule by structural induction, reusing the direct source-interface compiler.
The same annotation supplies closing-only callback interfaces and their source
declarations. Closing still requires a separate finite check because removing
saved handlers can change operation availability.

[SourceScheduledInvocationInterfaces.lean](SourceScheduledInvocationInterfaces.lean)
uses these annotations at an actual owner cut. Resumption checks the saved
segment, caller prefix and waiting tail at their recomposed receiving scopes.
Disposal checks only saved callbacks, followed by the complete caller prefix and
waiting tail. The existing recomposition theorems assemble those schedules and
derive compatibility. Known continuation rights, the required permission and
owner availability remain independent premises. Disposal additionally checks
protection and the existing finite closing route. No old or target schedule is
an input to either invocation theorem.

[SourceScheduledInvocationInterfaceExamples.lean](SourceScheduledInvocationInterfaceExamples.lean)
checks a caller-installed handler supplying a saved request and effectful
cleanup without an outer provider. A complete local clause plan installs both
scopes around resumption; another example uses the caller handler during
disposal. Negative checks reject a nearer handler missing the operation, a
missing provider, denied permission and a consumed owner. A further example
passes normal scheduling but fails closing after its provider is removed.

These results discharge primitive invocation scheduling for the operation
interface class. They do not complete general consuming declarations: the
retained plans covered by `Footprint` still exclude free continuation invocations,
and the runtime declaration discipline still uses the existing recipe grammar.
Generating broader annotations from declarations and retaining them through
selection and runtime execution remain required. These are source-plan proofs,
not a claim of complete expression admission or Core correspondence.

## Recursive continuation capability annotations

[SourceScheduledCapabilityAnnotations.lean](SourceScheduledCapabilityAnnotations.lean)
removes the operation-only restriction from retained source scheduling.
The mutually inductive `Code` and `Retained` annotations follow the existing
plan grammar and every retained-frame form. They retain actual owner cuts,
request cuts, code and callbacks; they are independent of the action and phase
maps. Neither annotation stores a `Local`, `Pending`, or successful whole-body
transformer. Existing operation interfaces are reused as leaf annotations.

`Code.Valid` and `Retained.Valid` validate these data structurally. Invocation
validation checks the selected owner's permission and availability separately,
then checks recursively retained source with that owner spent. Resumption uses
the actual saved, caller and waiting pieces. Disposal uses the actual closing
source and additionally checks protection and the closing route. Selected
requests keep the existing structural captured-owner bounds, capture guard and
recursive closing checks. Handler requirements are checked at their actual
receiving scopes. Resource bodies retain the universal fresh-identity rule;
this is not a claim of a finite executable checker for arbitrary source families.

The mutual compilation theorem constructs the existing `Local` and `Pending`
derivations by induction on these annotations. It reuses selected-request
compilation, the invocation rules, recomposition and compatibility theorems.
Recursive annotations can therefore contain further outside continuation uses
at any finite depth. No new operational transition or ownership axiom is added.

[SourceScheduledOutsideInvocations.lean](SourceScheduledOutsideInvocations.lean)
checks resumed code that invokes a distinct outside owner, including a mixture
of resumption and disposal. The same annotation is rejected when the owner is
reused or the outside action lacks permission. A closed plan also checks a
selected disposer capturing armed effectful cleanup; this is broader than the
earlier special empty-capture pattern. These examples establish source scheduling,
not rich expression typing or reachability of an initial program.

[SourceAnnotatedInitialInterfaces.lean](SourceAnnotatedInitialInterfaces.lean)
now accepts validated recursive annotations when assembling the initial runtime
invariant. Its generalized finite-progress and terminal-accounting theorems
reuse the common-event proofs. Earlier closed operation interfaces are wrappers
around this connection. `initial_atPackets_from_annotation` also constructs the
stronger packet-aware execution invariant for general declaration policies.
It compiles the same validated annotation under the supplied policy laws,
constructs its admitted initial snapshot from the checked bounds, and derives
admission of the empty packet stack. Existing initial assembly and
`AtPlan.empty_packets` supply the runtime result; no runtime invariant is an
input. Rich source typing, the finite initial check, completion typing and
signature agreement remain independent inputs.

General declaration admission remains open. These annotations are indexed by
actual receiving forests; the declaration rules must generate them and retain
their meaning through source transformations, selection and runtime use. In
particular, the earlier finite-safety specialization uses the existing declaration
recipe discipline; the general packet-aware construction exposes declaration
policy laws. Both retain the separate rich source, finite initial check,
completion and signature-agreement premises. Neither complete
source admission nor general Core correspondence follows from this connection.

### Reconstruction and transport of general capability annotations

[SourceScheduledCapabilityCuts.lean](SourceScheduledCapabilityCuts.lean)
splits a validated retained annotation at an actual forest boundary. The saved
source retains its real receiving suffix, including recursively dormant source,
branches and outside-owner calls. `retained_at_cut` authenticates both pieces
against the actual handler cut. Resumption and disposal decomposition reuse
the same split; disposal retains the closing callback annotations. The proofs
reuse existing scope, hint, forest and operation-interface equations.

[SourceScheduledCapabilityReconstruction.lean](SourceScheduledCapabilityReconstruction.lean)
proves the converse of the existing annotation compiler by mutual induction on
`Local` and `Pending`. Requests recover the selected source cut; invocation
cases decompose the recursively reconstructed retained annotation. All other
constructors reuse their induction hypotheses. The only translation premise
concerns declaration evidence. This covers every current structural scheduling
constructor, not only operation interfaces or resumption chains.

`local_annotated_iff` and `pending_annotated_iff` establish equivalence between
these structural scheduling judgments and existence of validated annotations,
under the stated declaration laws. `retained_append_iff` reuses established
ordered recomposition. `annotations_at_cut` constructs both captured and waiting
annotations from the current whole-source derivation and the actual cut.
It does not require annotations or scheduling checks for a successor.

[SourceScheduledCapabilityTransport.lean](SourceScheduledCapabilityTransport.lean)
reuses neutral expansion and structural handler adaptation to obtain validated
annotations at changed receivers. Neutral expansion and handler adaptation
retain generic declaration policies with the stated laws. The generalized
`SourceScheduledHandlerAdaptation.sound_all_with` preserves the supplied
declaration evidence by the same mutual induction. Retained requests use the
policy-independent schedule rule directly; newly intercepted requests transport
their existing callback evidence through the source-level declaration laws.
Structural adaptation is still required. The retained result reuses the
established equality of owner lists, preserving order and multiplicity.

These are scheduling results. Reconstruction may omit optional handler bound
metadata, so it is not preservation of `Snapshot.Admitted` or
`StackBounds.Admitted`. An existing scheduling derivation is still needed;
this is not complete initial source admission. Generating the broader bounded
capture input, deriving every reachable input check, and integrating the broader
declaration policy through execution remain open. In particular, the annotation
grammar is general, but the current bounded capture-input generator still has
operation-only and resumption-chain branches.

### Capability phases preserve the actual annotations

[SourceScheduledCapabilityPhases.lean](SourceScheduledCapabilityPhases.lean)
proves permission and phase transport for the same `Code` and `Retained` values.
Permission extension retains existing entries. Phase extension need retain
availability only for live owners in the actual receiving forest, including
recursively dormant captures. Mutual induction reuses the existing selected-owner,
resumed-owner, closing-owner and spending lemmas. Operation requirements remain
independent of these capability checks.

Fresh allocation preserves validation when the new permission entry was absent.
Spending that new outer owner also preserves the earlier annotation when the
owner is absent from its receiving forest's live-owner inventory. These results
cover general branches and outside-owner calls. They do not reconstruct the
annotation, so every optional bound field remains the same data.

This closes the permission/phase transport obligation for general annotations.
Changing the actual receiving forest is a separate obligation: the current
reconstruction-based receiver transport can still omit bound metadata. Neither
phase transport nor the generalized adaptation policy establishes the broader
captured-source validity proof or complete initial source admission.

### Capture bounds independent of source scheduling

[SourceConsumingCaptureSnapshots.lean](SourceConsumingCaptureSnapshots.lean)
separates bound-data construction from captured-source scheduling. The selected
bounded declaration supplies an admitted `SourcePlanBounds.Annotation` for its
actual clause plan, using the existing nested-bound admission proof. The actual
capture cut then moves the original saved and waiting metadata into a live
continuation through `capture_snapshot` and `Captured.admitted`.

`Bounded.capture_snapshot` therefore constructs an admitted successor snapshot
for arbitrary captured forests and the stated nested declaration policy. Its
result is indexed by the exact selected plan and exact saved/waiting pieces.
It assumes neither a successful captured-source check nor validation of a
future clause annotation. This is bound-data admission only; it does not prove
that the selected clause can execute safely at that receiver.

The current-plan bound projection intentionally excludes saved/caller
continuation annotations. General capture integration can carry the declaration's
admitted current bounds beside the independently derived scheduling annotation,
while retaining the original pending snapshot. It need not first prove that
reconstruction preserves every optional annotation field. The existing bounded
runtime wrapper for operation-only and chain inputs still uses the narrower
`GeneratedCapture` evidence with an `ofCode` projection. The general certificate
connection below uses the independent construction directly.

### Certified capture with independent bound snapshots

[SourceAnnotatedStoredCertifiedCapture.lean](SourceAnnotatedStoredCertifiedCapture.lean)
connects an existing structural `Capture` certificate to the actual allocator.
The certificate names the exact source cut and selected clause and contains
recursive capability annotations. Its `Valid` check remains an explicit input.
Cut and clause uniqueness derive the allocator's legacy requirement premise;
no universal successful-body function is supplied by the caller.

`CapturedBounds` packages current-plan and retained bound data independently of
capability annotations. The selected installed packet supplies the bounded
declaration; `Bounded.capture_snapshot` supplies its actual admitted snapshot.
`capture_from_certificate_retaining` reuses both existing allocation branches
and returns the exact annotated successor, joint source/packet typing, physical
packet movement, ownership balance, owner inventory and effect-row inclusion.
It imposes no operation-only or resumption-chain restriction on captured source.

`capture_from_certificate_snapshot` exposes the admitted successor snapshot and
installed packet admission in the same result. Existing cut recomposition and
`StackBounds.Admitted.capture` supply those proofs. The raw step and successor
shape are retained explicitly, without equating targets through erasure.

Capture certificates, typed allocation data and both raw allocation branches
are parameterized by declaration policies. `Capture.requirements_with` uses
`DeclarationLaws` to compile the certificate's structural declaration evidence
into the scheduling admission and certification policies. `DeclarationProjection`
connects admission to certification when source checks are erased. These laws
concern declarations; they contain no future execution or successful clause-body
premise. The original recipe certificate compiler is a specialization of the
same proof. Contract refinement, substitution, ownership and packet movement
reuse the existing proofs under these policy parameters.

[SourceAnnotatedStoredCaptureAssembly.lean](SourceAnnotatedStoredCaptureAssembly.lean)
factors the common completion, ledger, usage and ownership argument out of the
recipe and bounded capture proofs. It combines an actual raw transition and its
typed successor with one current action/source witness. It is an internal
preservation lemma, not a new source-admission rule. The existing disposal
certificate extracted from current source is now generic in declaration policies.

[SourceAnnotatedStoredCertifiedExecutionCapture.lean](SourceAnnotatedStoredCertifiedExecutionCapture.lean)
uses that shared assembly for general structural capture certificates.
`capture_certificate_retaining` pairs validation with the same existential action
map, usage, source and retained-completion proofs. It returns the combined
successor with exact packet movement, ownership balance and effect-row inclusion.
`capture_certificate_snapshot_admitted` also retains the actual admitted snapshot,
installed packet admission, exact forest and successor shape. It does not require
an operation-only or owner-chain shape for the captured source.

This does not derive every certificate's validation from initial source, change
the common finite-event theorem's policy, or establish complete initial admission.
The concrete policy laws below instantiate the static interface. Broader finite
execution must still derive the checks at reachable captures; adding a successful
capture premise to each event would not discharge that source-admission obligation.

### Concrete consuming declaration policies

[SourceConsumingDeclarationCertification.lean](SourceConsumingDeclarationCertification.lean)
derives declaration certification from the existing consuming-clause syntax.
Operation prefixes and callbacks reuse recipe certification and signature
transport. Handler cases use the supplied static declaration laws; resource
cases follow the existing fresh-binder derivation. No receiving forest, owner
phase, successful capture or future body check occurs in the premise.

[SourceConsumingDeclarationPolicies.lean](SourceConsumingDeclarationPolicies.lean)
defines a concrete cumulative family of policies. Layer zero is the existing
recipe policy. Each next layer retains earlier evidence and admits a bounded
consuming declaration whose nested declarations use the preceding layer. Its
source derivation starts in the empty resource world, so existing world
weakening supplies certification in every actual world. This is a condition on
declaration evidence; completeness for arbitrary source annotations has not been
proved. The index counts evidence layers. It adds no computation form or runtime
interpretation layer.

Induction proves `DeclarationLaws` at every finite layer. Admission and capability
reconstruction use the same judgment, and `projection` supplies the required
connection to certification. The laws use the existing structural `Bounded`
judgment; they do not replace missing capture validation with a future-success
predicate. They can instantiate the generic capability compiler and raw capture
interface, while continuation permissions and phases remain separate checks.

[SourceConsumingDeclarationTransport.lean](SourceConsumingDeclarationTransport.lean)
translates the existing syntax derivations along a pointwise implication between
declaration policies. The proof follows the existing world-weakening induction.
It preserves actual clause plans, rights, operation requirements and recorded
bounds, including nested bounds beneath resources. The transformation is a
structural function on the annotation data.

[SourceConsumingPolicyInstallation.lean](SourceConsumingPolicyInstallation.lean)
combines policy inclusion and world weakening. `bounded_at_world` keeps the same
bounds when the declaration is used under the next policy. `handler_admitted`
checks the actual installed packet with those exact bounds and plans. The
existing typed-frame `install` theorem also accepts general scheduling policies.

[SourceConsumingDeclarationPolicyExamples.lean](SourceConsumingDeclarationPolicyExamples.lean)
checks a handler-wrapped resumption accepted by the new policy and rejected by
the old recipe grammar. It also derives certification for every resource world,
compiles a handler installation through the existing source scheduler and
retains the original bounds at runtime worlds. This is evidence of broader
static admission, not a complete initial-program or finite-execution theorem.
General captured-source generation and derivation of every reachable capture
check remain outstanding.

### Direct consuming clauses over general captures

[SourceConsumingDirectCapture.lean](SourceConsumingDirectCapture.lean) removes the
operation-only and owner-chain restrictions on captured source for clauses that
retain the receiver or add builtin resource scopes and pure cleanup at consumption. `Body.Direct`
follows the existing clause syntax: resume, dispose, operation-prefix sequencing,
choice, resource allocation and cleanup whose callback checking plan is `.pure`
and whose callback dependency list is empty. Prefixes retain the existing
operation-footprint grammar; the restriction still excludes handler and
effectful-cleanup wrappers around consumption. It does not restrict the syntax
or owner references in the captured continuation.

`Bounded.selected_direct` extracts the exact selected body's structural
admission, direct-source derivation and declared bounds. `capture_direct` then
constructs a validated `Capture` certificate from the current request annotation
and whole retained-source annotation. The actual cut supplies saved and waiting
pieces. Disposal scheduling and its protection/route checks come from the
current request, using the selected clause's permitted disposal action. The
handler's outer operation requirements, permission-map freshness and absence of
the new owner from the current inventory remain explicit premises.

The proof reuses existing neutral receiver transport and capability phase
transport. Inserting the new spent-owner marker preserves recursive calls to
older owners, including owners outside the captured prefix. Source induction
handles choices and prefixes. Resource cases extend the resource world and
insert the actual cell into the caller context, including beneath running
protection on disposal. The cleanup case reuses neutral expansion for the actual
callback frame, including under running protection on disposal; the caller's
operation interface and callback requirement check come from the original
clause-local judgment. No new cleanup transport assumption is introduced.
The internal `generate` helper receives the
transported pieces; the public capture theorem derives those pieces and assumes
no validated future clause or successful capture event.

[SourceScheduledCapabilityProviders.lean](SourceScheduledCapabilityProviders.lean)
constructs retained annotations after resource-world extension and provider
insertion. It reuses the existing scheduling transport and annotation
reconstruction. The provider and pending-site proofs now accept declaration
policy parameters without changing their induction arguments. No target-source
validation or provider-specific declaration law is a premise. As with general
reconstruction, this does not promise identity of optional bound fields.

[SourceConsumingDirectCaptureExamples.lean](SourceConsumingDirectCaptureExamples.lean)
checks a captured choice whose two branches resume an owner in the waiting tail.
That owner is absent from the captured inventory. An operation-only interface
for the saved branch is impossible, while the new generator produces its outer
capture certificate. Spending the outside owner makes the original source
validation fail. A resource-wrapped clause allocates and reads a cell before
resuming that same general captured source; its annotation is generated from the
original source checks. A pure cleanup wrapper now composes with that resource
case, and a separate disposal example generates the same cleanup frame around
abandonment of the saved branch. A negative admission theorem confirms that
cleanup does not grant disposal to a resume-only continuation. These are
source-checking examples, not complete runtime traces.

This closes the resource-wrapper and pure-cleanup cases of general
captured-source generation. Handler and effectful-cleanup wrappers still need
their general transport derivation;
the chain-specific generator is not a proof for those arbitrary captures.
Complete initial admission and broader finite-execution preservation remain
open. The full one-shot milestone is incomplete.

### Handler boundary obligation for general captured source

[SourceConsumingHandlerInterference.lean](SourceConsumingHandlerInterference.lean)
identifies a necessary condition for extending the general capture generator
through handler wrappers. It reuses the existing closing-interference proof and
the capability compiler; it does not add a new operational rule.

The example has a saved G request and an armed callback that reads cell 4. G's
handler, in the waiting suffix, may dispose. The original source validates:
cell 4 survives G's capture and continues to supply the callback. The consuming
clause installs a resumptive handler for that cell effect before resuming.
Operation availability still holds, and owner 19 has its resume permission and
an available phase. The clause's local operation-bound judgment also holds.
Nevertheless, the next G capture would include the new handler. Disposal removes
that handler, changing the callback's original route to the surviving cell.

`restored_source_rejected` and `clause_annotation_rejected` rule out every valid
target annotation for the respective retained source and consuming clause.
The rejection holds under every declaration policy satisfying the stated static
compilation laws. This is stronger than failure of one attempted generator. It is a source-level
boundary example, not a counterexample to the existing runtime preservation
theorem: `operation_route_rejects` confirms that the earlier generator rejects
the input. G is disposing and is omitted from the clause's declared F-only
operation bound. The example rules out replacing that authentication with old
general source validity and local clause admission alone.

`selected_disposal_requires_shield` derives the existing finite shield check
from any validated selected disposing request. `closing_iff_boundary_exclusion`
factors the exact insertion check through `SourceHandlerInterference.exposed`:
given the old closing judgment, the installed effect must be absent from that
boundary's exposed callback list. `closing_from_boundary_bound` permits a
declared over-approximation authenticated against the actual list.
`bypassed_guard_from_boundary_bound` uses that evidence to construct the new
capture guard for a request handled beyond the inserted handler. Neither
construction assumes a successful target schedule.

The list records callback-routing dependencies. Its multiplicity does not count
continuation uses. A nearer builtin can shield an overlapping effect, as the
positive example checks. This closing condition does not discharge new operation
selection, declaration requirements or recursive retained-source scheduling.
Carrying and preserving boundary evidence through the general consuming-source
judgments remains open, alongside the cleanup-wrapper case. Existing source
admission has not been broadened to accept the rejected example.

### Callback boundary composition and consumption

[SourceHandlerBoundaryComposition.lean](SourceHandlerBoundaryComposition.lean)
proves composition and extraction for the existing `exposed` summary and
`Shielded` structural judgment. It introduces no second callback analysis.
For a prefix followed by a tail, an effect is exposed exactly when it is
exposed in the tail, or it is exposed in the prefix and the tail supplies no
builtin for it. Dormant captures receive the same tail in this calculation.

`boundary_append_iff` therefore splits a whole-scope bound into a tail bound
and a prefix bound enlarged by the tail's builtin providers. The enlargement
is necessary: an empty whole-scope summary does not imply an empty prefix
summary. The checked example has a dormant callback reading cell 4, supplied
by the receiver; detaching the prefix exposes that dependency.
`boundary_at_cut` derives these two bounds at the actual selected handler cut,
using the existing cut reconstruction theorem. `boundary_recompose` transports
the prefix bound to a replacement receiver with sufficient providers and its
own authenticated boundary bound.

The same module proves that resumption and disposal introduce no new exposed
callback effects. Closing retains normally visible builtins and may reveal
additional ones from dormant captures. The closing proof uses that inclusion;
the consumption proofs then reuse prefix composition. `shielded_resume` and
`shielded_dispose` preserve the existing structural judgment, and
`boundary_resume_at_owner` and `boundary_dispose_at_owner` preserve a finite
bound at an actual selected owner cut. The saved scope can contain arbitrary
recursive captures. Permission and phase checks remain independent.

`bypassed_guard_from_composed_boundary` connects these bounds to the existing
handler guard transport. Its separation check includes the receiver providers,
so a whole-scope bound cannot conceal a dependency exposed at insertion. This
is a sufficient bound rule; the exact local shielding check still allows
overlapping effects when a nearer builtin supplies them.

These results establish boundary-summary preservation for the stated scope
transformations. They do not establish preservation for every execution step:
code may register further callbacks, and newly intercepted operations require
their own declaration and capture checks. Generating general handler and
cleanup annotations from source declarations, carrying their evidence through
all execution families, and complete initial admission remain open.

### Effectful cleanup insertion and closing routes

[SourceCleanupClosingInsertion.lean](SourceCleanupClosingInsertion.lean)
identifies the exact additional closing obligation when a clause registers an
effectful callback around a captured computation. It reuses the existing
closing-composition theorem. Cleanup does not select operations, so insertion
preserves an outside handler's contract, offered modes and waiting suffix.
Existing callbacks keep their routes. Each newly declared callback effect must
resolve to the same target in the registered callback's original and closing
suffixes.

`inserted_closing_iff` proves that structural equivalence, and
`check_closing_inserted` factors the executable check into the old check and a
finite check of the new callback effects. `check_capture_inserted` gives the
corresponding exact capture-check equation at a selected outside handler:
non-disposing requests add no closing obligation. `guard_transport` derives the
new guard from the old guard and the primitive route evidence;
`guard_requires_routes` proves necessity. `request_requires_routes` derives the
same requirement from any validated request annotation under declaration
policies satisfying the existing compilation laws.

The source-level counterexample validates the original disposing request and
the callback separately. Inserting the callback still invalidates the request:
its selected capture contains a handler that supplies the callback operation,
but disposal removes that handler. `request_annotation_rejected` rules out any
validated request annotation for the resulting scope. This is not an admitted
runtime counterexample or a failure of the earlier restricted generator.
The positive example instead uses a cell provider retained during closing;
`retained_request_valid` checks the full selected-request annotation, including
the effectful callback's schedule, rather than only its capture guard.

`inserted_owners` retains the exact continuation-owner inventory, and
`pending_within` preserves existing pending-code bounds. The latter deliberately
does not check callback code; callback scheduling remains separate.
`realized_interfaces` connects the new closing rule to the existing typed
runtime closing certificate and exact plan-owner permutation. That permutation
includes the registered cleanup owner on the actual realized stack.

This supplies the route condition and ownership connection for general
effectful-cleanup transport. It does not yet generate callback schedules through
every recursive invocation or authenticate the route evidence from consuming
declarations. Pure cleanup remains the only cleanup case admitted by the general

broader finite-execution preservation also remain open.

### Exact cleanup plans through cuts and pending sites

[SourceScheduledCleanupInsertion.lean](SourceScheduledCleanupInsertion.lean)
adds structural insertion for an actual callback plan and its declared effect
list. Prefix and suffix composition retain that plan. `Insertion.cut` transports
an existing handler cut and locates the callback in its saved or waiting piece.
`Insertion.owner_cut` adapts the existing owner-cut induction: the owner keeps
exactly its old dormant computation, while the callback enters its caller or
waiting suffix. The corresponding split proofs retain the callback through
resumption, disposal and closing materialization. `Insertion.owners` preserves
the exact continuation-owner inventory. These are structural results, not
permission or callback-admission rules.

Ordinary capability and handler-requirement checks are unchanged by cleanup
insertion. The proofs reuse lookup composition and requirement transport;
disposing-request guards still require the separate closing-route condition.

Cleanup cannot use the old interpretation-insertion site theorem unchanged:
unlike a provider or handler frame, it adds stored code. `Registered` locates
the callback at a registration suffix under running protection. `Site.inside`
classifies every target site as unchanged, transported, or a registered callback
with the same dependency index and actual plan. `Site.outside` transports the
receivers of existing sites when the callback belongs to the outside forest.
The checked example proves that an effectful callback creates a site even when
the original forest contains only a cell and no code sites.

`pending_inside` and `pending_outside` reuse the existing pending-site
decomposition to recompose scheduling evidence. They derive the handler-interface
checks from the original pending judgment. They still require local transport
derivations; inside insertion also requires the callback check at its registered
receiver. These are internal composition theorems, not general source-admission
theorems. A concrete cell-reading callback example discharges the new site from
its operation footprint and actual provider, with no old sites to transport.

General effectful-cleanup generation must still construct those local transport
and callback derivations from structural declaration evidence and authenticate
the closing routes. The new structural machinery retains their exact source
plans and locations; it does not replace those remaining obligations with a
successful target check. General handler generation, complete initial admission
and broader finite-execution preservation remain open.

### Callback schedules from closing routes

[SourceScheduledCallbackRoutes.lean](SourceScheduledCallbackRoutes.lean) connects

interfaces at their original registration suffixes; ordinary pending code is
ignored and may contain free continuation uses.

`route_capability` relates existing source routes to capability lookup. Matching
routes preserve the operation check through two prefixes with a shared outside
