membership alone does not grant the operation. `check_from_routes` uses that fact
in a structural induction through callback interfaces, including dormant saved
branches. It derives their closing operation checks from `Covered`, normal
checks and the existing `Closing` judgment. The proof reuses scope composition
and the existing callback compiler. Operation signatures and payload typing
remain separate obligations.

`compile_from_routes` constructs the whole closing callback schedule.
`normal_from_retained` extracts the normal callback checks already present in
retained-operation interfaces. `closing_annotation` reuses annotation
reconstruction, with only a static declaration-policy inclusion law.
`request_annotation` obtains the required closing routes from the selected

remaining inputs are actual source callback interfaces and declarations,

bounds. It accepts no successful destination callback or closing-schedule check.

`Bounded.capture_direct_from_callbacks` connects this result to the existing
direct consuming-clause generator. It replaces that entry point's checked
request annotation with these structural source and primitive check inputs.
Validation of the original retained source, clause admission, fresh-owner checks
and contract refinement remain required. The supported clause grammar is
unchanged: this does not add general handler or effectful-cleanup wrappers to
`Body.Direct`.

The retained-cell example now generates the closing schedule previously supplied
by hand. A dormant example contains a plain invocation of an outside owner; that
code disappears during closing, while the actual callback receives the outside
handler. This proves callback generation, not admission of that entire normal
state. A negative example has an available callback operation and a vacuous
closing guard because its declared needs omit the operation. Closing removes its
handler, so the callback check fails; `Covered` rejects the missing declaration.
The earlier removed-handler example continues to show why normal availability
with correctly declared needs cannot replace a closing-route guard.

General cleanup insertion still needs to preserve these source interfaces,
coverage and normal checks, and to derive the primitive guards while transporting
arbitrary existing local code. The insertion theorem's generic local-transport
premise is not discharged here. General nested-handler generation, complete
initial admission, and broader execution with admitted snapshots remain open.

The induction covers operation interfaces, selected requests, resume, dispose,

The regressions preserve the earlier safety boundary. Every sound generated

This closes the constructor coverage of conditional cleanup annotation

The contextual cleanup rule below incorporates these structural obligations.
Uniform declaration admission and derivation of every reachable condition remain

### Contextual cleanup clause admission

[SourceConsumingCleanupAdmission.lean](SourceConsumingCleanupAdmission.lean)

The earlier conditional generator and `Context.cleanup` remain separate sound

Other retained constructors use classical choice from the proved generator.
Completeness, usable inferred checks and a law relating those chosen checks

`At.generate` proves validity by induction on contextual admission, using the

[SourceConsumingCleanupAdmissionExamples.lean](SourceConsumingCleanupAdmissionExamples.lean)

This completes the contextual rule and its soundness connection for these clause

The handler rule below extends this contextual judgment. The older `Body.Direct`

finite execution must still retain admitted bound snapshots and packets; resource

projection. They contain no target-validity assertion. Resource allocation maps

`Generated` follows the consuming source syntax and the emitted capability code
together. A resume/dispose leaf carries the actual owner cut with the original
saved/waiting forests, proves exact saved-or-closing and waiting projections, and
emits the caller through its operation interface. Sequence, choice, ordered
handlers and cleanup preserve that contract. Fresh-resource bodies use its world
extension for every fresh identity. Prefix and callback interfaces and nested
handler bounds are the source's own annotations. `Generated.current_bounds`
recovers the earlier current-expression bound equality from this derivation.

`Context.continuationBounds` projects these data from actual contextual evidence.
`BoundsAgree.continuationBounds_eq` and `resource_continuationBounds` reuse the
previous entry/transport guarantees. `At.generate_source` in

now constructs valid code together with `Generated`. The existing generation
induction was strengthened; its handler/cleanup cases reuse exact context
agreement, its `sameReceiver` case uses the required metadata equality, and its
resource case uses the world-mapping equation. `At.generate_retaining` is now a
projection of that result rather than another generation induction. Existing
scheduling and admitted-current-bound APIs keep their signatures.

`SelectedSource.capture_source` in
[SourceConsumingContextualCapture.lean](SourceConsumingContextualCapture.lean)
retains that correspondence for the actual stored clause selected by ordered

`capture_source_snapshot` additionally takes explicit equality between the input

snapshot share the actual saved/waiting split. No replacement snapshot is chosen

[SourceConsumingGeneratedSourceExamples.lean](SourceConsumingGeneratedSourceExamples.lean)
checks rejection of the earlier valid/current-bound witness with erased saved
metadata, generation with explicit saved handler bounds, and their preservation
through every fresh resource. It also checks two ordered handlers, effectful

The correspondence concerns snapshot projections of retained fields at the
bound owner's consuming leaves. It does not assert equality of every internal
capability-proof field or every observation below another captured continuation.
The structural request integration below now supplies canonical closing to that
context. Deriving and retaining all contextual request obligations from initial

broader-policy finite execution. No Core simulation or later continuation mode is

`Context.of_request_snapshot` now relates that context to both an admitted

`SelectedSource.capture_source_snapshot` retains the generated clause's structural
correspondence in that same result. These proofs reuse `discarded_of_closing`,

is introduced. The typed `capture_from_contextual_source` allocator also takes

[SourceScheduledClosingTransport.lean](SourceScheduledClosingTransport.lean)

transports the complete request evidence. The actual cut supplies saved/waiting

The remaining execution obligation is to derive and retain `CaptureSource` and

### Queued source admission at focus and return

[SourceConsumingQueuedAdmission.lean](SourceConsumingQueuedAdmission.lean)

frame; the runtime representation is unchanged.

`At.focused` follows all four existing bound splits used by the ten runtime
focus forms. A consuming body cannot have a pure plan. Sequence and argument

Pair-right focus keeps the consuming work current under a pure pending frame.
`FocusedSource` records that distinction. Its `queued_body` and `current_body`

`FocusedSource.child_valid` constructs valid code at the actual child receiver.

`Body.plug` follows the existing return grammar: one pure value prefix, or two
for an application argument. `QueuedBody.plug` derives the recomposed body's
source admission, nested declarations and finite checks. `QueuedBody.returned`
uses the actual `Returned` snapshot relation to identify the exact successor
and pending tail. There is no successor source-admission premise.

[SourceConsumingQueuedTransport.lean](SourceConsumingQueuedTransport.lean)

[SourceAnnotatedStoredQueuedAdmission.lean](SourceAnnotatedStoredQueuedAdmission.lean)

The lower runtime theorems retain the same action map and exact source plans.
The shared execution theorems reuse existing focus/return ownership, access,

The interval between focus and return remains open in the broader execution

current bounds. The reconstructed source record supports exact child descent,
return followed by computation, and further pure focus. Separate results check
permission/phase transport after spending 88, rich retained bounds, and rejection
when 19 itself is spent.
An additional example derives the caller interface while changing both the
caller prefix and waiting tail, then generates and recomposes the source.

[SourceAnnotatedStoredQueuedAdmission.lean](SourceAnnotatedStoredQueuedAdmission.lean)
adds `AtPackets.plug_expanded_waiting_step`: given the actual typed runtime state,
return boundary and structural transport premises, it reconstructs the queued
record, including its caller interface and finite checks, and invokes the
existing typed return theorem. Ownership, name/access
and completion preservation are reused, and the result retains successor source
evidence.

The examples are source and exact snapshot results, not a complete typed prefix
execution. Non-neutral restoration and source coverage at every reachable
request remain open. The one-shot milestone and general Core correspondence
remain incomplete.

### Non-neutral waiting reconstruction

[SourceConsumingWaitingRechecking.lean](SourceConsumingWaitingRechecking.lean)
removes the fixed-waiting restriction from general source rechecking.
`Context.recheck_waiting_retaining` accepts the original context, actual target
owner cut and caller interface, structural `ReceiverChange` derivations for the
original saved and closing annotations, and a `RetainedChange` derivation for
the original waiting annotation. These rules check primitive operations,
selection, protection and closing routes at their actual receiving positions.
There is no target context, target source admission or target code-validity
premise.

The theorem reuses `ReceiverChange.compile_retaining` for saved and closing
code and `RetainedChange.compile_retaining` for the waiting forest. Its result
has exact saved/closing bounds (`SavedAgree`) and structural waiting provenance
(`RetainedBounds`). The changed waiting bounds are not equated to the old bounds.
Existing `RetainedBounds.admitted` transports waiting-bound admission whenever
the original waiting bounds are admitted.

`QueuedBody.recheck_waiting` combines this evidence with the existing nested
`ReceiverChecks` and independent finite clause checks. It reuses
`ReceiverChecks.reconstruct` to produce the complete target source record,
retaining the original body, annotation and nested declaration evidence.
`generate_rechecked_waiting` generates against the actual current continuation
bounds. These results introduce no new induction: the existing structural
compilers and source reconstruction proof discharge the obligations.

`AtPackets.plug_rechecked_snapshot` in
[SourceAnnotatedStoredQueuedAdmission.lean](SourceAnnotatedStoredQueuedAdmission.lean)
now permits different original and current waiting forests. It reconstructs
the source record with saved agreement and waiting provenance, then invokes the
existing typed return theorem. The successor retains its source record and the
exact returned snapshot. This reuses the established runtime proof; the general
execution return theorem also accepts the reconstructed `QueuedBody` directly.

[SourceConsumingWaitingRecheckingExamples.lean](SourceConsumingWaitingRecheckingExamples.lean)
checks a waiting handler insertion that changes a saved operation from a
resumptive interpretation to a disposing one. The fresh-interception rule
derives selection and closing evidence, and reconstruction produces the context,
queued record and valid generated code. `not_neutral` proves that the example
lies outside neutral expansion. A second example keeps successful owner and
finite clause checks but inserts a handler missing the saved operation.
`masking_context_rejected` rules out every target context, independently of
compiler annotation choices, using the existing necessary request guard.

These are source/context results, not a typed execution from initial source.
General reconstruction now permits non-neutral waiting changes, but deriving
its structural rechecking premises through every actual restoration remains
open. Existing counterexamples in [SourceScheduledScopeExamples.lean](SourceScheduledScopeExamples.lean)
also rule out unconditional handler transport: a nearer handler can hide an
operation or make disposal capture running cleanup protection even while
independent owner checks pass. Complete source coverage must establish those
interference obligations from admitted source; ordinary ownership preservation
cannot supply them.

### Source-derived bypass rechecking

[SourceScheduledBypassedRechecking.lean](SourceScheduledBypassedRechecking.lean)
derives a non-neutral rechecking case for an already selected request. The new
handler is inserted after an effect-passing prefix and has a different effect
from the request, so selection still reaches the original handler. The inserted
handler becomes part of that request's captured prefix.

`shield_from_original_capture` obtains closing evidence from the original
request guard using `disposing_capture`, derives the captured callback bound
with `exposed_bound`, and splits it using `boundary_append_iff`. The prefix
bound includes both the captured suffix's builtin providers and the original
outward row. This restores requirements that were hidden by providers when
checking the whole capture. Excluding the installed effect from this bound
derives the exact shielding check. Exclusion is required only when the selected
contract permits disposal; it does not constrain a purely resumptive selection.

`Expression.bypassed_selected` accepts the exact finite shield and derives the
remaining structural request-rechecking premises. Existing `cut_prefix` and
guard transport preserve selection, and `pending_owners_inserted` preserves the
owner bound. `RetainedChange.erased_handler` reuses the proved equality of the
actual closing scopes, hints and forests: closing removes the inserted handler,
so the original callback annotation rechecks by reflexivity. No replacement
callback or target closing derivation is supplied.

`Expression.bypassed_selected_from_bound` combines these results. Its additional
source condition is the finite exclusion above; it takes no target guard,
target closing derivation or target-validity premise. The exact-shield API
remains available when a sufficient over-approximation is too coarse. Both
versions feed the existing structural rechecking compiler. No new induction
or ownership proof is introduced.

`Expression.waiting_selected` covers the complementary case where the selected
capture stays fixed and its waiting suffix changes. It reuses `replace_waiting`
and `guard_same_capture` to derive selection and the guard, and retains the
original owner bound. Only receiver rechecking of the original closing
annotation remains as a recursive premise. The theorem accepts no target guard
or independently valid target callback. It permits arbitrary changed waiting
forests for which that structural recursive premise is derived.

[SourceScheduledBypassedRecheckingExamples.lean](SourceScheduledBypassedRecheckingExamples.lean)
checks insertion of a handler sharing an armed callback's effect after the
callback's original builtin provider. The derived rule admits that overlap,
and the whole saved source is rechecked with exact retained bounds. Moving the
same handler before the provider fails the capture guard. A second example
retains an original closing callback that resumes another live owner, beyond
operation-only callback footprints. The original closing compilation is reused;
no target callback validity is assumed after insertion.
Another example uses `waiting_selected` with an actual effectful closing
callback and generates the request at the changed waiting suffix.

This discharges the bypassed selected-request case. It does not yet derive all
expression or retained rechecking judgments from initial source admission.
Requests intercepted by the new handler, recursive closing-source transport
for waiting changes, and reconstruction through other source constructors
remain parts of that proof. The one-shot milestone remains incomplete.

### Rechecking requests at non-disposing interpretations

`Expression.capability` in
[SourceScheduledSourceRechecking.lean](SourceScheduledSourceRechecking.lean)
reuses the existing `SourceContextualClauses.RequestCapability` judgment. It
accepts any original annotation of the same atomic request when the new
receiver supplies a builtin or a resume-only handler with both ordinary and
protected modes. Exact nearest lookup authenticates that capability. A missing
operation does not fall through a nearer same-effect handler.

The earlier `Expression.operations` rule could recheck only an original
operation-only annotation and retained its requirement list. The new rule also
accepts an original selected request whose old interpretation could dispose.
Its target annotation uses the singleton operation requirement. The existing
mutual compiler proves validity and preserves current-plan bounds: an atomic
request has no current-syntax handler-bound annotation. This does not discard
retained callback code or assert equality of saved request-closing proofs.
World extension and phase restriction follow the same existing inductions.
The rule grants no continuation permission and does not restore a spent owner.

`ReceiverChange.request` in
[SourceScheduledReceiverRechecking.lean](SourceScheduledReceiverRechecking.lean)
handles a retained atomic request independently of the annotation constructor
chosen by an earlier compilation. Case analysis on its original annotation
reuses either the operation interface or `Expression.capability`. The existing

[SourceScheduledBypassedRecheckingExamples.lean](SourceScheduledBypassedRecheckingExamples.lean)
checks a selected cell disposer changing to a builtin, a saved disposing request
changing to a resumptive handler while its effectful cleanup remains checked,

Disposing requests remain available through the separate selected and fresh

[SourceConsumingWaitingRecheckingExamples.lean](SourceConsumingWaitingRecheckingExamples.lean)
composes two non-neutral waiting reconstructions. The first changes a saved

constructor, reconstructs the queued source record, and generates valid

waiting metadata follows structural provenance.

These results extend request and source-context reconstruction. They do not
prove a typed execution of the examples or derive all rechecking obligations
from initial source admission. General recursive capture-source generation and
broader-policy finite execution remain open.

### Fresh capture from structural closing

`Expression.reinterface` in
[SourceScheduledSourceRechecking.lean](SourceScheduledSourceRechecking.lean)
permits an original operation-only annotation to use another structural request
footprint for the same plan. The new footprint must pass its finite operation
check at the new receiver. The original declaration annotation remains intact.
The existing mutual compiler preserves the original current-plan bounds, and
the world-extension and phase-transport proofs include the new rule.

This matters when an annotation conservatively lists an operation that its
actual syntax does not need. Removing a handler during closing may remove that
operation capability while leaving every actual request supported. Reusing the
old requirement list would reject this source. A new footprint proof justifies
changing the list; merely omitting a failing requirement does not.

`Closing.at_fresh_handler` and `Expression.fresh_closing` in
[SourceScheduledStructuralClosing.lean](SourceScheduledStructuralClosing.lean)
connect the original normal prefix's structural closing derivation to a newly
intercepting handler. They reuse the existing equality of closing scopes,
hints and actual forests: adding the delimiter contributes neither callback
code nor an owner. This equality includes dormant saved branches. The existing
fresh-request rule then consumes the derived rechecking judgment. No new
closing traversal or ownership proof is introduced.

[SourceScheduledFreshClosingExamples.lean](SourceScheduledFreshClosingExamples.lean)
checks a prefix with an effectful resource callback and a callback that resumes
an outside owner. Its original operation annotation contains a conservative
requirement supplied by an internal handler. Closing erases that handler, and
the old requirement list fails. A precise footprint for the same callback
passes; the outside continuation is separately rechecked using the original
resumption annotation. Structural closing generates the fresh request and
preserves exact canonical callback metadata. Negative proofs reuse the existing
source compiler to reject omission of the actual request, and the original
phase check to reject invocation of an already-consumed outside owner.

The input still includes original normal-source validity, the finite capture
guard and pending-owner bound, and structural closing of that original source.
The example constructs its closing derivation recursively; no valid target
callback annotation is supplied. Deriving such closing and source-rechecking
derivations for every reachable capture remains open. These are source/context
proofs, not an initial-source typed execution theorem.

### Separate ownership bounds for disposal callbacks

[SourceScheduledClosingOwners.lean](SourceScheduledClosingOwners.lean) defines
`CallbacksWithin` by the retained scope structure. It checks every cleanup body,
including bodies in dormant saved branches, and omits ordinary pending code
that disposal discards. Each body uses the existing `Within` judgment over
source dependencies, including nested computations and fresh-resource families.
The new judgment checks owner references independently of effect requirements,
permission modes and one-shot phases.

`Local.disposal_owner_bounds` derives two bounds from the existing scheduling
judgment for a request and its actual disposing handler cut:

- `PendingWithin` bounds ordinary pending-code references by the captured
  segment's owners. This reuses `checked_request_owners`.
- `CallbacksWithin` bounds callback references by the surviving receiver's
  owners. This follows from the request's actual closing schedule.

The distinction is necessary because closing recursively removes every live
owner from the captured segment. `owners_closing_empty` proves that fact.
`Pending.closing_owner_bound` reuses the existing ordered pending decomposition
and invocation checks to derive the callback bound. `Closing.callback_owners`
and `CaptureSource.callback_owners` connect it to structural source closing and
the authenticated original capture. None adds a successful-target premise to
source admission. Callback bounds split and recompose over ordered append,
survive resource-world extension, and are equivalent before and after the
closing traversal.

An owner inventory also contains dormant owners, so membership alone does not
establish an active invocation target. `OwnerCut.closing_prefix` preserves an
actual active cut in the surviving receiver when any closed prefix is added;
the selected saved body and tail remain exact. Closing cannot shadow that
selection because its owner inventory is empty. The mixed-callback example in
[SourceScheduledFreshClosingExamples.lean](SourceScheduledFreshClosingExamples.lean)
now uses this general cut lemma when rechecking its outside-owner invocation.
Permission, phase and recursive restored-source checks remain independent.

`OwnerCut.survives_closing` also derives the target cut from the original active
cut, membership in the surviving receiver and the existing unique-owner
invariant. Uniqueness separates the prefix's owners from the receiver's owners;
`OwnerCut.drop_prefix` then locates the original selection in the receiver.
Closing preserves that selection with its exact saved body and tail. The target
cut is a conclusion, not an input. This resolves the active-selection part of
callback transport under those premises; it does not establish the recursive
source checks required after invoking the selected continuation.

[SourceScheduledClosingOwnerExamples.lean](SourceScheduledClosingOwnerExamples.lean)
checks a contrary case. A normally valid callback resumes owner 37 inside the
segment that a fresh disposing handler captures. The request passes its capture
guard and ordinary pending-owner bound, but the surviving receiver has no owner
37. The callback bound fails, and the general request theorem excludes every
valid target annotation, not just a particular generator result. A positive
example retains the earlier mixed callbacks using a surviving outside owner.

This is a source/context obstruction, not an unsafe typed execution. The new
bound is necessary, not sufficient: it does not derive active owner cuts,
permissions, phases, operation compatibility or recursive source rechecking
from membership. Incorporating sufficient callback conditions into initial
structural admission and proving their preservation remain open.

[SourceScheduledClosingTransport.lean](SourceScheduledClosingTransport.lean)
now connects canonical closing compilation to captured-owner retirement.
`Closing.compile_retiring` first derives the actual closing annotation from the
original source and structural closing judgment. It then reuses the general
annotation phase theorem, restricted to owners in the surviving receiver.
The existing pointwise `spendAll_at` equation supplies their unchanged
availability. Permissions use the same action map, and the exact canonical
callback metadata remains unchanged.

`CaptureSource.compile_retiring` derives the required separation from the
original capture's actual cut and unique-owner invariant, then transports the
original request's checked closing annotation. It accepts any retired subset of captured owners, including an intermediate subset. Neither
proof assumes a valid target annotation or requires the discarded normal source
to remain valid at the later phases. This is phase stability of closing source;
the existing operational trace and ledger proofs still govern when retirement
occurs and whether each owner is consumed exactly once.

The retirement example in
[SourceScheduledClosingOwnerExamples.lean](SourceScheduledClosingOwnerExamples.lean)
includes ordinary code that resumes captured owner 19, plus the resource and
outside-owner-37 callbacks. The original source is valid before retirement and
provably invalid after owner 19 is consumed. Structural closing drops its
ordinary code and generates a valid annotation at those later phases, retaining
both callbacks and their exact metadata. Thus retirement transport is applied
to the generated closing source, not to the discarded normal source. General
closing generation and recursive receiver rechecking remain the missing source
connection; the retirement phase change introduces no additional condition
beyond the proved owner separation.

### Protected-mode request rechecking

A request crossing a running callback captures its protection marker. The
existing capture guard therefore excludes disposal of that segment.
[SourceScheduledProtectedRechecking.lean](SourceScheduledProtectedRechecking.lean)
proves this by reusing `disposing_capture`, including for an arbitrary bypassed
prefix before the running marker. `protected_capture_check` characterizes the
remaining finite check exactly: disposal is disabled, the protected effect row
is present, and the matching protected source-body family is present. Nearest
selection is still the actual selected cut; an unavailable nearest operation
cannot fall through to another handler.

The existing reusable `RequestCapability` deliberately requires both ordinary
and protected modes. It is stronger than this local request check. The new
`Expression.nonDisposing` source rule in
[SourceScheduledSourceRechecking.lean](SourceScheduledSourceRechecking.lean)
checks the actual cut, capture guard and disabled disposal. Its compiler creates
the existing selected-request annotation: the disabled permission eliminates
both disposal obligations. It retains the exact original request bounds and
adds no source-computation or runtime rule. General permission/phase transport
and resource-world transport include this source-rechecking rule.

`Expression.protected_request` derives disabled disposal from the selected
protected segment. `Expression.crosses_cleanup` authenticates that segment
using the existing prefix-cut theorem and any prefix bypassed by the request.
Neither theorem needs a target closing annotation or a successful target
schedule. Builtin requests continue to use the existing operation-capability
rule. A request intercepted by a handler before the running marker does not
satisfy this crossing case and retains its recursive source obligations.

[SourceScheduledProtectedRecheckingExamples.lean](SourceScheduledProtectedRecheckingExamples.lean)
checks a callback under a changed outside interpretation offering only the
protected mode. Its original source is valid; rechecking generates valid request
and closing annotations with exact original bounds and callback metadata. The
uniform capability correctly rejects the same target because its ordinary mode
is absent. Additional negative cases reject ordinary use, a missing protected
body family and disposal across the running marker.

These are source/receiver proofs, not authorization to exchange interpretations
or ignore the existing capture-route checks. Initial admission must still
supply the actual protected-mode availability after a receiver change. For this
crossing case, however, the recursive fresh-disposal branch is impossible rather
than a further ambient-source obligation. The following request and caller sections supply further structural cases;
general reconstruction must still derive their recursive premises from admission.

### Requests selected inside an unchanged prefix

[SourceScheduledInternalRechecking.lean](SourceScheduledInternalRechecking.lean)
handles selection before a callback's running boundary. `Cut.suffix` appends an
outside receiver while retaining the exact saved forest, contract and mode
families. It reuses waiting replacement, cut reconstruction and associativity.
`Cut.drop_suffix` recovers the actual internal cut from an existing whole-source
cut when lookup stops in the prefix. The proof uses the existing lookup-append
equation, hint uniqueness and forest uniqueness to identify both the saved
forest and the waiting decomposition. A new local cut is a conclusion, not an
independent source premise.

An atomic request has two source annotation forms, handled separately:

- `Expression.internal_operations` derives the precise target capability from
  the original operation footprint and validity. `Footprint.request_member`
  proves that even a weakened footprint includes the actual request. The same
  selected contract retains its two-mode capability when only its waiting
  receiver changes. Extra conservative requirements need not survive.
- `Expression.internal_selected` retains the original selected capture, guard
  and owner bound. Only the original closing annotation is recursively rechecked
  at its new waiting receiver. This annotation is already a child of the
  original selected-request source; no new normal captured-source witness or
  independently validated target annotation is required.

The latter proof reuses `Expression.same_capture_selected` in
[SourceScheduledBypassedRechecking.lean](SourceScheduledBypassedRechecking.lean).
The existing `waiting_selected` entry point now delegates to that generalized
two-cut theorem, so guard transport and receiver rechecking have one proof.
The selected capture need not be syntactically the entire receiving prefix.

[SourceScheduledInternalRecheckingExamples.lean](SourceScheduledInternalRecheckingExamples.lean)
checks both cases. An operation-only annotation lists a real internal request
and an unused outside requirement; after removing that outside receiver, the
old list fails but the actual request rechecks from its original footprint.
The second example selects a local disposing handler before the running
boundary. Its captured callback uses an outer effect, whose receiver changes
to a handler offering only the protected mode. The original closing callback
is reconstructed with `crosses_cleanup`, and the local request reuses its
original capture guard and owner bound. The recursive receiver compiler also
preserves exact callback metadata.

These results identify the request cases needed by general source reconstruction.
They do not yet supply the whole mutual source-generation theorem. The selected
case still requires structural receiver rechecking of its original closing child;
callback owner invocations likewise require their original saved/caller source
children to be reconstructed. Initial source admission and runtime retention
must supply those recursive premises. No handler-exchange law follows from
changing a receiver in these source/context examples.

### Partial caller closing during continuation invocation

[SourceScheduledPrefixClosing.lean](SourceScheduledPrefixClosing.lean) defines
`PrefixClosing` on the original retained caller and an explicit prefix boundary.
It discards ordinary pending code, handlers and spent frames inside that prefix;
retains cells, cleanup callbacks and running frames; and closes each dormant
saved branch before the running remainder. At the boundary, receiver rechecking
retains the suffix. The protected stopping rule also inserts the running marker
introduced by disposal. No rule accepts a replacement caller or a valid target
annotation as its premise.

`PrefixClosing.rechecking` embeds the traversal in the existing retained-source
judgment. Its proof reuses `Closing.rechecking`, `ReceiverChange.rechecking` and
forest associativity; it adds no runtime transition. `surviving_owners` proves
that the resulting caller has exactly the suffix's live-owner list. Closing
removes the prefix's owners, and the optional running marker adds none.
`compile_admitted` reuses the general compiler and its structural metadata
provenance theorem. The stronger compiler described below also proves exact
canonical snapshot equality and carries original source-record payloads.

`Expression.resume_closing_caller` and `dispose_closing_caller` share this caller
traversal. They take the original outside owner selection and the source
annotated with its prefix extension. The existing owner-cut theorem supplies
the new selection after closing. The selected saved forest and tail stay fixed;
resumption rechecks the original saved-body child at its changed receiver, and
disposal rechecks the original stored closing child. The original tail is reused
unchanged. Permissions, availability and disposal guards remain obligations of
original source validity and the existing compiler.

[SourceScheduledPrefixClosingExamples.lean](SourceScheduledPrefixClosingExamples.lean)
checks resumption with a nonempty saved body, a retained caller suffix and a
closing prefix containing a dormant callback. Ordinary caller code requests a
handler that cleanup removes; the traversal drops that code. The saved body
requests a surviving handler, although its original conservative interface also
listed the removed handler. Rechecking narrows that interface using the actual
request footprint. The resulting source is valid, saved metadata is identical,
and caller metadata remains admitted. A second case disposes an outside owner
with a nonempty stored closing body and preserves that body's exact metadata.
A spent outside owner remains rejected.

The negative case changes the saved body's actual request to the erased handler.
The original body is valid, but `lost_no_target` excludes every valid annotation
at the closing receiver, and `lost_no_rechecking` excludes receiver rechecking.
This is a necessary source-admission distinction: unused conservative requirements
may be removed; actual requests in a resumed saved body must remain available.
The proof reuses the existing compiler and necessary request guard.

These are structural invocation cases, not a complete initial-source preservation
theorem. The saved-body/closing-body receiver derivations and callback obligations
must still follow from initial admission and remain available recursively.
The original caller decomposition and exact metadata retention are connected
below. Derivation from initial admission and integration into the broader runtime
invariant remain open. These examples are source/context evidence, not complete
initial executions or Core simulation.

### Canonical partial closing and original caller decomposition

[SourceScheduledPrefixRetention.lean](SourceScheduledPrefixRetention.lean)
strengthens partial closing to exact canonical metadata. The compiler splits the
original snapshot with the existing `Retained.splitAt`, closes its prefix with
`forClosing`, and appends the original suffix. `BoundaryBounds` has exactly two
structural cases: the same suffix, or that same suffix wrapped in the disposal
running marker. It cannot supply another suffix's code bounds.

`PrefixClosing.compile_retaining` constructs the source annotation and its exact
snapshot together. Callback and dormant-body cases reuse the existing expression
and closing compilers. The suffix reuses receiver compilation, and the dormant
case reuses ordered retained recomposition. `Retained.append_assoc` proves the
corresponding metadata associativity using the existing scope, hint and forest
laws; it moves every recorded bound unchanged. Admission follows from the
original snapshot's split, closing and append laws. No successor validity or
successor metadata-admission premise is introduced.

[SourceScheduledCallerDecomposition.lean](SourceScheduledCallerDecomposition.lean)
connects an arbitrary original owner cut to this traversal. `caller_unique`
uses deterministic owner lookup and forest append injectivity to identify the
caller's scope, hints and actual forest. `drop_prefix_retaining` strengthens the
existing outside-cut recovery with those equalities. `prefix_cases` then
eliminates the original caller at that authenticated split, without a second
cut induction.

`Code.resume_caller_source` and `dispose_caller_source` apply this elimination
to the original source children. The resulting saved or closing child and caller
child are heterogeneously equal to their original values. The entire rebuilt
invocation annotation is equal to the original `Code`, not just its current
bound projection. Thus the prefix traversal receives the original stored source,
with only its dependent indices rewritten; no replacement source witness is
chosen from validity alone.

[SourceScheduledPrefixRecords.lean](SourceScheduledPrefixRecords.lean) carries
actual queued payloads through the same transformation. `Records.forClosing`
drops ordinary pending prefix records, retains callback records, and visits
dormant branches before their running tails. Its entry list is exactly the
original list filtered to callback positions, preserving payload values, order
and multiplicity. Record splitting reconstructs the entire original payload
tree. Boundary protection leaves suffix entries unchanged. `compile_records`
joins this record movement with the exact source compiler: the resulting caller
contains the prefix's original callbacks followed by all original suffix entries.
This is more than finding some records with compatible metadata indices.

The existing partial-closing examples now check exact canonical snapshots with
and without the boundary marker. Both retain explicit nested-handler bounds in
the dormant callback and caller suffix. A payload example assigns `11` to the
discarded pending source, `22` to the dormant callback and `33` to the retained
pending suffix. The generated caller carries exactly `[22, 33]` in that order.

These results close the caller-decomposition and canonical-retention obligations
for a supplied structural `PrefixClosing` derivation. They do not derive that
derivation from initial program admission. In particular, the checked erased-
handler counterexample still requires admission to ensure that actual requests
in a resumed saved body remain available. The general mutual source-generation
and preservation theorem, adoption of the generated annotations and records by
the broader execution invariant, and complete initial admission remain open.

### Independent recursive admission checks

[SourceScheduledAdmissionFactors.lean](SourceScheduledAdmissionFactors.lean)
factors the existing recursive source validator into two structural projections.
`InterpretationChecks` checks operation requirements, selected capture contracts
and cleanup effects. It takes neither the external continuation permission map
nor the one-shot phase map. `ContinuationChecks` checks invocation permissions,
availability before consumption, and the unprotected-capture condition for an
explicit disposal. It takes no outward effect row and checks no operation list.
Selected capture guards still check their selected contract and protection mode;
the factorization does not remove those contextual conditions.

The mutual theorem `admission_factors` proves that their conjunction is exactly
the existing `Code.Valid` and `Retained.Valid`, in both directions. It follows the
existing source recursors through every constructor, including saved and closing
bodies, caller and tail annotations, dormant branches, and all fresh resource
instances. Each invocation checks its owner before spending that owner in all
of its actual continuation children. The projections retain the original
validator's scheduling structure; this theorem does not independently prove a
trace property such as absence of repeated consumption.

`Code.compile_factors` and `Retained.compile_factors` reuse the existing source
compiler to produce `Local` and `Pending` from the two checks. No successful
target judgment is an input. Source declaration evidence, actual cuts and owner
bounds remain in the original annotation. The result is a factorization of that
annotation's validation, not a claim that an effect list alone admits a program.
Because resource annotations range over arbitrary fresh-name families, this is
not a new whole-program decision procedure.

[SourceScheduledAdmissionFactorsExamples.lean](SourceScheduledAdmissionFactorsExamples.lean)
checks a resumption whose saved body resumes a second owner. Both the current
source and its retained form compile from separately proved factors. With the
interpretation factor unchanged, missing permission for the second owner,
consumption of that owner, or consumption of the first owner rejects the control
factor. Conversely, an unprovided effect has a trivial control factor but fails
the interpretation factor and full validation.

This makes the two recursive obligations explicit for the full annotated source
grammar. It does not construct the contextual rechecking derivations needed
after closing, nor establish that a transformed source preserves either factor.
Those transformation proofs and their connection to initial source admission
remain necessary for the general one-shot milestone.

### Source-only recomposition and independent checks

[SourceScheduledSourceJoin.lean](SourceScheduledSourceJoin.lean) constructs
`Retained.joinSource` directly from the actual prefix and suffix annotations.
Construction takes no interpretation check, continuation permission, phase map
or successful validation. An operation-only prefix is expanded far enough to
retain the suffix's explicit metadata. Structured source follows its existing
constructors. Current code, callbacks and dormant saved code are transported
through the existing receiver associativity laws; heterogeneous equality proves
that this transport retains the original source value.

The two validation factors characterize this one output independently:
`joinSource_interpretations` equates its interpretation check with the conjunction
of the two original interpretation checks, and `joinSource_continuations` does
the same for permissions and phases. Both are equivalences, so a rejected input
cannot become accepted merely through joining. `joinSource_bounds` separately
proves exact snapshot append. `joinSource_valid` combines the factors through
the existing admission equivalence.

This strengthens the earlier existential recomposition interface, which required
successful validation before returning a source witness. The data constructor
exists even for rejected inputs, and both factor proofs concern the same output.
It does not choose separate source witnesses for interpretation and control
checks. The main structural rechecking compiler, the closing compiler and the
partial-caller retention compiler now use this constructor when joining a closed
dormant segment with its running tail. Their earlier exact metadata conclusions
remain checked.

[SourceScheduledSourceJoinExamples.lean](SourceScheduledSourceJoinExamples.lean)
retains explicit handler metadata in callback, dormant and suffix positions, and
checks a compact prefix followed by a rich suffix. A suffix with nested owner
invocations remains rejected when its second owner's permission is missing or
that owner is already consumed. A source with an unprovided effect is also
constructible but remains rejected by the interpretation factor.

This removes the validation prerequisite from the recomposition constructor.
It does not yet make every rechecking compiler branch independent of original
validation, derive its contextual transformation from initial admission, or
complete broader-policy execution safety.

### Rechecking compilation before full validation

`compile_factors_retaining_all` in
[SourceScheduledSourceRechecking.lean](SourceScheduledSourceRechecking.lean)
constructs one target annotation from a structural `Expression` or
`RetainedChange` derivation without a blanket original `Valid` premise. For that
same output, it proves that original interpretation checks imply target
interpretation checks, original continuation checks imply target continuation
checks, and the existing metadata conclusion holds. Current-code bounds remain
equal; retained bounds follow the existing structural provenance relation.

The proof strengthens the existing mutual compiler induction. It retains the
original constructor cases, uses the existing fresh-interception compiler, and
uses the source-only join for closed dormant branches. Invocation cases transport
the saved or closing source, caller and tail separately, preserving the original
permission and phase facts when the control implication is applied. Resource
cases choose one output family, shared by both implications and the metadata
proof. They do not choose separate witnesses for effect and control checking.
The earlier validity-preserving compiler API now follows by combining these two
implications for the same annotation through `valid_iff_factors`.

These implications are not equivalences for every rechecking rule. Dropping
ordinary pending source can discard a failed check.
[SourceScheduledFactorCompilationExamples.lean](SourceScheduledFactorCompilationExamples.lean)
exercises construction when full original validation is unavailable: a request
with a missing original provider still transports its control factor, and a
branch containing an unpermitted nested invocation still transports its
interpretation factor. A fresh-resource example checks both factors for one
output family. A discarded invalid ordinary frame leaves a valid empty target.
None of these examples admits the rejected original as an executable program.

The structural transformation derivation remains a premise. In particular,
`freshRich` still carries validation of its original normal prefix; the new
compiler does not manufacture that evidence or remove it from the rule.
Deriving and retaining the contextual transformation evidence from initial
source admission is still open, as are broader-policy execution integration and
complete initial callable/resource contracts. Compilation before validation
closes a construction dependency, not the whole admission theorem.

### Original source at fresh interception

[SourceScheduledInterceptSource.lean](SourceScheduledInterceptSource.lean)
recovers the normal prefix captured by a newly inserted handler from the
original whole retained source. `InterceptSource.recover` combines the existing
interception decomposition and retained-source split: the recovered prefix and
waiting suffix are valid at their original receivers, and their ordered metadata
append is exactly the original snapshot. `recoverAt` retains a prefix index
already known by a syntax traversal. Neither requires a separately supplied
valid normal-prefix annotation.

For whole source constructed from its actual prefix and suffix,
`recoverJoined` reuses `joinSource_valid` to derive the child checks. It retains
the actual prefix annotation up to receiver equality, including invocation
children and fresh-resource families. It does not choose a replacement source
annotation. This distinction lets clients reuse proofs about those original
children rather than reconstructing them from a metadata equation. The proof
uses the existing join and receiver-transport laws; it adds no split induction.

`InterceptSource.rechecking` supplies the recovered normal prefix to the
existing fresh-disposal rule. Three independent obligations remain: the capture
guard, the bound on owners referenced by discarded pending code, and structural
closing for callbacks at the surviving receiver. Whole-source validity alone
does not imply these obligations. The primitive `Closing.request_callback`
derives closing for a single actual request callback from an outside uniform
operation capability, for either compact or structured original annotation.
It supplies no continuation permission.

[SourceScheduledInterceptSourceExamples.lean](SourceScheduledInterceptSourceExamples.lean)
checks a nonempty callback prefix recovered from whole source and compilation of
the newly intercepted disposing request with unchanged current-code metadata.
A second example retains the actual prefix from the existing mixed-callback
fixture, reuses its closing proof for an outside-owner invocation, and obtains
the same compilation result. The existing consumed-owner rejection transfers
to the joined whole source. A separate negative check rejects the primitive
callback capability at an empty outside receiver.

This establishes original-prefix recovery for fresh interception. It does not
derive the residual closing obligations for arbitrary callbacks, construct a
general handler-insertion traversal, or retain initial admission through every
runtime transition. Those remain part of the open initial-source and execution
integration work. Core correspondence and the excluded continuation modes are
unchanged.

### Handler admission from original operation interfaces

[SourceScheduledHandlerInterfaceAdmission.lean](SourceScheduledHandlerInterfaceAdmission.lean)
derives handler-entry receiver changes for original retained source whose code
positions carry operation footprints. `OperationSource` relates that actual
source to its interface. It covers compact annotations and every expanded
retained-frame constructor, including callbacks and dormant captures. Its
`valid_iff` theorem identifies the interface check with the original source's
validation. It does not erase or replace the source annotation.

`OperationSource.extract` traverses the original annotation and returns its
interface together with this structural evidence. Extraction is complete for
the view and retains the exact requirement lists, including duplicates. It
returns no result when a code position uses a richer selected-request or
continuation-invocation annotation. This is a representation distinction, not
program rejection. Such source retains the existing richer rechecking rules.

The new `Interfaces.check_handler_insert` theorem composes the existing exposed
interface and ordered-scope replacement proofs. Assuming the original interface
checked, its check after insertion is equivalent to checking only the operations
that pass the unchanged receiver prefix and match the newly installed effect.
That check runs against the inserted table alone. A nearer matching handler
with a missing operation cannot fall through to an older provider. Internal
providers discharge requirements before this boundary; dormant providers do not
supply active sibling requests.

`OperationSource.receiver` derives the existing `ReceiverChange` rules for all
retained frames. `handler_receiver`, `handler_here` and `handler_running` then
use the finite insertion criterion, reusing original validity for unrelated
operations. `At.handler_interfaces` applies these results to the actual
resumption and closing source in a continuation's context. The rule takes their
source views and primitive table checks instead of supplied receiver-change
derivations. The recursive clause-body admission, declaration evidence, and
independent permission and phase checks remain the existing obligations.
Metadata preservation follows through the existing receiver compiler.

[SourceScheduledHandlerInterfaceExamples.lean](SourceScheduledHandlerInterfaceExamples.lean)
uses extracted source evidence to admit a handler over a nonempty saved request,
followed by a choice of resume or dispose. Another example derives both paths
with a nonempty cleanup callback, retaining the protected closing receiver.
Negative and boundary checks cover masking, unrelated effects, consumed owners,
dormant requirements, active builtin shielding, and dormant cells that do not
shield siblings. A disposing override that fails this uniform-interface test
is still admitted by the existing richer fresh-capture proof. A valid callback
invoking an outside continuation likewise remains valid when extraction returns
no operation-only view.

The source views now persist across entry. `OperationSource.bounds` proves that
compacting source represented by this view retains its complete snapshot. This
is limited to positions already carrying operation footprints; it does not
erase richer continuation annotations. `Context.OperationSources` packages the
views of the actual saved and closing source. Its `handler` and `cleanup`
constructors create explicit successor annotations from those interfaces,
retain the waiting tail, and prove `BoundsAgree` with the original context.
`after_handler` and `after_cleanup` retain the same extracted interfaces for
the next entry. Resource entry retains their existing world extensions:
`OperationSource.world_weaken` transports the structural source view, and
`Context.OperationSources.resource` uses the established provider-insertion
law to check the new builtin receiver. `resource_bounds` proves equality with
the original continuation metadata's world extension, including its waiting
projection. `after_resource` supplies the extended source views for subsequent
entries. Freshness remains a premise of the existing resource-body rule.

This source-shape fact is stronger than the previous compiler result, which
promised a valid annotation and matching metadata but did not promise that the
chosen annotation had an operation-interface view. The new
`At.handler_retaining_interfaces`, `At.cleanup_retaining_interfaces` and
`At.resource_retaining_interfaces` rules connect explicit successors to the
existing admission constructors using
`sameReceiver` and their established metadata preservation proofs. They do not
change those constructors or bypass their checks. Cleanup receiver transport
reuses the existing insertion theorem; the newly registered callback still has
its separate footprint, coverage, and clause-side capability check.

[SourceConsumingInterfaceNestingExamples.lean](SourceConsumingInterfaceNestingExamples.lean)
uses induction to admit every finite nesting depth of the supplied resumptive
table and derive the existing `Generated` source correspondence and scheduling
results. The same induction applies to saved paths containing an actual cleanup
callback. A consumed owner is rejected at every depth. Further examples put an
unrelated disposing table around the nesting and interleave an outer handler,
effectful cleanup registration, and arbitrarily many inner handlers. The
resource examples quantify over every fresh identity and perform an actual
builtin read before the nested consuming body. The combined example composes
all three entry forms and generates source with the original continuation
correspondence. These results reuse the existing source-generation compiler;
they are not runtime all-transition safety or general Core correspondence
theorems.

This closes interface-based handler receiver derivation for that structural
source class. It is not a complete generator for arbitrary recursive
continuation annotations or fresh disposing interceptions. Those cases still
need the general closing and receiver derivations, followed by retention through
execution and complete initial-program admission.

### Initial interface admission at continuation use

An entry-by-entry interface check can demand saved-source validity too early.
The checked example in
[SourceConsumingLeafInterfacesExamples.lean](SourceConsumingLeafInterfacesExamples.lean)
installs an empty E handler, then an E handler supplying the saved request, then
resumes. The initial `Admitted` judgment accepts it and the existing scheduling
compiler validates it. The saved interface fails at the intermediate empty
handler, where it is still dormant. This proves an obstruction to that eager
interface construction, not an impossibility theorem about every `At` derivation.

[SourceConsumingLeafInterfaces.lean](SourceConsumingLeafInterfaces.lean)
provides a direct route from initial admission to generated source for this
source class. `Body.generate_leaf_interfaces` follows the existing consuming
body grammar and checks saved or closing requirements at the consuming leaf's
actual caller. It reuses `Interfaces.check_from_bound`, the original source
views, permission/phase checks and disposal protection. Handler, sequence,
choice and cleanup constructors retain their order. Resource entry reuses world
extension for the interfaces, original waiting annotation and bound snapshots.

The waiting annotation is arbitrary and is retained verbatim, except for its
existing resource-world extension. Saved and closing annotations are compacted
only where `OperationSource.bounds` proves exact metadata preservation. The
result includes the existing `Generated` correspondence for every consuming
leaf, including actual owner cuts and the original saved/closing/waiting
projections. `Context.OperationSources.initial_source` obtains its local checks
from `Admitted.at_capture`; it needs no future `At`, receiver-change derivation
or target-validation premise. Original validity and authentication of the
saved/closing interface bounds remain explicit inputs. The construction is a
proof of generation; resource-family witnesses use classical choice, so it is
not advertised as an executable inference algorithm.

[SourceConsumingLeafCapture.lean](SourceConsumingLeafCapture.lean) connects this
route to the actual selected stored clause and its recorded offered-mode
contract. Existing selection and snapshot lemmas derive a valid capture
certificate, admitted canonical capture metadata and canonical metadata for
every permitted disposal. An actual request example instantiates that boundary.
Other examples retain a waiting computation whose handler-bound snapshot is
provably different from the absent snapshot, extend it through a fresh resource
with an actual read, and reject an already-consumed owner.

This removes eager intermediate checking as an obstacle for saved and closing
operation-source views. It does not generate views for richer saved annotations
that invoke other owners or contain selected disposing requests. Deriving those
cases from initial admission, retaining evidence at every reachable request,
and broader-policy finite-execution integration remain open. No operational
rule, normative Ash semantics or Core implementation changes here.

### Rich source rechecking at continuation use

[SourceConsumingUseAdmission.lean](SourceConsumingUseAdmission.lean) defines
`AtUse`, a structural judgment over the existing consuming body and the original
captured source. Its sequence, choice, handler and cleanup rules accumulate the
actual caller without recompiling dormant saved code. Cleanup retains its
explicit dependency-coverage premise. The resource rule extends the world of
the original annotations and adds the builtin frame to the caller. It does not
validate saved source at intermediate handler contexts.

At a resume or dispose leaf, `AtUse` requires the existing `ReceiverChange`
derivation from the corresponding original source to the full caller at that
leaf. Those rules recursively inspect actual source, including other owner
invocations and fresh disposing requests. They take primitive checks and
structural recursive evidence, not target `Valid`, `Local` or `Pending` proofs.
The original context supplies original validity; `Body.BoundCheck` separately
supplies clause operation checks, rights and owner availability. Disposal also
retains its independent protection and closing-route requirements.

`AtUse.generate_source` reuses `ReceiverChange.compile_retaining` at the leaves
and assembles the existing `Generated` correspondence through the body. Saved,
closing and waiting snapshots remain exact. `initial_source` derives the
clause-side checks from initial `Admitted` evidence while retaining `AtUse` as
an explicit additional structural obligation. `AtUse.world_weaken` reuses
receiver-world transport; composition of the original context maps handles the
resource binder without choosing a replacement source annotation.
`AtUse.provide` now proves that structural provider insertion anywhere in the
caller preserves an existing use derivation for arbitrary captured source.
Its induction follows all consuming-body constructors. Resume and disposal
reuse the new receiver rule and the original context's checks; nested handlers,
cleanup and resource binders lift the same insertion. This discharges provider
transport without a second capture or scheduling proof. Handler and cleanup
interference still require their own source-derived conditions.

Local clause admission alone cannot discharge that additional obligation.
`MissingCaptureContract` in
[SourceConsumingUseAdmissionExamples.lean](SourceConsumingUseAdmissionExamples.lean)
proves a counterexample using the existing compiler: a clause installs an empty
E handler and resumes, declaring an empty continuation interface. `Admitted`
accepts that declaration, but the actual saved source requests E. The masking
clause has no `AtUse` derivation for that valid original source. Declaring the
actual E requirement makes the existing clause checker reject it. This is a
failure of the implication from clause-local admission to contextual admission.
`empty_handler_not_source_typed` also proves that full `SourcePlannedSources`
typing rejects this empty handler whenever E's signature contains operation 0:
the existing coverage premise requires a clause for it. Thus this example
cannot refute admission based on the full source judgment, or justify adding a
new source contract on its own.

The stronger source premises also have an admission limitation.
`ClauseRowAdmission.UncheckedTemplate` in the same example module proves that
`Expression` types a handler for E operation 0 around `resume`, with complete
operation coverage, port typing, one-shot use and hereditary declarations for
both modes. The former unrestricted `Body` rule rejects it for the stated
continuation contract, regardless of its checking signature;
`nested_unrestricted_body_rejected` retains that exact old-rule result.
Unrestricted `Rows` quantifies over every template store. Its invocation interface accepts a stored E operation 1 when the
original caller supplies that operation; the newly installed operation-0
handler then masks it. The actual source signature has no E operation 1.
This is a proved admission restriction caused by an unauthenticated template,
not a reachable well-typed program violating safety.

Consequently, unrestricted `Rows` cannot supply the intended general admission of
nested handlers around continuation use. The source connection must constrain
its template quantification by authenticated source information, or supply a
replacement structural interface with that information. The existing recursive
requirement checker and its soundness proof remain reusable. This evidence does
not establish that operation-signature authentication alone suffices for
cleanup-route preservation or general `AtUse`; those remain separate parts of
the same admission obligation. Finite interface inclusion already supplies the
operation-source case.

`Rows` now has an explicit template-source parameter. Its default retains the
unrestricted rule. `Rows.instantiate` requires evidence that the actual store
satisfies a relative certificate's source parameter; the existing finite
contextual derivation still supplies the checked requirements and row bound.
`AuthenticatedTemplate` in the same example module constructs such a relative
certificate for the handler-around-resume case. Its source contract requires
lookup of the exact saved template, an existing structural `Outward` derivation,
and a finite bound containing only E operation 0 in both protection modes. The
valid operation-0 store instantiates this certificate. The earlier operation-1
store cannot satisfy its source contract. There is no target-body validation or
future execution premise. `Outward` excludes further owner invocations, so this
is a local repair, not general recursive admission.

The hereditary source judgments now use `Rows` relative to `SourceStore`
for their operation signature. This includes declared, dependency, planned and
annotated source bodies; their offers retain the same source-relative premise.
`SourceStore` witnesses structural `StoreModeSource`, exact normal resume-body
certificates and `StoreClosingRecords`, together with `StoreAnnotation` relating
those resume and disposal lists to the actual checking store. These judgments retain legacy source
evidence and admit mixed value/unwind boundaries and lexical closing summaries.
It is indexed by the clause header's owner and contract, and the witnessed
source registry must contain that exact contract.
This ties input and answer types, demands, rows, protection and effect interfaces
to the same owner. It does not require successful checking or future execution.
`SourceStore.resume_template` reuses record certification to recover the selected
saved source at the header's exact input and resumption demand, its relation to
the actual annotated body, and an exit boundary equal to its answer or unwinding.
The capture proofs obtain the registry equation from the same fresh-owner
insertion that constructs the source and closing records, including the path
without a new closing record. Erasure preserves the owner contract as well as
the operation signature.

The contract index matters: the former store-only predicate could use a source
segment expecting a function argument when checking a header that accepts
`unit`. That function's latent row could contain an operation absent from the
source signature. Thus existential source provenance alone did not establish
the intended connection to the clause's continuation type. The registry equation
repairs that missing connection; it does not assert that all remaining latent
operation or receiver checks follow from it.

The local interface also excludes an active occurrence of its newly allocated
owner from the receiving tail. Without that condition, consuming the owner can
change an unrelated protection marker in the abstract tail. The
`CleanupTailFreshness` regression in
[SourceConsumingUseAdmissionExamples.lean](SourceConsumingUseAdmissionExamples.lean)
uses an authenticated empty saved continuation and a typed effectful cleanup
around resumption. A tail that repeats the allocated owner passes the old resume
and advertisement checks, then fails the callback export after consumption.
The fresh concrete tail succeeds. `cleanup_resume_rows` now supplies a general
row certificate for that requirement form when the saved continuation has no
additional owner demand; the literal clause receives hereditary body admission.
Actual capture interfaces derive the new condition from their existing
allocation freshness and ownership decomposition. This changes source checking,
not the operational stack or Core semantics.

This connects source-relative row contracts to actual allocation. It does not
prove that every intended nested-handler body has such a contract, or that
operation-signature authentication suffices for receiver preservation. General
initial admission still has to derive `AtUse` and preserve its evidence through
all transitions. The row interface has not been substituted for that obligation.

For an outside-owner call whose saved or closing annotation has an authenticated
operation view, `Expression.resume_from_bound` and `dispose_from_bound` in
[SourceScheduledHandlerInterfaceAdmission.lean](SourceScheduledHandlerInterfaceAdmission.lean)
derive the receiver-change premises from finite interface inclusion and caller
checks. They reuse the original permission, phase and disposal-route evidence,
and retain the arbitrary waiting annotation. The existing outside-owner,
resource and closing-callback examples now use this derivation. This covers
operation-interface callees; recursively richer callees and general selected
disposing requests still require the broader admission connection above.

[SourceConsumingUseCapture.lean](SourceConsumingUseCapture.lean) connects this
judgment to the selected stored clause, existing capture certificate and
canonical capture/disposal snapshots. It reuses stored-source selection,
nested-bound admission and the existing snapshot theorem. It adds no new
operational capture or ownership proof.

[SourceConsumingUseAdmissionExamples.lean](SourceConsumingUseAdmissionExamples.lean)
checks captured code that requests E and then resumes outside owner37 under the
previous temporary-mask arrangement for owner19. Its saved annotation has no
operation-source view and has a provably non-absent snapshot. A fresh resource
with an actual read precedes the same consuming body, reusing that body's
existing initial admission. A separate closing callback resumes owner37 during
disposal of owner19; the callback also has no operation-source view. The existing
fresh-disposer example reuses its original structural rechecking proof. A
consumed outside owner is rejected, and an actual request instantiates the
stored-clause theorem to produce an allocator certificate.

This removes operation-only compaction and eager intermediate checks from the
structural clause compiler. It does not derive all `AtUse` leaves from initial
program admission. Queued source and actual focus/return integration are
provided below. General derivation at reachable requests, reconstitution after
arbitrary receiver changes and broader-policy finite execution remain open.
The earlier `At` APIs remain unchanged; neither a general translation between
`At` and `AtUse` nor full initial-program safety is claimed.

### Queued consumption-time source at focus and return

[SourceConsumingUseQueued.lean](SourceConsumingUseQueued.lean) connects `AtUse`
to source records with explicit current owner cuts and caller interfaces.
`UseQueuedBody` retains the original captured-source context separately from
that current receiver. Its fields are the actual body, exact bound origin,
structural use-site admission, nested declaration admission and independent
clause checks. This permits an intermediate masking caller without demanding
that dormant saved code validate there.

Source inversion and `Body.plug` reuse the existing focus/recomposition syntax.
`UseQueuedBody.focused` covers the existing `Focused` relation: an operation
prefix queues its consuming remainder, while a pure pending frame leaves the
consuming body current. `UseFocusedSource.child_valid` constructs the actual
child annotation, using existing neutral code expansion for the latter case.
Return constructs the plugged source record and its bound equality from the
record on the actual plain frame; successor admission is not supplied anew.

[SourceConsumingUseTransport.lean](SourceConsumingUseTransport.lean) transports
`AtUse` through permission extension and phase changes by induction, reusing
`ReceiverChange.transport` and its phase specialization at consuming leaves.
World extension commutes with both context maps, including fresh-resource
bodies. `UseQueuedBody.transport` composes permission, phase and world changes
on the retained source, nested declarations, finite checks and bound index.
The finite check derives equality of the selected owner's existing permission
entry. Phase transport preserves availability of every owner in the original
source scope; preserving only the selected owner's availability is insufficient.

`UseQueuedBody.generate` obtains source validity, exact current bounds and the
original continuation correspondence from the consumption-time compiler.
`CanonicalPayload` adapters reuse existing code normalization to compile these
records at canonical indices and recompose them on return. They retain the
original source payload and prove expanded code, exact canonical current bounds
and bound admission. Normalization is not asserted to preserve an unnormalized
`Generated` index unchanged.

[SourceConsumingUseReceiver.lean](SourceConsumingUseReceiver.lean) retains a
`UseQueuedBody` together with a structural `Expansion` from its recorded
receiver to the actual receiver. `UseReceiverBody.generate` reuses neutral
compilation, with exact current bounds. Successive expansions compose by the
existing `Expansion.trans` theorem. Focus retains the same path for queued
source and adds the actual pure frame when the consuming body remains current.
Return reconstructs the source record at that actual receiver. This closes the
local neutral-receiver connection without reconstructing `AtUse` at every
administrative frame. It does not allow insertion of a different handler or
assert equality of every saved annotation after neutral compilation.

[SourceAnnotatedStoredUseQueued.lean](SourceAnnotatedStoredUseQueued.lean)
connects the record to actual typed focus and plain-return steps. It reuses the

accounting and completion preservation. All ten runtime focus forms share the

operational transition. These theorems now take `UseReceiverBody` and retain
`UseReceiverFocused`, so the source cut can differ from the actual receiver by
the recorded neutral expansion. An unchanged receiver uses `.at_receiver`.

[SourceConsumingUseHandlerEntry.lean](SourceConsumingUseHandlerEntry.lean)
adds source-directed handler entry. `AtUse.handler_body` inverts the parent's
structural rule. The child retains the same original captured context, extends
its recorded cut and caller by the entered handler, and inherits the parent's

the existing neutral path under that handler. The `EnteredHandler` relation

plans differ from checking witnesses by their existing signature equality.
This derivation does not require saved-source validity at the intermediate
caller or a newly supplied admission proof for the child.

[SourceAnnotatedStoredUseHandlers.lean](SourceAnnotatedStoredUseHandlers.lean)
connects that descent to actual typed packet installation and execution. The
execution theorem takes the same explicit action witness for the initial typed
state and source record, and returns both at the same successor. Runtime
ownership, access, name and completion accounting reuse the established handler
entry assembly. The existing declaration-retention law remains a premise; this
does not prove it for arbitrary declaration policies or establish source
coverage for every pending position.

[SourceConsumingUseTransitions.lean](SourceConsumingUseTransitions.lean) reuses
the four `Body.Reduction` rules for binding, application and branch selection.
`Body.reduced_source` determines the actual surviving source; the new judgment
and finite check follow by inversion. `UseReceiverBody.computed` retains the

connects this result to typed computation and full execution with the same

The transition module also derives cleanup and resource children. Cleanup

operation annotation valid under the actual running receiver, and retains

[SourceAnnotatedStoredUseEntries.lean](SourceAnnotatedStoredUseEntries.lean)

now carries both derived records through full execution. The source context and

Existing entry assembly supplies ownership, access, name and completion

[SourceConsumingUseCaptureRecords.lean](SourceConsumingUseCaptureRecords.lean)
constructs the selected clause's `UseQueuedBody` from its `AtUse` derivation and

[SourceAnnotatedStoredUseCapture.lean](SourceAnnotatedStoredUseCapture.lean)
packages that concrete evidence in the existing allocator's `ClauseEvidence`
interface. Exact handler-packet, cut and selected-clause uniqueness identify the
source witnesses with the actual allocator's witnesses. Both runtime capture
branches therefore return the new source record beside the actual typed
successor and exact owner-inventory extension. The theorem does not assume a
source invariant for the successor or add a new ownership induction.

[SourceAnnotatedStoredUseExecutionCapture.lean](SourceAnnotatedStoredUseExecutionCapture.lean)
connects the same result to full execution through `assemble_capture`.
`AtPackets.capture_use_step` now chooses the source/action witness already stored
in the execution invariant. On the bounded packet route it extracts declaration
source and its bounds check from admitted stored packets, then uses
`Declarations.selected_source` to identify the selected body. These are no
longer separate caller inputs. `StackBounds.Admitted.capture` also supplies
packet admission at the actual successor; ticket allocation leaves the resource
world unchanged. It reconstructs canonical original capture/closing
source and derives its snapshot origin, the selected clause's disposal
permission, waiting-scope requirements, and owner freshness. The separate
