`absent` and `aligned` inputs have been removed. Physical allocation freshness
and the stored-packet admission, bounded route and physical/planned selection
inputs remain explicit. `AtPackets.capture_plan` derives the offered contract,
dependency mode, saved/waiting plan cut and selected body from the current
source and physical cut at the exact stored packet. It reuses source splitting,
capture-guard inversion and ordered clause lookup; it does not require `AtUse`.

The same allocator returns the typed and full execution successors with the
same owner-inventory result. The event's operation-port lookup now fixes the
concrete successor configuration in the theorem statement, rather than returning
an existential configuration and a shape equation. It returns one admitted successor snapshot used
by both successor judgments, with `Captured owner snapshot.normalize nextSnapshot`
and admitted stored packets. The snapshot is extracted from the existing
capture payload; no new admission premise or capture induction is added.
Existing normalization preserves incoming snapshot admission. The payload also
retains the selected body's source record and resumption/closing metadata.
The `AtUse` premise checks the selected body against the reconstructed context.
It remains an independent source obligation, so this theorem does not yet derive
request-site admission from an initial program or establish complete source
retention through execution.

[SourceConsumingUseConsumption.lean](SourceConsumingUseConsumption.lean)
activates the saved or closing source at a consuming leaf. Inversion of `AtUse`
supplies the original structural receiver checks, and the independent finite
check supplies the permission and caller requirements. Existing receiver
compilation and retained-source recomposition construct the whole successor
source tree, including callbacks and dormant branches, with exact original
bounds. `UseReceiverBody` also activates source after its recorded neutral
receiver changes, using the actual owner cut and a `Retained.Neutral` relation
for the resulting metadata. That neutral relation alone does not identify a
particular runtime snapshot.

[SourceBoundDisposalRecords.lean](SourceBoundDisposalRecords.lean) completes the
record-movement counterpart of capture and resumption for disposal. It reuses
the existing source-record split and closing traversal. Saved pending code is
dropped; saved callbacks retain their original values, order and multiplicity;
caller and waiting records survive. This includes every recursive dormant
branch. `Discarded.carry_records` applies directly to the actual disposal
snapshot relation. Its ordered-filter result does not assert that arbitrary
payloads are valid at their new receiver.

[SourceBoundConsumptionSelection.lean](SourceBoundConsumptionSelection.lean)
authenticates the consuming source cut against that snapshot relation. Existing
owner lookup and forest append injectivity identify the cut's caller, saved
forest and waiting tail. A shared elimination proof then identifies both
resumption and disposal metadata from uniqueness of the original live owners
and equality of the original bound data. The bound split/join lemma concerns
data representation; the existing operational ownership proofs are unchanged.

[SourceConsumingUseConsumptionSnapshots.lean](SourceConsumingUseConsumptionSnapshots.lean)
uses those identities to place the activated source at the exact `Resumed` or
`Discarded` successor. The input record has a consuming leaf and an exact
current cut. Separate premises identify its saved bounds, operation-only caller
bounds and waiting bounds with the original snapshot. Disposal additionally
uses the original saved snapshot's canonical closing projection. The result is
full retained capability source, valid after spending the owner, whose bound
projection equals the successor's pending snapshot. It does not construct a
new `AtUse` record for every source position.

[SourceAnnotatedStoredUseConsumption.lean](SourceAnnotatedStoredUseConsumption.lean)
connects both activations to actual typed consumption. Source owner uniqueness
comes from the existing frame realization and runtime inventory: recursive live
tickets are an ordered sublist of owned tickets. The existing consumption trace
identifies the spent phase map with the actual successor's available owners.
[SourceAnnotatedStoredUseExecutionConsumption.lean](SourceAnnotatedStoredUseExecutionConsumption.lean)
then reuses full execution assembly for resumption and disposal, sharing the
explicit action witness with the original consuming record. Both results retain
all moved payloads and construct valid retained source at the same successor,
with exact pending bounds. Resumption uses its saved/caller permutation; disposal
uses the ordered callback filter. These connections still require original
a combined consuming-source/metadata record, as strengthened below. Its
structural neutral movement determines the exact destination bounds. Maintaining
usable source records throughout arbitrary capture/restoration remains part of
the global invariant obligation.

[SourceConsumingUseQueuedExamples.lean](SourceConsumingUseQueuedExamples.lean)
queues the supplying inner handler under the empty outer E handler, retaining
the earlier rich captured code that will invoke outside owner37. The intermediate
E requirement is proved false, while the queued source still generates valid
code with its exact bounds. Both focus alternatives, ordinary return and
canonical return are checked. Existing generic record capture and resumption
preserve the payload itself; the recovered record generates code at the restored
receiver with its additional spent marker using neutral expansion. It retains
that path through return, current-child focus and a second neutral insertion.
The transport examples also extend the permission registry, retire unrelated
owner88 and enlarge the resource world, then generate and recompose the same
queued source. A negative theorem rejects retiring outside owner37, which the
original saved code still invokes. Handler-entry examples derive the two
successive child records from one parent record, compile both children, and
repeat the descent after a neutral restoration. The outer entry has an exact
bound-snapshot witness. The record
movement example tracks this designated payload, not complete source coverage
of every code position or a whole typed execution trace.

These are local computation, focus/return, entry, capture and consumption
connections. They do not derive `AtUse` at every reachable request, prove usable
source-record coverage and metadata alignment for every reachable queued
position, or establish broader-policy finite-execution safety from initial
admission alone. The operational ownership proofs are reused unchanged.

[SourceConsumingUseTransitionsExamples.lean](SourceConsumingUseTransitionsExamples.lean)
reuses the rich masking source for binding and application reductions, two
branches with different annotation shapes, and resource allocation after a
neutral restoration. The effectful-cleanup fixture checks both its child and
callback at the actual receiver and rejects an omitted cleanup dependency.

The current connections for this source-record representation are:

| Transition family | Checked connection | Remaining boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ordinary computation | All four reductions, typed state and full execution, sharing the action witness | Initial and reachable source coverage |
| Focus and plain return | Source reconstruction at typed and full-execution successors, including neutral receiver paths | General capture/restoration of the queued records |
| Source-directed handler entry | Child descent, exact packet installation and full execution | Initial coverage and the existing declaration-retention premise |
| Cleanup and resource entry | Child descent and full execution; exact callback check or fresh-world mapping at the same typed successor | Initial and recursively retained source coverage |
| Fresh capture | Selected source record and exact capture/disposal bounds at the actual typed and full-execution successor; existing ownership proof reused | Request-site structural evidence and original source/bounds alignment remain explicit premises |
| Resumption and disposal | Full execution activates retained source from the combined record at the actual neutral receiver, with exact successor bounds, phase equality and all-record movement | Derive usable recursive source-record coverage across arbitrary restoration and at later requests |

### Consuming source with actual metadata provenance

[SourceConsumingUseMetadata.lean](SourceConsumingUseMetadata.lean) records one
original captured bound tree, equality of each permitted resumption projection
to that tree, equality of each permitted closing projection to its canonical
closing, and structural neutral movement from the original caller/live/waiting
metadata to the actual pending data. This is a data correspondence invariant.
It contains no assumption that a future source or execution is valid.

Source-directed handler, cleanup and resource frames extend both the source
caller and actual metadata. Administrative pure frames, pure completion frames
and spent history extend only the actual receiver. Permission extension, phase
restriction and resource-world extension retain the same correspondence, using
the existing context and annotation transport laws.

[SourceConsumingUseAligned.lean](SourceConsumingUseAligned.lean) pairs that
invariant with the existing `UseQueuedBody`. Its `at_receiver` derives the
receiver expansion from metadata movement and the existing owner-cut
reconstruction; no separate receiver-expansion field is assumed. Computation
and plain return produce a successor with the same pending correspondence.
Focus retains the combined record on the consuming remainder, or on the current
consuming child beneath its actual pure pending frame. Handler, cleanup and
resource descent preserve the combined record, as do independent permission,
phase and world changes. The operation-prefix case keeps its existing source
interface; it is not falsely treated as a consuming body.

[SourceConsumingUseAlignedSnapshots.lean](SourceConsumingUseAlignedSnapshots.lean)
connects these records to actual handler, cleanup and resource entry snapshots.
Selected-clause capture initializes the combined record from
`Context.of_request_bounds`, which supplies both original saved metadata and
canonical closing metadata. The same original split constructs the actual
`Captured` snapshot, with the generated clause's admitted annotation. The
request-site `AtUse`, capture-source evidence and source/snapshot equality
remain inputs. This result does not derive them from an initial term.

[SourceScheduledNeutralActual.lean](SourceScheduledNeutralActual.lean) closes a
separate metadata transport obligation. `Retained.expand_neutral_at` takes a
given structural movement to the actual destination bounds and constructs valid
retained source whose projection equals those exact bounds. The earlier
`expand_neutral` constructs a destination with neutral provenance but does not
identify it with a separately supplied runtime snapshot. The strengthened proof
follows the given metadata relation, reusing existing code and receiver
transport. Its operation-only case uses the proved fact that neutral movement
preserves absent bounds. It covers callbacks and dormant saved captures without
replacing their original annotation values.

[SourceBoundNeutralOwners.lean](SourceBoundNeutralOwners.lean) now decomposes
the actual bound data at the selected owner. It reuses the owner-cut
reconstruction and metadata split, retaining one identical captured bound tree
on both sides. A structural induction tracks only the changed caller and
waiting data. Prefix and append composition retain the original annotations.
[SourceBoundNeutralConsumption.lean](SourceBoundNeutralConsumption.lean) uses
that decomposition and the existing unique-owner snapshot-cut theorem to prove
neutral correspondence through actual `Resumed` and `Discarded` events.
Resumption moves the original captured data ahead of the changed caller and
waiting data; disposal uses its canonical closing projection above the running
boundary. No target-source validity or scheduling premise is added.

[SourceConsumingUseAlignedConsumption.lean](SourceConsumingUseAlignedConsumption.lean)
combines those actual movements with the existing consuming-leaf compiler and
`expand_neutral_at`. Both `UseAlignedBody.resumed` and `discarded` now construct
valid full retained source whose projection equals the actual successor's
pending data, even after neutral receiver changes. The runtime integration in
[SourceAnnotatedStoredUseConsumption.lean](SourceAnnotatedStoredUseConsumption.lean)
and [SourceAnnotatedStoredUseExecutionConsumption.lean](SourceAnnotatedStoredUseExecutionConsumption.lean)
uses the combined record directly. The source cut belongs to the original
source forest; separate exact-receiver, saved-origin and pending-equality
arguments are no longer required. Actual owner uniqueness and the successor's
phase map still come from existing runtime proofs.

The existing typed and full-execution source connections now retain this
combined record for computation, focus/plain return and handler/cleanup/resource
entry. Their runtime assembly proofs are reused in place. The capture payload
`CapturedUseBounds` also retains the combined record, through the existing
allocator and full-execution capture theorem; its exported resumption and
canonical disposal facts are preserved. Focus returns the combined record in
its existing current-child/queued-remainder split, with metadata for the exact
pending tail. These are local transition theorems, not a proof that every state
has all the required records.

[SourceCodeRecords.lean](SourceCodeRecords.lean) now derives concrete code records
at every pending body, callback and dormant saved branch of valid retained
source. Each record contains its source annotation, current validity, exact
bound projection and receiving forest. The structural `AtReceivers` judgment
places ordinary code at its waiting suffix, callbacks at that suffix under a
running marker, and dormant saved code at its own waiting suffix. No code slot
is optional. Operation interfaces construct operation-only records using their
existing checks; richer annotations retain their original code.

[SourceCodeRecordPositions.lean](SourceCodeRecordPositions.lean) proves that
positioned records compose and split at the existing forest boundaries. Actual
capture preserves the same records at the same receiving suffixes; the proof
reuses forest reassociation and the existing record movement relation.
[SourceCodeRecordCapture.lean](SourceCodeRecordCapture.lean) additionally applies
the existing capability transport theorem to every record when a fresh owner
is introduced. The annotations, receivers and bound projections remain fixed
while validity moves to the extended permissions and introduced phase. The
existing capture payload now includes these complete positioned records, so
both typed and full-execution capture retain them without a new input premise.
Resumption and disposal also return complete positioned records, constructed
from their activated source at the actual successor's available owner phases.
Those reconstructed records need not be identical to the old payload values.

[SourceCodeRecordReassembly.lean](SourceCodeRecordReassembly.lean) reconstructs
valid retained source with its exact original bound projection from positioned
code records and a pending schedule. The schedule supplies handler requirements;
code annotations and their validity come from the records. Its
`source_of_schedule_all` also reconstructs current and retained source directly
by mutual induction on the existing structural `Local` and `Pending` checks,
at the same receiver and owner phases. It uses the existing normalization to
match any prescribed canonical bound spine. Requests with disposal, recursive
owner invocations, callbacks and resource families are included; invocation
cases reuse the existing retained-source split. `CaptureSource.of_schedule`
then derives original capture and closing source with canonical metadata from
the request and pending checks, reusing the actual cut and normalization laws.

[SourceAnnotatedCodeRecords.lean](SourceAnnotatedCodeRecords.lean) derives those
checks from the existing runtime state's current code and stored segment.
`AtPackets.canonical_code_coverage` constructs complete source coverage for the
normalized snapshot without input code records. At a request,
`AtPackets.canonical_capture_source` also constructs the original capture and
closing source and proves its snapshot origin. Neither theorem assumes a
successful check under a changed receiver. `capture_capabilities` recovers the
selected clause's disposal permission and waiting-scope requirements from its
actual stored handler; `fresh_action_absent` reuses action registration and the
realized live-owner inventory. Full execution capture now consumes these derived
facts directly. The earlier `AtPackets.retained_source` retains the exact
unnormalized projection when positioned records are supplied.

[SourceCodeDecomposition.lean](SourceCodeDecomposition.lean) now recovers valid
child code from the existing bound computation and focus relations. Compact
operation-only annotations split their original request interface, including
conservative weakening; explicit sequence and choice annotations expose their
original children. Both forms retain the exact selected bound projections.
The pair-right focus case reuses neutral receiver expansion for its pure pending
frame. Plain return prefixes the queued code with the pure values prescribed by
the existing context grammar.

[SourceCodeCoverage.lean](SourceCodeCoverage.lean) combines current code at the
actual snapshot receiver with complete positioned pending records. Its
`computed`, `focused` and `returned` theorems derive this same coverage at the
actual successor. Focus constructs the queued record from the current source
and retains the old tail records. Return reads the head record at its proved
receiver and reconstructs the current source without a new queued-admission
premise. All four computation cases and four focus metadata cases are covered;
the latter serve all ten expression focus forms.
`ordinary_code_snapshot`, `focus_code_snapshot` and `plug_code_snapshot` in
[SourceAnnotatedCodeRecords.lean](SourceAnnotatedCodeRecords.lean) connect those
proofs to the existing typed runtime steps, retaining their source typing,
ownership, effects and exact snapshot movement. Plain frames add no owner, so
focus and return use the same available-owner phase map.

Canonical coverage and original capture/closing source now follow at every
state carrying `AtPackets`; they need no separate source-record invariant for
each transition family. This does not derive `AtUse`: a consuming clause can
change the ordered receiver, so source validity at its original receiver is
insufficient. Deriving that changed-receiver admission from declarations and
preserving the complete execution invariant remain open, as do complete initial
admission and the initial-to-finite-execution theorem. Ownership proofs and
current Core are unchanged.

### Finite requirements at a surviving interpretation boundary

[SourceScheduledSurvivingRequirements.lean](SourceScheduledSurvivingRequirements.lean)
derives receiver rechecking for operation-only source from finite requirements
at the surviving outside interpretation. `survivingRequirements` first removes
requests supplied by unchanged local source providers, then removes requests
supplied by cells retained in the closing prefix. User handlers in that prefix
are erased and cannot discharge the latter requirements.

`requirements_surviving_iff` proves an exact criterion for a fixed requirement
list, assuming its original internal checks passed. The proof composes the
existing replacement and closing factorization lemmas. A running marker does
not change this uniform interface check because it already requires both modes.
`Expression.surviving_operations` also permits narrowing conservative metadata,
provided a footprint of the same source justifies the smaller requirement list.
Actual requests cannot be removed merely to make the check pass.

The retained-source theorem uses `Interfaces.exposed`, which already accounts
for ordinary code, callbacks and dormant bodies. `check_closing_receiver_iff`
factors its receiver check without another traversal. `check_any_closing` proves
a stronger sufficient condition: if the surviving outside supplies a finite
bound containing the whole exposed interface, every closing prefix is supported.
This bound is checked at the outside, not against a chosen successful target
annotation. Repeated requirements are membership obligations, not counted
continuation permissions.

`ReceiverChange.surviving_operations` connects the factored condition to the
existing exact metadata compiler. `request_any_closing` additionally handles an
atomic saved request with either original annotation form. The partial caller
resumption example now uses that rule instead of checking its target body by
hand. [SourceScheduledSurvivingRequirementsExamples.lean](SourceScheduledSurvivingRequirementsExamples.lean)
checks ordinary, callback and dormant source together: a retained cell supplies
the callback's request even though the outside handler cannot. A stronger
outside bound covers arbitrary closing prefixes. Removing the handler for an
actual request rejects the fixed interface. This last result does not quantify
over every possible target annotation; the earlier partial-caller counterexample
provides that stronger rejection for its own fixture.

Protected-only selected requests use a separate existing contract theorem.
`Expression.crosses_cleanup_from_contract` in
[SourceScheduledProtectedRechecking.lean](SourceScheduledProtectedRechecking.lean)
derives the guard from three fields: disposal is disabled, a protected row exists,
and its body family exists. The original outside cut and bypassed-prefix proof
authenticate selection. Neither an ordinary mode nor a successful target capture
check is a premise. The protected callback and internal-disposal examples now
use this rule. It does not weaken the reusable operation interface, which still
requires both modes.

These proofs establish finite operation obligations at the changed receiver.
They do not establish the general recursive initial-source judgment: continuation
invocations, disposal-enabled selections and resource-dependent contracts must
retain their independent obligations. Construction of all structural rechecking
derivations from initial admission, their adoption by the broader execution
invariant, and complete callable/resource admission remain open. No Core alignment
or later continuation target is included.

### Canonical source annotations before rechecking

Exact retention of compact annotation data can prevent a valid change of
interpretation. [SourceScheduledCompactBoundsGap.lean](SourceScheduledCompactBoundsGap.lean)
proves this for `sequence(request E, pure)`: its original operation-only source
is valid under a resumptive handler. Adding a nearer disposing handler leaves
no valid target annotation with the original compact `.absent` bound shape.
This quantifies over every target annotation, not just the compiler's output.
The same computation with a structured sequence annotation rechecks through
the existing fresh-capture rule. Its bound lookups agree with the compact
source, although the annotation trees are unequal.

[SourcePlanBoundNormalization.lean](SourcePlanBoundNormalization.lean)
defines a canonical bound tree by expanding absent compound nodes along the
actual plan syntax. Every recorded handler bound remains unchanged, including
the distinction between missing metadata and a recorded declaration that does
not offer a particular mode. Induction proves exact equality of every original
bound lookup and separately preserves structural bound admission. Lookup
equality alone is not used to infer admission.

[SourceScheduledOperationExpansion.lean](SourceScheduledOperationExpansion.lean)
and [SourceScheduledSourceNormalization.lean](SourceScheduledSourceNormalization.lean)
prove normalization for the full mutual current/retained source grammar. The
result has three properties: validity at the original receiver, exact equality
to the canonical bound tree, and a structural `Expanded` judgment. Compact
`Code.operations` remains only at pure computations and atomic requests;
compact `Retained.operations` remains only at an empty forest. Every stored
branch recursively exposes its source structure, including dormant captures,
cleanup callbacks, continuation invocations and fresh-resource families.
Operation expansion reuses footprint and declaration-signature proofs; mutual
source normalization reuses the existing source induction. The declaration
policy must accept the existing recipe declarations.

`Expanded` is independent of capability validation. A checked counterexample
shows why it must be part of the returned witness: an operation-only retained
annotation for an atomic pending computation already has canonical bounds but
does not expose its retained frame. Bound normalization by itself cannot prove
that a classically chosen output has expanded source structure.

[SourceScheduledNormalizedRechecking.lean](SourceScheduledNormalizedRechecking.lean)
uses the actual chosen normalized source, with all three properties, as input
to the existing `Expression` compiler. Rechecking normalizes the compiled
result too, so its returned source remains expanded for subsequent rechecking.
Normalization is idempotent for plan bounds, retained bounds and snapshots;
this second normalization preserves the canonical tree exactly and therefore
preserves every original bound observation. The compact sequence counterexample
now rechecks through this generated source and returns an expanded target.
This normalizer is a proof-level witness construction using classical choice,
not an executable elaboration algorithm.

The same module prepares current and retained source against one admitted
normalized snapshot. Both sources retain the original plan, forest, world and
owner phases, align exactly with that snapshot, and carry `Expanded` evidence.
Normalization commutes with retained append and closing, and with the existing
capture, resumption and disposal metadata movements. These proofs reuse the
actual cuts and ordered saved/caller/waiting forests. They neither introduce a
new operational transition nor replace ownership preservation.

[SourceBoundNormalizedRecords.lean](SourceBoundNormalizedRecords.lean)
connects normalization to actual queued source records. `CanonicalPayload`
retains the original bound index, the actual original payload, and a proof that
its index normalizes to the recorded canonical index. Idempotence proves that
this record index is itself stable under normalization. The package does not
assert that an arbitrary payload inhabits its old type at a different index. The record
traversal preserves original payload values, code positions, order and
multiplicity. The existing capture and resumption record proofs then move these
packed values at normalized snapshots, preserving the original capture order
and resumption permutation. No new transition induction is needed.

For an actual `QueuedBody`, the packed original structural derivation generates
valid expanded code with exactly the canonical record's admitted bounds.
Recomposition reuses the existing queued-source `plug` proof for every return
context; an actual plain return yields a generated expanded annotation aligned
with the returned snapshot. Generation is at the queued source's recorded
context. Moving its payload does not establish validity at a changed receiver.

The broader runtime invariant has not yet adopted canonical annotations and
packed records. General derivation of `Expression`, receiver changes and
closing from initial source judgments remains open. Normalization removes the
demonstrated representation obstruction and now preserves queued source
provenance through capture, resumption and return; it does not establish
contextual admission at every reachable request or complete finite safety for
the broader declaration policy.

### Contextual capture from selected source

`At.generate_retaining` in

[SourceConsumingContextualCapture.lean](SourceConsumingContextualCapture.lean)

original request. Original source validity, the fresh owner
and compatibility of the offered disposal permission remain explicit inputs.

`SelectedSource.capture_retaining` combines the selected stored source's finite
requirements with its contextual `At` derivation. It produces the actual selected

body's exact bound projection, and constructs admitted bound data across the

[SourceAnnotatedStoredContextualCapture.lean](SourceAnnotatedStoredContextualCapture.lean)

[SourceConsumingContextualCaptureExamples.lean](SourceConsumingContextualCaptureExamples.lean)

The remaining obligation is to construct and retain contextual `At` and
rechecking derivations at every reachable request from initial source admission.
The new allocator theorem still receives those structural derivations and the
current source evidence explicitly. General finite execution under the broader
declaration policy, complete initial callable payload/result and support

## Annotation rewriting, substitution and selection

[SourcePlanRewriting.lean](SourcePlanRewriting.lean) defines signature-preserving
rewrites of literal clause witnesses. A rewrite preserves required continuation
actions, operation/dependency indices, ordered scopes and owner identities. It
maps pending code and cleanup plans throughout recursively saved forests.
Rewriting commutes with forest append and closing, and transports the exact
handler and owner cuts. Closed value substitution supplies one such rewrite by
the existing declaration-signature theorem. These facts concern checking
witnesses; they do not make arbitrary signature-preserving changes observationally
equivalent source programs.

[SourceScheduledAnnotationRewriting.lean](SourceScheduledAnnotationRewriting.lean)
transports the general `Code` and `Retained` annotations through those rewrites.
Mutual induction proves validation equivalent before and after rewriting, for
the same outward operations, action permissions and owner phases. This covers
recursive continuation uses, selected disposing requests, resources, cleanup and
both branches of dormant captures. Rejection is preserved as well as acceptance.
Existing operation-interface and declaration-signature transport supply the
leaf cases; recomposition equalities identify the actual target forests.

[SourceScheduledAnnotationSubstitution.lean](SourceScheduledAnnotationSubstitution.lean)
connects this transport to the established rich annotated-source substitution
proof. A closed substitution preserves both expression typing and independent
validation of its rewritten scheduling witness. Saved-plan registries retain
their scopes, their exact recursively captured plans, and their insertion law
under the same rewrite. Separately, `Selected.substitution` retargets the selected
literal clause while retaining its exact offered plans, for both modes and
arbitrarily many skipped clauses. That selection theorem does not require those
plans to belong to the older recipe grammar.

These results establish substitution and selection retention components. They
do not generate general consuming declaration annotations or replace the runtime's
recipe discipline. Full source admission and the integration of a broader
declaration judgment remain required; no new Core correspondence claim follows.

## Concrete capture annotations

[SourceScheduledCaptureAnnotations.lean](SourceScheduledCaptureAnnotations.lean)
defines `Capture` data for one actual selected clause. Its constructor retains
the exact source cut, the selected offered plans and a recursive `Code`
annotation for the new live continuation. It carries no successful scheduling
or future-body proof. Independent `Capture.Valid` checks that annotation using
the selected body's action permissions and the newly available owner.

`Capture.requirements` derives the allocator's previous universal selected-body
premise from this single validated annotation. The proof reuses exact cut
uniqueness, forest recomposition injectivity and clause-selection uniqueness;
it does not reprove continuation safety by enumerating captured stack shapes.
[SourceAnnotatedAllocationData.lean](SourceAnnotatedAllocationData.lean) exposes
`capture_typed_data_from_annotation`, which uses that result with the existing
typed allocation theorem. Source typing, the current request and retained-stack
checks, operation formation and freshness remain separate premises.

The regression example constructs its annotation from a clause that installs a
handler, performs two operations supplied by that handler and resumes the outer
continuation. `requestPrefixAnnotation` constructs the request annotations from
the request list; its validity theorem reuses the established requirement
checks. The example proves both annotation validity and rejection by the old
outer declaration recipe grammar. Its inner handler still uses the existing
declaration rules. This is source-plan evidence, not a complete initial-program
typing example.

The result connects concrete structural admission to typed allocation. It does
not yet generate annotations from general consuming declarations, change handler
installation, or replace the default runtime capture rule's recipe premise.
Those connections and complete initial-program admission remain open.

## Declaration policies and handler installation

[SourcePlannedChecks.lean](SourcePlannedChecks.lean) separates declaration
admission from scheduling with a `DeclarationPolicy` parameter. It states the
judgment on the actual clause plans. Recursive `Certified`, `Local` and `Pending`
judgments retain that parameter. Their existing erasure, certification,
selection and request-scheduling proofs now apply to every policy. Existing
clients use the contextual recipe policy by default.

[SourceScheduledChecks.lean](SourceScheduledChecks.lean) makes the same
separation for checks that retain actual forests. Handler admission and
recursive certification have separate policy parameters. `erase_all_with`,
`Local.erase_with` and `Pending.erase_with` require a proof that the admission
judgment supplies the corresponding certification judgment. The earlier
projection supplies this implication from recipe erasure. Continuation access,
phases, request guards, closing schedules and exact retained forests are
unchanged. These are parameters of the same structural judgments and source
syntax.

[SourceDeclarationPolicyTransport.lean](SourceDeclarationPolicyTransport.lean)
transports certification and scheduling along pointwise implications between
declaration judgments. The source, cuts, actions, phases and retained forests
remain identical.

[SourceScheduledCapabilityAnnotations.lean](SourceScheduledCapabilityAnnotations.lean)
now parameterizes `Code` and `Retained` by declaration evidence. Their independent
validation is unchanged. `compile_all_with`, `Code.compile_with` and
`Retained.compile_with` reuse the mutual compiler under declaration laws that
provide admission, recursive certification and compatibility with existing
operation interfaces. These laws concern static declaration evidence; they do
not assume successful execution or scheduling of a future selected body.
The transport theorem supplies the existing operation leaves. Ordered
recomposition and scoped invocation proofs now accept the same scheduling
parameters. Selected requests compile directly from their recursive closing
schedule through `request_from_schedule`; the earlier callback API remains a
specialization.

[SourceStructuralHandlerEntry.lean](SourceStructuralHandlerEntry.lean) connects
that source boundary to the actual annotated runtime frame. `handler_frame`
extracts declaration evidence from a structural handler check, installs it in
the typed frame for those exact clauses, and retains the body's check under the
new handler. Rich clause typing, coverage, operation modes and capability usage
remain independent premises. The existing annotated handler-entry proof now
uses this theorem with its current policy.

The policy parameter is an integration interface, not itself a completed
declaration admission rule. No arbitrary policy is claimed to guarantee safe
clause execution. General consuming declarations must still generate the
concrete annotations, justify the required policy implications and supply
capture validation. The default annotation APIs, rewriting/substitution clients
and full execution invariant still use the earlier recipe discipline.
Propagating a concrete broader declaration judgment through those clients and
deriving complete initial admission remain open.

## Consuming-clause annotation generation

[SourceConsumingClauseAnnotations.lean](SourceConsumingClauseAnnotations.lean)
defines source derivations before the captured forest is known. `Body` describes
resumption, disposal, operation prefixes, choice, handler installation, fresh
resource scopes and effectful cleanup around consumption. `Modes` and `Declarations` retain these
derivations for both offered modes. `Declarations.selected` reuses the existing
ordered selection relation to recover the actual selected body's derivation.
Neither these data nor their constructors contain a successful `Local`,
`Pending` or future-body validation premise.

`Body.annotate` takes the actual saved and waiting operation interfaces and
constructs the recursive capability annotation. Descending through handlers and
cleanup constructs the corresponding owner cut and retained caller annotation.
`Body.Check` separately checks operation availability, continuation rights and
phase, the disposal route, and the exact restored or closing receiving order.
`Body.annotate_valid` proves equivalence with validation of the generated
annotation by structural induction. `Body.compile` then reuses the existing
annotation compiler. `Body.check_available` proves that every accepted body
requires its owner to remain available.

[SourceScheduledInterfaceWorld.lean](SourceScheduledInterfaceWorld.lean)
preserves operation-interface data and checks under resource-world extension.
The resource constructor uses this result for saved code, closing callbacks,
the caller and the waiting tail. `Body.world_weaken`, `Modes.world_weaken` and
`Declarations.world_weaken` retain source derivations when evaluation allocates
resources; `Body.check_world_weaken` preserves their checks. Fresh binders use
the existing resource-world inclusion and fresh-name results. The universal
fresh-resource premise is the existing source rule, not an executable
whole-program decision procedure.

The handler example generates the earlier hand-written capture annotation:
install F, perform F twice, then resume E beneath F. The same derivation is
retained in the offered declarations and supplies the existing concrete capture
admission. A second example checks an effectful cleanup callback under F,
including its protected running scope. A negative example rejects consumption
of an already consumed owner despite operation availability.
A resource example introduces a fresh cell inside the consuming clause and
uses it in an effectful cleanup callback around resumption. Its generated
annotation compiles to the existing scheduling judgment for every fresh identity.

This completes annotation generation for these source constructors, not general
declaration admission. The generator currently takes operation interfaces for
saved and waiting code; recursive free continuation uses still require
integration. Inner declarations use the supplied policy,
whose default remains the earlier recipe discipline. In particular, this result
does not derive `Body.Check` at every capture from handler installation, install
the new declaration data as the runtime policy, or establish complete initial
admission. Those are remaining obligations of the one-shot target.

## Finite continuation operation bounds

[SourceScheduledInterfaceRequirements.lean](SourceScheduledInterfaceRequirements.lean)
extends the existing ordered-scope boundary proof to retained operation
interfaces. `Interfaces.exposed` collects the requests that reach the outside
of their actual retained suffix. Given the original check,
`Interfaces.check_replace_iff` characterizes every replacement receiver by
checking this finite list. Its proof reuses `requirements_outward` and
`requirements_transport`; internal handler selection and missing-operation
failures remain unchanged. `Interfaces.check_from_bound` allows a declared
superset by membership. Repeated requirements do not count continuation uses.

[SourceConsumingClauseContracts.lean](SourceConsumingClauseContracts.lean)
uses these bounds in `Body.BoundCheck`. This source-facing judgment traverses
the clause and its generated caller contexts. Resumption checks the declared
resume requirements at the restored receiver; disposal checks the close
requirements under the running boundary. It neither inspects the unknown saved
code nor assumes that the future selected body checks successfully.

`Body.check_from_contract` derives the concrete `Body.Check` by structural
induction. Its independent premises are inclusion of the actual exposed
requirements in the declared bounds, original retained checks for each allowed
action, the waiting-tail check and disposal protection. Resource cases reuse
world-extension and interface-invariance proofs. Continuation rights and phase
remain separate from operation availability.

The checked example restores a captured F request beneath a newly installed F
handler and reaches the existing scheduling kernel. The negative example shows
that supplying the clause's own F requests is insufficient when the captured
continuation requires an unavailable G operation.

This establishes the contract-to-capture checking implication. The structural
source rules below derive the clause-local contract checks. Authentication of
actual captured-interface bounds and execution retention remain separate.
General recursive retained
continuation annotations, the broader runtime declaration policy and complete
initial admission remain open. No Core correspondence or later continuation
mode is claimed by these results.

## Structural consuming-declaration admission

[SourceConsumingClauseAdmission.lean](SourceConsumingClauseAdmission.lean)
defines the inductive `Admitted` judgment on source clause derivations. Resume
and dispose leaves require their respective rights and expose the declared
continuation operation bounds. Sequence, choice and cleanup combine finite
requirements. A handler checks the operations it intercepts and passes the
remaining requirements outward. It also records bounds for its nested clauses
and checks that each available mode's resume bound covers the body requirements
remaining after interception, together with the declaration's requirements.
This conservative finite check covers resumptive interception; it does not
replace the separate disposal checks. A resource discharges its builtin operations;
weakening uses membership inclusion. These rules reuse the established
operation-footprint discipline and contain no future-body success premise.

`Admitted.bound_check` derives `Body.BoundCheck` by induction on that source
judgment. It keeps a check of the syntax-generated caller as its induction
invariant and reuses the existing handler, resource and passing-prefix lemmas.
`Admitted.at_capture` starts with an empty caller and proves the clause checks
under any captured prefix when its finite outer requirements are supplied by
the waiting scope. Neither theorem needs the captured continuation's code.
`Admitted.schedule` then combines the source derivation with the original
retained checks, authenticated interface inclusions and independent owner and
disposal facts to derive the existing scheduling judgment.

`ModeAdmitted` records the bounds and source derivation for an offered mode.
`DeclarationAdmitted` aggregates both modes and every actual clause.
`DeclarationAdmitted.selected` recovers the selected body, its bounds and its
share of the declaration's external requirements. World-extension proofs
retain all three judgments during resource allocation.

[SourceConsumingDeclarationSubstitution.lean](SourceConsumingDeclarationSubstitution.lean)
preserves declaration admission and selected offered-body evidence through
value substitution. Actual offered plans are retained. The proof reuses
preservation of required continuation actions and the existing
selection-substitution theorem; rich source typing remains independently
authenticated by its established substitution theorem.

[SourceConsumingDeclarationEntry.lean](SourceConsumingDeclarationEntry.lean)
packages this concrete structural evidence for the existing typed handler
frame. `install` retains it alongside the finite waiting-scope check, rich
clause typing, coverage, uniqueness and operation modes. The evidence also
transports through world extension and value substitution. This constructs an
actual typed frame; it does not change the default whole-state invariant.

The source-admitted example installs F, uses F twice and resumes a continuation
whose declared interface includes F. Its clause-local checking theorem applies
to any captured prefix, and a concrete capture reaches the existing scheduler.
A resource/cleanup clause also has a structural admission derivation. A missing
G requirement is rejected by source admission, reusing the earlier contract
counterexample.

The remaining boundary is precise: actual saved and closing interfaces must
be proved to fit the declared bounds, and that evidence must be retained by
request typing and full execution. The source generator still uses operation
interfaces for retained code; recursive free continuation uses require the
existing richer annotations to be integrated. Inner declarations use the
supplied policy, whose default is still the earlier recipe discipline. Neither
complete initial admission nor a broader default `State`/`Run` policy follows
from these results.

protection and closing-route checks remain independent.

`Bounded.schedule` combines source admission with this finite checker to derive
the actual post-capture schedule. `Bounded.capture_annotation` ties the result
to an exact cut and selected clause and constructs the concrete `Capture`

operation requirements, irrelevant bounds for unavailable actions, missing
captured operations and different ordinary/protected bounds.

[SourceConsumingTypedAllocation.lean](SourceConsumingTypedAllocation.lean)

[SourceScheduledInterfaceCuts.lean](SourceScheduledInterfaceCuts.lean) derives

`check_atCut` factors its normal check at the existing selected handler cut.
The split covers all retained frame constructors, including dormant captures.
`forClosing` derives the closing annotation from the same source and retains

`ClauseBounds.checkSource` checks the actual source-derived interfaces against

These results authenticate a particular capture when the finite check passes.
Request typing and preservation must still establish that check at every
reachable capture and retain the same bound annotations through the full

The default `State`/`Run` policy, recursive retained continuation integration
and complete initial admission remain open.

### Recursive resumption bounds

[SourceConsumingRecursiveBounds.lean](SourceConsumingRecursiveBounds.lean)

operands retain their pure sequencing prefix. This is a source-annotation
generator for the existing calculus, with no new execution relation.

`annotate_valid_iff` factors validation into the terminal operation-interface
check, unique owner names, each owner's resume permission and available phase,
and the receiver check when a call occurs. The proof uses induction on the
finite source chain. `annotate_trace` reuses the established phase-trace theorem
to account for that consumption order; it does not claim termination.
`annotate_valid_from_bound` reuses operation-interface transport to derive the
new receiver check from an original check and a finite declared bound.

`annotateSuffix` retains an actual suffix after the recursive prefix. A selected
handler must occur on this active spine to constitute a physical capture.
Its requirements combine with the terminal source through the existing ordered
interface-append law. Fresh outer-owner allocation preserves the distinct
nested owners' annotation checks.

`handlerAnnotation_valid` uses the existing structural consuming-clause judgment
to derive the checks for a handler installed around resumption. It generates
the recursive captured-source annotation from original evidence and the finite
bound. `handler_schedule_and_bound` derives both the existing scheduling
judgment and the selected nested mode's bound check for the terminal-and-suffix
operation summary. `capture_annotation` includes the value operand's pure
prefix and produces the existing allocator's `Capture` certificate for an
actual cut and selected clause. It assumes no successful future clause body.

The concrete example captures owners 23 and 31 at an active E boundary and
allocates owner 19 for the selected clause. That clause installs F and resumes;
the terminal source uses F and G, with G supplied outside. Checked negative
cases reject a missing G operation, an empty nested bound, a denied nested
resume permission and a repeated owner. The physical cut and nonempty capture
certificate are constructed explicitly.

This establishes the resumption-chain source form. General recursive retained
branches and calls to owners outside the captured segment still need
integration. The consuming-clause and allocator integration below uses this

`segment_annotations` extract initial annotations from the existing typed

This extraction establishes availability of annotations; it is not a rule for
choosing replacement bounds at each subsequent request.

The canonical `capture_typed_data_from_bounds` now takes the retained stack
annotations and lookup evidence. Its rich clause source is indexed by the

For the bounded route it accepts either source form described above and checks

The actual clause-mode evidence remains an independent premise. Both branches
return the established typed allocation result and admission of the same

This closes bound identity and retention for the individual capture theorem.
It does not yet install these annotations throughout the default `State`/`Run`

current Ash specification or Core implementation changes here.

### Exact selected-plan data and capture snapshots

[SourceAnnotatedAllocationData.lean](SourceAnnotatedAllocationData.lean)
now exposes `TypedClauseDataAtPlan`, which indexes the existing typed clause
certificate by the actual selected plans. `capture_typed_data_exact` retains
that index together with the actual source cut and selection derivation.
`capture_typed_data_at_cut` aligns them with a supplied cut and selection using
the established uniqueness and forest-recomposition proofs. Equal dependency
families alone are not used to equate plans. The annotation specialization
supplies the site checks from one validated source-generated annotation.

`TypedClauseDataAtPlan.allocated_body` retains that same plan through contract
refinement and closed payload substitution. `capture_step` applies the existing
source capture theorem at that plan, obtaining the actual raw step, the exact
owner increment, owner uniqueness, the phase-map equation and the substituted
source body. The original existential typed-data APIs delegate to these stronger
proofs; no new operational rule or ownership argument is introduced.

[SourceConsumingTypedAllocation.lean](SourceConsumingTypedAllocation.lean)
joins these results to installed packet admission. Its
`capture_typed_data_from_bounds_at_selected` returns typed data and admitted
current-bound metadata at the same selected plan and actual saved/waiting
forests. For the bounded route, it also returns the generated code annotation
whose exact projection is that metadata. For the inherited route, the metadata
is absent and its admission follows from the existing recipe-derived source
check. Both routes preserve the original handler packets through capture. The
older typed-allocation theorem projects from this result.

[SourceBoundCapture.lean](SourceBoundCapture.lean) defines `Captured` on source
snapshots. Its constructor takes the original saved and waiting annotations,
whose append is the original queue, and places those exact values under a live
owner. `capture_snapshot` reuses the retained split/recomposition theorem at the
actual source cut. `Captured.admitted` derives admission of both retained parts
from the original snapshot; only the new current clause needs its separately
proved source admission. Dormant captures and cleanup callbacks are retained
by the same structural split.

[SourceAnnotatedBoundCaptureData.lean](SourceAnnotatedBoundCaptureData.lean)
joins the exact typed clause, source-generated current bounds, original retained
metadata and admitted packet stack in `capture_snapshot_data`. This constructs
an admitted snapshot for the selected live forest without assuming successor
admission. The exact-plan typed certificate also supplies the raw capture and
substituted-body result after a compatible contract is allocated.

The exact-plan transport now reaches the runtime and combined execution
interfaces below. Bounded capture still needs its generated annotation joined
to those interfaces at the actual installed packet. Packet source typing must
agree with the rich answer and residual interfaces of the retained source
segment throughout execution. The finite source checks must also be derived
for every reachable capture, and general captured-source shapes remain beyond
the current chain generator.

### Exact clause evidence through runtime capture

[SourceAnnotatedCaptureInterfaces.lean](SourceAnnotatedCaptureInterfaces.lean)
now uses the exact typed clause certificate. `capture_interfaces_retaining`
keeps an already proved fact about the selected plan and its receiving forest
when aligning the actual source cut with the typed saved and waiting segments.
The `ClauseEvidence` parameter names this proof-transport interface; it is not
a source admission rule and supplies no proof by itself.

[SourceAnnotatedCaptureData.lean](SourceAnnotatedCaptureData.lean) stores the
same exact plan and fact in `CaptureData`. Its `allocated_retaining` theorem
keeps them through contract refinement and payload substitution. Both
[allocation branches](SourceAnnotatedAllocation.lean) use that certificate in
the original shared allocator. The branch that builds a closing plan carries
the fact through the existing closing-template certificate as well.

[SourceAnnotatedRuntimeCapture.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntimeCapture.lean)
returns an `AtPlan` successor and the retained fact at that very plan in
`capture_preserves_retaining`. Both the available-closing-plan and unavailable
branches reuse their previous runtime checks, effect inclusion and owner
accounting. The older existential `State` results project from these proofs.

[SourceAnnotatedRecipeCapture.lean](SourceAnnotatedRecipeCapture.lean)
still derives finite capture requirements from the original structural
recipes, while preserving the additional selected-plan fact. Its
[combined execution wrapper](SourceAnnotatedExecutionCapture.lean) now returns
an `AtPlan` with the same fact alongside the ledger, access, name, action and
completion invariants. The original `Run.capture_preserves` delegates to this
proof. This transport does not derive the bounded route's missing finite checks
or establish packet/source agreement.

### Admitted inherited snapshots through capture

[SourceAnnotatedBoundCapture.lean](SourceAnnotatedBoundCapture.lean)
instantiates the transport with the concrete `Captured` snapshot relation.
`AtPlan.capture_recipe_snapshot_admitted` applies when the source carries
structural recipe evidence and the selected installed packet records the
inherited route. It moves the original pending annotations beneath the new
live owner using `capture_snapshot`. The current clause has absent bound
metadata; its actual checked source supplies the declaration proof required
for that annotation. The theorem does not erase a bounded packet's recorded
bounds or assume an admitted successor.

The result joins the admitted snapshot to the actual combined `AtPlan`
successor. It retains the exact original installed packets: the returned packet
stack is heterogeneously equal to `stored.capture` at the physical cut. The
existing packet admission theorem, source declaration projection and raw
ownership proof supply these parts. `capture_recipe_progress_snapshot_admitted`
chooses a fresh owner from the existing finite ledger and reuses preservation.
Neither theorem needs a new ownership induction.

This closes the inherited-recipe case of the remaining capture constructor.
It does not close general bounded capture, whose packet/source agreement and
finite checks remain explicit work. Thus there are 20 fully connected raw
constructors and a connected inherited case of the twenty-first. The final
execution interface still needs installed packet admission for the other 17
snapshot rules, complete initial source admission and finite-run composition.
These results remain experimental; they change neither current Ash semantics
nor Core.

### Joint source typing at stored packets

[SourceAnnotatedStoredTyping.lean](SourceAnnotatedStoredTyping.lean) adds a
structural judgment joining runtime frames to their recorded handler packets.
`PacketSource.handler` checks `packet.plans` at the frame's rich answer and
residual interfaces and retains the declaration evidence for that same plan.
The other constructors follow the non-handler frame shapes. `Frame` pairs this
judgment with the existing typed frame; `Segment` shares each intermediate
rich interface through `nil`, `push`, `live` and `spent`, including dormant
saved segments. The actual packet stack is an index of the judgment.

This avoids comparing two independently chosen clause witnesses. A dependency
family or erased port does not determine a rich signature. The earlier frame
judgment existentially hides its clause plan, so equality of proof derivations
also cannot establish equality of those hidden plans. The joint judgment
instead requires source typing at the already recorded plan and shares the
rich interfaces by construction. `Frame.handler_source` projects that exact
source. `Segment.forget` supplies the original runtime judgment, preserving
its source, scheduling and owner requirements.

The joint judgment survives contract, permission and phase extension,
resource-world growth, and rechecking under a new receiving suffix. Input and
output effect-interface weakening also retain the same packet data. These
proofs reuse the established source transports and the existing segment
induction. The original annotated frame/segment contract transport now exposes
its declaration-policy parameters; its proof is unchanged.

[SourceAnnotatedStoredCuts.lean](SourceAnnotatedStoredCuts.lean) lifts physical
handler selection to this joint judgment. `capture_segments` returns the packet
identified by the original lookup, its source at the matching rich interface,
and saved/waiting judgments indexed by the original `stored.atCut` values.
It preserves the original forest, demand, record and requirement-recomposition
equations. `segment_split` and `segment_append` also split and recompose the
exact packet data at arbitrary physical boundaries. The proof follows the
existing structural cut/recomposition induction and reuses its forest and
requirement laws; there is no new operational or ownership argument.

[SourceAnnotatedStoredRegistries.lean](SourceAnnotatedStoredRegistries.lean)
transports the joint judgment when interpretation registries agree at retained
activations. The result is indexed by the existing packet transport, so handler
registration cannot silently replace recorded plans or ignore dormant branches.
It reuses the packet's exact source-transport theorem and the original runtime
registry theorem.

[SourceAnnotatedStoredCaptureData.lean](SourceAnnotatedStoredCaptureData.lean)
connects the joint cut to bounded and inherited clause generation.
`capture_snapshot_from_stored_source` derives the selected packet's declaration
source and clause modes from that cut, then applies `capture_snapshot_data`.
The former independent packet-source premise is absent from this interface.
The exact selected plan, generated current annotation, original pending split
and admitted captured packet stack remain the existing witnesses.

The stronger runtime state below now constructs this joint judgment at
handler installation and can start from the original empty-stack invariant.
The capture path below preserves it through allocation and closing records;
the other execution transitions remain to be connected. Finite capture-input
checks remain explicit and must be
derived from complete initial source admission. Local transport and
recomposition do not by themselves establish agreement at every reachable
state or complete bounded capture.

The other transitions and finite execution must retain the same stronger

admission follow from the existing stack split/append proofs. This metadata
operation grants no disposal permission; its plan is authenticated by the
execution theorem.

[SourceAnnotatedRuntimeDisposal.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntimeDisposal.lean)
derives the closing effect interface from the retained runtime certificate and
joins the snapshot result to the actual execution step. Its older `Run.discard_at`

[SourceAnnotatedBoundDisposal.lean](SourceAnnotatedBoundDisposal.lean) adds
snapshot and packet admission on that same successor. It covers supplied plans,
every actual access-checked disposal step, and source-derived progress. The
result retains `demand = owner :: remaining` and resource-world equality;
creating a closing owner does not allocate a resource.

The stronger snapshot connection now covers 20 of the 21 raw constructors.
Capture remains in this transition stage, including admission of the selected
clause body that starts executing. The count describes rule coverage, not
relative effort or milestone completion. Installed packet admission still
needs to join the other 17 snapshot transitions in the final interface. Initial
source admission, reachable-request bound acceptance and the complete
finite-execution connection remain open.

### Source-bound retention and installation

The handler constructor of `SourceScheduledCapabilityAnnotations.Code` now
retains optional `ClauseBounds` for its actual plans. Both `Body.annotate` and
`Body.annotateRecursive` attach the bounds recorded by the consuming source
derivation. Their generator laws establish exact equality with that data.
Older operation-only annotations can omit it; absence is distinct from an
annotated declaration whose selected operation or mode is unavailable.

[SourceScheduledBoundRetention.lean](SourceScheduledBoundRetention.lean)
proves exact lookup preservation under clause-witness rewriting at every
annotation path. The induction covers ordinary code, recursively retained
captures, caller segments, cleanup, conditional closing branches and fresh
resource openings. Path labels describe annotation children; they add no
language syntax. Reindexing retains operation order, ordinary/protected mode
choice and the recorded bound lists, including repetitions. Closed
substitution reuses this theorem. Signature-preserving rewriting alone does
not prove admission of an arbitrary rewritten declaration.

Checked examples distinguish nonempty ordinary and protected bounds beneath
a resource and cleanup, preserve repeated requirements, and retain both
missing metadata and unavailable operation results through rewriting.

[SourceConsumingAnnotationInstallation.lean](SourceConsumingAnnotationInstallation.lean)
connects these annotations to the existing runtime packet operation.
`installFromAnnotation` reads the bounds from the source annotation and has no
replacement-bound input. Missing metadata returns no bounded installation.
`enter_fromAnnotation` checks the declaration against those exact bounds and
reuses the actual handler-entry rule, packet admission and dispatch lookup.
The source observation and installed ordinary/protected lookup agree exactly.
This proves metadata coherence; rich expression-to-plan coherence remains a
separate source-typing obligation.

[SourceConsumingBoundResumption.lean](SourceConsumingBoundResumption.lean)
uses the existing split and append operations to move the saved packets ahead
of the caller and replace the selected live boundary by a spent boundary.
`resume_reconstructs` gives exact before/after data equations for any finite
caller prefix, including dormant branches. Packet admission is preserved.
`resume_cut_preserves_bounds` combines this result with the established full
source-state resumption theorem, retaining its exact ownership trace on the
same successor. It does not reprove source typing or ownership consumption.

These results close source-generation and rewriting loss, connect bounded
installation to the source data, and cover packet transport through capture
and resumption. The combined `State`/`Run` invariant must still retain current
and queued source annotations through every transition, connect their packets
to the richer declaration policy, and derive acceptance at every reachable
request. No general progress claim follows from merely guarding a request with
the finite bound checker.

[SourceScheduledChecks.lean](SourceScheduledChecks.lean) separates the

likewise covers all eight value-return forms and builtin replies. Ticket

proofs reconstruct the actual saved segment and caller. Disposal selects the
stored template at the exact owner cut, materializes its original annotated
callbacks and reuses the existing owner-record consumption proof. Both paths
preserve the shared runtime invariant and consume the selected owner once.

Resource and cleanup entry likewise retain these parameters through their

This generality removes an implicit restriction to the old recipe policy in
