### Bounds under a newly installed interpretation

[SourceConsumingReinterpretationBounds.lean](SourceConsumingReinterpretationBounds.lean)
exhibits a gap in capability-only handler installation. An F handler can offer
its requested operation and have an admitted resume-only clause with an empty
resume bound. If it captures a continuation containing an outward G request,
that bound check fails. Admission of the declaration and availability of F do
not establish acceptance of the captured continuation.

`Interfaces.exposed_append` proves the exact exposure law for recomposition:
the receiving suffix filters the prefix's exposed requests, then contributes
its own. The proof reuses the existing scope-append law and covers every
retained interface constructor. `Bounds.resume_recomposition` derives an
accepted resume-bound check for any retained source within a declared bound,
provided the filtered declared bound plus the caller's exposed requirements
fit the intercepting handler's bound. This premise uses finite bounds and
caller syntax. It does not inspect the unknown retained source.

`Body.handler` now records the nested `ClauseBounds`. `Admitted.handler`
checks a finite envelope against those bounds with `acceptsResume`.
`acceptsResume_lookup` derives coverage for the exact mode selected by ordered
lookup. `Admitted.handler_bounds` extracts that obligation even after outer
requirement weakening. Resource-world extension retains the same bound data
and source derivation; declaration substitution retains the offered bodies.

`Admitted.handler_resume_recomposition` specializes the general recomposition
law to a handler directly around resumption. Source admission supplies the
finite compatibility premise, so every operation-only retained source within
the declared resume interface passes the selected nested handler's resume
bound. The empty-bound counterexample is rejected by the source judgment
itself for any claimed outer requirements; an annotation containing G is
admitted. This is a proved source-admission and recomposition case, not a proof
of all machine transitions.

The nested declaration policy still supplies separate declaration evidence.
Its default structural recipes can now use the inherited runtime admission
route without manufacturing a new finite-bound clause proof. The
[source annotation compiler](#source-bound-retention-and-installation) now
retains the recorded nested bounds through rewriting and closed substitution,
and installation reads them from that annotation. Connecting this data throughout the current-expression and
runtime invariants, then preserving coverage through every execution step,
remains necessary for the broader progress theorem. Recursive continuation
calls under explicit reinterpretation bounds and complete initial source
admission also remain open.

## Source-derived entry annotation guards

Focusing and installation previously chose one annotated transition from a
valid source state. The source and runtime layers now expose the data needed
to check alternative supplied names and type annotations, and prove
preservation for every choice passing those checks. The existing progress
theorems choose canonical annotations and reuse these stronger results.

| Transition | Data extracted from the current source | Supplied choice and check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Focus | Reference input and output ports, actual context and scope | Any `PlainData` with the same context, scope and erased ports |
| Resource entry | Answer port and finite forbidden-name list | Any identity absent from both the resource world and forbidden list, and any answer type erasing to that port |
| Handler entry | Answer port, actual mode table, clause families and declaration requirements | Any activation absent from handler history and any answer type erasing to that port |
| Cleanup entry | Answer port and actual callback request list | Any fresh cleanup owner and any answer type erasing to that port |

[SourceScheduledFocus.lean](SourceScheduledFocus.lean),
[SourceScheduledResources.lean](SourceScheduledResources.lean),
[SourceScheduledHandlers.lean](SourceScheduledHandlers.lean) and
[SourceScheduledEntries.lean](SourceScheduledEntries.lean) supply the source
results. The focus theorem retains the same child and context plans for every
matching frame. Resource freshness reuses
`ResourceRequirements.checked_open_resource`: the extra forbidden list comes
from hidden requirement support, so freshness in the resource world alone is
not the stated sufficient condition. Handler metadata and cleanup requests are
selected before the caller supplies a fresh name or answer type. They are not
arbitrary caller-supplied tables or request lists.

[SourceScheduledRuntimeControl.lean](SourceScheduledRuntimeControl.lean) and
[SourceScheduledRuntimeEntries.lean](SourceScheduledRuntimeEntries.lean) join
those results with the existing completion, access, freshness and ownership
proofs. Their `focus_annotations`, `resource_annotations`,
`handler_annotations` and `cleanup_annotations` conclusions contain an actual
named/access-checked step and its preserved `Run`. Handler and cleanup entry
construct the source-selected frame records with the supplied identity and
answer type. The source cleanup theorem accepts any identity; the runtime join
adds the required owner-history freshness check.

The logical order matters: a current invariant determines annotation data;
then every supplied choice satisfying the finite data checks preserves it.
There is no premise asserting successful checking of the whole successor or
future execution. The proofs reuse the original source decomposition and
recomposition bodies, with their old existential progress results derived as
corollaries.

These results do not yet authenticate annotation provenance along an entire
execution. Some type choices remain existential inside the current source
invariant, and unannotated code does not supply those choices. The final event
interface must retain their source provenance; it cannot take arbitrary port
pairs or mode tables and call them source annotations. Six focus forms now
resolve their ports through fixed signatures, continuation contracts, or context
and stack shape, and enter `RetainedStep` below. Application, binding and cleanup
focusing and installation still need that connection.
Capture's changing contract and saved-plan registries,
general declaration admission, and complete initial-term admission remain open.

## Source type choices and finite hints

[SourceFocusAnnotationGap.lean](SourceFocusAnnotationGap.lean) identifies an
annotation omission in the experimental `Code` representation. Consider the
ordinary binding `let x = (let y = unit; fn z => unit); unit`. The unused lambda
parameter can have type `Unit` or `Integer`. `program_source` constructs both
rich source derivations with the same initial code, final `Unit` result,
requirements and plan signature. `scheduled`, `admitted`, `completion` and
`initial_run_with_choice` connect the example to all five current initial
admission premises, reusing the existing initial-state theorem. `actual_focus`
selects its nonvalue initializer. The child's function port differs between
the two choices.

`no_unique_binding_port` proves that no single port agrees with every admitted
choice for that fixed code and plan. This does not prove that type inference is
impossible or that either program execution is unsafe. It rules out assuming
that the existing unannotated representation already determines the selected
intermediate type. A canonical inference rule would change admission; retaining
the elaborated type preserves the choice already made by source checking.

The module defines finite hints using the existing `Instantiation.ValueType`,
which distinguishes lexical resource names from activation identities.
`SourceFocusHints.inputPort` reuses type instantiation and decoding.
`checkSource` matches that port to the rich source type; `checkFrame` compares
it with the supplied operand frame and checks the answer against the actual
stack. `source_port_unique` and `source_frame_agreement` prove that a shared
hint makes those ports agree. These checks establish neither source expression
typing nor continuation permission by themselves.

The existing `decode_realized_type` and `realized_type_cannot_be_rebound`
proofs supply the realization and retention results. A hint opened at resource
activation 11 keeps that identity when moved under an environment binding the
same lexical name to activation 29. Executable examples reject unresolved
names and switching the `Unit` and `Integer` choices, while accepting both
correctly annotated alternatives. No new substitution or name-realization
induction is introduced.

The [annotated-node representation](#finite-annotated-nodes-and-transport) below
now retains the hints at syntax positions and projects its transformations to
the existing operations. The source judgment still needs to authenticate those
positions, and execution must preserve that connection through substitution,
instantiation and frame creation. The finite hint guard is therefore **not**
yet a `RetainedStep` constructor. Adding it before proving that the event uses
the source's actual retained hint would leave the provenance gap intact. Focus
coverage remains six of ten cases.

This omission is not evidence that current Core lacks type annotations.
The [Effect Core lowering contract](../../../../spec/elaboration.md#effect-core-lowering)
retains each node's structural value type, computation row and causal origin;
[AD-0007](../../../decisions/AD-0007-typed-core-dialects.md) requires typed nodes
and binders with independent validation. The next source-representation change
should retain that existing kind of metadata in the experiment. Formal
extraction and execution correspondence remain unproved; no Core changes are
made or requested by this result.

## Finite annotated nodes and transport

[SourceAnnotatedCode.lean](SourceAnnotatedCode.lean) implements finite annotated
nodes for every constructor of scoped `Code`, including handler clauses,
resource scopes and cleanup. Each node retains an `Instantiation.ValueType`;
its lexical resource names are distinct from activation identities. This is a
metadata representation for the existing direct calculus. `Term.erase` and
`Clauses.erase` remove the hints; there is still one ordinary binding form and
no computation wrapper or conversion operation. The current admission and
runtime invariant still use erased `Code`; adopting the annotated nodes in
those judgments remains open.

Substitution replaces a variable with the entire annotated value. Lambda and
ordinary-binding parameters shadow ordinary substitution; a handler clause's
payload parameter shadows substitution in its body. Resource instantiation
transforms both code and hints. An acquisition initializer uses the enclosing
environment; its body masks the local resource binder until that scope is
opened. `erase_subst` and `erase_instantiate` prove that both transformations
erase to the existing scoped operations for all nodes and clauses. The old
`Code.instantiation_subst` theorem supplies the corresponding commutation result
for erased annotated terms.

Annotated contexts retain their sibling subterms and whole-expression hint.
Plugging a result preserves that context hint and erases to ordinary context
plugging. The ten annotated `Focus` constructors erase to their existing raw
counterparts, and `focus_lift` reconstructs an annotated focus from every raw
focus of an annotated term. Thus the representation omits none of the ten
positions. `Focus.unique` and `input_hint_unique` show that a fixed annotated
term selects one child and one retained hint. This addresses the representation
ambiguity identified above without assuming that arbitrary typings of the
same erased code are unique.

`checkFocusFrame` reads the selected child's hint. `checked_focus_ports` reuses
the previous source/frame agreement proof when source checking authenticates
that hint. The constructor coverage and uniqueness results are about syntax;
they do not establish that every node's supplied hint is well typed. The shared
source judgment must authenticate the tree, and its preservation proofs must
retain that connection across execution, before this guard can enter the
common event relation.

Annotated binding, beta reduction and branch selection project to the existing
`OrdinaryStep` and `RawStep` rules. The beta rule enters `.none` continuation
scope, matching the existing machine. These projection theorems introduce no
new owner or effect behavior. Examples cover all four previously ambiguous
focus forms, both admitted binding-type choices, binder shadowing, nested
resource masking, opening a body's hints, and copying a frozen resource value
under a later same-name resource binding.

`erased_closure_does_not_freeze_hints` records a separate limit: a lambda's code
can be resource-closed while its function annotation mentions an unresolved
lexical resource. Instantiation and substitution can then disagree on the
annotation even though their erased code agrees. The example describes open
metadata, not an admitted unsafe runtime value. The [metadata closure and transport proofs](#metadata-closure-and-full-tree-commutation)
below now supply the full-tree theorem under a finite annotated closure check;
erased `Code.ResourceClosed` alone remains insufficient. Source admission must
establish the annotated check before applying that theorem.

No extra focus case is added to `RetainedStep` by this representation work.
Universal execution preservation still covers six of ten focus cases. The
[annotated source checking](#annotated-source-checking-and-focus) below now
supplies structural source authentication and finite metadata-closure checks.
Preservation of that evidence and integration of the annotated source/context
data into the runtime state remain open.

## Metadata closure and full-tree commutation

[SourceAnnotatedNames.lean](SourceAnnotatedNames.lean) defines finite lexical
closure for annotated terms. `hintNames` traverses function input and result
types, latent effects and retained support. `Term.freeNames` includes those
annotation names, expression names and handler-clause names. A resource binder
removes its name only from the body's free names. Its initializer and declared
result hint remain in the enclosing scope. Thus local resource scopes are
accepted without treating every syntactic hint as globally closed.

`checkClosed` decides whether this list is empty, and `check_closed_iff` proves
its exact relationship to annotated `ResourceClosed`. The instantiation proofs
reuse the existing effect/name transformations, missing-name decomposition,
resource masking and unresolved-name equations. `instantiation_free` computes
exactly the names left unresolved by any environment. `instantiation_closes_iff`
therefore characterizes closure by coverage of the original free names.
`closed_instantiation_identity` proves that any later environment leaves a
closed annotated tree unchanged. `closed_erasure` obtains the old code-closure
property using the existing erased instantiation theorem, without a second
structural free-name inclusion proof.

`Term.instantiation_subst` and `Clauses.instantiation_subst` now establish the
full annotated-tree equation: substituting a closed annotated value and then
instantiating equals instantiating first and substituting that same value.
The proof follows the existing scoped binder cases; only the metadata identity
lemma changes. It preserves lambda, ordinary-binding and clause-parameter
shadowing, and permits inserted values containing their own locally bound
resource scopes. No source typing, capture or ownership induction is duplicated.

`acquisition_closes_body` derives annotated body closure when a closed resource
scope is opened at an activation identity. This is a lexical-name result;
fresh allocation, live access and effect interpretation remain separate
obligations. `closed_hint_fixed` and `closed_frame_check_fixed` show that a
closed term's retained root hint and finite frame check are independent of a
later lexical environment.

The examples count names in all four function-metadata positions, reject the
previous open-hint counterexample, accept a function containing a local resource
scope, reject unresolved names in an acquisition initializer or result hint,
and transport that accepted value through arbitrary annotated target terms.
They also open the local body and recover the old erased closure property.

These results complete the lexical metadata transport lemmas. The annotated
source judgment below now checks node hints and metadata closure structurally.
Preserving those checks at each execution point and retaining their evidence
in the runtime remain necessary before the remaining four focus forms enter
`RetainedStep`. Its coverage is still six of ten forms.

## Annotated source checking and focus

[SourceAnnotatedSources.lean](SourceAnnotatedSources.lean) defines mutually
structural expression, node, clause-body, offer and declaration judgments over
`Term` and annotated clause syntax. Each expression checks its root hint against
the selected rich value type and checks finite lexical metadata closure. The
node rules retain the existing types, effects, owner demands, requirements,
continuation permissions and plan signatures. Recursive child premises use
those same selected types; they do not combine independently chosen typings.
Handler plans are indexed by the erased annotated clauses. Resource bodies are
checked after annotated instantiation at each fresh identity, retaining their
local lexical templates.

The five erasure theorems project these derivations to `SourcePlannedSources`
with unchanged rich types, requirements and checking signatures. The main proof
uses the existing mutual-induction pattern; resource opening reuses
`Term.erase_instantiate`. Thus the established control and ownership results
remain available. `hint_checked` and `resource_closed` expose the two finite
checks. `port_unique` proves that two derivations of the same annotated term
agree on its erased output port, even when their other rich indices differ.
It does not assert uniqueness of full effect or continuation contracts.

[SourceAnnotatedContexts.lean](SourceAnnotatedContexts.lean) retains annotated
siblings in every evaluation-context form. Evaluated pair/function siblings
keep their original source proof and value evidence; the existing value-summary
theorem supplies their pure erased summary. `Context.erase` projects to the old
rich context. `focus_decompose` covers all ten focus forms and returns the actual
annotated child and context at one shared intermediate type, together with the
existing signature split, owner-demand equation and requirement-evaluation law.
The proof reuses the old sequence, value-evaluation and effect-composition laws.

`focus_frame_ports` connects that child's checked hint to any frame passing the
finite guard. `focus_prepare` reuses the established frame constructor to produce
an actual raw focus step, its rich frame certificate, a successful child-port
guard and the context's checked result hint. The caller supplies the current
scope typing and agreement between the expression result and the stack input.
There is no premise asserting successor validity or successful future execution.

[SourceAnnotatedAdmission.lean](SourceAnnotatedAdmission.lean) projects annotated
source admission to the existing initial `Run` theorem. It retains the same five
premises: source typing, scheduling, the finite initial requirement/support
check, completion and operation-signature agreement. Both unit-parameter and
integer-parameter versions of the earlier binding example now have annotated
source proofs and establish that initial runtime invariant. A negative theorem
rejects changing the initializer type while retaining its annotation. A resource
example contains a reference to its locally acquired cell and checks its opened
body at every fresh identity, including the body annotations.

This completes the source-authentication and focus-decomposition connection.
The [substitution and reduction proofs](#annotated-substitution-and-ordinary-reduction)
below now preserve that source judgment through ordinary computation. The [runtime retention layer](#annotated-runtime-retention-and-focus) below now
retains annotated syntax in current/saved records. Preservation across the full
runtime and integration with `RetainedStep` remain open. Its coverage remains six of ten. General consuming declarations, complete initial admission
and entry/capture integration remain open. These are informative proof
experiments; they do not change current Ash or establish Core correspondence.

## Annotated substitution and ordinary reduction

[SourceAnnotatedTransport.lean](SourceAnnotatedTransport.lean) adapts the existing
source-transport induction to the finite checked nodes. Agreement on ordinary
variable dependencies permits an environment change; resource-world growth,
continuation-contract extension and an enlarged allowed-effect list preserve
the same source types and signatures. Hint and metadata-closure checks remain
unchanged. Fresh resource bodies reuse the old environment-agreement and world
lemmas through annotated instantiation erasure.

[SourceAnnotatedValues.lean](SourceAnnotatedValues.lean) supplies the same pure
value summaries as the earlier source judgment. It retains latent function
bodies and their annotations. Value context changes, closed-environment changes,
world growth and contract extension reuse these transports. Erasing a summary
reuses the existing value port and usage proofs.

[SourceAnnotatedSubstitution.lean](SourceAnnotatedSubstitution.lean) proves
closed substitution for the full mutually structural source judgment. Metadata
closure of the substituted tree follows from the previously proved
instantiation/substitution equation and closure-by-name-coverage equivalence;
no additional free-name induction is needed. `substitution_hint` handles the
only root-hint change: replacing a variable. Its environment lookup identifies
the exact rich input type authenticated by the replacement value. Every other
root hint remains unchanged.

The source substitution proof follows the existing binder, clause and resource
cases. `substitutePlans` retargets clause witnesses to the actual substituted
annotated bodies; its signature theorem reuses raw required-action preservation.
Clause port typing, continuation usage, coverage and mode checks reuse their
existing substitution laws through erasure. The resource case uses full-tree
instantiation/substitution commutation and the replacement's checked metadata
closure. The conclusion retains the same rich result type, owner demand,
requirements and checking signature. No successful successor execution is
assumed.

[SourceAnnotatedReduction.lean](SourceAnnotatedReduction.lean) extracts the
original annotated lambda body, substitutes it and reuses the existing
requirement-evaluation proofs for bind and beta reduction. Beta enters the
existing no-ticket scope. Branch selection retains the selected annotated
source derivation, preserves the owner-demand multiset and obtains a sublist of
the previous checked effect row. `reduction_preserves` combines these cases for
every supplied `SourceAnnotatedCode.Reduction`: bind, beta, true branch and
false branch. This relation does not include resource/handler entry, capture,
resumption, disposal, builtin operations or frame returns.

[SourceAnnotatedReductionExamples.lean](SourceAnnotatedReductionExamples.lean)
binds and calls a closed function whose body acquires a local resource and
refers to that cell. The actual bind and beta steps and both successor source
judgments are checked, with unchanged requirement evaluation. The local resource
body still has its source proof for every fresh opening; no globally closed
replacement for its local resource names is imposed.

This completes annotated closed substitution and source preservation for those
four syntax reductions. The [runtime retention layer](#annotated-runtime-retention-and-focus) below now
adds context recomposition, annotated current/saved records and all ten focus
forms at the stronger scheduled-state level. The older combined runtime
preservation theorem still covers six focus forms; its connection to that
stronger state remains open. General declaration admission, complete
initial admission and entry/capture integration remain open.

## Annotated runtime retention and focus

[SourceAnnotatedRecomposition.lean](SourceAnnotatedRecomposition.lean) defines
finite context closure by plugging a closed unit placeholder. `plug_closed_iff`
proves that a plugged expression is metadata-closed exactly when the saved
context and child are closed. It covers all ten contexts, including the local
binder in a saved resource body. Actual focus derives this context property
from the parent's source proof. `context_plug` combines the structural context,
its checked result hint and finite closure with any checked child of the same
rich input type. The conclusion constructs the complete annotated source and
reuses the existing requirement-evaluation and owner-demand equations. It has
no premise about successful future evaluation.

[SourceAnnotatedRuntime.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntime.lean) retains annotated
contexts, handler clauses, cleanup callbacks and saved callback results as
runtime data. All seven frame forms and all four stack forms are represented,
including recursively saved live continuations. Erasure projects these records
to the existing scoped machine. Stack append preserves erasure. Focus, plugging
and the four ordinary syntax reductions project to their existing raw steps;
no new ownership or continuation operation is defined. Runtime data carry the
existing lexical translation and raw closed-value evidence, not source typing
or a successful-execution certificate.

[SourceAnnotatedRuntimeTyping.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntimeTyping.lean) checks
those actual records. A plain frame retains its annotated context source,
checked result hint and finite metadata closure. Handler frames retain annotated
declarations; armed/running frames retain annotated callback and saved-value
source. The segment judgment follows the full stack, including dormant saved
segments. `Frame.erase` and `Segment.erase` construct the old scheduled judgments
at the same rich types, demands, requirements and plan forest. Port projections
identify the incoming type from the actual stack. These proofs do not choose a
second source typing after discarding annotations.

[SourceAnnotatedRuntimeState.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntimeState.lean) combines
annotated current source and those pending segments with the existing closing
records, scheduling, resource/owner checks and plan-registry match. Its erasure
constructs `SourceScheduledState.State`. Initial construction, current-source
replacement and bind/beta preservation are checked. Their pending annotated
stack stays intact; the existing requirement-evaluation proof reconstructs the
combined check. Closing records and saved-plan registries still use their old
erased interfaces, so retaining annotations through their execution remains an
integration obligation.

[SourceAnnotatedRuntimeFocus.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntimeFocus.lean) proves
progress and preservation for all ten focus forms in this stronger state.
`focus_checked` uses the existing signature-splitting theorem to obtain actual
child and context plans. `focus_preserves` accepts any frame matching the actual
annotated context and scope whose finite port guard passes. The guard reads the
child hint and the retained stack input; source checking and segment typing
derive agreement with the same rich intermediate type. The proof constructs
the annotated child state, saved plain frame and combined scheduling/effect
check. It reuses the existing template transport and row-reassociation laws.
`focus_progress` constructs a passing frame from current source evidence, then
applies that preservation theorem.

[SourceAnnotatedRuntimeExamples.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntimeExamples.lean)
constructs an initial annotated state for both parameter-type choices in the
earlier ambiguous binding program. Each focuses using its matching frame and
then evaluates the inner binding while retaining that same annotated saved
frame. Returning reconstructs the outer binding, whose reduction reaches unit
with an empty stack and empty owner demand. A finite negative check rejects the
other parameter type. No intermediate invariant is supplied independently.

The boundaries are distinct: the stronger annotated scheduled state now covers
all ten focus forms, while the older combined `RetainedStep` theorem below still
covers six. Connecting that combined theorem to the stronger state remains
open. Capture allocation, including registry extension, resumption and disposal
now have the annotated preservation proofs described below; disposal retains
its explicit typed-plan interface at the source-state layer. Entry and builtin results below cover the scheduled-state
layer; their connection to the common execution interface remains separate. Value returns and retirement
are covered by the following results. General consuming declaration
admission and complete initial admission also remain open. This work neither
changes Core semantics nor establishes a general Core simulation.

## Annotated returns and retirement

[SourceAnnotatedRuntimeReturns.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntimeReturns.lean) derives
value summaries and pending checks from the annotated state. `plug_checked`
reconstructs the actual context plan and source from the saved frame and returned
value. `plug_preserves` restores the saved scope and constructs the successor
state, including its transported closing templates and requirement evaluation.
It uses the stored context hint and metadata closure, with no successor-source
premise.

[SourceAnnotatedRuntimeComputation.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntimeComputation.lean)
lifts branch selection to this state. `ordinary_preserves` combines it with the
existing bind and beta proofs, retaining the annotated pending stack and deriving
the resulting demand permutation and effect-row sublist. Its ordinary reduction
relation covers binding, application and both branches; builtin operations are
separate obligations.

[SourceAnnotatedRuntimeBoundaries.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntimeBoundaries.lean)
preserves annotated state across handler, cell and consumed-clause returns,
cleanup startup/completion and closing completion. Cleanup startup constructs
the annotated invocation from the retained callback source and saves the actual
annotated return value in the running frame. These proofs reuse existing
requirement export and closing-template transport. They do not broaden the
current declaration recipe grammar.

[SourceAnnotatedRuntimeRetirement.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntimeRetirement.lean)
transports annotated frames and recursively saved segments through phase changes
that preserve availability for their retained live owners. It reuses
`SourceScheduledPhaseRestriction.local_restrict`; there is no replacement
scheduling algorithm or added future-validity premise. `retire` constructs the
successor after removing a retiring frame, proves that the old demand is exactly
the retired owner followed by the remaining demand, and derives the corresponding
ownership phase trace. Source annotations and the actual retained plans survive
this restriction.

[SourceAnnotatedRuntimeReturnSteps.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntimeReturnSteps.lean)
collects all eight annotated return forms. `ReturnStep.erase` projects each to
the existing raw machine. Conversely, `ReturnStep.of_raw` lifts **every** raw
step whose current expression is a value to an annotated step with the same
erased successor and owner events. This converse uses only runtime data and
value shape; it does not assume successor typing. `return_preserves` then derives
annotated successor state, exact retired-ticket demand consumption, no newly
allocated owner, and the ownership phase trace. `raw_return_preserves` combines
these results for arbitrary raw returned-value steps.

This closes returned-value preservation at the annotated scheduled-state layer,
including retirement. It does not yet connect that layer to the combined runtime
ledger/completion theorem or derive complete initial admission. Capture
allocation, resumption and disposal are covered below.
The following entry/builtin results
retain the same boundary on the combined theorem. Core correspondence remains
an assessment rather than a general simulation theorem.

## Annotated entry and builtin replies

[SourceAnnotatedRuntimeEntries.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntimeEntries.lean) derives
cleanup entry from the current annotated source and a value callback. It exposes
the callback requests and answer port, constructs the actual annotated action
for any supplied identity and matching answer type, and derives the body state
with that armed frame. Callback source and its latent plan stay together.
`cleanup_preserves` chooses an answer type representing the exposed port. The
existing requirement evaluation and callback scheduling proofs supply the
successor checks; none are assumed for the successor.

[SourceAnnotatedRuntimeHandlers.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntimeHandlers.lean)
transports annotated frames and segments when registry entries agree at every
retained activation, including activations in dormant captures. `handler_annotations`
exposes the source table, clause families, declaration requirements and answer
port. For any fresh activation and matching answer type, it constructs the
annotated handler, registers those source entries and proves the resulting body
state. The pending source and plans survive the registry update. This reuses
existing registration agreement and activation relocation; it still uses the
current structural recipe evidence and does not broaden its grammar.

[SourceAnnotatedRuntimeWorld.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntimeWorld.lean) transports
annotated declaration/context sources, frames and recursively saved segments
into a larger resource world. It reuses the existing annotated expression
transport, value transport and scheduled-plan transport. Metadata checks and
stored type choices remain unchanged.

[SourceAnnotatedRuntimeResources.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntimeResources.lean)
uses that transport for resource acquisition. `resource_annotations` derives
that the ready initializer is an integer, exposes an answer port and a finite
forbidden-name set, and proves entry for every supplied identity fresh in both
the world and that set. The actual annotated body is instantiated at the new
identity, including its metadata; its erased body executes the existing resource
entry rule. `resource_preserves` chooses a fresh identity and matching answer
type. The additional forbidden-name set comes from the existing hidden-requirement
support proof. It is not replaced by freshness in the visible world or by the
answer type's resource names.

[SourceAnnotatedRuntimeCells.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntimeCells.lean) retains
annotations during builtin selection. Its structural `CellUpdate` changes only
the selected active cell payload, respects a nearer matching source handler,
and leaves dormant captures untouched. `CellUpdate.erase` gives the existing
raw update; `CellUpdate.of_raw` lifts every such raw update while retaining the
actual annotated frames and captures. `update_segment` preserves the same rich
source indices and plan forest. `read_preserves` and `write_preserves` derive the
reply source, remove the request's checked effect row and preserve the owner
set. `builtin_step_preserves` covers every nonallocating raw step from a request
with a value operand, assuming the authenticated builtin operation signatures;
it constructs an annotated successor erasing to that exact raw successor.

These results cover entry witnesses and builtin replies at the annotated
scheduled-state layer. They do not assert that arbitrary raw entry annotations
are correct. The common execution interface still needs to obtain and check the
exposed entry data, including resource support and fresh handler registration,
and combine source preservation with the runtime ledger and completion proofs.
Capture allocation and disposal must also preserve this stronger state;
resumption is covered below. General
declaration admission and complete initial admission remain separate obligations.

## Annotated capture splitting and resumption

[SourceAnnotatedRuntimeSegments.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntimeSegments.lean)
proves append and physical splitting for annotated segments. Both directions
retain the actual frame sources, rich intermediate types, plan forests, demands
and stored requirement records. The requirement-evaluation equation uses the
same ordered receiving suffix as the existing scheduled proof. Reassociation
uses the existing scope, hint, forest and requirement laws. Rechecking consumes
the structural schedule supplied by invocation rules and retains the same
source; it does not recover source typing from erased dependencies.

[SourceAnnotatedRuntimeCuts.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntimeCuts.lean) lifts raw
prefix/suffix and live-boundary splits to the original annotated runtime data.
Its `HandlerCut` mirrors exact interpretation selection, including matching
builtin blockers and dormant saved segments crossed inside live frames.
`HandlerCut.erase` projects selection to the existing machine;
`HandlerCut.of_raw` lifts every raw selection back to the actual annotated
capture, suffix and handler. `HandlerCut.reconstructs` recovers the complete
stack by append. Annotated `ClauseAt` similarly preserves selection in both
directions, retaining the chosen clause body. These are structural data proofs,
with no successor typing or capture-admission premise.

[SourceAnnotatedRuntimeCaptureSplitting.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntimeCaptureSplitting.lean)
applies that cut to the annotated segment judgment. `capture_segments` retains
the selected handler's **annotated** declarations and frame check, the captured
source and waiting source, their exact plan-forest split, and the demand and
record equations. It also preserves exact operation selection and the existing
requirement-evaluation equation. Crossing a live frame keeps its dormant source
attached. This proves typed capture decomposition; fresh continuation allocation,
contract insertion and selected-clause entry are subsequent obligations.

[SourceAnnotatedRuntimeResumption.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntimeResumption.lean)
reuses the existing invocation-check decomposition and ownership-consumption
proofs. `replace_live` splits the checked stack at the selected live boundary,
obtains the captured and caller schedules from the invocation, and reconstructs
the annotated saved/caller segments after spending that owner. `resume_segments`
combines those sources with the existing record removal, effect evaluation,
closing-record transport and ownership phase trace. `resume_cut_preserves`
therefore constructs the complete annotated scheduled successor for a ready
resume, with demand equal to the consumed owner followed by the remaining demand.
No successor-source or restored-schedule premise is independently supplied.

`raw_resume_preserves` removes the requirement to supply an annotated cut: every
raw resume step from a checked annotated resume expression lifts to an annotated
successor with exactly the same erased configuration. The theorem preserves the
checked row, derives the remaining demand and records exactly one consumed
continuation owner. It supports arbitrary finite prefixes and recursively saved
segments; it does not restrict resumption to an immediate or unnested boundary.

These results complete resumption preservation at the annotated scheduled-state
layer. They do not yet supply capture allocation/clause-entry preservation,
disposal preservation, complete initial/declaration admission, or the combined
runtime ledger/completion theorem. Entry's source-derived annotation and resource
support data still need a common execution interface. No multishot, escape or
suspension rule is introduced.

## Annotated clause selection and allocation components

[SourceAnnotatedCaptureSources.lean](SourceAnnotatedCaptureSources.lean)
selects the actual annotated body and plan from the installed declarations.
The same operation lookup fixes the argument and resumption input types, and
the offered mode fixes the selected body family. `capture_body_from_requirements`
reuses the existing structural requirement compiler and pre-capture scheduling
proofs for that plan. Its site obligations remain explicit; `capture_body`
derives them for the current recipe grammar using the existing declaration
capture theorem. No additional recipe constructor or whole-future-body premise
is introduced.

The module's substitution and payload-extension wrappers reuse the checked
annotated source proofs. Lexical readiness comes from the existing erased
source theorem. `body_step` pairs the substituted annotated body with the
corresponding raw capture step, exact owner addition, owner uniqueness and phase
introduction. These conclusions refer to the same selected body and payload;
there is no independent source proof for the successor.

[SourceAnnotatedRuntimeTransport.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntimeTransport.lean)
extends contracts, permissions and phases while retaining annotated declaration
and context sources, frames and recursively saved segments. Source extension,
port-interface extension and scheduled-plan transport are existing proofs.
Finite metadata checks and actual plan choices remain unchanged.

[SourceAnnotatedAllocationData.lean](SourceAnnotatedAllocationData.lean)
retains the selected annotated clause with the actual saved/waiting forests and
scheduling checks. `capture_typed_data` derives that data from physical selection,
the installed annotated declarations and the existing structural capture-site
obligations. `allocated_body` refines the allocated contract and substitutes the

previous scheduled allocation data, including its source body, instead of
assuming a separately chosen old derivation.

[SourceAnnotatedCaptureInterfaces.lean](SourceAnnotatedCaptureInterfaces.lean)
connects this selected clause to typed capture decomposition. Exact source
operation selection and forest append injectivity identify the same captured
and waiting pieces. The selected frame retains its annotated declarations and
supplied requirements, and the clause source agrees with that frame's refined
answer and operation input.

[SourceAnnotatedCaptureData.lean](SourceAnnotatedCaptureData.lean) keeps those
pieces together through allocation. `CaptureData.allocated` inserts the refined
contract, continuation rights and actual saved-plan registry entry; derives the
annotated substituted body; and rebuilds the annotated live segment from the
original captured and waiting source. Fresh extension preserves older contracts,
permissions and saved-plan matches. The existing owner/protection realization
proof establishes the new contract's held mode. The same source data also
erases to the earlier scheduled capture certificate for reuse by the allocator.

These allocation components now join the closing certificate, stored disposal
records and clause-effect evaluation in the annotated capture theorem below.
The closing-source construction retains actual callbacks and constructs their
typed closing frames. Annotated disposal is connected below with an explicit
typed-plan interface. General declaration admission, complete initial admission
and the combined execution theorem remain open.

## Annotated closing sources and stored records

[SourceAnnotatedClosingRuntime.lean](SourceAnnotatedClosingRuntime.lean)
retains annotated callbacks in executable closing entries. Plan construction
traverses every stack form, including dormant saved continuations, in the same
order as the scoped machine. `makePlan_erase` proves exact agreement with its
plan builder; `makePlan_of_raw` recovers the annotated plan from any successful
raw construction on the same stack. `closeControl_erase` proves that the
annotated closing frames erase to the machine's closing control. Protected
running, closing and retirement frames still reject plan construction.

[SourceAnnotatedClosingPlans.lean](SourceAnnotatedClosingPlans.lean) extracts
callback sources from the actual annotated saved segment. Its structural
`Contents` and `Template` judgments retain each original callback, rich function
type, latent footprint and declaration plan. `plan_contents` also preserves the
exact saved forest's closing projection, including dormant callbacks. Erasure
constructs the older template at those same indices. Contract extension,
resource-world extension and handler-table changes preserve the retained source;
closing contexts contain no handler frames, so the existing table-independence
proof applies.

[SourceAnnotatedClosingRecomposition.lean](SourceAnnotatedClosingRecomposition.lean)
materializes the template's callbacks as annotated armed frames. Scheduling and
port-level plan typing remain explicit premises, and both check the template's
actual erased plan. `Template.scheduled_source` derives the annotated segment;
it does not assume successor typing or reannotate an arbitrary erased callback.
`Template.scheduled_recompose` reuses annotated segment append and retains its
exact retirement demand and requirement-evaluation equation under the waiting
stack. Changing the caller scope reuses the existing closing-context equation.

[SourceAnnotatedClosingRecords.lean](SourceAnnotatedClosingRecords.lean)
stores this stronger template certificate at the existing raw plan and exact
saved-forest indices. Record transport reuses captured-origin and unique-owner
proofs. It preserves annotated templates through capture relocation, ordinary
steps, contract extension, resource-world extension and handler registration.
The annotated runtime state's `templates` field now uses these records.
State erasure projects them to the older records; the previously established
annotated transition proofs preserve the strengthened invariant.

[SourceAnnotatedClosingData.lean](SourceAnnotatedClosingData.lean) connects
capture data to this certificate. `capture_closing` recovers the annotated plan
from the actual raw construction, extracts its source once, and retains it in
the allocator's capture witness. The older allocator certificate is a projection
of this witness. `selected_template` connects actual record lookup, unique
capture location and saved-plan matching to the stronger stored certificate.
`Certificate.materialize` uses that certificate, its schedule and plan typing to
construct an annotated closing segment whose erasure is exactly the machine's
closing control.

This closes the callback-source retention and materialization gap. The capture
theorem below joins that witness to clause-effect evaluation and the complete
annotated successor state. The disposal theorem below joins the constructed
closing segment to caller recomposition, record consumption and the same
state's accounting. The general handler-admission and initial-admission
obligations are unchanged. These results remain experimental proof evidence; they do not change
current Ash or establish full Core correspondence.

## Annotated capture preservation

[SourceAnnotatedAllocation.lean](SourceAnnotatedAllocation.lean) joins the
annotated clause, captured and waiting segments, stored closing certificates
and source-plan registry at one fresh continuation contract. `allocate` reuses
`SourceDependencySchemes.allocate_capture_source_from_closing_interfaces` with
the annotated capture and closing witnesses. The generic allocator supplies
record insertion, invocation checks and ownership accounting; annotated
substitution and segment reconstruction retain the original rich source types.
Existing disposal records keep their original annotated callback certificates.

`allocate_without_closing` covers captures whose plan builder fails or whose
pending owner uses cannot be internalized. Existing checked-cut and clause-mode
proofs derive disposal denial. The branch installs the resume record, retains
older disposal certificates, and derives the substituted clause's effect check
from the same structural row instantiation. This branch is part of the complete
capture classification, not a restriction to resumptive clauses.

[SourceAnnotatedRuntimeCapture.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntimeCapture.lean)
connects both allocation branches to the annotated runtime `State`.
`capture_preserves` constructs the actual substituted annotated clause and live
stack, proves their raw capture step, and retains source typing, the shared
schedule, annotated closing records and the combined effect check. The new
owner is added exactly once; the successor demand is a permutation of that
owner followed by the previous demand, and its effect row is included in the
previous row. Ownership completion, phase transport, row bounds and footprint
checking reuse established proofs.

The theorem applies to every supplied physical handler cut and selected clause
under its stated premises. It uses the operation-derived input annotation for
the allocated continuation; it does not validate arbitrary annotations supplied
to the raw capture rule. The general theorem retains explicit capture-site
requirements and captured resource support. Its combined statement uses the
existing empty outward guard needed by closing-budget admission; the branch
without closing also supports a general outward guard.

[SourceAnnotatedRecipeCapture.lean](SourceAnnotatedRecipeCapture.lean)
derives the capture-site requirements for the existing structural recipe
grammar. `capture_from_recipes` uses the actual pending source, request schedule,
selected clause mode and installed requirement check; it adds no successful
future-body premise. Resource support and registry freshness remain explicit,
for later connection to the full runtime invariant. General nested-handler
consumption and effectful-cleanup declaration admission are still separate open
obligations; this specialization does not enlarge the current recipe grammar.

Capture preservation at this annotated source-state layer is now connected.
Annotated disposal is connected below. The milestone still requires complete
declaration and initial-source admission, the common execution interface, and
the combined progress/preservation and finite-execution result. Core correspondence remains
a status assessment; no Core alignment is included.

## Annotated disposal preservation

[SourceAnnotatedDisposal.lean](SourceAnnotatedDisposal.lean) connects the actual
stored annotated closing certificate to caller recomposition and record
consumption. `disposal_parts` splits the annotated caller at the selected live
owner, obtains the certificate from the actual store lookup, and rechecks the
waiting frames under the spent owner phase. The resulting waiting segment keeps
its original source annotations. The invocation schedule supplies the closing
and caller checks; no successor source or scheduling judgment is assumed.

`discard_segments` materializes that certificate's annotated callbacks and
joins them to the waiting caller through the closing frame. The reconstructed
stack erases exactly to the scoped machine's closing control. Existing record
permutation, lookup transport and consumed-owner proofs remove the discarded
continuation's resume record and the records owned by its captured stack. The
remaining records retain their annotated certificates. Existing phase and
requirement-evaluation equations establish the successor's effect check and
unique ownership.

`discard_cut_preserves` constructs the complete annotated successor state for a
ready disposal at the supplied live cut. It produces the machine step, preserves
the checked effect row, removes exactly the selected owner from current demand,
and proves the owner permutation and phase transition. Cleanup entries still
carry the captured owners until their retirement steps consume them; disposal
does not silently remove those owners from the accounting.

The source-state theorem retains an explicit typed-plan interface, together
with the actual closing-plan construction and owner resolution. It does not
claim progress from this source state alone. The existing
`SourceScheduledExecution.Run.discard_preserves` derives that interface from the
runtime's retained continuation certificate. Connecting the annotated state to
the same runtime invariant must reuse that derivation. Captured source admission,
initial admission and the common execution theorem remain open; this proof adds
no multishot, escaping or suspending continuation behavior.

## Annotated runtime integration

[SourceAnnotatedExecution.lean](SourceAnnotatedExecution.lean) joins the actual
annotated configuration to the existing runtime invariant. Its `Run` retains one
action map, owner registry, issued-name history, completion result and annotated
source forest. `Run.erase` constructs the older scheduled run from those same
witnesses. It does not assume an unrelated source derivation for the erased
program. Initial assembly still requires separate source, scheduling, finite
initial-check, completion and signature premises; it is not complete program
admission.

[SourceAnnotatedRuntimeDisposal.lean](SourceAnnotatedRuntimeDisposal.lean) proves
`Run.discard_preserves` for every actual named/access-checked disposal step from
this state. `raw_discard_shape` recovers the actual annotated live cut from the
raw step through the existing stack decomposition lemma. The retained runtime
certificate supplies plan typing for the same contract and plan. Annotated
source preservation then constructs the restored cleanup and caller, with exact
erasure to the raw target. Runtime assembly reuses completion, ownership,
access, usage and name-history preservation. The result consumes exactly the
selected owner from the source demand. `Run.discard_progress` derives an actual
step and this successor from the invariant alone; neither theorem takes a
separate typed-plan or successor-validity premise.

[SourceAnnotatedExecutionCapture.lean](SourceAnnotatedExecutionCapture.lean)
connects both capture allocation branches to the same runtime. For the supplied
physical handler cut and selected clause, retained access and unique ownership
derive captured resource support. The issued-name history supplies freshness for
contracts, actions and saved annotations. The source-selected operation result
annotation and clause substitution determine the actual successor, and the
existing completion proof constructs its owner record. Existing certificate
allocation preserves disposal evidence. `Run.capture_progress` chooses the new
owner from the finite ledger. The result adds exactly that owner, retains the
annotated captured and waiting pieces, and produces an effect row contained in
the previous row.

This capture result uses the existing structural declaration recipes. It still
takes handler selection, clause selection and the offered operation lookup as
premises. It does not cover arbitrary raw capture input annotations or complete
general declaration admission. Its source-derived annotation is the one already
used by the annotated capture theorem.

[SourceAnnotatedExecutionFocus.lean](SourceAnnotatedExecutionFocus.lean) lifts
all ten annotated focus forms into `Run`. `Run.focus_preserves` handles every
supplied frame satisfying the existing finite port guard. `Run.focus_progress`
constructs such a frame from the retained source hints. Both reuse source focus,
completion and runtime assembly; the frame and guard carry no successor typing.
This includes function position, application argument, binding initializer and
cleanup action, in addition to the six forms in the older retained-event theorem.

The other annotated transition families and exhaustive progress now join this
`Run` below. The [checked annotated event relation](#checked-annotated-events)
separately proves universal preservation for every transition family.
Exact annotated disposal and progress within that relation are now connected
below. General consuming declaration admission and complete initial-program
admission remain open.
The older retained-event theorem continues to have its stated six-focus scope.
This is proof-experiment evidence, with no change to current Ash or Core
correspondence.

## Annotated progress and finite execution

[SourceAnnotatedExecutionStable.lean](SourceAnnotatedExecutionStable.lean)
connects every raw returned-value step, including cleanup completion and ticket
retirement, to the annotated runtime. The actual successor erases to the supplied
raw target. The source demand loses exactly the tickets retired by that step.
Returned-value progress is terminal at an empty annotated stack and otherwise
constructs such a successor. Ready builtin replies reuse the retained operation
signature and exact cell-selection proof; they preserve owner demand and may
reduce the checked effect row.

[SourceAnnotatedExecutionComputation.lean](SourceAnnotatedExecutionComputation.lean)
recovers an annotated reduction from every raw ready bind, beta or branch step.
The selected body or branch is the actual retained term. Existing source
substitution and completion proofs then preserve `Run`, with the same owner
multiset and a sublist of the previous effect row. Ready progress reuses the
existing raw source progress theorem and this preservation result.

[SourceAnnotatedExecutionResumption.lean](SourceAnnotatedExecutionResumption.lean)
joins full-prefix resumption to `Run` for every actual annotated live cut.
Existing usage and accessibility locate the live owner for progress. Stack
lifting recovers the original annotated capture and waiting caller. Resumption
consumes exactly the selected owner; it does not assume a new caller source
or restrict nesting depth.

[SourceAnnotatedExecutionEntries.lean](SourceAnnotatedExecutionEntries.lean)
connects resource, handler and cleanup entry to the same invariant. Resource
annotations expose a finite forbidden-name set, including requirement support,
and an answer port; all supplied identities and types meeting those conditions
are admitted. Handler annotations retain the source-selected capability table,
clause families and declaration requirements, and register them under a fresh
activation. Cleanup annotations retain the original callback, request list and
answer port. Existing completion and ledger proofs establish the corresponding
runtime successors. Each entry theorem also constructs a fresh choice for
progress. These are source-derived annotation witnesses; a final event interface
must still authenticate its metadata choices independently of successor validity.

[SourceAnnotatedExecutionProgress.lean](SourceAnnotatedExecutionProgress.lean)
proves `Run.progress` for every configuration satisfying the annotated invariant.
It reuses the existing typed current-form classification and lifts raw focus,
handler cuts and clause selection to the actual annotated syntax. Request
coverage derives both the selected clause and its offered capability entry;
these are no longer premises of the combined progress theorem. Every case
returns either an ordinary terminal or an actual named/access-checked step and
a successor `Run`, including updated owner and interpretation registries.

[SourceAnnotatedExecutionFiniteRuns.lean](SourceAnnotatedExecutionFiniteRuns.lean)
reuses the existing counted machine steps and finite-prefix induction pattern.
For any fuel, `Run.finite_prefix` constructs that many steps unless an ordinary
terminal is reached first. The endpoint retains the annotated invariant.
`Run.terminal_accounting` reuses the owner ledger to prove that every issued
owner has been discharged exactly once at termination. `initial_finite_prefix`
starts this construction from the current explicit source, scheduling, finite
initial-check, completion and signature premises.

This is exhaustive progress and existence of finite checked executions. It does
not establish preservation for every trace of the final event interface, and it
does not combine the initial premises into complete admission. That interface
must authenticate annotation and registry choices without carrying intermediate
or successor `Run` proofs. General handler-bearing and effectful-cleanup
consuming declaration admission remains open. No multishot, escape, suspension,
async or Core alignment is included.

## Checked annotated events

[ResourceRowNarrowing.lean](ResourceRowNarrowing.lean) proves that inserting a
builtin interpretation can narrow a successfully checked effect row while
preserving the owner demand. It reuses ordered residual composition and the
existing requirement-checking rules. The new
[resource source theorem](SourceAnnotatedResourceEntry.lean) therefore accepts
every identity fresh in the resource world; equality of the old row no longer
requires excluding additional hidden requirement names.

[SourceAnnotatedExecutionResourceEntry.lean](SourceAnnotatedExecutionResourceEntry.lean)
checks a supplied resource answer annotation against the source node's finite
hint and derives the successor for every historically fresh resource owner.
[SourceAnnotatedExecutionCheckedEntries.lean](SourceAnnotatedExecutionCheckedEntries.lean)
does the same for the concrete handler and cleanup records. The handler's clauses,
effect and scope are the actual source fields. Cleanup checks both the enclosing
answer port and the callback's request list. The existing handler and cleanup
source proofs now expose these exact witnesses; preservation constructs the
handler tables, clause families and requirements. An event supplies none of
those proof registries. Positive and negative examples check wrong answer ports,
unresolved resource hints and fabricated cleanup requests.

[SourceAnnotatedExecutionExactControl.lean](SourceAnnotatedExecutionExactControl.lean)
reuses ordinary, returned-value and builtin source preservation at the supplied
annotated successor. Existing runtime completion and ownership proofs assemble
the shared invariant. This avoids treating equality of erased successors as
equality of annotated syntax. Capture preservation now also exposes its existing
exact substituted clause, saved stack and operation input type witnesses.

[SourceAnnotatedExecutionEvents.lean](SourceAnnotatedExecutionEvents.lean)
defines a common `Step` relation for all ten focus forms, ordinary reduction,
all eight return forms, full-prefix resumption, builtin reads and writes,
resource/handler/cleanup entry, both capture branches, and disposal. Its fixed parameters
are the operation port signature and result port. Constructors carry actual
syntax and structural selection, finite port checks and name freshness. They do
not carry source judgments, proof registries or successor validity. Capture
uses the canonical embedded result port of the selected operation; preservation
derives the corresponding rich contract and owner record.

`step_preserves` proves preservation for every supplied event in that relation,
with an exact annotated target. `steps_preserve` applies induction to every
supplied finite trace. It constructs all intermediate invariants and threads
changes to contracts, owner records, handler tables, declaration families,
requirements and saved annotations. The final effect row is a subset of the
initial row. `terminal_accounting` derives exact-once owner discharge for every
terminal endpoint of such a trace.

Disposal now retains exact annotated-plan provenance.
[SourceAnnotatedCaptureIdentity.lean](SourceAnnotatedCaptureIdentity.lean) lifts
capture location to the annotated stack and proves uniqueness under the existing
one-shot ownership invariant. Closing certificates are indexed by the actual
capture and retain its `makePlan` equation. Record transport reuses structural
capture-origin proofs through cell updates, resumption and disposal.
`Run.discard_at` therefore preserves the supplied annotated closing control;
the common disposal event needs only resolution, actual plan construction and
freshness. Existing ownership, access and completion proofs are reused.

[SourceAnnotatedClosingIdentity.lean](SourceAnnotatedClosingIdentity.lean)
retains a regression for the former erased-only certificate representation:
two well-typed callbacks can erase identically while carrying different internal
annotations. Its `ErasedCertificate` witnesses explain the need to retain
provenance; they do not apply to the strengthened `Certificate` index.

[SourceAnnotatedEventSelection.lean](SourceAnnotatedEventSelection.lean) reuses
existing source progress, exact entry witnesses, physical capture selection and
hint agreement to select common events.
[SourceAnnotatedEventProgress.lean](SourceAnnotatedEventProgress.lean) reuses
the typed current-form classification to prove `progress`: every runtime state
satisfying `Run` is terminal or has a `Step` of the same relation used by
preservation. `finite_progress` applies `steps_preserve` and this theorem to
any supplied finite trace, deriving endpoint progress from just its initial
runtime invariant. General consuming declaration admission and complete
initial-program admission remain separate obligations.
This evidence concerns the DN-0033 experiment; it does not change current Ash
semantics or establish general Core correspondence.

## Universal preservation for retained events

[SourceScheduledRetainedRuns.lean](SourceScheduledRetainedRuns.lean) establishes
universal preservation for an explicit part of the final execution interface.
`RetainedStep operations contracts result` has five constructors: the existing
`CallableRuns.StableEvent`, an actual named/access-checked disposal step,
`focusRequest`, `focusResume` and `focusContext`. The fixed `result` is the erased
initial result type, not a new type chosen at each step. Stable events include value returns and their cleanup/closing
transitions, ready bind/application/branch computation, builtin reads/writes,
and resumption. Disposal may allocate a closing owner; the source contract,
handler and saved-plan registries remain unchanged.

`focusRequest` takes a nonvalue operand, the actual request context, and
`checkRequestPorts = true`. This executable guard compares the frame's erased
input/output ports with the fixed operation signature. Its soundness theorem
exposes exactly that equality. The event requires no source typing or runtime
invariant at the intermediate node. `Run.request_frame_ports` extracts the same
port equality from a retained typed request frame. `request_focus_preserves`
uses that fact and the earlier `focus_annotations` theorem to admit every
supplied matching frame. It applies to any operation and retained stack;
the cell-read example is not a restriction on the rule.

`RequestFocusExamples.focus_bind_plug` constructs a three-event trace: focus a
cell-read operand, evaluate its ordinary binding, then return the reference
through the plain request frame. `focused_trace_preserves` applies the common
finite-execution theorem to this mixed trace. Separate executable checks reject
wrong input and output ports. The example assumes the starting `Run` for its
preservation result; it does not claim new initial-program admission.

`focusResume` resolves the lexical continuation binder, looks up its retained
contract, and checks both erased ports with `checkResumePorts`. The
`Run.resume_frame_ports` lemma extracts those ports from the actual typed frame;
`resume_focus_preserves` reuses `focus_annotations`. The guard grants no resume
permission and cannot revive a consumed owner. The resume examples check
unresolved binders, missing contracts and wrong ports, construct operand
binding/return followed by full-prefix resumption, and reuse the common finite
preservation theorem.

`focusContext` uses `checkContextPorts` for four context forms. `stackInputPort`
reads the incoming port of the actual annotated stack; for an empty stack it
uses the fixed execution result port. The existing source-to-port erasure and
`StackTyped` constructors prove this agrees with the source derivation.
`contextInputPort` then projects the appropriate component for a pair, returns
`boolean` for a branch condition, or `integer` for a resource initializer.
`Run.context_frame_ports` combines these facts, and `context_focus_preserves`
applies the same generic focus theorem. No new substitution, capture or
ownership induction is needed.

The context guard rejects reversed pair ports, wrong result ports, and forms
whose input types these data do not determine. Its local stack-head examples
are guard checks, not claims that arbitrary whole stacks are well typed.
`ContextFocusExamples.nested_resume_branch` supplies a seven-event mixed trace:
resume focus, branch-condition focus, binding, condition return, branch choice,
resume-argument return and one-shot consumption. The caller prefix and saved
continuation are arbitrary finite stacks. `nested_resume_preserves` applies the
common finite theorem from an assumed initial `Run`; the example does not add
initial-program admission. None of its intermediate nodes carries a `Run`.

No constructor contains the successor invariant or successful checking of
future code. Stable events carry their existing raw transition and local syntax
premises. Disposal carries the existing freshness and access checks;
`Run.discard_preserves` derives its closing-plan typing and source successor
from the current retained evidence. The event interface does not accept an
arbitrary raw disposal without those checks.

The runtime computation layer now exposes `ready_preserves` for any supplied
ready raw step. It reuses the source substitution/branch theorem and the result
contract theorem. `ready_progress` selects a source step and applies that
preservation result. `stable_preserves` then reuses the value, ready, builtin and
resumption proofs; `retained_step_preserves` adds the existing disposal and
focus proofs.
No capture, recomposition, ownership or substitution induction is duplicated.

`retained_run_preserves` uses `Relation.TransGen` and its ordinary induction.
For every supplied nonempty finite `RetainedStep` sequence and one initial
`Run`, it derives the actual named/access-checked execution, an endpoint `Run`
with its retained forest and owner demand, and an endpoint effect row that is a
sublist of the initial row. Intermediate invariants are conclusions of the
induction, not fields of the execution trace. The empty sequence retains its
initial invariant directly. Existing endpoint progress and terminal accounting
apply to the derived `Run`.

This is a universal theorem for the stated event forms, not the completed
one-shot execution theorem. Six of the ten focus cases are integrated; the four
remaining cases are function position, application argument, binding initializer
and cleanup action. Their source type choices are not determined by the current
context/stack guard. Resource/handler/cleanup installation still requires
authenticated source annotations; capture additionally changes the contract and
saved-plan registries. Those events must be integrated into
the final interface. General consuming declaration admission and complete
initial-term admission remain separate obligations. No Core semantics change
or general correspondence theorem follows from this result.

## Remaining proof construction

The one-shot milestone remains incomplete. The selected execution model is
lexical unwinding, described below. Earlier plan-dependent source theorems are
reusable components, not a safety theorem for this changed machine.

| Connection | Verified components | Outstanding obligation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Runtime typing and interpretation | Local port proofs cover capture, resume, discard, all value/unwind transitions, ordinary computation and scope entry. Effect checking reuses the existing ordered interfaces through a lookup-preserving projection. Source focus and plug now construct matching runtime and source frames. | Finish authenticating annotations at the other constructing transitions and join the port and effect facets throughout execution; construction of a typed successor does not prove preservation for arbitrary raw annotation choices. |
| Structural source admission | Existing expression typing, capability annotations, completion bounds and structural receiver checks; lexical source capture/append, resumption, focus/plug, cleanup entry/return and fresh-environment transport, with the local premises described below | Preserve source evidence for continuation use, interpretation availability, release exclusion and outward operand support in reachable states. The recorded protection bit now agrees with actual captures and supplies the source discard guard; source expressions and callback annotations still need preservation. Integrate the lexical source checks in place of legacy plan-routing checks throughout admission and preservation. Preserve rich captures, outside-owner calls, branches, callable/resource bodies, effectful cleanup and disposing interpretations. |
| Common event preservation | Generic ownership preservation; resource-support preservation with two local pre-step checks; local typing and effect results; exhaustive use-accounting and continuation-access preservation for structurally checked events, joined with ownership and ticket history; capture-protection preservation under source-registry extension and authenticated allocation | Assemble a common invariant and derive its successor for every admitted event, including callback execution and return to unwinding. No event may assume its successor invariant or safety of future execution. |
| Initial-source safety and progress | Legacy initial-source construction, finite-trace induction, progress components and terminal ledger accounting | Establish the new common invariant from sufficient source admission, propagate it through finite execution, and prove progress and terminal accounting. Run the final combined verification. |

The existing `AtUse.provide`, structural receiver rechecking, cleanup obligation
checks, `AtPackets.capture_use_step` and initial annotation theorem are evidence
to reuse where their premises still apply. Completing their old plan-dependent
variants is not a prerequisite for the selected semantics. Their intended source
coverage remains required; a smaller grammar or an assumed future-safe state
would not complete the milestone.

Source admission may combine independently checked expression types, capability
annotations, their structural validation, completion bounds and signature
agreement. Deriving every check from plain expression typing is not a separate
requirement. The missing connection is from these source checks to the new
runtime invariant, not from a supplied runtime invariant to itself.

Core correspondence remains a status assessment: report proved relations,
unproved obligations and demonstrated mismatches. Aligning Core or its
specification is outside this milestone. Multishot, escape, suspension and
asynchronous continuations remain separate targets whose integration is deferred.

## Lexical cleanup and local unwinding

The selected design direction is local unwinding of an abandoned continuation.
Its captured scopes retain their structure: run each scope's cleanup before
leaving that scope, while enclosing interpretations and resources remain
available. A handler installation has a distinct identity. Cleanup bound to an
installation does not choose another finalizer when a nested scope is installed.
This does not by itself pin every effect performed inside that finalizer.
Closure capture must preserve the referenced scope's lifetime; explicit early
finalization is not introduced by this change.

The existing experimental `makePlan` does not implement this rule. It extracts
callbacks, releases and ticket retirements, but drops captured source handlers
before any callback executes. `InitialCleanupRouteGap` already contains a small
source example exposing this difference. The local-unwind work replaces this
planning dependency; it does not require repairing or extending the planner.
This is a change to the experimental calculus, not current Ash or Core.

[SourceResourceRoutes.lean](SourceResourceRoutes.lean), under `LexicalUnwind`,
now defines the administrative fragment. It removes only the top ordinary frame,
handler boundary, cell or spent boundary. A live captured owner exposes its
saved scopes with a retirement marker after them. It cannot skip an armed or
running callback. `append` proves that each local step leaves an added enclosing
suffix unchanged. `accounting`, `preserves_ledger` and `no_double_completion`
reuse the existing ownership representation, ledger and list-permutation laws.
They do not require a generated plan or assume a valid successor.

The example `disposal_scope_mismatch` checks that the original callback scope
resolves to handler installation 101 and the old plan has lost it. `cleanup_runs`
and `cleanup_run` reuse the current ordinary scope-exit rules and trace-to-run
proof: the callback invokes its enclosing handler, resumes once, completes, and
only then leaves the handler scopes. This verifies reference behavior for the
small example; it is not a proof of general disposal or source admission.

`LexicalUnwind.Machine` now distinguishes ordinary evaluation from unwinding.
The existing stack has one additional internal `unwinding` frame. Starting a
cleanup replaces its armed frame with that return marker and calls the same
closed callback. When it returns Unit, evaluation switches back to unwinding.
The enclosing handler records, including their original answer types, remain
unchanged. `cleanup_entry_ports` reuses the existing Unit-to-Unit callback typing;
it does not invent an ordinary return value for the abandoned scope.

`Transition.discard` enters unwinding on the captured stack itself, with a close
boundary delimiting the disposing caller. At that boundary it returns Unit to
the caller. It constructs no cleanup plan. The reused ordinary evaluator excludes
`RawStep.discard`, so the old planner is not an alternative disposal rule in this
machine. Running cleanup remains protected from abandonment by the existing
protection check. Capture and resumption carry the new return marker through the
same stack operations; `callback_cut` reuses the existing handler cut unchanged.
Ordinary pending computation encountered during unwinding is abandoned; its
registered cleanup is still executed before its scopes are left.

Normal return through a retirement marker preserves the returned value. Normal
return through a disposal boundary produces Unit for its caller. These two local
exits generalize the old plan's Unit-only boundary behavior; unwinding itself
still produces no ordinary result.

`transition_accounting` covers every new machine transition. The event wrapper
checks fresh owner allocation against lifetime history. `execution_preserves_ledger`
and `execution_no_double_completion` use the existing ledger and the library's
finite-trace induction. `DisposalExample.execution` executes the earlier small
counterexample in eleven transitions, including disposal, an effectful callback,
one resumption, local scope exit and return to the caller. Its final ledger and
`exactly_once` show that all issued owners are completed exactly once.

`FramePorts`, `StackPorts` and `MachinePorts` give structural local port rules
