for ordinary evaluation and unwinding. Ordinary stack typing embeds through
`ordinary_stack_ports`. Composition is explicit at each adjacent frame. The
administrative steps, cleanup call/return and both boundary exits preserve these
ports; retirement carries the same port through, and a close boundary returns
Unit regardless of the abandoned answer port. Existing callable typing is reused.

`handler_cut_ports`, `capture_ports`, `resume_ports` and `discard_ports` extend
the existing stack decomposition and recomposition proofs to the new marker.
They reuse ordinary clause selection, substitution, scope typing and historical
ticket extension. Capture constructs an actual transition and a typed successor;
resume restores the typed capture and clause prefix; discard enters unwinding
without changing the captured handlers or constructing a plan. These are port
results, independent of whether requests have an available interpretation or
whether continuation use and resource access are permitted.

`value_transition_ports` covers every transition starting from a value, including
ordinary frame returns and the new cleanup return marker. `unwind_transition_ports`
covers every transition starting in unwind mode. Both derive successor typing
from predecessor typing and the transition; neither assumes it. Existing value,
context plugging and substitution proofs supply the expression cases.

`ordinary_step_ports` handles bindings, application, branching and builtin cell
reads/writes through the existing ordinary step family. `focus_ports`,
`handler_entry_ports`, `cleanup_entry_machine_ports` and `resource_entry_ports`
construct typed transitions using the existing focus elaboration, clause typing,
callback typing and fresh resource instantiation proofs. World extension checks
every retained frame and dormant capture. These construction results do not
admit arbitrary raw annotation choices.

`effectView` is a proof-only projection that reads an unwind return marker as its
retained armed action for effect checking. It keeps every handler, cell, callback,
and dormant capture. `effect_view_resolve` proves identical nearest-handler
lookup; `effect_view_cut` preserves the selected handler record. Execution,
port typing, ownership and protection use the original stack. This projection
neither builds a disposal schedule nor fabricates a saved result.

`MachineEffects` reuses the existing effect interfaces through this projection.
`machine_request_provided_or_exported` derives interpretation availability or
membership in the outward row. `unwind_transition_effects` covers every
unwind-mode transition, while `capture_effects` and `resume_effects` reuse the
existing effect decomposition, substitution and recomposition proofs.
`discard_effects` requires the captured outward row to be covered by its closing
row. Capture allocates equal resume and closing rows; `closing_rows_insert`
preserves that coverage in the historical registry. `initial_machine_typing`
derives initial port and effect typing from source expression typing alone,
without claiming the other source-admission facets.

`MachineAccess` reuses structural retained-resource support. `discard_access`
uses the existing resumption support proof because the disposer restores the
same enclosing scopes. The close boundary has no resource payload or visibility.
`transition_access` covers every new transition, requiring only local release
and capture checks for ordinary evaluation. Those checks exclude a released
resource from a returned value and establish outward support of a captured
request's operand. Unwind-mode steps need no extra access check, and disposal
has no plan-based access premise. Source derivation of the two ordinary checks
remains necessary.

`UnwindPrefix` structurally checks the scopes before a disposal delimiter,
including recursively owned captures and locally introduced retirement markers.
It has no case for skipping an already running cleanup or crossing another
disposal delimiter. `unprotected_unwind_prefix` derives it from the existing
protection guard at discard; `UnwindReady` places this prefix before the actual
closing boundary and an unrestricted ordinary caller suffix. Every actual
discard constructs this evidence, and administrative unwinding preserves it.

`unwind_progress` proves that such a state has a next transition: pop a scope,
enter a callback, expand a dormant capture, or finish at the delimiter.
`checked_unwind_progress` joins that result with port, effect, resource-support
and ledger preservation for the same actual event. Callback evaluation remains
an ordinary successor; its success or termination is not assumed. Preserving
readiness through callback capture/resumption and return still requires the
source/runtime connection. Neither this branch theorem nor its structural
readiness premise establishes full source progress.

`checkUnwindPrefix` and `checkUnwindReady` decide the structural boundary
judgments. Their soundness/completeness proofs inspect the existing stack,
without building or executing a cleanup plan. `unwind_ready_append_iff` gives
an exact open-stack interface: a composed stack is ready precisely when the
boundary is already in its first fragment, or that fragment is unwindable and
the enclosing suffix supplies the boundary. A capture is therefore not required
to be independently ready.

`handler_cut_unwind_boundary` applies that interface to the existing handler cut.
`callback_resume_ready` recomposes the scopes behind a captured cleanup return
marker. If the boundary is captured, inserted clause frames are outside it;
otherwise the proof requires those inserted frames to be unwindable. The theorem
retains the same selected handler and derives readiness of the restored suffix.
Deriving this local compatibility condition from admitted source, and covering
arbitrary ordinary callback prefixes, remain obligations of the runtime/source
connection; the theorem does not assume the restored successor is ready.

The old `FrameTyped` and source judgments deliberately do not admit the new
internal marker. `FrameUse` and `StackUse` now distinguish ordinary evaluation
from unwinding, with entry and exit modes for each open fragment. Ordinary
frames reuse `FrameDemand`; unwinding skips their pending code and counts only
internal retirement. A live boundary in unwind mode additionally counts its
own eventual retirement. The callback-return marker changes ordinary evaluation
to unwinding; the closing delimiter changes unwinding back to ordinary evaluation.
These are proof interfaces, not additional runtime modes or cleanup plans.

`MachineUse` balances current and pending ticket demand against ownership. It
is an accounting facet, not a replacement for lexical accessibility, protection,
or source admission. The checked results cover all administrative unwind steps,
cleanup entry and return, closing and retirement, evaluation focus, and capture.
Capture retains the saved fragment's actual exit mode and reuses clause-use
substitution and historical registry extension. Initial accounting follows from
the existing source use judgment.

`prefix_use_unwind` converts an abandonable fragment to its owned-ticket demand.
Resume and discard recomposition have checked event-level accounting results.
`discard_machine_use` derives exact capture-demand balance from predecessor
accounting, unique ownership, the existing protection guard and finite bounds
on pending uses in the three affected fragments. `capture_demand_balance` reuses
`balanced_middle_demands`; exact balance is no longer an admission premise.

`returnMode` computes the captured fragment's exit mode from its actual lexical
boundaries. `ReentryBounds` distinguishes ordinary return, which imposes no
abandonment condition, from return into unwinding. The latter checks that the
inserted caller fragment is unwindable, its pending uses are internal, and the
saved and outer fragments do not demand its owners. `reentry_from_bounds`
derives exact caller accounting with the same existing disjoint-demand lemma;
`resume_machine_use` then proves accounting after actual recomposition.
`checkReentryBounds` has a soundness/completeness theorem and inspects only
finite predecessor fragments. The same bounds establish the earlier callback
boundary compatibility through `callback_resume_ready_from_bounds`, including
open captures whose delimiter remains in the enclosing suffix.

`SourceDependencyOwners.PendingFrame` and `PendingStack` connect these pending-use
checks to source dependency annotations for actual retained code. Plain frames
reuse the existing typed context and `Within` judgment; frames with no pending
invocations contribute no pending-use obligation. This includes the new
cleanup-return marker, without pretending that it is an armed callback for
protection or execution. `segment_pending_stack` projects existing source
segments and their `PendingWithin` evidence. Append, decomposition,
administrative unwinding and callback-marker insertion preserve this annotation
with its fixed owner bound.

`source_discard_use` and `source_resume_use` derive event accounting from these
source annotations and predecessor accounting/uniqueness; `ReentrySource`
supplies the local resumption bounds. These judgments check only retained
pending code. Callback bodies, protection and the other runtime facets remain separate
obligations. Establishing and preserving all required source annotations through
arbitrary execution, and joining them in the common invariant, remain unfinished. None of these theorems assumes a valid successor or safe future run.

`UseTransition` now joins all transition families for continuation-use
accounting. Ordinary evaluation reuses the established value-demand,
substitution, context-replacement, scope-entry and resource-update proofs;
resumption and disposal carry the structural bounds described above. Focusing
a nonvalue resumption operand remains ordinary evaluation. Every checked use
transition erases to the existing `Transition`; this introduces no alternative
runtime semantics. The source invocation constructors build its resume/discard
cases from `ReentrySource` and `PendingStack` evidence.

`UseTransition.preserves` is exhaustive for this accounting facet. `UseEvent`
adds fresh allocation and the actual historical ticket registry.
`UseEvent.preserves` combines ownership, registry history and `MachineUse`;
uniqueness and registry freshness follow from the existing ledger and history.
`use_execution_preserves` reuses finite-trace induction, and the initial use
judgment establishes this combined accounting invariant. An event carries no
successor invariant. This theorem concerns checked event sequences: deriving
and preserving their source evidence, combining typing/effects/access/protection,
and proving that a next event exists remain necessary for source safety/progress.

`TicketAccess` now supplies structural continuation accessibility at the same
entry/exit modes as `StackUse`. Ordinary pending code must refer to live tickets
in its enclosing suffix or explicit outside interface. A dormant capture is
checked against the outer tail, excluding its own live owner. Unwinding skips
pending code; internal retirement requires ownership rather than a visible
continuation. The judgment reuses the established pending-name/demand
correspondence, admits every old ordinary `StackUsage` derivation, and introduces
no restriction to nearest-clause invocation.

Append, decomposition, capture, resumption, disposal and administrative unwinding
preserve these interfaces. Removing access to a consumed owner uses existing
uniqueness and demand balance. `MachineTicketAccess` additionally checks the
currently evaluated expression. `UseTransition.ticket_access` and
`UseEvent.preserves_ticket_access` cover every checked transition, including
ordinary callbacks and callbacks entered from unwinding.
`use_execution_preserves_ticket_access` combines accessibility with the existing
ownership/history/use invariant over finite checked executions; initial
accessibility follows from the existing source use judgment.

`live_clause_cannot_return` reuses the existing ownership contradiction to rule
out a value returning past an unconsumed live continuation. This discharges that
specific progress obstruction; it does not by itself prove progress for other
heads or construct the source evidence required at every invocation. Preservation of source expressions and annotations, and the common
typing/effect/resource invariant remain outstanding. The protection connection
below supplies the discard guard from those source expressions.

`CaptureProtection` records a separate fact for each live continuation: its
source contract's protection bit equals the protection of its actual saved
scopes. It recursively checks dormant captures and their tails. It does not
identify disposal permission with absence of protection. The projection
`captureModes` reads these bits from the existing source contracts; there is no
additional runtime registry.

`transition_capture_protection` covers every actual lexical-unwinding transition.
It requires that existing records are retained and that a newly allocated
continuation records the protection of its actual capture. Source contract
extension supplies the former; `source_protection_allocation` supplies the latter
from the contract's capture equality. `segment_capture_protection` extracts the
initial correspondence from the existing source segment, and
`source_capture_protection` reuses fresh insertion and the exact handler cut to
preserve older records while introducing a new capture.

`source_discard_unprotected` inverts the existing source discard rule and uses
the recorded correspondence to establish the runtime protection guard.
`source_checked_discard_transition` combines that guard with the existing
pending-owner bounds to construct the checked disposal transition. It assumes
neither a successful cleanup plan nor a safe successor. These results do not
establish preservation of the current source expression or of callback bodies;
those remain necessary to apply the rule throughout execution.

`SourceDependencyFrames.LexicalFrame` retains every existing rich source-frame
derivation and adds the actual unwinding return frame plus the general answer
interfaces of internal closing and retirement markers. Its `ports` and
`interface` theorems derive both runtime interfaces from the same source frame.
The unwinding rule retains the callback's full function and dependency
annotations without inventing a saved result value.

`LexicalFrame.start_cleanup` constructs the actual callback application using
the existing source application and value-transport rules, preserving its latent
body annotation. `LexicalFrame.finish_cleanup` recovers the Unit input, original
answer interface, saved scope and unchanged effect boundary. The source-stack lift below reuses these local results. Preserving source
expressions throughout callback execution and deriving contextual checks for
callback requests remain necessary.

`LexicalSegment` lifts these frames to the actual recursive stack with the
existing enriched values, requirement indices, dormant continuation records and
dependency scopes. `Segment.lexical` embeds every existing source segment.
Its `ports`, `connected`, `capture_protection` and `realizes` results derive
coherent runtime interfaces and physical protection from that same source.
The effect projection uses the existing permission-sensitive `Connected`
judgment: a dormant continuation does not acquire a resumption obligation when
its clause denies resumption. This is not an unconditional `MachineEffects`
derivation for disabled actions.

`lexical_capture_segments` and `lexical_segment_append` adapt the existing
structural inductions, reusing the same phase, append and requirement-evaluation
lemmas. They preserve the enriched intermediate type, exact dependency scopes
and continuation records, including captures containing unwinding markers.
`LexicalSegment.start_cleanup` constructs the callback source application and
retains the typed suffix; `finish_cleanup` recovers that same suffix and saved
scope. `lexical_segment_pending_stack` connects finite pending-owner bounds on
these scopes to the existing invocation checks. These results preserve source
structure at these boundaries; they do not assert that every resulting
contextual requirement is satisfied or establish a whole-machine source
invariant.

The existing dependency-scope realization now recognizes `.unwinding` as a
running, protected frame. Stored contextual handler declarations recognize it
as a frame with no handler of its own. Their structural checker still checks
each actual handler at its exact suffix; it does not check callback bodies.
`SourceContextualForest.Forest.start_cleanup` and `finish_cleanup` preserve the
suffix's stored handler declarations when changing or removing this marker.
Callback body typing remains the separate source-expression obligation.

`lexical_extract_live` and `lexical_replace_live` adapt the existing source
extraction proof to the lexical stack. They retain the saved enriched source,
replace only the selected live boundary, preserve the continuation-record
permutation, and reuse the existing requirement-evaluation equality after that
owner is consumed. Other captures in the caller prefix remain intact.

`lexical_resume_source` starts from the current source `resume` expression and
the same retained source stack. It derives the closed operand, constructs the
checked runtime resumption, and constructs the resumed value's rich source type
and recomposed stack derivation. The new stack retains the saved and waiting
records, with the consumed owner's resume entry removed. The theorem still
takes the existing finite reentry bounds and the selected action permission;
it does not establish preservation of all contextual requirement checks or
infer those bounds throughout arbitrary execution.

`UnwindRecords.resume_split` now reconstructs the cleanup records from the actual
saved and caller scopes. `UnwindRecords.resume` uses existing owner uniqueness
and record-filter laws to show that the new records are exactly the old records
with the consumed owner's entries removed, up to order. Summaries for nested
captures remain unchanged; no cleanup plan is constructed.

`SourceDependencySchemes.Lexical.resume_segments` joins this result with the rich
source extraction and append proofs. Existing recursive transport checks the
saved and waiting requirements in the recomposed stack, preserving their combined
effect row. The old owner-lookup proof identifies the same source scopes used by
`Local.resume`, so pending-source checks also survive at the actual new owner
phases. Source ownership balance accounts for every remaining continuation.

`resume_source` derives those invocation and waiting checks from a typed current
`resume` expression and the combined pre-step requirement check. It returns the
actual checked runtime step, closed value source, rich recomposed stack, both
record collections, unchanged combined effect row, pending-source checks and
exact ownership accounting. It retains the finite reentry-bound and action
permission premises. Stored handler-declaration certificates, resource-support
checks and cleanup-effect annotations still need to join this result before it
constitutes the full common invariant.

`UnwindRecords.discard` reuses the same record-removal result and inserts the
actual closing delimiter. `selected_template` combines lookup provenance with
physical owner uniqueness to identify the stored summary with the capture being
discarded. It does not choose another handler or infer a fresh cleanup summary.

`SourceDependencySchemes.Lexical.discard_source` now starts from the typed
current discard, its combined requirement check and its local source check.
It retains the rich saved and waiting source fragments, actual stored cleanup
summary, both record collections after owner removal, callback and waiting
checks at the new owner phases, and exact ownership accounting. The existing
finite pending-owner bounds construct the actual checked disposal transition.
The saved fragment remains evidence for its retained scopes; its abandoned
ordinary computation is not asserted to execute or to have a checked row.

The effect conclusion uses `ClosingEffects` for that exact summary at the
surviving closing delimiter followed by the actual waiting stack. It derives
the combined cleanup-and-waiting check and bounds its row by the original row.
The annotation is a finite pre-step obligation; this theorem does not derive
it from ordinary typing or from the earlier capture-time cleanup check.
`closing_delimiter_changes_check` reuses the existing handler-row example to
show why this distinction is necessary: a retained handler can export an
unprotected request, which the surviving closing marker protects again before
it reaches a disposing outer handler. The check without that marker succeeds;
the check with it rejects the request. This is checker evidence, not a claim
that the complete source admission accepts the example.

These disposal results do not yet constitute common preservation. Initial
admission must supply the actual-context cleanup annotation and preserve it,
and handler-declaration and resource-support evidence must accompany callback
execution and subsequent unwinding.

`SourceDependencyProviders.Lexical.local_transport` now preserves the mutual
lexical checks for expressions, pending scopes and unwinding scopes when a
builtin provider is installed. It reuses the existing exact handler and owner
lookup laws, including the case where the builtin handles a request previously
served by a source handler.

`SourceContextualRequirements.Lexical` compiles the existing structural clause
recipes into lexical declaration certificates. The same finite operation
requirements and ordered receiving scopes are checked; there is no new source
syntax. `SourceContextualRechecking.Lexical.resume_rechecked` and
`discard_rechecked` reconstruct stored certificates from these recipes and a
finite check at the actual restored scope. Lexical discard retains the captured
handlers above the closing delimiter. Verified examples include a nonempty
caller stack and a retained handler delegating to an outer interpretation.
These invocation results still require the actual receiving-scope check;
they do not prove that initial admission supplies it at every use.

For these finite handler requirements, `advance_checked` proves preservation
through all six administrative unwind transitions: ordinary-frame pop,
handler pop, resource release, spent-marker pop, entering a live capture and
retiring its owner. The live-capture case reuses capability lookup through the
retirement delimiter and stack-append factorization. It derives the successor
check from the current check. `advance_rechecked` reconstructs the resulting
lexical handler certificates from retained recipes. This transport concerns
operation capabilities with both protection modes; it does not make the
closing delimiter transparent to arbitrary cleanup-effect checks.

`SourceDependencySchemes.Lexical.local_restrict` and `unwind_restrict` now
reuse the existing finite `AvailableOn` relation and owner-cut laws. They
preserve lexical checks when phase changes retain availability for the live
owners those scopes can reach. The independent relation, cut laws and
`realized_available` proof were moved upstream with their existing names and
proofs so both lexical and legacy checks can reuse them. No invocation right
is inferred from an effect occurrence.

`SourceDependencyFrames.unwind_owner_phases` projects the existing runtime
owner-accounting permutation onto continuation owners. The established
phase-consumption theorem then identifies the resulting map with availability
in the actual successor stack, and preserves owner uniqueness.

`SourceContextualCapture.Lexical.advance_unwind_components` joins these results
for an active unwind prefix and an arbitrary retained caller suffix. From the
current authenticated source summary, cleanup-effect annotation, callback
checks, finite handler checks and recipes, resource support and unique ownership,
it derives
the corresponding successor evidence for all six administrative transitions.
Callback and effect checks use the actual successor owner phases. The new
summary still accounts for precisely the owners in the remaining prefix, and
the cleanup-effect budget is unchanged. The proof reuses administrative resource
support, source-summary preservation, finite handler rechecking and ownership
accounting; it assumes no successor certificate.

The same theorem now retains the rich waiting source and its continuation
records. `unwindStore` states the exact administrative record update: opening a
live capture removes that owner's callable entries; other administrative steps
keep the store unchanged. It is a proof-level store projection, not a cleanup
schedule. The existing record-removal laws preserve all surviving payloads and
unique keys. `UnwindRecords.advance` preserves the structural disposal-record
collection, and `resume_records_advance` preserves each surviving resume
record's actual-capture provenance and rich source certificate. No replacement
record is inferred.

The active summary's ownership permutation and the existing phase laws identify
the caller's phase map after cleanup with precisely its retained owners.
`unwind_waiting_checked` then reuses removal of a consumed owner's records to
preserve the caller's requirement check. The combined theorem derives the
cleanup-and-waiting requirement check in the updated store at the actual
successor phases, with the same cleanup budget and waiting row. The waiting
source's own resume records are unchanged. `opening_before_retirement` verifies
that opening removes both modes' records while the retirement marker still
owns the ticket; only its later pop discharges that ownership.

`UnwindSource` now retains the summary and dependency scope in one structural
derivation. Its cleanup rule uses one typed callback for both the effect row and
dependency annotation. `LexicalSegment.unwind_source` constructs this witness
from the actual unprotected captured source. Append, registry extension and
administrative unwinding preserve it. `Scope.afterUnwind` names the resulting
source scope; the runtime `Advance` rule still determines which pop is legal.
The combined administrative theorem now retains this shared witness instead of
independently choosing a summary and a stack realization.

The handler rule also retains the installed handler's original rich `Frame`
derivation. A callback may still request that interpretation while its scopes
are being abandoned. `UnwindSource.handler_source` retrieves this declaration
at the actual handler cut. `unwind_selected_body` joins it with the contextual
forest's certificate at the same remaining suffix, then reuses the established
clause-selection theorem to recover the rich typed clause body and dependency
family. Append, source-registry extension and unwinding preserve this evidence.
No ordinary pending-code effect composition is required for the abandoned suffix.
This supplies selected clause source; it does not yet prove the complete mixed
callback state is preserved through dispatch and resumption.

`allocate_disposing_capture` constructs that witness from the same saved source
used for the selected clause. It retains the exact witness under the fresh
continuation contract. `start_unwind_cleanup_components` then joins actual
callback application typing, its checked effect row and budget, its lexical
dependency check, retained handler certificates and resource support. The
remaining abandoned source and its cleanup budget are retained separately from
the callback being evaluated. Both continuation-record collections remain
unchanged, with their capture provenance intact, and the owner ledger is
preserved. The caller suffix is arbitrary.

`finish_unwind_cleanup_components` joins the existing return-marker, record,
support and ledger proofs at an actual Unit return. It resumes unwinding at the
callback's saved scope and discharges precisely its cleanup owner. It does not
assert that a callback terminates, or establish the intervening evaluation.

`UnwindAnnotated` connects each stored disposal body to its actual captured
source and recorded dependency scope. It reuses the existing structural
`Closing.Bound` judgment to connect the recorded scope to the live boundary.
`selected_unwind_source` combines record lookup, that bound and capture
uniqueness to recover the exact `UnwindSource` checked at disposal. It does not
assume that independently chosen annotations of the same callback are equal.
Bare `UnwindRecords` remains the structural store layout; these certificates
supply the additional source evidence for its exact payloads.

`capture_annotated_records` records the annotation with the fresh capture, and
`allocate_disposing_capture` now returns that bound and all resulting record
certificates. `resume_segments` and `resume_source` retain them during actual
recomposition. `discard_source` now returns the selected authenticated source,
the bound for the actual closing marker and caller, and certificates for every
surviving record. The proofs reuse record-removal permutations, capture
provenance and annotation splitting. Administrative unwinding and both callback
boundary theorems retain these same facts. No extra runtime lookup or cleanup
schedule is introduced.

`allocate_resuming_capture` now returns the same recorded-scope invariant.
Its lower allocation proof chooses any optional disposal body from the actual
saved `UnwindSource`: protected captures add no disposal entry, while
unprotected captures retain the chosen body's exact dependency annotation.
Both cases preserve all earlier certificates under the fresh contract.

`UnwindRecords.ordinary_step` derives the surviving disposal collection for
ordinary evaluation without continuation capture. It includes resource and
cleanup allocation, cell updates and resumption. Resumption reuses the existing
owner-removal permutation; the other cases keep the entries unchanged. The
legacy plan-based discard is excluded by the lexical machine's ordinary-step
condition. `annotated_records_ordinary_step` then reuses saved-capture origin and
uniqueness to preserve each retained entry's source witness. It assumes no
successor record collection.

The thirteen ordinary source-boundary theorems in
`SourceDependencyNeutral.Lexical` now also preserve `Closing.Bound` for the
same source scopes: focus and plug; cleanup registration, normal callback entry
and return; handler entry and exit; resource entry and exit; cell read and write;
spent-clause return; and value return through a closing delimiter. They reuse
the existing bound constructors and recover the retained suffix from the same
source frame. No transition chooses a fresh annotation for an existing capture.
The judgment's declaration moved to `SourceDependencyChecks`, retaining its
name and constructors, so these earlier source proofs can use it without an
import cycle. Capture, resume, discard and unwinding retain their existing
bound proofs.

These results cover the stored-certificate facet of ordinary evaluation; they
do not yet preserve the complete machine invariant. Expression typing,
actual-context effects and the recorded-scope bound must still be joined across
callback body execution, including a running prefix above abandoned scopes.
Sufficient initial admission and the complete preservation/progress chain remain
unfinished. The administrative theorem's handler-recipe premise has the same
coverage limit as the rechecker above.

The lexical forest also now has append, cleanup-entry and cleanup-return
proofs, reusing the corresponding structural inductions. These results concern
stored handler certificates. Callback expression checks, resource support and
cleanup effects remain separate facets to combine. The existing recipe language
covers a useful structural subset, including only pure cleanup in its cleanup
constructor; it does not yet provide the full source admission required here.

`LexicalFrame.transport` and `LexicalSegment.transport` reuse ordinary source
transport to preserve the exact rich annotations when fresh continuation
contracts, action records or resources extend their environments. This includes
callbacks and dormant non-resumable captures. Neither transport changes the
existing requirements, dependency scopes or effect boundaries.

`rich_focus_decompose` and `rich_context_plug` adapt the existing declared
source context proofs to enriched dependency annotations. All ten strict focus
positions are covered. Their requirement-evaluation equations reuse the
existing sequence, value and phase laws. `FocusDependencies` records the exact
dependency-tree transformation: ordinary sequencing, a pure pair, removal of a
silent left value, or removal of a silent function prefix. Latent bodies remain
in the same enriched function type.

`lexical_focus_source` chooses one actual plain frame from the source derivation
and constructs both the checked runtime focus step and its typed source stack.
`lexical_plug_source` restores the scope stored in that frame, transports the
returned value's rich annotation, and constructs the checked plug step and
remaining source stack. `focus_dependencies_checked` and
`plug_dependencies_checked` connect the same dependency transformations to the
existing local contextual checks. The former reuses neutral-scope transport
only when inserting a pure waiting frame; the latter uses the returned value's
silent dependencies. These are preservation components for ordinary evaluation,
not a proof of all lexical-disposal admission checks or whole-source progress.

`SourceDependencyChecks.UnwindPending` checks an abandoned source prefix
against a separate enclosing suffix. It drops requirements for ordinary code
that will not execute, retains each callback check at its actual running scope,
and checks a nested live capture with its pending retirement marker. Callback
checking is an explicit parameter, not an assumption that future execution is
safe. The `append_iff` proof adapts the existing pending-source induction.
`advance` connects this judgment to all six actual administrative unwind rules,
using the existing scope realization and append proofs. Actual runtime rules
still determine which protected markers may be removed.

The strengthened lexical cleanup-entry theorems identify the exact stored
callback dependencies and source suffix. `UnwindPending.start_cleanup` uses
these equalities to construct the typed callback application and recover its
check at that same suffix; `finish_cleanup` retains the suffix checks when the
actual unwinding marker is removed. `cleanup_application_checked` reuses the
existing silent-prefix law. Positive and negative resource examples show that
a callback can use its still-enclosing resource, while removing that resource
first invalidates the callback check.

`SourceDependencyChecks.Lexical` now supplies concrete mutual `Local`,
`Pending` and `Unwind` judgments for these boundaries. Its capture guard retains
operation selection, clause-row availability and protection checks without a
closing plan. Its disposal rule checks the actual accessible owner, independent
disposal permission, available phase and unprotected capture. It then checks the
abandoned callbacks against the actual closing delimiter and waiting caller,
and checks that caller's ordinary retained code. Both checks use the phase in
which the disposed owner has been consumed. A disposing request also carries a structural `Unwind` check of its captured
callbacks at the actual enclosing suffix, under a closing marker. This supplies
the callback premise used when admitting a disposing clause. It inspects retained
source syntax; it does not extract a plan or assume successful future execution.
The old plan-dependent judgments remain available for legacy proofs; they are
not the selected lexical rules.

`Local.discard_step` reuses source owner lookup and scope realization to
construct the actual lexical discard transition. It retains the capture and
caller annotations separately, together with their respective checks.
`Local.resume_step` reuses the existing resumption correspondence and retains
pending-source checks for the actual recomposed stack. These are transition
connections, not rich-expression preservation or whole-source progress proofs.

The mutual `Unwind` judgment converts to and from `UnwindPending` with its
concrete `Local` callback predicate. This allows administrative popping and
cleanup entry/return to reuse the preceding generic proofs. The mutual form
avoids Lean's restriction on nested inductive parameters containing local phase
indices. The ordinary silent-source, sequencing and pending-scope append/capture
proofs use the existing structural inductions unchanged. Examples accept
disposal whose captured cleanup still needs a captured handler, reject a handler
that would cancel a running callback, and reject both resume and discard when
the owner is already consumed.

`SourceDependencyNeutral.Lexical.local_transport` adapts the existing mutual
scope-expansion proof to all three lexical judgments. It reuses the existing
operation-cut and owner-cut transport results. The disposal case transports
its captured callbacks and waiting caller separately; no plan projection is
used. Pure waiting frames, pure cleanup and spent markers preserve checks,
including checks nested in callbacks and dormant captures.

The lexical focus/plug bridges now retain the exact dependency-tree relation
from the rich source proofs. `focus_preserves_source` constructs the same actual
runtime frame, typed child, typed pending stack, child check and retained caller
check. `plug_preserves_source` obtains the waiting check from that exact frame
and proves the recomposed expression checked. The strengthened
`lexical_plug_source` conclusion explicitly equates the original source scope
with the returned context and suffix annotations; an unrelated existential
context annotation cannot supply this check. Both combined theorems return the
actual checked runtime step. Existing substitution, bind, beta and branch proofs
also retain the new lexical checks, reusing their original rich-source and
requirement-evaluation lemmas.

The lexical scope connections now also cover cleanup registration, normal
cleanup invocation/return, and handler installation/exit. Cleanup registration
constructs one actual action from the source callback value, retaining its rich
body annotation and the body check under the armed frame. Normal invocation
retains the returned body value in the running frame and obtains the callback
check from the actual pending source. Return restores that same rich value and
saved scope. Handler exit similarly recovers the existing checked suffix.
Each theorem constructs the corresponding checked runtime transition.

`frame_registries` and `segment_registries` adapt the existing handler-table
transport proof to preserve both tables and rich clause families. They cover
dormant captures as well as the active stack. `enter_handler_source` chooses an
installation identity fresh for the supplied activation history, registers the
exact table and families obtained from source inversion, and constructs the
typed installed frame and body checks. Existing installations keep their table
and family annotations. This does not yet prove contextual admission of a
selected clause when a later operation invokes it.

The support connection reuses the independent finite support environment in
`ScopedPorts.Support`. `substitution_preserves_source_support` retains rich
source typing, the lexical dependency check and the support calculation for the
same substituted body. Its closed instance reuses the existing parameter-binding
support theorem and applies equally to a local binding or selected clause
parameter. Neither theorem infers physical captures from a function port.

`Scope.visibleResources` follows only active lexical resource scopes.
`Realizes.visible_resources` identifies that list with actual runtime visibility;
dormant captures remain ownership without caller access. `source_payload_at_cut`
reuses the existing handler-cut correspondence to show that an operand bound
checked at the selected source handler's outer suffix supplies the actual
runtime payload condition.

`source_request_access` packages that result into the ordinary machine's local
access conditions. It reuses the same source selection for every actual runtime
cut of the request; operand and effect identities follow from the concrete
request expression. The value-release case is impossible for an operation
request. The result adds no restriction on operation ports or callable values.

`leave_resource_source` combines a finite value-support annotation excluding the
released identity with rich source typing and the actual cell frame. It derives
the local access checks, constructs the checked resource-exit transition, and
preserves the source suffix and runtime resource-access invariant. This applies
to closures as well as scalar values. The existing escaping-closure example
cannot satisfy such an annotation excluding its captured resource.

These are connections from explicit support annotations, not a proof that
initial admission supplies and preserves every required annotation. Existing
finite template and completion-contract analyses remain reusable where their
premises hold; their unknown application results or finite operation-port
restrictions are not adopted as restrictions on the target source grammar.
The lexical world-extension proofs now cover `Local`, `Pending` and `Unwind`
by mutual structural induction. Resource-body checks instantiate only identities
still fresh in the enlarged world. Checks in callbacks and dormant captures retain
their exact scopes; extending the historical world grants no new resource access.

`enter_resource_source` constructs the actual opened body and cell frame at a
supplied fresh identity. It preserves the checked pending suffix in the enlarged
world, derives the body's lexical check from the source resource rule and retains
the exact requirement-hiding relation for effect checking. The body, frame and
runtime allocation use the same identity. This construction does not yet join
fresh lifetime-history accounting or requirement-row evaluation to a common state.

`cell_update_segment` adapts the existing cell-selection induction to rich lexical
segments. Read and write preserve the exact dependency scope, demand, requirements
and stored continuation annotations of the pending segment, including dormant
captures. `read_cell_source` and `write_cell_source` derive the reply's rich type
from the operation signature and construct the checked runtime step. They take an
actual cell selection as input; deriving selection at every reachable builtin
request remains part of the common progress proof.

`leave_clause_source` restores the caller stored in an already-spent boundary,
preserving the returned value's rich summary and the checked suffix.
`close_value_source` produces Unit at a disposal delimiter and restores its actual
caller. Neither boundary consumes a continuation owner; these proofs do not
replace the outstanding transport across resume, discard or retirement phases.

`SourceDependencySchemes.Lexical` now adapts the existing fresh-owner admission
proofs to these lexical checks. Its `CaptureSource` contains finite checks of the
saved computation, waiting caller and abandoned callbacks after consumption of
the newly allocated owner. `capture_source_from_request` derives those premises
from the current request and pending source: fresh permission insertion preserves
old permissions, and consuming the newly introduced owner restores the original
phase map. This does not establish preservation when consuming an existing owner.

The uniform `ClauseFamily` rule supplies reusable proofs for simple resume and
discard families. Both follow the existing owner-cut, append and neutral-history
transports. This uniform rule is not the general clause-admission requirement:
the existing outer-handler counterexample shows why the enclosing interpretation
scope must be retained.

`SourceContextualClauses.Lexical.FamilyAt` instead checks each dependency family
at its actual enclosing scope. Its `DeclarationsAt` judgment selects the family
of the actual clause and protection mode; value substitution and resource-name
instantiation preserve these certificates. The existing exact-tail operation
capability supplies reusable nondisposing requests. Positive examples admit a
clause that calls an outer handler before resuming, including repeated calls;
the corresponding absent-handler case remains rejected.

The lexical stored `Forest` in `SourceContextualForest` attaches each handler's
certificate to its exact annotated suffix and checks dormant captures recursively.
Its cut and alignment proofs reuse the existing structural handler-cut induction.
Successful selection aligns stored and typed source decompositions; no uniqueness
of arbitrary annotations is assumed. Capture retains both certified subforests.

`SourceContextualCapture.Lexical.capture_checked_interfaces` joins the actual
lexical runtime cut, rich source segment and contextual forest. It authenticates
the handler, captured segment, caller, source family and requirement decomposition,
and derives the selected family's local check and retained live-scope check at
the fresh owner. Its typed body remains parametric in a matching fresh continuation
contract. Constructing that contract's complete resume/disposal requirements,
substituting the operand and joining the resulting runtime capture remain open.
Initial construction and preservation of the contextual forest through the other
execution families are also outstanding. The positive disposing-request example
retains the captured handler needed by cleanup, so the new request premise does
not restore the old planner's scope loss.

`SourceDependencyFrames.UnwindTemplate` now describes disposal requirements by
structural traversal of the actual captured stack. It drops abandoned ordinary
computation, retains each callback's actual enclosing interpretation context,
and places a nested owner's retirement after its saved scopes. Its demand is a
permutation of the stack's recursively owned continuations, with multiplicity.
The construction follows any unprotected rich source segment and does not use
`makePlan`. This is proof data; runtime unwinding still inspects only the top scope.

`UnwindTemplate.append` preserves callback contexts under stack recomposition.
Its evaluation does not depend on the continuation-template store. Contract and
resource-world extension preserve the same summary. `advance_checked` covers
all six administrative unwind cases and spends exactly the continuation owners
discharged by the actual step. `start_cleanup` extracts the typed callback
application, its checked effect row under the actual unwinding marker, and the
checked requirements for the remaining scopes. These results do not establish
preservation during the callback's intervening evaluation.

`UnwindRecords` collects disposal entries from the rich source stack, including
dormant captures. A protected capture contributes no disposal entry; its nested
records are retained. Each entry is certified against an actual saved capture.
`lookup_ownership` identifies that capture and proves that the looked-up demand
accounts for exactly its owned continuations. Collection requires no successful
future execution or pre-existing closing plan. Record composition and extension
reuse the existing structural inductions; uniqueness of combined resume/disposal
keys reuses the existing ownership and list laws.

The retained-handler example uses the callback and captured stack from
`InitialCleanupRouteGap`. Its structural summary checks with an empty outward
row and supplies an authenticated disposal record. Removing the callback's
handler leaves an outward requirement, so the same callback cannot check as a
closed disposal. This checks the scope distinction that the old planner lost.

`SourceContextualCapture.Lexical.disposing_capture_summary` connects construction
to the actual selected request: its lexical capture permission establishes that
the typed saved stack is unprotected, and that stack supplies its disposal
summary and ownership equation. This construction does not itself show that
the ordinary source demand accounts for those owners or that the closing row
checks in the receiving context.

`SourceDependencyOwners.Lexical` now supplies the ownership-balance connection.
Its `ResumeCertified` retains the exact rich saved derivation behind each resume
entry, including lexical cleanup return markers. Ordinary frame retirement and
pending-call bounds reuse source erasure and the existing proofs. The additional
markers have no direct invocation; retirement contributes its actual owner.
Mode-specific lookup combines these resume certificates with `UnwindRecords`.

The existing checked-derivation inductions now use these lexical certificates.
`checked_capture_spines` connects consumption of an owner to consumption of its
saved immediate owners. `checked_internal_demand` keeps demands within an actual
captured region when its pending uses are internal. Both reuse the established
capture inclusion and uniqueness lemmas; disposal uses the structural summary's
ownership equation instead of a plan's retirements.

`captured_segment_balance` reuses `ownership_tree_consumed` unchanged to prove
that a checked rich capture's ordinary demand is a permutation of its recursively
owned continuations. Its premises are an authenticated source/record store,
unique physical owners, the actual capture location, internal pending uses,
a check of the saved requirements, and availability of the captured owners.
`captured_modes_balance` therefore equates that demand with any authenticated
lexical disposal summary. `captured_closing_requirements` constructs such a
balanced summary for an unprotected capture. Neither theorem assumes budget
equality or successful future execution.

The whole-stack instances derive ownership balance and consumption of every
owned continuation from the current check. `source_ownership_balance` includes
the present rich expression and pending lexical segment; balance is a consequence
of their checked requirements, not an additional admission premise.

`LexicalSegment.owned_registered` and `fresh_unowned` connect contract-registry
freshness to actual ownership, including pending retirement markers. Capture
uniqueness then reuses the existing ownership equation. `UnwindRecords` splits
at the actual lexical cut and constructs the new disposal entry from its chosen
summary. A protected capture preserves its nested entries without gaining a
disposal entry.

`SourceDependencySchemes.Lexical.allocate_split` constructs the fresh rich
contract, live source segment and extended disposal records from the typed split.
It preserves the saved and caller requirement checks with the existing generic
fresh-record insertion lemmas. The new source uses the same input, answer,
dependency scopes, interfaces and requirement indices as that split. The proof
also derives the fresh resumption invocation check and the exact phase equation.

`allocate_disposing_split` specializes this construction to an unprotected
capture with internal pending uses. Its closing row is the evaluation of the
actual lexical summary. The constructed source and records supply the premises
of `captured_modes_balance`, so allocation derives owner-demand agreement
without assuming that the two demands match. The disposal invocation check follows whenever that
row evaluation succeeds. `closing_invocation_from_record` reuses the established
invocation construction, replacing only plan ownership and store independence
with the lexical summary lemmas. These are allocation connections from the
present split checks; they do not assume an admitted successor.

`ClosingEffects` supplies the remaining finite cleanup annotation. Its four
structural rules cover callback requests, retirement, spent boundaries and
sequencing in the exact closing requirement tree. A request carries an upper
footprint, its export through the actual nearer and receiving interpretations,
and inclusion of that export in the declared budget. Sequencing advances the
owner phase by the first part's demand. A spent boundary checks consumption;
retirement readiness follows separately from actual ownership.

`ClosingEffects.checked` reuses uniform residual coverage and owner-trace
composition to construct the existing requirement check. `UnwindTemplate` then
derives the required trace from physical ownership, uniqueness and availability.
The converse `effects_of_checked` and `effects_iff` show that this annotation
accepts every successfully checked lexical closing row within the budget. The
existing finite evaluator can therefore check it. There is no new runtime
evaluator, generated cleanup plan or restriction on the callback's source syntax.
The retained-handler example constructs the annotation; removing that handler
still rejects an empty budget.

`advance_effects` preserves this annotation through all six administrative
unwind cases by reusing `advance_checked`. `start_cleanup_effects` derives the
actual callback application, its checked effect budget and the annotation for
the remaining scopes using `start_cleanup`. Both use the current ownership
trace. Neither repeats the runtime case proof or assumes a checked successor;
callback execution and the combined source invariant remain separate work.

Given this annotation with budget `requestRow ++ capRow`,
`allocate_disposing_split` now constructs the complete clause invocation
interface. Closing-row success, its advertised coverage and caller owner
freshness are conclusions. The proof derives retirement availability from the
actual cut and uses the already constructed resume and disposal invocation
checks. Establishing and preserving the annotation from initial source admission
remains a source-invariant obligation; it is not a claim that ordinary saved-row
typing alone supplies the cleanup budget.

`SourceContextualCapture.Lexical.disposing_capture_summary` also derives the
actual capture's pending-owner bound from the selected request's structural
source check. It reuses `lexical_segment_pending_stack`, `PendingStack.internal`
and the realization equation for live owners. The allocation theorem's internal
use premise therefore has a source derivation at this same cut; it is not an
independently assumed fact about the runtime capture.

`ClauseRowAdmission.SourceStore` accepts structural source evidence for
lexical completion frames and disposal records. Legacy `StoreSegment` evidence
embeds in `StoreModeSource`; the mixed constructors distinguish value results
from unwinding. `StoreClosingTemplate` retains each typed callback and its
actual interpretation suffix. Legacy stores embed through `SourceStore.of_source`;
this proof compatibility does not add a runtime disposal path. Resume-record
certification recovers the registered header's exact input and owner demand,
and a return boundary equal to its answer or unwinding.

`LexicalSegment.row_store` constructs that evidence from the actual rich lexical
segment, its `UnwindRecords` and the same registered contract. The existing
`Rows` checker and its instantiation theorem are unchanged. A clause's source
certificate now ranges over lexical stores as well as the earlier stores; it
does not assume arbitrary stores are authentic. No successful row evaluation or
valid successor is part of store authentication.

`LexicalSegment.instantiate_clause` joins this store evidence with the selected
rich clause and actual operand. It reuses substitution and `Rows.instantiate`
to derive the substituted expression and its check at the same requirement
index, with the advertised effect bound. Its local invocation interface is now
constructed by disposing allocation from the structural cleanup annotation. The
selected clause, allocation and actual runtime capture results are now joined
at their exact shared inputs by the two allocation cases below. These source
checks are not yet preserved through every execution step or assembled into
initial-source safety.

`SourceDependencySchemes.Lexical.allocate_disposing_clause_from_split` combines
allocation, the structural cleanup annotation and clause instantiation. It
returns the actual raw capture step, the exact new owner list and its uniqueness,
the live source stack and records, and the substituted clause with its checked
effect bound. `complete_allocated_clause` reuses clause-usage substitution,
`consuming_usage_completed` and `consuming_clause_balance` to derive the selected
clause's consumption and demand permutation. Both allocation cases now join the
clause and waiting requirements at their actual successive owner phases, then
reuse `source_ownership_balance` to account for every owner in the new stack.
The combined check and ownership permutation are conclusions, not extra
admission premises.

`SourceContextualCapture.Lexical.allocate_disposing_capture`
derives the split, selected clause factory and cleanup summary from the same
pre-step source witnesses. It also retains the selected clause's local check,
pending checks and contextual forest. Cleanup-effect coverage remains an
explicit finite annotation; this result does not infer it from ordinary typing.

The corresponding `allocate_resuming_clause_from_split` and
`allocate_resuming_capture` cover clauses without disposal permission. They
handle protected and unprotected captures without an internal-use restriction
or a successful cleanup-effect premise. For an unprotected capture, the stored
cleanup summary is structural bookkeeping; it grants no disposal permission.
Both cases use the existing allocation and substitution proofs. Neither assumes
a successor invariant or changes runtime unwinding.

Remaining source integration must cover support propagation, selected clause
execution, continuation phase changes and the other control boundaries, then
establish the combined invariant from initial source admission. No preservation
result for the legacy plan-dependent checks discharges those obligations.

General progress for this machine is not proved. Earlier plan-dependent source
theorems do not prove it. This work replaces the disposal part of the handler/cleanup
connection in the remaining proof construction above; it is not a new milestone.
The scope-exit mechanism is intended to be shared by later continuation targets,
but only the one-shot ownership policy is being implemented and proved here.

The earlier `ExplicitCleanupReference` experiment in the same module proves
installation identity binding and unchanged operation ports. It remains only
binding evidence: lookup by identity does not keep a removed scope alive, and
its reference type is not a new dispatch rule. Retain these lemmas only where
the local scope representation uses them. The retained-plan prototype remains
scratch comparison evidence and is not part of the selected execution design.

## Pending checks across cleanup returns

`SourceDependencyChecks.Lexical.ModePending` retains the actual runtime frame
alongside its dependency scope and the existing ordinary/unwind usage modes.
Ordinary plain frames retain their local source check; abandoned plain frames
are skipped. An unwind-callback return marker changes ordinary execution back
to unwinding, and a closing delimiter restores ordinary execution. Armed
callbacks retain their local check in either mode. Opening a live capture for
unwinding checks its saved scopes behind the actual retirement marker.

Recomposition joins the first fragment's exit mode to the second fragment's
entry mode. Splitting at an actual handler cut derives that intermediate mode,
including cuts across a callback return marker. The judgment agrees with the
existing runtime `returnMode`; it adds no runtime mode or evaluator. Existing
ordinary `Segment` checks and authenticated `UnwindSource` checks embed into
it. The ordinary embedding does not assert that every `LexicalSegment` has an
ordinary exit mode.

The existing `advance_unwind_components`, `start_unwind_cleanup_components`
and `finish_unwind_cleanup_components` now take these structural checks for
the current actual stack and derive them for the successor stack. Administrative
unwinding also derives their restriction to the actual successor owner phases,
reusing local capability restriction and `realized_available`. Cleanup entry
checks the callback in ordinary mode; Unit return exposes the retained suffix
in unwind mode. No successor mode check is a premise.

These results preserve contextual pending-code checks at those boundaries.
The mixed source judgment below supplies rich source composition and selected
expression boundaries. `Local.resume` still uses the existing restored
`Pending` premise; replacing that connection and joining the remaining source
facets remain necessary. Complete initial admission, common preservation,
progress and terminal accounting are still unproved for the lexical-unwinding
source calculus.

## Rich source across ordinary execution and unwinding

`SourceDependencyFrames.ModeSource` composes source at a `ModeValue` boundary:
either a rich value is expected, or execution is unwinding and no abandoned
result value is supplied. This is a source judgment, not a new runtime mode.
Its return mode agrees with the existing runtime `returnMode`.

Ordinary frames reuse the rich `Frame` derivation, including higher-order value
and callback annotations. In unwind mode, skipped plain frames contribute no
ordinary requirements. Installed handlers retain their typed declarations and
armed callbacks retain one typing witness for their latent requirements and
dependencies. An unwind-return marker changes a Unit boundary to unwinding;
a closing delimiter changes unwinding back to Unit. Dormant captures retain
their source, while opening an abandoned capture contributes its cleanup
requirements and the existing retirement requirement. Continuation permissions,
stored-record certificates and physical resource support remain separate checks.

`Segment.mode_source` embeds ordinary source with the same rich values, demand,
requirements and scope. `UnwindSource.mode_source` embeds abandoned source with
the same demand and scope; additional empty sequencing nodes have exactly the
same requirement evaluation. The mixed relation does not impose an ordinary
effect-interface inclusion across abandoned frames. Its executed requests must
still pass the contextual `Checked` requirement judgment and local dependency
checks; the relation alone is not source admission.

`ModeSource.append` and `split` preserve the complete requirement-evaluation
equation for arbitrary stores, receiving interpretations and owner phases.
`handler_cut` reuses the split and retains the selected handler declaration from
the same derivation. The captured boundary is either that handler's rich answer
or unwinding. This covers cuts across callback return markers without assigning
ordinary requirements to abandoned code. `mode_selected_body` reuses the
existing contextual clause proof at the actual selected installation; the older
`unwind_selected_body` now follows through the abandoned-source embedding.

`ModeSource.start_cleanup`, `finish_cleanup`, `advance_checked` and
`finish_close` derive the successor rich source and its checked requirements
at the actual control boundaries. Callback entry reuses the factored
`cleanup_application_checked` calculation also used by `UnwindSource`, including
protection at the real unwinding marker. The existing
`SourceDependencyNeutral.Lexical.focus_preserves_source` and
`plug_preserves_source` now use `ModeSource` and `ModePending`, preserving the
same recorded-scope bound while ordinary expression evaluation proceeds over a
mixed suffix. Their rich expression decomposition and substitution proofs are
reused.

`ModeSource.unwind_source` now derives the caller fragment's cleanup source
from its retained source and the existing `UnwindPrefix` check. It keeps the
same dependency scope, handler declarations and callback typing witnesses;
it skips ordinary code and includes retirement markers. The resulting demand
accounts for precisely the fragment's owned continuations by the existing
`UnwindTemplate.ownership` theorem.

`reentry_unwind_balance` factors the existing usage-accounting proof so source
reentry can reuse it. `ModeSource.reentry_from_bounds` derives the caller's
source at the actual captured return mode. `resume_recomposition` then joins
the saved continuation, the derived caller fragment and the spent-owner suffix,
with total demand equal up to permutation to the physical owned continuations.
The source-demand and usage-demand lists are related by explicit permutations;
identical order is not required. These are source and ownership results. They
do not yet establish that the new cleanup requirements pass their effect check
in the actual receiving scope, or preserve all contextual capability checks.

`ModeSource.extract_live` obtains the three fragments from the predecessor
source. It derives exclusion of the invoked owner from pending demand using
`checked_once` on the current resume requirement and pending requirements. That
owner therefore cannot be in the implicit-retirement case. The live boundary
retains the exact contract input and answer types and the saved return mode.

`ResumeAnnotated` pairs a stored resume body with its chosen `ModeSource`,
contract and recorded dependency scope. `selected_resume_source` recovers that
exact body through lookup, capture identity and `Closing.Bound`. The contract
fixes the rich answer and the actual `returnMode` distinguishes ordinary return
from unwinding; the proof assumes no general uniqueness of typing annotations.
`extract_recorded_resume` joins this lookup to predecessor-source extraction,
replacing the saved witness with the exact recorded requirements. Fresh capture,
registry extension, administrative unwinding and removal of the resumed owner's
records preserve the paired certificate. The existing capture-location and
source-transport proofs are reused.

`ReturnEffects` gives the caller's additional check two structural cases.
Ordinary return reuses its existing source and requirement check. Unwind return
carries its lexical `UnwindSource`, a demand permutation and `ClosingEffects`
at the actual receiving interpretations and owner phase. The demand permutation
checks that abandoning the caller accounts for the same outstanding owners.
The effect budget is explicit and must cover the ordinary caller row as well.
This annotation contains no successor machine or quantification over execution.
`ReturnEffects.unwind_iff` proves that, for the retained cleanup source, its
effect obligation is equivalent to the existing finite requirement evaluator
succeeding within that budget. It does not establish whole-program inference.

`ReturnEffects.source_checked` derives retirement readiness from the
predecessor's checked owner trace, using the existing trace-permutation and
cleanup-effect lemmas. It produces the caller's source and effect check for
the actual return mode. `ModeSource.append_checked` and
`resume_checked_recomposition` then derive the check for the complete restored
stack. They retain the declared caller budget and the saved-body and tail rows.
They do not assume a checked successor.

`resume_checked_fragments` joins the strengthened `extract_recorded_resume`
to requirement checking: it obtains the exact saved body's check from the
actual invocation, splits the caller and tail checks from the predecessor, and
removes the consumed owner's records. Context transport reuses normalization
of the actual live-to-spent boundary. The extraction result also retains its
requirement-evaluation equation and the restored recorded-scope bound.

`resume_mode_segments` uses those results with `ModeSource` and
`ResumeAnnotated`. Given a matching cleanup branch in the annotated predecessor
when the capture returns by unwinding, it derives the restored source, bounded
effect row, actual successor owner phase and exact physical owner balance;
surviving resume and disposal certificates are preserved.
Ownership derives the predecessor's whole-state demand balance from its checked
source and exact records, then uses the established physical resumption
permutation. This checked route does not require the three
source-versus-usage fragment permutations of the earlier source-only theorem.
Its conclusion exposes the exact caller source and the structural branch
coverage still required. It does not prove that every previously admitted
resume site supplies that coverage.

`capture_mode_segments` now constructs the mixed source, exact resume and
cleanup certificates, recorded-scope bound and checked resume interface from
the actual predecessor handler cut and a selected checked annotation branch.
A normal branch is always supplied. The allocated contract has no advertised
disposal row, as in the existing resume-only allocator. Protected captures
retain their nested cleanup records; unprotected captures derive their cleanup
source through the existing structural unwind-prefix proof. The result retains
the selected handler declaration and the actual capture step. It proves fresh
physical ownership, uniqueness and demand balance, using an explicit fresh
physical owner and a predecessor balance derived from the mixed stack's checked
source and exact records. It does not infer physical
freshness merely from contract freshness: mixed source includes retirement
markers without such a contract premise.

This source/store allocation result does not check the selected clause body or
its local capabilities and resource support. The main capture allocators and
the source-step connection still need to join those facets.

`mode_source_ownership_balance` and `mode_stack_ownership_balance` establish
those predecessor balances without a separate balance premise. They use the
actual `ResumeAnnotated` and `UnwindAnnotated` records, physical owner
uniqueness, and the existing requirement check starting with exactly those
owners available. The expression case also uses the established fact that
source expressions introduce no direct retirement requirements. Both main
mixed-mode capture and resume results now call these proofs.

The mixed-mode argument retains the earlier ownership-tree, capture-identity
and trace-endpoint proofs. Its additional structural case is opening a dormant
capture during unwinding. Such source checks the saved cleanup before retiring
the still-present owner, so its direct retirements cannot all be classified as
already installed retirement markers. `mode_segment_retirement_spines` proves
that the saved capture's spine is consumed before that retirement completes.
`mode_checked_capture_spines` combines this fact with authenticated resume and
disposal lookups; the existing ownership-tree induction then accounts for all
nested owners. No new ownership axiom, future-execution premise or restriction
to empty caller demand is introduced. This removes the two balance assumptions;
it does not establish the remaining source cleanup-coverage invariant.

Clause-row admission now accepts the actual mixed source through
`StoreModeSource`. Its frame rules retain normal values or an unwind boundary,
and its live-capture rule retains the selected contract's input and either its
answer or unwinding. `SourceStore` separately authenticates the active source,
every exact normal saved resume body at its physical capture location, and the
cleanup record collection under the same registries. A structural
`StoreAnnotation` relates these normal records to the actual checking store.
Ordinary source certificates still construct this interface through
`SourceStore.of_source`, using the reflexive annotation. This broadens the
stores quantified over by declaration row certificates: they must justify the
advertised row for mixed stores and annotated bodies. It does not assert that
an arbitrary old certificate automatically meets the stronger obligation.

`ModeSource.row_source` and `ResumeAnnotated.row_source` erase existing rich
source witnesses into this interface without changing their normal requirement
trees. `mode_row_store` combines them with the actual `StoreAnnotation`.
`capture_mode_segments` preserves existing annotations and stores the selected
relative annotation for the fresh resume body, while retaining its exact normal
source record. It returns the resulting store relation and source certificate.
`instantiate_mode_clause` reuses source substitution
and `Rows.instantiate` against the annotated checking store and that store's
actual continuation interface. It returns both the annotated clause check and
its projected normal-source check in the same annotated store, within the
advertised bound. No checked successor or substitute normal store is assumed.
The earlier ordinary `LexicalSegment.row_store` uses the reflexive case of the
same interface. These are source-provenance and clause-row
results; caller cleanup reentry, local capabilities and physical support remain
independent obligations.

Capture projects the predecessor check only to reuse the normal-source
ownership proof. Its actual saved and tail checks remain in the annotated
checking store. `StoreAnnotation.split` preserves the existing resume/disposal
partition; `StoreAnnotation.append` rejoins it around fresh closing entries.
The predecessor certificate is normalized around the actual handler cut. A
checked choice retains both the original annotation and the normal split into
captured and tail requirements, within the original bound. Explicit paths
retain both branches, so the normal case remains available without another
admission premise.

A structural path in this normalized certificate selects a sequence whose
first part is a relative captured annotation with the actual tail
interpretations prepended, and whose second part is the tail annotation. Each
part must annotate its corresponding exact source fragment. The path supplies
both checks at their correct owner phases; no separately checked captured body
or successor is assumed. The fresh record stores only the relative body.
An explicit lookup equation identifies that selected body, and its checked row
becomes the resumption advertisement. The pending tail retains its annotation
through the spent marker. The selected split's row stays within the predecessor
bound, including the effects of previously annotated nested records.

This is a local source rule for a structurally identified branch. It does not
infer a relative body from an arbitrary annotation whose leaves may already
contain the outer interpretations. Initial source admission must supply the
appropriate branch and establish that its extra paths cover the required
cleanup executions. The normal fallback alone does not establish that coverage.

`ModeSource.unwind_checked_empty` derives the lexical cleanup source and its
checked effect row from existing mixed source and requirement checks when the
caller's remaining continuation demand is empty. It uses the structural
`UnwindPrefix` and availability of physically owned continuations. A dormant
live continuation would require its owner both consumed and available, so that
case is excluded by the existing checks. Nested handlers, resource frames,
spent boundaries and typed effectful finalizers retain their original metadata;
ordinary pending code is skipped. The cleanup row is contained in the original
caller row at the same receiving context and phase.

`return_effects_of_empty` consequently constructs `ReturnEffects` from that
source evidence. `resume_checked_recomposition_empty` uses it to derive checked
resumption within the original saved/caller/tail effect budget, without a
separately supplied cleanup certificate. These results discharge one local
admission case. They do not establish initial-program admission or remove the
cleanup obligation for callers with nonempty continuation demand.

`SourceDependencyBudgetGap.Lexical` checks the remaining budget question
against lexical unwinding itself. It reuses the existing typed nested-capture
fixture: normal execution resumes its saved callback beneath an inner handler,
whereas abandonment skips the pending resume, pops that handler, then opens the
saved continuation. Cleanup consequently exports through the outer handler.
The normal row is empty and the lexical cleanup row is nonempty. The exact
cleanup requirements reject an empty row and admit the explicit cleanup budget
through `ReturnEffects`. No global cleanup plan is used in these proofs.

This fixture has a rich `ModeSource` and finite requirement checks; it is not a
reachable closed initial execution. It establishes that a proof for arbitrary
typed callers cannot simply bound their cleanup by their normal row. Initial
admission must either establish an additional invariant that excludes this
mismatch or retain and check the separate cleanup bound. Handler identities
and callback metadata are already unambiguous in the fixture; the issue is the
bound for the alternate lexical execution path.

The same module's `Lexical.Admission.authenticated` now establishes that the
source-relative `SourceStore` predicate includes the example inside an enclosing
continuation. It supplies exact normal resume records and structural lexical
closing records for both owners. `body_admitted` constructs the current enriched
`Body.typed` judgment for a normal-only resume of the enclosing continuation.
`admitted_normal_cleanup_gap` instantiates the existing hereditary `Rows` proof
at that authenticated store: the normal resume has an empty row, while lexical
cleanup of its saved body has the nonempty row above. Thus source provenance
and the existing normal-only row rule do not alone imply that cleanup fits the
normal budget. This reuses the existing source, registry-extension and row
proofs; no runtime plan or execution rule is added.

This evidence still does not establish closed-program reachability, or that this
particular resume must unwind its caller. It does not require a resumption-only
clause to budget an unused explicit disposal. The remaining source-admission
obligation is to establish coverage at the boundaries where lexical execution
actually requires cleanup, and preserve it through capture and resumption.

`ModeSource.return_choice_admission` supplies a local admission rule for
arbitrary caller demand. Existing lexical source, an unwind prefix and owner
balance construct the cleanup requirements and their demand permutation.
The annotation uses the existing requirement-tree `choice` constructor to check
normal execution and cleanup from the same owner phase and interpretation
suffix. Both alternatives consume the same outstanding owners; the check does
not execute or sequentially consume both alternatives. Its row covers both
paths, so the cleanup row need not fit the normal row alone.

`UnwindSource.choice_return_effects` proves that this single finite check yields
the ordinary caller check and `ReturnEffects` for either return mode. It reuses
`ClosingEffects` and the existing alternative-check rule. The lexical budget
fixture checks this rule with a nonempty owner demand. No evaluator, runtime
