annotation or source grammar restriction is introduced. This is a sufficient
local rule; hereditary source admission must still establish and retain these
alternative checks at each applicable caller boundary. The theorem does not
claim that the earlier normal-only check already supplies them.

The hereditary `SourceDependencyAnnotations.Body` judgment now has an
`annotated` constructor. It retains the original expression derivation, a
structural `RowAnnotation` relating its normal requirements to the annotated
tree, and a `Rows` certificate for that annotated tree. The relation permits
additional alternatives beneath sequencing, emission and choices; all paths
retain the original owner demand. It does not identify an arbitrary extra path
as lexical cleanup. `Rows.alternatives` composes independently certified paths
under the same advertised bound using the existing checker.

`RowAnnotation.checked` projects a checked annotation to a bounded check of the
original source. `RowAnnotation.prepend` retains that relationship when ordered
interpretations are installed. Environment, world and contract transport and
source substitution preserve the actual annotation. Handler declarations carry
it through their existing `Offer` families, so no separate annotated-body
hierarchy or runtime registry is introduced. Normal erasure remains available
through `Body.normal_rows`; the mixed clause instantiator retains both trees
through `Body.row_annotation`.

`StoreAnnotation` relates checking-store bodies to their exact normal source
bodies, entry by entry with identical keys, order and owner demands. Its checked
projection recursively reuses `RowAnnotation.checked` at invocations, preserving
owner phases and deriving a normal effect row within the annotated bound. Both
lookup directions retain the actual body annotation. Removing a consumed owner
preserves the relation. These are proof certificates; no runtime store or
execution rule is added. Normal source records continue to justify ownership
without attributing an added annotation branch to the source syntax.

`RequirementPath` records a structural position inside the complete annotated
requirement tree and the owners consumed before that position. Its `checked`
lemma extracts the selected check at that owner phase, within the root effect
bound. Paths compose and survive installation of ordered interpretations.
`RowAnnotation.focus` locates an annotated child without removing alternatives
from the enclosing tree. The ten strict source-focus forms return the exact
child's path. `RequirementPath.remainder` constructs a remaining certificate
from any selected path: it retains the selected subtree and following
requirements, removes the preceding demand, and derives the check at that later
owner phase within the original row bound. Its proof is structural induction
on the existing path; enclosing choices follow that path. This is a static
certificate transformation, not a runtime cleanup plan.

`focus_preserves_source` and `plug_preserves_source` now retain an annotation of
the complete current expression and waiting stack in the same format. Their
source decomposition proofs establish equality of the old and new normal
requirement evaluations, reusing the existing neutral-frame and value lemmas.
`RowAnnotation.rebase_checked` then uses the existing choice constructor to
check the rebuilt normal tree alongside the entire prior annotation. The old
annotation remains an exact subtree, so its stored alternatives and their
paths remain available. Both alternatives consume the same owners; the rule
does not execute both paths. Its effect row stays within the previous bound,
even though the checking tree and row may contain repeated entries.

Both source transitions also preserve the exact `UnwindSource` requirements
in both directions: a plain evaluation frame adds no cleanup action. This
connects a retained cleanup branch to the actual successor stack and dependency
scope, rather than just retaining an unrelated checked tree. Neither transition
consumes an owner or changes the checking store or phase. This argument does
not yet cover computation, capture, resource or handler entry, or transitions
that consume owners; it does not establish complete source admission.

`ready_preserves_source` uses the same complete certificate for ordinary bind,
beta and boolean-branch reduction. Existing port typing supplies the actual raw
step and closed-substitution readiness; the existing rich substitution and
branch proofs supply its successor source and local capability check. The
pending source stack, cleanup requirements and physical owners remain the same.
Bind and beta retain the normal effect check exactly. Selecting a branch uses
its previously checked effect subrow and the established permutation of owner
demand; the existing phase-permutation lemma preserves the pending check.
The successor annotation retains the entire predecessor certificate as an
alternative within its previous effect bound. The theorem assumes no checked
successor and proves local progress for these ready forms, not progress for
arbitrary admitted programs.

Handler installation and normal exit now retain that same complete certificate
and the exact cleanup-source association. Installation reuses
`RecursiveHandlerTables.checked_activation` to replace the static checking label
with the fresh installation identity. `unwind_source_registries` transports the
unchanged lexical cleanup requirements through the registry extension, including
callbacks and dormant captures. Existing installations keep their tables and
clause families. Pushing the new handler adds no cleanup action of its own;
normal exit recovers the unchanged suffix certificate after the returned value
and handler frame contribute empty rows. Both results construct the checked
annotation for the actual successor, retain the predecessor annotation as a
subtree, and preserve its effect bound. These results do not establish that
source admission supplied every required cleanup alternative before entry.

`UnwindSource.clause_return_effects` connects a static clause-row certificate
to a caller obligation at any structural path to `choice normal cleanup`. It
checks that alternative at the owner phase after the path's preceding demand,
and requires the cleanup branch to match the exact lexical `UnwindSource`
requirements. It then supplies `ReturnEffects` for either mode within the
clause's advertised bound. The earlier sequence-prefix case is the path into
its second operand; nested sequences and surrounding alternatives use the same
rule. The theorem assumes the source certificate and authenticated invocation
interface, not a checked successor machine. Existing source rules still admit
normal-only bodies: this extension does not prove that every applicable caller
boundary has the required alternative. Establishing that coverage and
preserving its association with the actual caller remain source-admission
obligations.

`resume_mode_segments` now takes the typed ready `resume` expression and its
whole expression/stack certificate. Source inversion, the resolved owner and
value silence derive the invocation requirement check and its exact demand.
Projection of the same certificate supplies the pending requirement check after
that demand; neither requirement check is a separate premise. The result retains
the operand's rich value source for the resumed computation and exposes the exact caller requirement
tree selected by source decomposition.

For an unwind-returning capture, the theorem now constructs the caller's
`UnwindSource` and its owner-demand permutation before requesting effect
coverage. `mode_reentry_unwind_balance` derives the caller's ownership from the
checked saved, caller and tail fragments, authenticated surviving records and
the existing reentry dependency bounds. Recursive demand membership stays
within each preserved region; the saved region includes the outer tail, so
outside-owner calls remain supported. The proof reuses
`Syntax.balanced_middle_demands` and `ModeSource.unwind_reentry`.

The remaining obligation is only a structural path to `choice normal cleanup`
for that derived cleanup in the same enclosing certificate, after the invoked
owner's and capture's demand. Both branches carry the caller's actual outer
interpretation context. Cleanup source and its owner balance are results,
rather than additional premises of the effect-coverage obligation.
Ordinary-return captures require no cleanup branch. Keeping the enclosing tree
allows alternatives above the pending subtree to remain usable.

The proof extracts the cleanup check from that path and reuses the existing
consumed-owner normalization and record-removal proofs to transport it to the
spent caller boundary. It derives the internal `ReturnEffects` evidence, then
reuses checked mixed-mode recomposition and ownership accounting. There is no
separately supplied invocation requirement check, pending requirement check,
`ReturnEffects` or caller budget. The successor row stays within the original
certificate's effect bound.

The resume theorem accepts a checking store structurally related to the exact
normal source records by `StoreAnnotation`; reflexivity admits the previous
unannotated case. Lookup supplies the selected saved annotation and its checked
body at the actual caller context. Projection derives the normal saved-source
check and its effect subrow. Projecting the predecessor and fragment checks to
the normal store allows reuse of the existing ownership proofs. The successor
retains the store relation after removing the consumed owner.

The successor also carries a checked `RowAnnotation` for its rebuilt source.
`RowAnnotation.focus` extracts the pending annotation from the predecessor;
consumed-owner record removal preserves its check. For unwind return,
`RequirementPath.remainder` also retains the selected normal/cleanup choice
and the requirements following it, even when that choice lies above the
pending subtree. Owner-demand cancellation aligns these remaining requirements
with the caller suffix. The saved continuation's checked annotated requirements
precede both retained alternatives. An explicit path retains that saved
annotation with its actual receiving interpretations. Further paths locate the
pending annotation and the selected cleanup choice in the successor after the
saved demand. The annotated row remains within the predecessor bound.

This proves retention of these concrete subtrees through the actual resume
step. It does not prove that initial source admission supplies matching cleanup
branches at every applicable site, or that every future coverage obligation
can be recovered from the retained trees. Capture now constructs the fresh
annotated record and its `StoreAnnotation` from a relative split branch in the
predecessor certificate; resume checks and retains that stored annotation.
Clause admission accepts the resulting annotated checking store.

`capture_mode_segments` also joins the allocated capture to its actual clause
and pending tail. Its predecessor premises now include source typing and a
requirement check for the ready operation request. The existing request-evaluation
and cut-residual proofs identify the selected handler's offered row and its
export through the receiving suffix. The source declaration at that handler
supplies the exact dependency family, clause body and continuation effect
interfaces through `selected_body`; the operation signature aligns the operand
and continuation input types. Operand closure follows from its source typing.
No clause certificate, continuation effect interface or advertised export is
supplied independently. Both resumption-only and disposal-capable offers use
this same allocation and clause-joining theorem.

The theorem instantiates that hereditary clause certificate in the actual
annotated allocation store. Substitution retains its normal expression and
`RowAnnotation`. `complete_allocated_clause` supplies the existing consumption
argument: the clause demand is a permutation of the fresh owner followed by the
saved continuation's demand. This aligns the annotated tail check with the
phase where the clause finishes. The combined successor annotation checks
within the actual request row plus the predecessor pending certificate's bound,
and its whole demand is a permutation of the successor's physical owners. The
normal combined check follows by the existing annotation projection. No
independently checked successor or new ownership induction is assumed.

For a disposal-capable offer, the existing structural request check now supplies
the protection guard and `PendingWithin` owner bound. The capture theorem no
longer assumes an independent physical `InternalUses` bound. The same physical
cut and complete lexical annotation identify the exact saved scope through
`Realizes.append_scopes_unique`. `Bound.captured_pending` carries its source
owner bound to every stored continuation referenced inside that scope.

`mode_source_calls_within` bounds the calls that the mixed source executes;
skipped frames contribute no calls. It does not reconstruct typing or pending
uses for abandoned raw code. `mode_capture_ownership_balance` combines these
source bounds with the existing checked-demand, ownership-tree and retirement
proofs to show that the saved demand accounts for exactly the captured owners.
The exact `UnwindSource` supplies cleanup's demand over the same owners, deriving
the permutation between the two demands. This removes the separate owner-bound
premise without claiming preservation of the whole mixed local judgment.

A structural path identifies those lexical cleanup requirements in the checked
saved annotation. Reading that path supplies cleanup's successful row and its
bound within the saved row; no independent cleanup row bound is assumed.
The existing record-insertion and closing-invocation proofs then construct the
fresh disposal interface, including row availability and coverage. The result
retains that interface alongside the source, records, normal resume interface
and actual clause check. Resumption-only offers still require no cleanup path
or usable disposal interface. Their allocation retains structural closing
records where lexical abandonment permits them.

Capture now derives the successor `ReturnHints.Recursive.Pending` from the
same recursive judgment for its predecessor, with matching annotations on the
actual stack. `Pending.handler_cut` reuses `Realizes.cut` and the existing
physical-prefix split to identify the captured and waiting annotations.
`Pending.split` keeps the exact receiving suffix for executed code and

The rich source and annotation return-mode results identify the same captured
boundary. `Recursive.local_transport` and `pending_transport` reuse the existing
phase-spending and permission-extension laws through every recursive check.
The live-boundary constructor then yields checks for the actual allocated
stack. No separately checked successor stack is supplied.

The capture theorem also takes the recursive check of the whole `perform`
expression. `Local.ready_request` uses rich-source inversion and sequencing to
extract the request check, replacing its separate primitive-request premise.
That check supplies the existing protection and owner-bound arguments for a
disposing offer. Both capture and resumption now use the same recursive

This result covers the retained stack, not the selected clause's current
recursive `Local` judgment. The existing `ClauseFamily` interface takes
ordinary `Pending` checks for saved and waiting scopes. It does not supply the
required recursive clause check when the capture returns into unwinding.
Joining that check remains part of the same M1 obligation; the existing clause
source, row, usage and support results do not establish it implicitly.

The ready-resume rule now retains the missing return-mode information in
`SourceDependencyChecks.Lexical.ReturnHints`. Each annotation follows the

and exit modes. Ordinary code is checked when executed and skipped during

The earlier `ReturnHints.Resume` rule checks a ready primitive against retained

`ModePending.annotate_return` reconstructs annotations for the earlier retained

establish that returning into cleanup accepts a skipped dependency on an

`ReturnHints.Recursive.Local` and `Pending` now check dependency syntax and

The main resume theorem takes the recursive check of the whole current

`Local.resume_at_cut` reuses deterministic lexical lookup and the existing

rules and cannot express every case admitted by the recursive judgment. The

The recursive judgment also supplies the actual lexical discard transition and
the retained abandoned/waiting checks through `Local.discard_step`.
`Pending.cleanup_step` supplies the actual callback-entry transition, its
recursive dependency check and retained unwind suffix. Bind and beta reduction
reuse existing rich-source substitution and value-silence results in
`SourceDependencyNeutral.Lexical.Recursive`; no new substitution argument is
introduced. Local examples check resumption under sequencing and a nested
handler, and a callback that installs a handler before resuming. Consumed owners
remain rejected for both invocation modes. These are local checking and
transition results, not initial-program safety results.

The main capture theorem now derives recursive checks for both permitted
primitive continuation actions at the newly allocated boundary. It uses the
selected clause's actual `code.requiredActions`; no broader binder policy is
substituted. `resume_clause_from_retained` derives the restored check from the
saved and waiting source. `dispose_clause_from_retained` combines those checks
with the current request's abandoned-callback check. Existing clause-mode
selection supplies disposal permission, and protection proves that the captured
segment preserves its input mode. Neither action assumes its successor check.

These derivations use return-aware history transport in
[SourceDependencyNeutral.lean](SourceDependencyNeutral.lean). Its structural

the existing lexical selection; erased ownership and protection observations
reuse the existing neutral-scope proofs. Mutual induction transports the

The existing structural declaration recipes now compile to recursive `Local`
checks. `compile_recipe_providers` in
[SourceContextualRequirements.lean](SourceContextualRequirements.lean) reuses all

provider transport in
[SourceDependencyProviders.lean](SourceDependencyProviders.lean) retains callback
and continuation modes; a matching provider may correctly replace handler

`capture_selected_recipe` in
[SourceContextualCapture.lean](SourceContextualCapture.lean) connects that compiler
to an actual handler cut. The predecessor's finite forest test supplies the

check and retained-stack check at the same allocated runtime stack. It also
preserves the installed recipes and their finite forest test across capture.
No selected-body or primitive-successor check is an input. The returned family
lookup is the same one used by rich declaration typing to authenticate the

Effectful cleanup wrappers now have a structural admission theorem for the
recursive dependency checks. `compile_footprint` in
[SourceScheduledAdaptationCompilation.lean](SourceScheduledAdaptationCompilation.lean)
reuses `SourceRequestFootprints.Footprint` and the existing finite operation

Explicit continuation invocations are outside this footprint judgment and keep

`cleanup_admission` in
[SourceScheduledCleanupInterfaces.lean](SourceScheduledCleanupInterfaces.lean)
checks the body with the new armed frame present. Its structural `Supplied`

suffix. Handler cuts split that evidence between captured and waiting segments.
Owner cuts retain the dormant capture and move the registration evidence with

and `Pending` checks through resumption, disposal and both callback-return modes.
No runtime plan is constructed, and no handler is removed during unwinding.
The callback check is derived at the registration suffix whenever that frame is
traversed. Existing owner inventories and pending owner bounds are preserved.

`compile_recipe_cleanup` joins this rule to the existing consuming-clause
compiler. It accepts a structural body recipe, a callback footprint, their finite

assumes neither the callback's execution check nor the wrapped body's check.
`registered_pending` derives the new armed frame's retained check in either

`ClauseRecipe` extends the existing structural consuming recipes with effectful
cleanup, operation-footprint prefixes, resources and choices. It embeds existing
recipes rather than replacing their established proofs. The operation interface
filters requirements supplied by locally allocated providers; the declaration's
receiving suffix supplies the remainder. Its compiler reuses `cleanup_admission`
and the existing primitive continuation interface. No constructor contains a
successful future-body check. This is an annotation judgment over the existing
dependency syntax, not a second computation calculus.

`ClauseDeclarations` stores these recipes for both offered modes using the actual

structural declaration evidence with its finite lexical scope test and preserves

recipe at an actual handler cut, compiles its complete dependency tree, and
preserves the declaration evidence and finite forest check. It reuses
`capture_clause_interface` factored from the established capture proof in
[SourceContextualCapture.lean](SourceContextualCapture.lean). The previous
`capture_selected_recipe` theorem also uses that same factored proof, so the
capture mechanics are not duplicated. Substitution and instantiation retain the
new declarations by the existing required-action preservation lemmas.
`selected_typed_clause` joins this structural compiler to the existing rich
source-selection theorem. Its compiled dependency family is the same family
that rich declaration typing authenticates for the actual clause, offered mode
and higher-order parameter environment. Matching action rights alone cannot
substitute a different dependency body.

Higher-order declaration retention reuses the existing `SourcePlannedChecks.Certified`
judgment with an explicit lexical declaration policy. Its constructors traverse
nested bodies and both offered clause modes; they contain no receiving stack or
execution-success premise. `ClauseDeclarations.signature_congr` supplies the
source law needed by the shared certification transport in
[SourcePlanSignatureChecking.lean](SourcePlanSignatureChecking.lean). The previous
recipe clients use that same transport proof. No alternative function type or

`bind_preserves` and `beta_preserves` combine the existing synchronized-source

function signature; neither successor certification nor successor `Local` is a
premise. `actual_source_handler` retrieves the actual raw clause witness from

`source_handler_install` then combines it with the current scope test and retained
stack facts for the actual handler-entry transition. It derives the successor
body source/check, stored declarations, matching stack, recursive pending check
and finite forest test. It does not yet join the separate row, store, usage and
resource-support components of common preservation.

`capture_source_clause` now joins the stored structural declarations to the rich
`SourceDependencySchemes.Lexical.capture_mode_segments` result. Its successor
contains the selected clause's recursive `Local` check together with the same
clause's source typing, row and store certificates, ownership balance, usage,
ticket access and resource access. It derives the whole-clause check from the
independently proved primitive capabilities and the actual selected declaration;
no successor `Local` or primitive capability proof is an input. Stored
declarations and finite receiving-scope checks survive this same capture.
The proof reuses the existing rich capture theorem and clause compiler.

This closes the join between the selected clause's dependency check and the
rich capture result for the supported declaration grammar. The predecessor must
still supply source typing, structural declarations, recursive pending checks,
the finite forest test, row/store annotations and operand support. The result
also retains the exact cleanup-path premise for disposing capture. It does not
prove initial admission or coverage of every required clause form. The separate

to this allocation result remains open.

`source_handler_install` also returns `CertifiedClauses` for the actual typed
clause plans. `selected_plan_certified` follows the source lookup witness through

Equality of dependency families alone is not used to identify clause plans.

`capture_certified_source` combines the lexical capture result with the existing
planned-source clause selection and substitution proofs. It returns the selected
body's stable signature and nested declaration certification, its recursive

parameters with an existing allocated contract supplies the actual substituted

that same contract; ownership demands, rows and effect interfaces are unchanged.
Higher-order payloads use the existing refined value summary and substitution
proof. This result alone does not select or construct the allocator's row/store
contract. The planned mixed-mode source below retains its witness through
capture and recomposition; `capture_planned_allocation` now joins capture to
row/store allocation at that exact source witness.

`CertifiedFrame` retains one actual plan witness shared by pending-context
source typing and certification. Handler frames retain their actual typed clause
plans, structural declarations and `CertifiedClauses`; armed callbacks retain
their typed callable signature and certification. It projects to the existing
`SourcePlannedFrames.Frame`. Certification is not attached to a separately chosen
typing proof, since that would not identify the same hidden plan.

`PlannedModeSource` extends planned source retention to the same normal and
unwind boundaries as `SourceDependencyFrames.ModeSource`. Erasure produces that
existing judgment with the same runtime stack, dependency scope, owner demand
and requirements. There are no new runtime terms or transitions. Skipped code
has no ordinary requirements; handlers and callbacks survive abandonment; live
captures retain saved source, and abandoned captures retain their retirement.

Its `append`, `split` and `handler_cut` lift the existing structural proofs and

`unwind_source` produces both the planned cleanup source and the existing

at the captured return mode, restores the complete saved and caller prefixes,
and proves the successor demand accounts for the physical owned continuations.
It does not assume an already typed reentered caller, and it covers unwind return.

`transport` reuses existing expression, declaration and context extension proofs.
`capture_retention` retains the saved and waiting planned source under the

extracts the structural declarations from this source, including dormant captures.
`capture_from_planned_source` then recovers the selected typed declaration and
its certification at the actual handler cut and invokes `capture_certified_source`.
Those three predecessor witnesses are now derived from retained source rather
than supplied independently at capture.

`capture_planned_allocation` in
[SourceScheduledCleanupInterfaces.lean](SourceScheduledCleanupInterfaces.lean)
now joins the retained planned source to the actual capture allocation. Its

clause plans and certification are extracted from that stack source.

`capture_mode_segments_at_body` in
[SourceDependencySchemes.lean](SourceDependencySchemes.lean) factors the existing

The old `capture_mode_segments_at_cut` and `capture_mode_segments` interfaces

the planned input and answer types.

The joined result constructs the planned successor stack, substitutes the
higher-order payload into the same selected clause, and instantiates that

check. The same successor also carries whole-clause lexical checking, retained

The erased allocator's independently returned expression is not used as evidence

`PlannedResumeAnnotated` retains the planned source and its certification for

extension. Resumption and administrative unwinding preserve surviving records
using the existing location lemmas.

`selected_planned_resume_source` recovers the precise stored source through

`resume_planned_fragments` joins that source to the saved, caller and tail row

`resume_planned_segments` now derives the planned successor source, normal and

For an unwind return, `unwind_source_evaluation` derives the caller's planned
cleanup source together with an existing `UnwindSource` whose requirement
evaluation is equal. The established ownership proof supplies their common
owner demand. The predecessor's selected cleanup branch then checks that same
planned source; checked append joins it with the saved source and spent-owner
suffix. Ordinary return reuses the caller's ordinary check. No reentered source
or successor requirement check is a premise.

These results close the source/row connections for capture allocation and
resume/recomposition, including unwind return. Capture still requires the
predecessor's exact cleanup branch when disposal is available and its operand
resource-support bound; resume still requires the exact caller-cleanup branch
when returning into unwind. Initial admission must establish these annotations
at every applicable site. Integration of disposal, cleanup and the remaining
boundaries into the common invariant, complete clause/callback admission,
common preservation and initial progress remain open. M1–M4 remain open.

The cleanup boundary connections now retain the same source and certificate
witnesses. `start_planned_cleanup` derives the actual callback application,
its declaration plan and recursive local check, the pending unwind-return
stack, and their combined checked requirements. `finish_planned_cleanup`
returns from that callback to unwinding; `finish_planned_close` returns from
the closing marker to the waiting ordinary computation. Each theorem preserves
ownership balance, one-shot usage, ticket/resource access, finite declaration
checks, and all surviving planned resume and disposal records. The original
annotated requirement tree remains a checked alternative with an explicit
path, so this boundary step does not discard previously checked cleanup
branches. These three transitions leave the continuation store and owner
phases unchanged. They reuse the existing transition, access and ownership
proofs; no successor check is a premise.

`advance_planned_unwind` now joins all six administrative cases to their actual
store and phase changes. It derives the successor's planned source, normal
requirement check within the predecessor certificate's row bound, recursive
capability checks, stored source certificates, declaration checks, owner balance,
one-shot usage and ticket/resource access. Opening a capture removes its callable
records while leaving its ticket for the later retirement step.

The store proof reuses the checker's existing demand-uniqueness theorem. The
saved cleanup demand cannot contain the opened owner because the same checked
sequence already contains its later retirement. `checked_remove_undemanded`
then removes that owner's records throughout the recursive saved check; the
waiting suffix uses the existing removal theorem for consumed owners.
`recursive_local_restrict` and `recursive_pending_restrict` lift the established
live-owner availability argument to the recursive return-mode judgments. The
actual successor stack supplies the availability bound, rather than a new
source-admission premise.

`advance_planned_unwind_annotated` strengthens the administrative result with
checked successor annotations and explicit retained paths. The earlier normal-row
theorem is now a projection of this stronger result. `UnwindAnnotationStep`
records three structural cases:

- Plain, handler, cell and spent-frame pops retain the entire predecessor
  annotation as a checked alternative.
- Ticket retirement retains the waiting source's annotated subtree, checked
  after consuming that ticket.
- Opening a capture retains the saved-cleanup and waiting-source annotations,
  with paths at their original demand prefixes. Their checked sequence includes
  the intervening retirement, under the store with that owner's records removed.

The proof uses `RowAnnotation.focus` to select the exact source subtrees and
`RequirementPath.checked` to obtain their checks. Annotations retain each
subtree's owner demand, so the existing demand-uniqueness and store-removal
proofs apply. Every path below either retained subtree can be composed with its
successor path using the existing `RequirementPath.trans`. The successor's
annotated row stays within the predecessor certificate's effect bound.

This closes local transport for those source-positioned annotation subtrees.
It does not establish that they contain every cleanup branch required by source
admission. Enclosing alternatives outside those subtrees are not retained on
opening or retirement. Connecting all required cleanup paths to the common
invariant, complete initial admission, common preservation and initial progress
remain open. The conditional mixed-source disposal connection is proved below.
M1–M4 remain open.

The capture allocator now exposes its choice of cleanup source.
`capture_mode_segments_with_closing` and
`capture_planned_allocation_with_closing` accept the exact stored cleanup
requirements and their source proof, together with the existing certificate
path when disposal is offered. They return an equation identifying the newly
allocated disposal record. An unprotected capture receives that exact record;
a protected capture retains only the previous records. This also covers the
existing unprotected allocation case when the clause has no explicit disposal
right. The previous allocation interfaces are wrappers with unchanged statements.

`PlannedUnwindSource` pairs a planned cleanup source with the exact stored
`UnwindSource` and a proof that their requirements evaluate equally in every
store, receiving context and owner phase. `planned_unwind_source` constructs
this pair from a planned source using the established cleanup conversion.
`PlannedUnwindAnnotated` retains the pair with the captured-stack identity and
recorded scope. `capture_planned_unwind_records` uses the allocator's equation
to attach that supplied pair and transports the existing records. Lookup uses
physical capture uniqueness and the recorded scope; it does not require unique
source typing.

`PlannedUnwindSource.annotated_checked` transfers a checked stored certificate
to the paired planned cleanup, retains its annotation as a checked alternative,
and supplies the existing cleanup ownership balance. Planned disposal records
also retain their witnesses across resumption, discard rearrangement and
administrative unwinding. These results connect the stored cleanup body to its
planned source. The following discard result uses these exact witnesses. Initial
admission and adoption of the stronger records throughout the common invariant
remain open.

`discard_planned_segments` now joins the actual lexical discard transition to
its planned source, recursive capability checks, normal and annotated effect
checks, stored source records, owner balance, one-shot usage, ticket access and
resource access. The successor opens the captured stack for unwinding, places
one closing boundary before the waiting caller, and removes the discarded
owner's callable records. Its requirements account for exactly the successor's
physical continuation owners. Both the exact stored cleanup annotation and the
waiting source's annotated subtree remain checked paths in the successor.

`PlannedModeSource.extract_discard` derives the ordinary waiting boundary from

`discard_waiting` reuses source splitting, append and normalized-context transport
to replace the live owner by its spent marker. `discard_pending_at_cut` identifies
the same lexical cut in the recursive capability judgment and joins its saved
and waiting checks through the actual closing boundary. Ownership, usage and
resource preservation reuse the established discard and resumption lemmas.
The closing boundary's scope typing follows from the resolved owner contract.

The predecessor certificate must contain a cleanup invocation checked with the
protected closing boundary. The existing counterexample
`UnwindExamples.closing_delimiter_changes_check` shows why an ordinary invocation

constructs this additional finite branch from the owner, cleanup demand and

There is no successor-validity or future-execution premise and no runtime plan.

This closes the conditional mixed-source discard connection. The generated
annotation layer below discharges its separate protected-path premise. Complete
source admission and preservation of required cleanup coverage remain open.

`annotateDisposals` constructs the protected invocation alternative at every
explicit disposal leaf in a finite requirement tree. It preserves the owner

`annotateDisposalStore` applies the same construction to referenced source bodies,

`disposal_check_sound` reuses the recursive checker to derive the normal source

`disposal_store_lookup` authenticates the exact generated stored body;
`disposal_record_sound` exposes its checks when that record is invoked. The

`disposal_source_focus` selects the generated annotation of a source-positioned
subtree. `retained_disposal_path` then carries every disposal check below such a

`discard_planned_segments_generated` uses the generated source and store check
to supply the protected path required by `discard_planned_segments`. It has no

Its surviving store is exactly the generated annotation of the remaining records.
The regression pair rejects the existing closing-boundary counterexample and
accepts cleanup delegation when the receiving interpretation supports protected

The capture allocator now exposes the exact disposal lookup in the annotated
store through `capture_mode_segments_with_closing_lookup`. The existing

`ProtectedClauseInterface` extends the ordinary clause interface with a disposal
check under the actual closing boundary. `protected_interface_from_record`
derives this check from the checked resume record, the exact stored cleanup

`protected_discard_source_checked` connects the stronger interface to an actual

`ClauseRowAdmission.ProtectedRows` records the generated requirement derivation

Existing source substitution, world extension and registry transport carry the

The generator and protected interface live in the common clause-contract

The resume and discard admission constructors supply the protected certificate.

`capture_planned_allocation_with_protected_closing` now instantiates the

and common preservation/progress remain open.

`capture_mode_segments_with_closing_store` exposes the exact allocated checking

The original lookup theorem is a projection with its statement unchanged.
`capture_planned_allocation_with_protected_store` carries that equation through

The prior protected-allocation API projects this stronger result.

`capture_generated_store` proves that allocation preserves the generated-store

`capture_planned_allocation_generated` connects those results at the capture

The chosen saved and tail annotations supply their generated fragment checks

The generated entry returns an annotated raw successor store whose generated
image checks the actual substituted clause and waiting tail. It retains the

Generated cleanup checks now survive the paired cleanup-source reconstruction.

`PlannedUnwindSource.disposal_evaluation` therefore reuses the established

`PlannedModeSource.append_disposals` factors the existing append induction so

`PlannedModeSource.split_disposals` similarly strengthens the existing split

`disposal_annotation_map` proves that generation preserves the existing

Neither fragment check is an extra premise. Extraction leaves the original

`capture_annotation_generated_iff` identifies the exact finite evidence for a

`capture_annotation_from_effects` constructs the generated annotation and its

It derives the equality of ownership demands from the source ownership balance
and the cleanup template. Every branch stays within the supplied effect budget.
The converse proves that these effect premises are necessary for this particular
annotation, not an additional conservative restriction on its accepted checks.

The nested-capture example reuses the existing effectful callback and its two
lexical handlers inside two dormant continuations. It constructs the annotation

pure-cleanup restriction. This is a construction from local effect evidence,

callback-effect judgments at every applicable capture and preserve them through

Generated annotations now survive the six administrative unwind rules in the
same successor state as the established source, ownership and access results.
`PlannedModeSource.advance_generated_annotated_checked` handles plain-frame and
handler pops, cell removal, spent markers, retirement and opening a dormant
capture. The first four retain the whole prior generated root. Retirement keeps

and waiting subtrees after removing the retiring owner's callable records.
The existing append equations check their reconstructed source.

`retire_annotation_checked_generated` and `open_annotation_checked_generated`
focus the original annotation before mapping the selected subtrees. This keeps

requirement tree. The opening helper reuses the established retirement-readiness

`advance_planned_unwind_generated` reuses the full administrative preservation

The successor therefore has the same generated-store and generated-annotation
form as the predecessor. No new admission premise is added. This closes that
transport obligation for administrative unwind; it does not establish all-site
cleanup coverage or the common preservation theorem for other transition
families.

Cleanup entry and both completion boundaries now preserve generated
certificates in their full transition results. `start_planned_cleanup_generated`
retains the callback's actual rich source and declaration plan, the waiting
stack's generated check, and the whole prior generated annotation.
`finish_planned_cleanup_generated` and `finish_planned_close_generated` retain
the same whole-root evidence when returning to unwind or ordinary execution.
The three results reuse the existing complete transition theorems for lexical
capabilities, stores, ownership and access. Their generated source checks come
from the corresponding `PlannedModeSource` lemmas; no successor certificate is
an input.

`outward_disposals` proves that the existing outward-row grammar has no direct

the existing rich beta-substitution and outward-extraction proofs to check the
actual substituted lambda body and retain the prior generated annotation.
The statement permits effectful bodies and internal handlers. Those handlers'
clause bodies keep their independent source-admission certificates; the lemma
does not assert that the entire program is free of continuation operations.
This beta result concerns source and row preservation, not a new complete
machine-transition theorem.

`bind_generated_annotated` preserves the actual substituted body and the whole

The result permits continuation invocations in the body.

`SourcePlannedSources.focus_decompose_disposals` and
`context_plug_disposals` provide ordinary and generated evaluation equations
for the same typed child, context and reconstructed source. Their proofs reuse

handles already evaluated operands: their immediate requirement trees contain

The original decomposition and plug interfaces project the ordinary equations.
`focus_step_disposals` carries both equations and the signature split through

focus-step statement is also preserved by projection.

`focus_generated_annotated` and `plug_generated_annotated` derive the generated
successor check from the predecessor certificate and retain its entire raw and
generated annotation as a subtree. Both checks remain within the predecessor
effect bound. These results cover the existing evaluation-context forms without

`focus_planned_generated` now joins focus's source and generated row proofs to

resume and disposal records, unchanged owners, and the existing use and access
judgments. `focus_signature_checks` selects the actual certified subplans in all

relation now permits inserting a pure waiting frame. The same induction retains

as exact subtrees. `plug_planned_generated` now provides the corresponding joint
connection for all ten context forms. It reuses the actual stored context and

of the common runtime invariant remains open.

Resumption source extraction now returns ordinary and generated evaluation
equations for the same source witnesses. `PlannedModeSource.extract_live_disposals`
and `extract_planned_recorded_resume_disposals` reuse the established generated
stack split and exact stored-source selection. The original extraction APIs
project their ordinary equations without changing their statements.

`disposal_store_annotation_map` maps authenticated records while retaining

generated copy of the saved annotation; type equality alone is not used to

and removing its callable records. It adds no fragment-check or reentered-source

`resume_planned_segments_generated` completes that recomposition for ordinary
and unwind return. It joins the generated saved, caller and tail checks at the

bound. Ownership, one-shot use, ticket access, resource support and recursive

proof is reused for generated checks by `requirement_remainder_generated`.
No successor source or fragment check is assumed. As in the original full
resumption theorem, unwind return requires the predecessor's caller-cleanup
branch; constructing that evidence through initial source admission remains
open. This result closes generated resumption recomposition, not M1 or M2.

All initial capture/caller alternatives, preservation of additional annotation
branches through every source transformation, and the common invariant remain

This removes the manual protected-path obligation for the generated discard
entry point. Complete initial source admission, coverage through source
reconstruction, automatic cleanup and unwind-return alternatives, and consistent
use of the stronger records in the common invariant remain open. M1–M4 remain
open; no complete milestone package is closed by this annotation layer.

Regression examples reuse the existing effectful-cleanup function through bind
and beta reduction, preserving synchronized source typing and both checks.
Another example substitutes a value into a callback inside a handler clause:
the raw clauses change, while the same-signature certification is retained.

The installation-to-capture example checks a clause with an effectful cell
cleanup and a resumption. Another example places cleanup inside resource

to the declaration's caller. These are dependency-admission results. Rich source

including nested declarations, effect bounds and resource support. The example

The older `DeclarationRecipes` grammar remains unchanged for its existing
compilers. The new lexical declaration path removes its pure-cleanup restriction
for footprint callbacks, including wrappers inside resources and branches.
Callbacks with explicit owner invocations, arbitrary nested-handler clause bodies
and disposal-capable inherited request prefixes remain required by the milestone.
The footprint checker still requires resumption-only inherited operation
capabilities. Initial source admission must establish and retain the complete
annotations through higher-order source; all-site cleanup coverage,

The same result now carries successor `MachineUse` and `MachineTicketAccess`
from their predecessor judgments. `scoped_least_enclosing_actions` reuses the

already used by source allocation. `capture_machine_use` and
`capture_ticket_access` then supply the successor facets without equating those

Capture now also carries the successor `MachineAccess` judgment. Its additional

`transition_access` then preserves support across the same concrete capture step

rule. The mixed local dependency invariant remains outstanding.

Initial source admission must still supply the required capture and caller branches at
every applicable site and preserve their association with the actual lexical
cleanup. Neither an arbitrary `RowAnnotation` nor the capture rule's normal

The same theorem now joins the actual resume transition to the independent
one-shot usage, ticket-access and resource-support facets. Its inputs are their

caller's actual captured return mode. The typed operand supplies value closure;
`ReentrySource.bounds` supplies the transition's local ownership conditions.
`source_resume_use`, `UseTransition.ticket_access` and the existing raw-step
resource-support theorem produce the three successor judgments for exactly the
same stack used by source recomposition. The resume expression form discharges
its resource-access side conditions through `ScopedPorts.resume_access_checks`.
No successor usage, accessibility or resource-support judgment is assumed, and
no new proof of their individual preservation is introduced.

These independent facets hold for the actual resume step; the joint successor
source/effect result still requires the cleanup-branch coverage described
above. The current expression's recursive source judgment supplies this
successor's recursive retained dependency checks. The capture clause's recursive
check is joined to its allocated source and rows by `capture_planned_allocation`
above. Complete future cleanup coverage and initial admission remain outstanding.
In particular, joining one-shot usage does not establish future callback
capability checks.

Existing `ResumeCertified` consumers have not been silently
reinterpreted as using `ResumeAnnotated`. Admission and preservation must supply
the structural caller coverage at every applicable resume site and establish

Eleven ordinary boundary results in
[SourceDependencyNeutral.lean](SourceDependencyNeutral.lean) now use `ModeSource`
and `ModePending`: cleanup registration, normal callback entry and return,
handler entry and exit, resource entry and exit, cell read and write,

and plug, these retain the same recorded-scope bound over a suffix whose final
mode can be ordinary or unwinding. Callback summaries, handler declarations,

Fresh handler installation transports the existing source and pending checks
only where the registries agree on installed identities. Resource installation
reuses source transport and local world weakening. Cell updates preserve both

modes. These proofs reuse the earlier boundary arguments; they introduce no

## Fixed milestone checklist

The selected lexical machine has eight outer transition constructors. Expanding
its evaluation and administrative cases gives 20 applicable `RawStep` cases,
six `Advance` cases and six other outer cases: 32 syntactic alternatives. The
legacy plan-based raw discard is excluded. Some value-marker alternatives
overlap, so this is a coverage count, not 32 independent proofs. The rich source
judgment has 17 constructors; structural induction also covers arbitrarily
nested handlers, values and callbacks through these same constructors.

M1's ordinary connection inventory has eight fixed batches, covering 17 raw
cases after the joint focus result and conditional capture/resume results.
The batches are a checklist within M1, not additional milestone packages.
The implemented results below are conditional transition connections; they do
not establish initial source admission or one common preservation theorem.
The combined 424-module dependency build passed with warnings treated as errors.

| Batch | Cases | Status and result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plug | 1 | Implemented: `plug_planned_generated` joins rich/generated reconstruction, certified and recursive checks, and strong records. |
| Computation | 4 | Implemented: `computation_planned_generated` covers bind, beta and both Boolean branches through existing substitution and reduction proofs. |
| Cleanup registration | 1 | Implemented: `register_cleanup_planned_generated` retains the actual callback and latent source evidence. |
| Normal callback execution | 2 | Implemented: `start_normal_cleanup_planned_generated` and `finish_normal_cleanup_planned_generated` preserve the saved rich value and effectful callback source. |
| Handler boundaries | 2 | Implemented: `enter_handler_planned_generated` and `leave_handler_planned_generated`; fresh installation authenticates actual clauses and transports rich records under the extended registries. |
| Resource boundaries | 2 | Implemented: `enter_resource_planned_generated` and `leave_resource_planned_generated`; entry preserves row coverage under ordinary world freshness and exit retains its explicit support premise. |
| Cell operations | 2 | Implemented: `read_cell_planned_generated` and `write_cell_planned_generated` preserve the actual updated stack and stored sources. |
| Value-marker returns | 3 | Implemented: `leave_clause_planned_generated`, `close_value_planned_generated` and `retire_value_planned_generated`, including general-value outer rules. |

A shared assembly obligation joins the already-proved generated capture,
resumption, discard, administrative unwind and cleanup results to one common
state. In particular, the state must retain `PlannedUnwindAnnotated` records:
generated discard needs the rich record. The wrapper
`capture_planned_allocation_generated_recorded` now carries those records through
the same generated capture allocation. It reuses the original theorem's exact
store equation and `capture_planned_unwind_records`; its supplied cleanup source
is the paired rich source. The existing capture interface is unchanged, and its
cleanup-effect premises remain explicit. All ordinary batches retain strong records. The existing generated resumption,
administrative unwind, unwind callback entry/return and closing-return interfaces
now also accept and return `PlannedUnwindAnnotated`, reusing the existing location
and store-filtering lemmas. Generated discard already used this relation. These
changes retain the exact cleanup source; they do not construct missing source
budgets or caller cleanup evidence.

Common-state assembly must instantiate checker entries, owner phases, stores and
receiving scopes consistently. Rich planned sources already project installed
clause recipes. `JoinedSource` and `JoinedState` now collect these components,
including finite `checkForest`, activation history and the lifetime ledger.
`JoinedState.computation` preserves that shared component for bind, beta and
both Boolean branches. Focus, plug, cleanup registration, normal callback
entry/return, cell operations, value-marker returns, and handler/resource

six administrative unwind alternatives, and the three unwind callback/close
wrappers cover callback entry, callback return and completion of abandonment.
This connects 29 of the fixed 32 syntactic alternatives. The closing and retiring
wrappers also cover their raw Unit subcases and general-value outer rules.
Capture, resume and outer discard remain unjoined. The corrected
`discard_planned_segments_checked_generated` now constructs the generated
successor-annotation check from the original predecessor premises. It keeps raw
annotations separate from their generated copies and retains the saved and
pending paths; it assumes no annotation idempotence. The finite check for the

callbacks: the abandoned handler only gets popped. It therefore exposes a

or a complete `JoinedState` counterexample. No successor check or new source
restriction has been added. Registration adds the exact cleanup owner to the

These wrappers
do not yet include the outstanding source-origin annotations below and are not

through a coherent enhanced predecessor derivation. Since `JoinedSource` is a
proposition, this does not establish identity of hidden annotation witnesses.
Resource exit retains its explicit support bound; cell operations retain their
builtin signature assumptions. These connections do not discharge those source
origins. The combined dependency build passed with warnings treated as errors;
the audit checks all 424 milestone modules and their exact dependency reports,
using only the established axioms.

Resource entry no longer needs the earlier additional row-name exclusions.

may discharge requests and shrink the exported row while preserving its upper

Retirement retains the exact tail annotation after consuming its
owner; other ordinary results retain the entire prior raw/generated root.
Retaining a subtree does not by itself establish applicability of future source
evidence after a scope change.

M2 has five remaining source-evidence families. These describe missing source
origins for existing theorem premises, not new runtime semantics.

| Family | Required fact |
| --- | --- |
| Capture cleanup budgets | Construct ordinary and protected cleanup-effect evidence for the actual captured fragment and retain its annotation paths. Local annotation construction from that evidence is already proved. |
| Caller cleanup on unwind return | Construct and check caller cleanup at its actual receiver and return mode. A skipped ordinary caller branch is not a required checked alternative. |
| Owner locality | Derive physical ownership from executable source demand in the actual return mode, and preserve lexical access separately. Legacy regional guards remain sufficient only for the fragment they cover. |
| Resource support | Finite annotations and their rich substitution proof are now constructible. Derive the capture boundary and released-cell exclusion for returned values from admission, and preserve them through control flow. |
| Consuming declarations and callbacks | Compile hereditary source evidence for both offered modes, continuation-using callbacks and disposing inherited requests. |

The inventory fixes the constructors and premises to cover. It does not prove

`ClosingEffects`; current footprint-based declaration recipes also exclude
invocations in some required positions. Source annotations and their structural
construction/preservation must address these gaps. New helper lemmas belong
under these existing obligations and must identify the case they discharge.

The owner-locality batch proves `plain_pending_demand` by source/context

The remaining region checks concern the front, saved continuation and tail at

The resource-support batch constructs `SourceSupport.Bounds` from actual

The checker may leave a final application, operation or handler result unknown;

`CleanupHints.Metadata` now decorates the eight lexical cleanup-source forms

Handler entry, capture, resume and outer discard remain the four outstanding
