## Actual-mode resume execution roots

`ResumeExecution` gives a structural root-composition rule for a ready resume.
The ordinary branch uses the authenticated caller requirements. The unwind
branch uses the caller's actual cleanup metadata. Its demand is the selected
owner followed by the saved demand, actual-mode caller demand and tail demand.
It does not require an ordinary caller alternative when that code is skipped.
This is a new composition rule, not an equivalence to the legacy invocation
checker. Permission, operand typing and lexical owner resolution remain
obligations of the structural resume primitive.

`RecordPendingRows.resume_execution_checked` connects this root to the actual
saved record and physical fragments. It constructs a single successor source
carrying rich record agreement and the finite check at the consumed-owner
phase. The consumed owner's records are removed by the existing store transport.
`resume_execution_owned` reuses mixed-stack ownership accounting to derive the
before/after physical ownership permutations. It assumes neither a caller
ownership balance nor the old regional `ReentryBounds`.

The checked example distinguishes ordinary caller demand from executable unwind
demand. A skipped caller invocation and a tail retirement of the same outer
owner make the old root demand repeat that owner. Such a root cannot pass the
phase trace. The new unwind root checks the actual retirement once. The example
checks root selection and accounting, not a complete admitted physical program.

The ledger and ticket registry are preserved separately by
`ready_resume_ledger_registry`, using the existing raw resume event and ledger
proof. The executable root supplies ownership accounting. Requiring the old
`MachineUse` in addition would reintroduce ordinary caller accounting and checks
for skipped code. The legacy `RetainedSource.eval` and `RetainedState` retain
their earlier definitions: their 28/32 transition coverage does not establish
preservation for the new root judgment. The corrected `ExecutableState` below
starts that migration with focus, ready-resume and discard successor proofs. Full
transition coverage and complete initial admission remain open within M1–M4.

For declaration admission, `SourceAdmission.ClauseSchema` now provides a finite,
receiver-indexed compiler for pure code, own resume/discard, choice, inherited
requests, sequence and pure continuation insertion. The first part of a
sequence is checked with its actual suffix installed. No rule lifts an own-owner
invocation across an arbitrary effectful suffix. A checked inherited disposing
request followed by own discard demonstrates that the compiler does not require
both offered modes or forbid disposal.

This is a partial structural compiler, not universal declaration admission.
Inherited requests retain structural callback, ownership and budget evidence,
plus exact selected rows, declared rights, predecessor pending source and a
recursive body derivation. This narrow schema still has no general rule for
lifting own-owner invocations across effectful suffixes. The stronger `Code`
judgment directly admits the checked effectful-suffix example described above.
Generic initial admission, including callbacks, resources and nested handler
declarations, remains open. Actual declaration selection and authentication
must supply the same body rows; this compiler does not originate those witnesses.
The old blanket forest check must not be reintroduced as a requirement on
handlers that are only returned through or popped.

## Executable roots through authenticated focus

`ExecutionSite` retains an authenticated current expression and its actual
pending source, including structural source certificates and saved-record
agreement. Its syntactic requirements remain separate from executable-root
requirements. `ExecutionSite.focus` reuses the established authenticated source
decomposition to construct a child site and a lexical waiting frame together.
The `Focused` relation retains their exact row split, packed receiver context,
suffix certificate and physical step. It does not equate independently chosen
source proofs.

`ExecutionRoot` has contextual execution and authenticated discard leaves,
with branch-selection and evaluation-focus constructors. Values and resumes
share the contextual execution judgment. The discard leaf retains its resolved
owner and actual rich source fragments. Focus carries the child's identical
root to the enclosing expression. In particular, entering a bind does
not append the body's ordinary requirements a second time: the body is already
represented in the authenticated waiting frame, whose execution is selected by
the saved return mode.

`ExecutionRoot.focus_step` preserves that exact root and finite check through
all existing focus forms. `ExecutionRoot.ownership` proves, by induction on this
finite derivation, that checked executable demand accounts for all physical
owners. Contextual execution reuses the shared accounting ownership theorem.
Focus relocates existing records without changing owners. Neither proof assumes
the old ordinary root check or a supplied predecessor ownership permutation.

The authenticated regressions construct source expressions, callback typing,
physical frames, saved-record agreement and the finite checks. One resumes an
inner owner beneath a plain continuation that invokes an outer owner; unwind
skips the invocation and retires the outer owner once. The bind example contains
two syntactic resumptions of the same owner. Its structural source certificate
checks the initializer beneath the actual non-pure suffix, while the resumed
unwind skips that suffix. Its executable root checks demand `[0, 1]`, whereas
requiring the ordinary syntactic demand `[0, 0, 1]` fails.
`AuthenticatedBindResumeExample.bind_focus_checked` applies the focus theorem to
that same checked parent root and constructs its authenticated child and actual
step. These are bounded source and machine fragments, not
proofs of initial reachability or complete machine safety.

The contextual interpreter currently covers pure rows, sequencing, choice,
resume and cleanup installation/execution. Admission for other execution leaves and complete common-state
transition coverage remain open. The corrected common-state layer below extracts
ready resume interpretations from its retained root; it does not yet construct
roots for arbitrary source programs. Existing 28/32 common-state coverage still refers to
the prior invariant. M1–M4 remain open; this does not change the one-shot scope
or the Core correspondence boundary.

## Constructing the checked resume successor

`ReadyResumeSite` now retains the structural `OwnerCut` selecting its exact live
boundary. A physical decomposition and matching owner number alone do not state
which lexical occurrence the primitive selected. This witness is already a
premise of the structural resume rule; retaining it lets the rule's restored
certificate align with the same rich front, capture and tail contexts.

`ReadyResumeSite.operand_summary` reuses authenticated value normalization to
recover the actual operand at the selected contract's input metadata.
`restored_pending` obtains the successor's structural certificate from the
current resume primitive, using the selected cut and exact decorated contexts.
It does not take a successor certificate as a premise.

`ReadyResumeSite.successor` combines those results with
`resume_execution_checked`. It constructs one returned-value `ExecutionSite`,
a value proof, the same scalar finite effect check after removing the consumed
owner's records, and the actual resume step. This legacy compiler does not assert
a central execution root. `successor_owned` derives both ownership permutations
for that same successor from the legacy accounting and physical resume proofs.
Both saved return modes use the established recomposition branches.

The bind regression now invokes this successor compiler. Its returned witness
contains the checked value site, restored lexical context, ownership before and
after the step, and the physical transition. No independently chosen successor
source is used for the accounting result.

This supplies legacy source and scalar-check evidence for an authenticated
ready resume. The contextual compiler below supplies the central-root successor
connection. Complete initial admission remains open within the same M1–M4 scope.

## Corrected common state and independent continuation access

`ExecutableSource` checks the actual `ExecutionRoot` for an evaluating machine.
An unwinding machine retains its actual unwind source and checked requirements.
Both retain structural source certificates and scope annotation bounds.
`ExecutableState` combines this source evidence with the existing saved records,
store annotation, lifetime ledger, registry history, resource access,
installation history, issued-resource support, continuation allocation history,
and allocation support for the contract and scope-annotation maps. Continuation access derives
from the source field rather than being maintained separately. The state does
not require legacy `MachineUse` or a blanket forest check. Omitting those old requirements
does not discharge the remaining structural declaration-origin obligations.

`ExecutableState.focus` preserves all these fields through evaluation focus,
retaining the identical executable root and its annotation. It reuses the
existing event, ledger, resource-access and record-relocation proofs. This is
preservation for the corrected common state; the older 28/32 coverage count does
not apply to it.

`RecordPendingRows.ticket_access` compiles continuation access from the exact
pending source and structural certificate. Its induction follows the existing
lexical source rules, including dormant captures and captures opened for unwind.
The saved context is checked against the outer lexical context, excluding its
enclosing live owner. This uses the existing lexical premises rather than
inferring visibility from ownership counts.

`ExecutableSource.pending_ticket_access` projects that existing compiler from
either source constructor, using the actual declared output mode.
`ExecutableSource.current_ticket_visible` derives resolved free-ticket visibility
through `expression_external_idle`, the source capability bound and physical
context realization. No second usage induction is needed. Authenticated source
still retains operation contracts, permissions and latent function-body typing;
closedness alone is not a substitute for those obligations.
The standalone legacy `resume_value_machine_ticket_access` theorem remains
available, but central-state preservation no longer needs its `CodeDemand`
premise.

`ExecutableState.resume_successor` now takes only the predecessor common state
at a ready resume and its closed value operand. It extracts the contextual
resume interpretation from the retained root and constructs an actual resume event together with
a successor satisfying every common-state field. Its successor access is derived
from that same reconstructed site's pending source and certificate. It reuses
record removal, ledger/history preservation, resource access, annotation bounds
and the physical owner-phase trace. The successor checks its contextual
execution requirements; caller code skipped by unwind does not enter that check.

This is a constructive successor theorem for ready resume, with a value result
interface for the complete program. It covers both saved return modes. It does
not yet prove preservation for every supplied machine transition or structural
admission for every source form. Remaining root constructors, initial admission
and full transition preservation remain open.

## Discard admission and corrected-state successor

`ExecutionSite.discard_origin` constructs the selected discard view from the
current authenticated expression, structural primitive certificate and rich
pending source. It requires only that the current expression is a discard.
Lexical lookup supplies the owner and exact cut; the existing source split
supplies the actual frames and decorated contexts. Unprotected capture supplies
the cleanup metadata. The predecessor's contextual `Accounting.Run` supplies
the interpretation of that same selected continuation. The removed scalar
`ExecutionSite.discard_root` shortcut is not an admission rule. General source
construction of these interpretations remains part of the open admission work.

The view retains the caller's actual intermediate mode. An ordinary live
boundary uses the contract's answer value. A caller within an unwind callback
can instead reach the selected boundary in unwind mode. The rich opening view
retains the ordinary saved source needed to authenticate the same capture.
Unprotected capture rules out a saved ordinary execution that returns unwind;
it does not rule out an unwind-returning caller.

`RecordPendingRows.discard_recompose` generates captured cleanup from the actual
lexical context and joins it to a closing frame, the caller and the spent-owner
tail. It chooses the ordinary or unwind tail from the retained intermediate
mode. The tail requirements describe the physical tail alone; using the whole
opening-boundary requirements here would count the selected capture twice.

The contextual discard root spends the selected owner once, interprets captured
cleanup behind the closing barrier, then follows the caller's actual return mode.
`Accounting.Run.discard_at` aligns this interpretation with the source view using
the existing uniqueness proof for lexical cuts. `discard_recompose` reconstructs
the rich source; its scalar requirements do not control the executable root.
The generic accounting induction proves ownership. The fresh closing identity
has no continuation ownership demand.

`ExecutableState.discard_successor` takes the common predecessor state and a
fresh closing identity. It extracts the contextual discard root, constructs the
actual event and preserves every corrected-state field. Its pending certificate
comes from the structural discard rule. Continuation access is compiled from
that same successor source; resource access, record removal, ledger and registry
preservation reuse existing proofs. No successor check, access proof or ordinary
caller restriction is an additional premise.

This extends the corrected root's ownership induction and common-state
successor construction. It does not transfer the legacy 28/32 coverage count.
Other primitive roots, complete structural initial admission and preservation
for every supplied transition remain open. The Boolean connection below reuses
ordinary source reduction. Bind and beta now use the common computation theorem
below, reusing the existing substitution proof.

## Boolean selection and the corrected execution root

`ComputationSelection` indexes row selection by the actual reducing expression.
Its true and false constructors select the corresponding source row subtree.
`Admitted.computation_selected_rows` strengthens the existing computation proof;
the previous `computation_rows` interface is a projection of that proof. Source
authentication and substitution are reused rather than proved again.

`ExecutionSite.select_branch` constructs the actual selected source site. The
branch relation retains the same runtime scope, physical stack, packed lexical
receiver, pending source and result rows. The structural `ExecutionRoot.branch`
rule carries the selected child's identical executable root. It does not append
the unselected branch or reintroduce the old syntax-based ownership check.

`ExecutionRoot.branch_step` extracts this child evidence from the predecessor's
root derivation. For a contextual root it selects the corresponding checked
alternative, preserving demand up to permutation and narrowing the effect row.
`ExecutableState.branch_successor` constructs the actual Boolean event and
preserves every field of the corrected common state with that successor check.
Existing source, ledger, access and stack evidence supplies the proof; successor
source or access facts are not additional premises.

`ExecutableState.computation` shares this connection across bind, beta reduction
and both Boolean choices. Its only additional inputs are `Ready` and the actual
ordinary raw step. The root proof uses the existing source/accounting compiler;
operational preservation reuses ordinary resource-access and ledger
lemmas. The branch-specific root and state theorems are wrappers around this
shared computation proof.

`AuthenticatedBranchResumeExample.branch_checked` wraps the existing bind and
unwind-resume example in both literal Boolean selections. Both retain its checked
executable demand `[0, 1]`, although the syntax still contains two references to
owner `0`. The example reuses the existing source certificates and root check.
Its identical arms demonstrate a nonempty admitted case with corrected accounting;
the syntax-indexed general theorem establishes which arm is selected.

This connects both Boolean reductions within the existing ordinary-computation
work. The shared computation theorem also covers bind and application. It does
not establish complete initial admission or all-transition preservation, and the
legacy 28/32 count remains inapplicable to the corrected common state.

## Administrative unwind in the corrected common state

`ExecutableState.advance` preserves the complete corrected state for all six
administrative unwind transitions: skipping a plain frame, leaving a handler,
leaving a cell, removing a spent frame, retiring an owner, and opening a live
capture. Its only inputs are the predecessor state and the actual `Advance`.
The lifetime event, continuation access, resource access and record transport
reuse the existing administrative proofs without `MachineUse` or forest checks.

The ordinary pop cases retain the actual tail source and its structural pending
certificate. Retirement uses the source-derived phase transport and removes the
owner at the retirement marker. Opening a live capture uses its retained unwind
source, appends one retirement marker and the physical tail, and removes that
owner's saved records. The owner remains available until the marker retires it.
The ordinary saved view authenticates the capture; it is not executed a second
time. The same recomposed source supplies the row and effect-check transport.

This is preservation for supplied administrative steps of the corrected common
state. It adds all six cases within the existing unwind work; it does not prove
callback entry, full source admission or all-transition preservation. The
remaining value-pop and other transition connections stay within the existing
milestone scope.

## Contextual execution and pending-source accounting

The [authenticated value fixture](SourceScheduledExecutableValueGap.lean)
contains an actual unit-valued site with a waiting bind frame. Its source, row
certificates, lexical context and pending source come from existing structural
judgments. Ordinary pending requirements count the two syntactic resumes and
have demand `[0, 0, 1]`; their finite check fails because the first resume enters
unwind and skips the second invocation.

`ExecutionRoot.contextualValue` is a derived rule using the same contextual
execution constructor as other expressions. Existing `Accounting.value_iff`
converts the structural `Accounting.Wait` interpretation of the exact pending
context into `Accounting.Run`. Conversely, `ExecutionRoot.value_wait` extracts
that waiting interpretation from every admitted value; a scalar pending check
alone is no longer an execution-root constructor. Sequencing places
its suffix in that continuation. Resume retires the selected owner and interprets
the restored continuation once; an unwind return skips the caller suffix. The
[positive regression](SourceScheduledContextualAccounting.lean) constructs an
actual checked root with demand `[0, 1]` and proves `ExecutableSource` admission
for the same authenticated site. The ordinary pending requirements remain
uncheckable. The earlier universal `no_checked_root` rejection is therefore
replaced by this positive root and source proof.

One structural induction over the existing `Dependencies.Silent` proves that
silent prefixes leave this interpretation unchanged. Existing `value_silent`
then supplies value, bind and beta laws, including pair-valued prefixes.
Authenticated substitution already preserves the body rows, so these laws need
no second proof about substituted function bodies.

`ExecutionSite.plug_accounting` reconstructs the successor from the actual
authenticated plain frame and retains the same accounting root. Its proof uses
the existing `AuthContext.plug_value_rows` reconstruction and a three-case
`PlugRows.accounting_iff`; it does not repeat the expression-context cases.
The same reconstruction also transports the lexical `Bound` judgment.
`ExecutionSite.computation_accounting` reuses the existing computation source
proof for bind, beta reduction and both Boolean branches. The same row selection
constructs the successor source and transports its accounting. Bind and beta
retain the check; a branch projects the corresponding checked alternative,
preserving demand up to permutation and narrowing the effect row. The regression
`plug_bind_accounted` follows the fixture's actual plug and bind steps with
authenticated source and finite accounting checks throughout.

`Accounting.Run.owned` and `Wait.owned` share an induction showing that a checked
interpretation accounts for exactly the decorated context's owners. Existing
phase-permutation and retirement lemmas handle resume and both return modes.
`Context.Source.owned_permutation` relates those owners to the actual stack,
including dormant captures and scheduled retirement. Plain row frames add no
owner. `Run.stack_owned` and `Wait.stack_owned` combine these facts with the
existing annotation-check projection. `ExecutionRoot.ownership` uses this result
for contextual values, without assuming the ownership balance it establishes or
a future source judgment.

`ExecutionRoot.contextual` admits an arbitrary authenticated expression using
`Accounting.Run` over its actual rows and receiver. Ownership uses the same
generic accounting theorem. Focus transport reuses `PureHistory`, the existing
relation for inserting harmless pure frames. The two `FocusRows` constructors
that remove a value prefix now retain its silence proof; the actual source
producer supplies that proof through `value_silent`. This strengthens the
decomposition witness without adding a source restriction or repeating the
expression-typing induction.

Legacy `ReadyResumeSite` successor proofs retain their actual source and finite
checks as separate evidence. They no longer assert a scalar central execution
root. The bind and resume fixtures reuse one contextual interpretation and its
finite check. The contextual interpreter remains a fragment: request accounting
is now supplied below, but disposing invocation and the full request state
transition remain open. Complete source admission and
preservation through all transitions remain open. General ordinary value plugging for the admitted fragment is
covered by `ExecutableState.plug`. The regression does not assert initial
reachability or a complete `ExecutableState` for its site.

`RecordPendingRows.captured_source` retrieves the actual saved source in either
pending mode from the existing rich source judgment. Its short constructor
inversion reuses the argument behind `resume_source`, while returning the
retained requirements existentially instead of requiring a lookup in the scalar
resume store. The older `ReadyResumeSite` view also requires that lookup and an
ordinary caller result. Those additional requirements cannot simply be inferred
from a site: agreement authenticates present store entries, and a source split
may cross an unwind boundary.

`resume_physical_from_code` reconstructs the successor from that physical
source for both caller modes and both saved return modes. The primitive's
existing budget evidence supplies caller cleanup when needed. Exact-cut evidence
alignment is shared with the older resume proof.
`ExecutionSite.resume_accounting_successor` combines this reconstruction with
the restored `Accounting.Wait` and the finite check after consuming the selected
owner. Its successor has an actual value root; no scalar record lookup or
assumed successor judgment is an input.

`ExecutableState.resume_from_site` assembles operational state from the actual
raw step, which determines the physical cut. Existing phase, record, access and
ledger proofs preserve the remaining fields. `ExecutableState.resume_successor`
uses the contextual interpretation exclusively; the duplicate scalar-state

The `resume_without_scalar_lookup` regression constructs an actual checked
successor with an empty scalar store, using the retained unwind-returning

`ExecutableState.plug` now derives ordinary value-return preservation from the
predecessor state and closed returned value. It obtains `Wait` by root inversion,
reconstructs the actual plugged source through `ExecutionSite.plug_accounting`,
and retains the same checked root. Existing record inversions, ledger and
resource proofs supply the other fields. It takes no successor certificate or
whole-expression consumption witness.

The central state no longer maintains `MachineTicketAccess` separately. That
legacy predicate combines lexical access with syntactic `CodeDemand`; its old
plug proof obtained the latter from `MachineUse`. Current and pending lexical

Ownership and one-shot consumption remain obligations of the checked execution
root. Source operation rules retain capability and phase checks. This removes

`Accounting.Run.installCleanup` interprets the body under its actual armed

for the current return mode. Ordinary completion uses the protected normal
marker; unwind completion uses the protected unwinding marker. Callback code is

The existing mutual ownership proof and `PureHistory` transport each gain the
two corresponding cases; `Context.callback_owned` and `PureHistory.callback`

`ExecutionSite.register_cleanup_accounting` constructs the actual callback
record, authenticated armed frame and body site from the registration source.
`ExecutionRoot.cleanup_run` extracts the ready registration's interpretation.
`ExecutableState.register_cleanup` preserves the identical root and finite check
while allocating the supplied fresh cleanup identity. Its only freshness premise
is the existing issued-owner uniqueness requirement.

`ExecutionSite.start_normal_cleanup` reuses that frame's authenticated callback
and saved value to construct the callback application under a protected running
frame. `ExecutableState.start_normal_cleanup` derives the actual event and
successor common state from the predecessor and closed returned value. Existing
silence and callback-context facts retain the same execution root; no ordinary
syntax-plus-pending check is reconstructed.

`ExecutionSite.finish_normal_cleanup` reconstructs the saved value from the
actual running-frame source and restores its recorded lexical scope.
`ExecutableState.finish_normal_cleanup` inverts `Wait.normal` and retains the
same execution root, annotation and finite check. Its independent operational
fields reuse `value_step_ledger_resources`, which also supplies the existing
ordinary plug helper. No new whole-machine use check or successor certificate
is required. The bounded cleanup examples check installation and both callback
return modes, including transport beneath a pure waiting frame; they do not
establish complete source admission. Normal registration, entry and completion
are connected to the common state. General unwind cleanup entry and completion

`Accounting.Run` and `Wait` now carry the source world's resource identities
and installation history. `Run.installHandler` and `Run.installResource` quantify
over names fresh for their respective domains, matching the existing source
rules. `Run.mono` and `Wait.mono` share one induction transporting interpretation
to larger domains. The existing ownership and pure-frame transport proofs cover
the new cases; no separate ownership theorem or allocation restriction is added.
The indexed examples check every supplied fresh name and permit a resource
identity to equal an installation identity when the respective freshness
conditions hold.

`ExecutionSite.enter_resource_accounting` selects the actual fresh body instance,
extends the resource world and retains the same ownership root.
`ExecutableState.enter_resource` connects it to the actual lifetime event and
successor state. Source transport, resource access and record weakening reuse
existing proofs. The finite ownership check and its annotation remain unchanged.

`ExecutionSite.install_handler_accounting` selects the authenticated body for
the supplied fresh installation. Existing frame and registry transport proofs
preserve rich saved records and the meaning of earlier installations. It returns
the actual handler transition, the same ownership root and the transported
lexical bound. `ExecutableState.install_handler` uses this theorem and existing
saved-record transport to construct the full successor state. It chooses a fresh
installation from the retained history and requires only the predecessor state.
These entry proofs do not establish initial source admission or the missing
request/capture interpretation.

`RecursiveRequirements.LocalOwner` supplies a finite structural check for a
locally bound continuation owner. It threads that owner's available/consumed
phase through sequencing and both branches. Only the bound owner's retirement
and spent markers disappear from the enclosing root; all other owners and the
sequence order remain. This relation covers the ownership-only root forms used
by contextual accounting. Effect capability and cleanup budgets remain checked
by the source judgments.

`LocalOwner.spend_eq` and `evaluate_eq` establish the phase and evaluation
correspondence between local and enclosing roots. `LocalOwner.checked` reuses
the existing evaluator soundness theorem to derive the local check from the
enclosing check. `demand_discharge` proves that exactly one occurrence of the
bound owner is removed; `outer_absent` proves that it does not remain in the

and premature spent markers.

`Cut.local_owned` relates the exact decorated capture and tail to the original
context, retaining owners nested in dormant captures. `Accounting.Run.capture_owned`
combines the local binding rule with the existing ownership induction and
cancels the fresh owner to recover the predecessor's ownership demand. Its

local binding derivation. It derives the finite local check; it does not derive
those inputs from source authentication. The bounded regression resumes a local

`RecordPendingRows.contract_extension` preserves the rich saved-source judgment
under compatible contract and usage extensions. Its frame and declaration
wrappers reuse existing source transport and authenticated expression extension.
`contract_insert` specializes this to a fresh owner with its actual endpoint
decorations, retaining ordinary saved evidence inside opening continuations.
Neither theorem requires a successor check or the earlier scalar ownership root.

`Accounting.Run.request` now uses the actual lexical `Cut` and
`CapturedClauseRows` for the selected operation and protection mode. The latter
pairs the terminal handler's exact row family with `ClauseRows.Selected`.
Uniqueness identifies both the cut and the dependent row family;
`Run.request_body` retrieves the corresponding body interpretation for the
actual fresh owner and resume-demand annotation. The rule retains the body

Freshness excludes every retained continuation marker, including dormant and
spent markers. `Context.ticketNames` agrees with physical stack names through

`AccountingTransport.DeepPureHistory` allows pure waiting frames in dormant

the original `Run.pure_history` and `Wait.pure_history` APIs are specializations.
The richer relation applies only to accounting and does not change the existing
source transport rules. The request regression resumes an arbitrary fresh local
owner, preserves outer owner 13, and excludes spent identity 17 from allocation
even though it contributes no ownership demand.

`CaptureMetadataHistory` retains allocation support for both the contract and
scope-annotation maps. It projects the history already used by the older
source-allocation proofs, without retaining their ownership-accounting rules.
Empty maps satisfy it; insertion and issued-history growth preserve it. The
corrected state retains this evidence through all its existing endpoints.
Together with runtime allocation freshness, it proves absence from both maps;
these are no longer extra freshness conditions on a source request.

`RecordPendingRows.cut_declarations` uses the existing rich-source splitting
proof twice to expose the actual installed handler and its authenticated

including the handler table, through ordinary and unwind modes.
`CapturedClauseRows.selected_at` aligns the request's retained selection with
those recovered rows. `AuthDeclarations.selected_origin` then derives the

selection and payload-substitution proofs can use those witnesses directly.
`Auth.ready_request_accounting` removes the ready operand's silent prefix and
identifies the actual operation instance. `ExecutionRoot.ready_request` derives

`Run.request_checked_body` combines selected-body inversion and local discharge
to derive the clause's ownership check from the predecessor check.
`LocalOwner.checked_relocate` proves that this ownership-only root can use the
allocated record store and receiving context; it contains neither invocation

actual authenticated ready expression. The regression derives a new clause
check in an arbitrary record store and receiver while retaining outer owner 13
and the consumed outer marker 17.

Complete source admission and the common-state request transition remain open.
`AuthDeclarations.selected` and `AuthBody.fresh_substitution` retain actual rows,
but authentication alone does not supply the body interpretation or local
binding derivation required by `Run.request`. Those premises still need to come
from structural source admission; neither a successor check nor a completed
admission theorem is asserted here.

The source judgment now indexes both its action environment and cleanup budget.
This permits recursive checking under an inserted continuation permission while
preserving the existing argument order and constructor premises. The change
reuses the existing mutual-induction proofs; it does not itself add a clause-body
premise to the request rule.

`SourceDemand` retains the demand of each ordinary source frame and distinguishes
ordinary return from unwind. Skipped caller code contributes no demand; an
ordinary live marker leaves its saved capture dormant, whereas unwind opens it.
`RecordPendingRows.sourceDemand` derives the annotation from the same retained
source and proves its exact fold. It also proves that each dormant ordinary
capture agrees with its recorded resumption demand. The annotation is data,
not a replacement source checker or an ownership count. A consumer must keep
the connection to its actual source; `Recorded` alone does not authenticate

even inside dormant captures.

`ExecutionSite.capture_source` reuses lexical splitting to package the actual
saved and tail sources in `CaptureSourceAt`. Their demands, requirements and

the selected clause's source certificate; `compile_clause_from_request` projects

`selected_certificate` aligns this certificate with the actual installed
declarations and the authenticated request payload. The existing handler-frame
extraction also retains the caller scope, answer annotation and selected plan's
certification. `selected_body` instantiates the fresh contract and substitutes
the payload in that same clause source. Its source-level closing-demand
annotation may equal the saved demand; actual lexical cleanup is generated

Fresh allocation preserves the retained syntax through `Code.introduce_absent`
and `Pending.introduce_absent`. The required freshness covers all retained ticket

`CaptureSourceAt.pending_live` then reuses permission extension, lexical splitting
and the ordinary live-frame rule; it checks no independently supplied successor.

`RecordPendingRows.capture_live` and its split wrapper preserve the exact saved
source and requirement body. `CaptureSourceAt.successor_site` combines these
facts with the substituted clause to construct the actual expression site,
including its current and pending source certificates. Its output retains exact

`CaptureSourceAt.successor_root` uses those identities to attach the predecessor-

`capture_record_package` reuses the existing bound and record-allocation proofs.
It installs the saved resumption record and preserves prior disposal records.
The corrected discard proof generates cleanup from the actual lexical source,
so this construction needs no separate disposal record for the new owner.
`capture_lifetime` reuses the actual lexical event to preserve the ledger,
permission registry history and ticket history.

These source and record constructions are components of the complete capture
endpoint below. Resource support must originate in structural source
admission at handler installation and survive retained code and higher-order
substitution. A bound on the global resource world alone does not establish
access in the selected handler's receiving scope. The later M0 and M2 results
establish that resource support and initial admission. The final section below
combines the transitions constructively; progress remains a separate obligation.

### Authenticated clause resource bounds

`ClauseRows.cons` now retains a finite resource bound for its clause.
`AuthDeclarations.cons` checks the actual body's dependencies against that bound,
evaluated in the ordinary environment extended with the operation's payload
parameter. The payload type comes from the same operation lookup as the clause
typing; it is distinct from the continuation's result type.

`AuthDeclarations.selected_support` projects this evidence for the actual selected
clause into `ClauseRows.resourceSupport`. Selection and substitution retain
arbitrary bounds. Environment agreement, world extension and contract extension
preserve authentication, reusing the existing support and substitution proofs.
Latent function rows carry the annotation through the existing row structure.

This completes the annotation migration, M0.1. The structural judgment and
transport results below check the bound at its lexical receiving scope and
preserve that evidence. Installed-handler support preservation is covered by M0.4
below.
The complete capture endpoint below uses this support. The initial-admission
result defines the finite proof-carrying source boundary.

### Structural installation resource admission

[SourceScheduledInstallationAdmission.lean](SourceScheduledInstallationAdmission.lean)
exports `InstallationSupport.CodeChecked` and `PendingChecked` over the same
source derivations, rows and lexical contexts as `SourceAdmission.Code` and
`Pending`. Their ten expression rules and thirteen retained-code rules add a
resource facet without changing the existing control or capability judgments.
These are proof judgments; no executable Boolean decision procedure is claimed.
Their definitions and transport lemmas reside beside `ExecutionSite` in the shared
source module, allowing each site to retain checks of its actual certificates.

Handler installation requires its authenticated declaration bounds to fit the
receiving scope's visible resources plus a fixed ambient allowance. Resource
installation extends the actual lexical context. Global resource-world membership
does not establish availability, and a dormant capture's resources are not visible
to its caller. The ambient allowance remains an explicit parameter; its origin
must be established when constructing complete source admission.

Sequence, choice and cleanup recursively check their existing source premises.
Request checks the same selected clause at the live captured/tail context and
retains its callback and waiting-code checks. Resume and discard use the actual
restored and closing contexts from their source rules. Pending code follows
ordinary return and unwind: skipped expressions need no execution check, while
callbacks are checked at their actual callback boundary. Already installed
handler frames introduce no second installation check; their ongoing support
belongs to the separate installed-handler invariant.

`CodeChecked.handler_supported` exposes the installation bound from the same
checked handler rows. Local examples accept a nonempty bound under its lexical
cell or an explicit ambient allowance, reject global-world membership and a
dormant captured cell as substitutes for receiver availability, and admit a
skipped plain frame during unwind. An application-shaped sequence also admits two
nested handlers using the same nonempty bound. These examples test this resource
facet; they do not assert authentication of a complete source program.

Latent function-body rows enter through the existing application sequence. This
judgment introduces no whole-input-port resource requirement. M0.2 completes the
structural judgment. The transport results below preserve its evidence under the
existing source transformations. They do not establish complete initial admission
or the runtime invariant.

### Transport of installation admission

[SourceScheduledInstallationTransport.lean](SourceScheduledInstallationTransport.lean)
preserves the structural resource facet through the source transformations needed
by the one-shot execution model. The proofs retain the existing row annotations,
lexical receivers and ordinary/unwind distinctions.

Exact context equalities and proof irrelevance handle reindexing at identical
source indices. A shared parameter-transfer proof separates resource evidence
from the already-proved source constraints on permissions, phases, worlds and
installation names. Its public wrappers use the existing source transformations
to construct destination admission. Ambient growth enlarges only the explicit
allowance; world growth does not make additional resources lexically visible.

Pending-source splitting and recomposition preserve checks at the same decorated
boundaries. Capture and callback extraction reuse the selected cut and declaration
uniqueness proofs. Resume and discard retain their actual saved and caller
premises, including the saved demand and callback return modes.

Deep spent-marker and pure-frame transport use the existing context-history
relations, including changes inside dormant saved continuations. Both relations
preserve visible resources. The handler case therefore retains its original
resource bound without assuming availability in a new receiver. Ordinary
computation selects the already-checked bind, application or branch rows;
source substitution reuses the authenticated same-row substitution result.

These are source-evidence transports, M0.3. M0.4 integrates the runtime resource
component below. The following sections give initial admission and complete
capture construction and combined constructive preservation; progress remains
separate.

### Installed handler support

[SourceScheduledInstalledSupport.lean](SourceScheduledInstalledSupport.lean)
checks the resource dependencies of an installed handler's actual clauses. A
parameter contributes its declared resource port only where the clause body uses
it. Authentication proves that these dependencies are included in the finite
bound stored in the same declaration rows. The installation checker then places
that bound within the handler's lexical receiver and the fixed ambient allowance.

The support view retains the physical stack, handler identities and resource
visibility. It checks declaration support inside both active frames and dormant
captured continuations. The existing machine access invariant still accounts for
ordinary values and cleanup callbacks. Neither component substitutes the global
resource world for lexical availability.

All 32 lexical transition cases preserve this support view. Handler installation
uses the predecessor's authenticated source and resource check. Capture,
resumption and lexical abandonment reuse the established structural support
proofs. Abandonment traverses the captured scopes and their cleanup boundaries;
there is no generated disposal-plan premise.

[SourceScheduledInstallationMachine.lean](SourceScheduledInstallationMachine.lean)
combines this support with the existing complete execution state. Resource checks
now belong to the actual `ExecutionSite`: they decorate its current source
certificate and retained-code certificate. Unwind source carries its own checked
pending certificate. A fixed ambient parameter passes through both forms.
Allocation therefore retains the same chosen types, declaration rows and runtime
identities for all components of the successor state.

The shared source implementation constructs these checks at all 24 execution-site
construction sites, including three fixtures. Its capture-site construction also
retains the selected clause and captured-code checks. Twenty-three thin wrappers
reuse the existing complete-state transition proofs and attach installed support
to their exact successors; these cover 31 of the 32 transition families. Neither
source preservation nor the wrappers accept a successor resource-check premise.

This completes the M0.4 resource component. The following sections establish
M2 initial admission and the remaining M1 capture endpoint. The generic 32-case
installed-support theorem alone is not a complete-state preservation theorem.
M3 combined constructive preservation and M4 fuel-bounded execution are
established below.
The experiment remains one-shot; other continuation targets and Core alignment
are outside this result.

### Initial source admission

[SourceScheduledInitialAdmission.lean](SourceScheduledInitialAdmission.lean)
connects a closed, annotated source program to the complete `InstallationState`
used by the transition proofs. The initial stack, stores, action map, contract
map, captured-scope annotations, issued owners and completion history are empty.

Admission is proof-carrying. It requires the following existing static evidence
on the same source and row decoration:

| Evidence | What it establishes |
| --- | --- |
| Source typing and authentication | The source has its declared result and its latent function and clause rows describe the actual code. |
| Plan certification | The declaration plans meet the existing clause-policy checks. |
| Structural `Code` certificate | Requests, continuation use and cleanup are checked at their lexical receivers, including retained code. |
| `CodeChecked` on that certificate | Installation resource bounds fit those same receivers. |
| `Accounting.Run` and a checked annotated root | Ownership accounting follows the executable source and continuation; its requirements satisfy the budget. |
| Initial resource-support check | The source refers to no unavailable external resource. |
| Immutable builtin signature compatibility | Every defined cell operation has the fixed read or write ports used by the runtime; undefined operations remain admissible. |

These are syntax-indexed derivations. Symbolic fresh-name premises reuse the
existing source rules; they do not quantify over future runtime executions.
The admission theorem does not take an `ExecutionSite`, `ExecutableSource`,
complete machine state or successor invariant as an input. It constructs the
site and all initial bookkeeping, reusing the established empty-state lemmas.

The closed-program interface fixes both the ambient resource allowance and the
external budget to empty. The more general assembly helper makes its ambient
allowance and budget explicit. Neither interface is a claim that a compiler
infers all annotations or decides every source judgment.

The resource/cleanup/application example constructs the entire initial state
without a supplied source-admission premise. Negative examples reject an
unavailable resource reference, an unhandled top-level operation and an initial
continuation use with no allocated ticket. These checks target the admission
boundary rather than merely constructing runtime bookkeeping.

[SourceScheduledInitialHandlerExample.lean](SourceScheduledInitialHandlerExample.lean)
constructs admission for a closed handler that performs an operation and disposes
its captured continuation. Its clause authentication, lexical source certificate,
resource check and ownership derivation are constructed explicitly, then passed
to the same closed initial-state theorem. The callback/application example uses
pure function bodies.

This is M2's source-to-initial-state result. The later M3 and M4 theorems use
that same complete state and the admitted immutable builtin-signature law.
Core alignment and other continuation targets are outside this one-shot
experiment.

### Complete capture-state construction

#### Structural capture and restoration boundary

[StructuralKernel.lean](StructuralKernel.lean) packages the existing structural
judgments used by the schematic request rules. `structural_capture` takes a
`CaptureAdmission`, predecessor `WellFormed` proof and fresh ticket. The
admission contains the exact `SourceCut` and the operand-access inclusion in the
outside support. The result chooses the answer type, proves the live control
well formed, retains payload availability and gives exact owner insertion.

`structural_resume` starts from the actual well-formed clause prefix around the
live boundary. It proves full saved-control recomposition, exact owner
permutation and absence of the consumed ticket. `structural_discard` separately
requires `Discardable` for that actual prefix and a fresh close owner; it proves
well-formed materialized closing control and exact accounting for the new close
owner and consumed ticket. Abstract `Discardable` plans do not establish the
lexical runtime's cleanup admission.

`structural_execution_ownership` lifts the existing ledger preservation theorem
over a supplied finite `Steps` derivation. It proves unique completion,
disjoint live and completed owners, and complete accounting at an empty control.
It does not construct steps or establish M4 progress.

These lower-level results do not replace the richer
`SourceAdmission.Code.request` judgment. That judgment checks the actual source
cut, capture guard, disposal callback, captured-owner bound, cleanup budget,
selected clause rows, retained continuation and recursively checked fresh-owner
clause body. Permission and one-shot usage checks remain independent. No single
capture guard proves every possible future clause prefix safe for resumption or
disposal.

[SourceScheduledCapture.lean](SourceScheduledCapture.lean) supplies M1's remaining
complete-state endpoint, `InstallationState.capture_successor`. Together with
the existing transition endpoints, this covers all 32 M1 transition families.

The theorem takes the complete predecessor state, an operational handler cut,
a closed operand, a fresh ticket and the contract's row annotations. It derives
the selected source clause and its checked ownership root from the predecessor.
It takes no successor source certificate, successor resource check or successor
machine invariant as a premise.

The proof reuses lexical selection and stack realization to find the physical
handler boundary. Four existing source helpers now retain clause closedness and
the captured boundary's answer mode, both already implied by their inputs.
The private assembly reuses the successor-site and successor-root proofs,
saved-record allocation, resource-access transport and lifetime bookkeeping.
All components refer to the same allocated contract, ticket and successor site.
The public endpoint attaches installed-handler support to that successor.

The result gives an actual lexical event and its complete `InstallationState`,
including source admission, resource access, saved records, permissions and owner
histories. As with the other allocating endpoints, the successor is existential.
The public result does not expose the internal target-stack and supplied-row
equalities. It does not assert preservation for arbitrary caller-supplied raw
transition metadata; the combined transition theorem remains M3.

[SourceScheduledCaptureExample.lean](SourceScheduledCaptureExample.lean) connects
the admitted handled-operation example to handler installation and then capture,
retaining the complete successor state. This checks that the new endpoint applies
to a concrete program admitted through M2.

M1 is complete at the individual-transition level. The following result combines
those endpoints. These results do not extend the one-shot scope.

### Combined constructive preservation

[SourceScheduledPreservation.lean](SourceScheduledPreservation.lean) combines all
32 M1 transition families into one theorem, `Preservation.preservation`.
For a valid predecessor and an applicable operational request, it constructs a
successor that realizes the request, an actual `LexicalUnwind.Event`, and the
complete successor invariant. No successor check is a premise.

[SourceScheduledPreservationState.lean](SourceScheduledPreservationState.lean)
packages the changing contracts, handler tables, annotations, resource world,
histories, saved stores, owner rows and concrete run in `Snapshot`. Validity is
a separate abbreviation for the existing `InstallationState`; the snapshot
does not contain a validity proof. The operation signature, outward interfaces,
ambient allowance, budget and terminal value type remain fixed.

The proof has two independently checked groups:

| Group | Transition coverage | Preservation result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Stable](SourceScheduledPreservationStable.lean) | 17 constructors cover 25 families: four ordinary computations, six unwind advances and fifteen remaining cases. | Every supplied stable step preserves its exact successor and gives an actual event. |
| [Allocating](SourceScheduledPreservationAllocating.lean) | Seven families: focus, cleanup registration, resource entry, handler installation, capture, resume and discard. | Every supplied request has a preserving realization using the existing M1 choices. |

The count retains the fixed inventory: 20 ordinary evaluation cases, six unwind
advances and six outer lexical transitions. Unit close/retire steps remain
separate from the general close-value/retire-value transitions. Focus has ten
expression forms but remains one transition family. The old disposal-plan raw
step is excluded by the existing lexical machine; discard uses local unwind.

`Request` and `Realizes` contain operational conditions and metadata equations,
not successor validity. The combined theorem dispatches to the two group proofs;
it neither duplicates their semantic proofs nor wraps a preservation assumption.
The stable group preserves metadata by record updates. Allocation and
continuation use retain the contracts, records and histories selected by the
same M1 endpoint that constructs the runtime successor.

The quantifier order matters: every valid predecessor and applicable request
has **some preserving realization**. This does not say that every raw successor
or every witness satisfying `Realizes` preserves the invariant. Raw allocation
permits annotation choices that disagree with source typing, as established by
the [entry-annotation comparison](#deterministic-computation-and-entry-annotations).
Capture retains the existential metadata boundary of M1. The result therefore
provides constructive preservation, not unrestricted raw-step subject reduction.

[SourceScheduledPreservationExample.lean](SourceScheduledPreservationExample.lean)
uses the combined interface to take the admitted handler example through handler
installation and capture, preserving the complete state and both actual events.

This closes M3 at the source-constructed transition boundary established by M1.

### M4 checked boundary

[SourceScheduledBuiltinSignatures.lean](SourceScheduledBuiltinSignatures.lean)
states the immutable environment condition used by builtin dispatch. Every
defined cell operation has either the read ports at key `0` or the write ports
at key `1`; operations may remain undefined. The negative checks reject an
extra cell operation and a read with the wrong input type. Initial admission
retains this law as a fixed program premise rather than adding it to evolving
snapshot validity.

[SourceScheduledM4Availability.lean](SourceScheduledM4Availability.lean) proves
`Preservation.available`: builtin compatibility and a valid snapshot determine
either `Terminal` or an applicable M3 `Request`. Authenticated source typing
supplies canonical functions and Booleans for application and branching.
Operation requests reconstruct the actual handler cut or builtin cell update;
capture and cleanup allocate owners fresh for the current ledger. No selection,
raw-step or successor-validity witness is assumed by the dispatcher.

M3 `Preservation.preservation` turns each available request into an actual
lexical event and a valid successor. `Preservation.finite_prefix` iterates that
construction for any fuel, returning a raw event trace of length at most the
fuel, a valid endpoint, and evidence that the fuel was exhausted or the endpoint
is terminal. [SourceScheduledM4Terminal.lean](SourceScheduledM4Terminal.lean)
gives terminal owner accounting and the empty terminal stack.

[SourceScheduledM4.lean](SourceScheduledM4.lean) connects that result to M2.
`InitialAdmission.Program.finite_prefix` constructs the initial valid snapshot
from a proof-carrying admitted program and then supplies its fuel-bounded run.
`Examples.handled_discard_finite_prefix` instantiates the theorem for the closed
handler example that captures and disposes its continuation.

[SourceScheduledM4Execution.lean](SourceScheduledM4Execution.lean) keeps the
raw and source-preserving claims separate. `RawTrace` contains only lexical
events. `RawTrace.ownership` proves exact ownership consequences for every such
trace from an initial ledger, while endpoint validity in `finite_prefix` is
reconstructed at each step through M3. This does not prove type or source
preservation for arbitrary raw annotation choices. Core correspondence and
other continuation targets remain outside the checked boundary.

## Laws and research boundary

Prove each proposed provider equation in a concrete state-and-observation model
or by contextual equivalence. Exhibit distinguishable closed observations, such
as different Boolean results, to establish non-collapse of the admitted theory.
A supplied provider law is a proof obligation, not an unchecked axiom. Handler
order is observable, so a scope-exchange law needs its own argument about
capture, support, and completion events.

[Plotkin and Pretnar](https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.1399) supply the connection
between effect theories and their handler interpretations. Their model account
does not require changing this operational syntax into a monadic calculus.
[Tang et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.09383) identify the mismatch between
continuation use and linear resource use, and prove resource integrity for
their calculi. That motivates the independent control-use checks here; it does
not prove Ash's disposal or scheduling extensions. DN-0033 records the other
[research sources and their transfer limits](../../DN-0033-direct-effects-and-continuation-capabilities.md#research-grounding-and-transfer-limits).
